# AGMessage 0.6.0: the plan

> **Where this plan lives.** This file is the merged 0.6.0 plan, committed from the planning workspace. Paths that
> begin `060/` name files of that workspace (the parts' working files, earlier revisions, benches and measuring
> scripts); they are not in the repository, and every reading the plan relies on is taken again by the unit that
> needs it. The owner's answers are `DECISIONS.md` beside this file, and the Board mock is `board-view/` (its
> screenshots at half size; the 63 device shots of `060/board-view/devices/` are not kept).

This is the one plan 0.6.0 is built from. It joins the design (`design.md`) and its six addenda, each kept whole as a
part, behind a Part 0 that says what 0.6.0 is, the release rule, every owner decision and where it lands, the one open
question, and one build order in which every unit has one number. It was assembled on 2026-10-28 by
`060/plan-build/build.py` from the files named in §0.3, then read back, corrected by hand, checked twice and
corrected again (§0.10). Nothing in the repository
was edited while it was planned. Code citations are to AGMessage at `89104d8` (0.5.1), as in every part.

---

# Part 0: the plan on one page, and its registers

## 0.1 What 0.6.0 is

AGMessage 0.6.0 is one release, made of the 80 units of §0.6 in that order. There is no 0.5.2 (answer 29).

- **Rooms within halls** (Part 1). A hall is its Main room, as today. Side rooms (Legal, Media) sit beside it, each with
  its own op log, seats, lock, invites and guest code. Rights are checked per room behind a fence (`rbac.canIn`). A
  message goes into another room by `room:send` when that room's allow-list names the sender's room, and it can be
  withdrawn. A file moves to another room only by `room:send` or `forward`. The room switcher shows a dot on a room
  with news.
- **People's pages** (Part 1 §5; Part 4 §5.9). Numbered takes, each confirmed page by page, go to the Board (everyone
  seated On stage in the Main room) or to one person, in two layers: the show, and information over it. A web page
  needs a right of its own, `stage.web`.
- **The Board's chat view** (Part 7, which replaces Part 1 §6). The chat comes first and is compact, with the clock
  (the default), Stagewatch's countdown or nothing beside it. Both the device and the admin set it, and the admin may
  lock it.
  - Pins for oneself, 👍 Got it, and the admin's On stage settings: two destinations, and whether Got it clears.
  - An On stage seat shares no file, asks no question, forwards nothing and answers no one else's help request. The
    server refuses each.
  - Dark by default.
- **The stage** (Part 4).
  - Files to transfer are kept apart from files shown on the stage.
  - A researcher shows a page as a picture, the document, what they see, or a picked word, line, item, paragraph,
    cell, row or column.
  - Downloads are for the backstage team, by ticket. A Board tablet keeps no copy, and offers ⬇ only on a whole file
    sent with "Let them download it".
  - A confidential mark, and a record of what was shown in the transcript and the minutes.
  - On stage seats come by invite, account or the admin.
  - Every stage feature works on the Board's mixture of devices.
- **Speed, stability, modules, the experience and right-click menus** (Part 5).
  - One op table, latest-wins frames, and an outbox that never loses or doubles a send.
  - Pages come back by themselves, and health keeps the day's peaks.
  - A module fence, and one gate for new verbs.
  - One action catalogue behind every button and menu.
  - A hall page that fits a phone, one word per thing, and help in two taps.
  - Bounds for remote phones through the tunnel, and a page floor for older devices.
- **The start window** (Part 2). The .bat says what is wrong, the browser opens on the copy that is serving, and
  whatever holds the port is named.
- **The audit chain** (Part 3). Keyed with HMAC-SHA256, exported signed with Ed25519 and checked offline. It carries on
  across events through archive points, and at one of them the admin may split the older part into a signed archive.
- **The Windows install** (Part 6).
  - A per-machine installer. The node is a startup task in session 0 under LocalService, with its data in
    `%ProgramData%\AGMessage` (B-task).
  - The Windows account that installs is the laptop's admin. It gives, takes back or hands over the token and the
    start, stop and upgrade rights.
  - An upgrade checked against its GitHub release needs no administrator.
  - A portable folder can be imported once.
  - An event is archived. The next one continues it, copies its settings and structure, or starts fresh.

## 0.2 The release rule

- **No 0.5.2** (answer 29, "wrap into 0.6.0"). Every unit of §0.6 is a 0.6.0 unit. Only #56 and #79 may move to 0.6.x,
  and only as §0.6 says: #56 may slip, and #79 lands only when reading 3 triggers it before the close.
  - #69 and #71 must land. They build what the owner asked for by name: the clock or countdown, with its "local and
    admin option" and its lock, and B2's "An admin can choose" and B4's "Clearing the message is an admin option".
  - The other changes a reading of 5-§13.4 triggers have no unit of §0.6: the burst of reading 2, the quiet-moment
    compaction of reading 4, the coalesced presence lines of reading 8, and a changed window or text size from readings
    1 and 9. The close (#80) puts each triggered reading in the release notes, and its change is designed as a 0.6.x
    unit.
- **One commit per unit.** The subject is `AGMessage 0.6.0, unit N: <what landed>`, where N is the global number of
  §0.6.
  - The body's first line names the part and its local id ("Part 6, unit U8"), then the reasoning.
  - The parts' own subject shapes (`unit S`, `unit Un`, `unit 3a`) are not used.
- **Before each commit:** `npm run check` is green and the browser smoke has run (AGMessage's `CLAUDE.md`, "How a change
  closes").
- **Unit #1 goes first.** It bumps `app/package.json` to 0.6.0 and opens the CHANGELOG's 0.6.0 entry.
  `app/test/version.test.js:76` fails any commit whose newest CHANGELOG header is not the version `app/package.json:3`
  names (0.5.1 today), so nothing lands before #1. Every later CHANGELOG line goes under 0.6.0's heading.
- **The papers move with each unit.** Each part's papers section names the lines its units move.
- **The close (#80) is last.**
  - It re-dates the CHANGELOG, sets `runBase`, and re-measures and raises the coverage gate.
  - It asserts that the catalogue's list of required verbs is complete.
  - It reads Part 5 §13.4's readings as they stand, and puts each of Part 6's U7 readings that missed its mark in the
    release notes.
  - It has `docs/DEVICES.md` walked on the owner's devices (Part 4 §5.15.3, Part 5 §15.10, Part 7 §17.7), with no ✕
    left standing. A row the owner has no device for reads "not walked", a fact in the paper and never a pass (5-§11,
    7-§17.7). A Board device of the owner's below the page floor (5-§15.10) is a ✕: it holds the tag until the floor is
    lowered for it or the owner retires it from the Board (answer 22).
- **The order of authority where the parts disagree:**
  1. the owner's answers (§0.4);
  2. Part 7, the Board addendum (the newest);
  3. Part 6, install;
  4. Part 5, architecture and UX;
  5. Part 4, the stage;
  6. Part 3, the audit chain;
  7. Part 2, the start window;
  8. Part 1, the design.

  A claim about the code yields to the code at `89104d8`, as every part says of itself. §0.8 lists each disagreement
  found and how it is resolved.

**How to read it:**

- **Headings.** Every heading of Part N carries the prefix `N-`, so a reference reads "3-H.4", "4-§5.9.2.2", "6-U.5.1"
  or "1-§2.3".
- **Bare references.** Inside a part, a bare § or a bare unit number is that part's own, unless the text names another
  paper ("design §2.3", "the stage addendum's 26"). §0.7 turns any local id into its global number.
- **File names name parts:**
  - `design.md` is Part 1;
  - `addendum-startup.md` is Part 2;
  - `addendum-audit-hmac.md` is Part 3;
  - `addendum-stage.md` is Part 4;
  - `addendum-arch-ux.md` is Part 5;
  - `addendum-install.md` is Part 6;
  - `addendum-board.md` is Part 7.
  - "The final", "the draft" and "revision N" name earlier versions of those files, kept in `060/`. None is part of the
    plan.
- **Global numbers.** Each unit's heading carries its global number, **[#n]**.
- **"The splice".** Where a part says its numbers are "placeholders until the splice", the splice is this plan. Its
  section numbers stand, with their part's prefix, and its units take the global numbers of §0.6. The parts' own
  orders of splicing differ; the order of the parts here is the reverse of the order of authority (§0.2).
- **Amendments.** A section that another part amends opens with a one-line note naming the governing text: **Amended
  by**, or **Replaced by** where another part's text stands in its place. Otherwise the parts stand as their authors
  left them, except for the exact replacements listed in §0.9, which are applied in place, and the corrections of
  §0.10, made in the part's own file.

## 0.5 The one open question

**"4 - Admin defined".** The owner wrote it in the message of 2026-10-27 (§0.4.1). `DECISIONS.md` reads it as the
stage reading **S4**, "(to confirm: S4, not A4)". The plan applies that reading as written.

- **Applied (S4):** a per-hall `settings.guestWeb`, off by default. While it is on, a locked hall's backstage code
  guests show web pages.
  - The admin (`theAdmin()`, §0.8 C14) sets it on the Roles & invites panel with `admin:guestWeb`.
  - It writes a `room.guestWeb` row, and an unlock turns it off.
  - Guests' pages hear of a change at once (`pages:rights {canWeb}`).
  - It lives in global unit **#54** (Part 1's unit 19, as 4-§11 amends it). See 4-§5.9.2.2, 4-§5.11 and 4-§7.7.
- **A4 keeps its default:** the first keyed start asks, and holds no sign-in, take or send (3-H.6; #5).
- **If the owner meant A4:**
  - S4 takes its default: no code guest shows a web page, and `admin:guestWeb`, its switch, its row and its tests
    leave #54 (4-§12, "The one open question").
  - "Admin defined" would make holding sign-ins at the first keyed start an admin's setting. No part designs that, and
    the plan does not build it unless the owner says so (3-H.15).
- **A third "4" in the papers:** design question 4, "Is a 'blank page' black or white?" (1-§12). Its default is black.
  - The questions put to the owner run in one sequence: the design's 1-9, the stage's 10-20, the architecture
    addendum's 21-33 and the install addendum's 34-45.
  - On that numbering, "4" is design question 4, and "Admin defined" would make the blank page's colour an admin's
    setting.
  - No part designs that. If it is what the owner meant, S4 also takes its default, and the blank page's colour as an
    admin's setting is designed as a unit of its own.
- **The question to put to the owner:** "Did '4 - Admin defined' mean S4 (a locked hall's backstage guests showing web
  pages), A4 (holding sign-ins at the first keyed start until the token holder answers), or design question 4 (the
  colour of a blank page)?"
- **When to ask:** before #50 lands, so that the blank page's colour, if that is what was meant, is designed before the
  store of what people's pages show (#50) and the pushed screen (#53) are built. Of the units of §0.6, the answer
  changes #54 only.
  - S4: #54 lands as written.
  - Otherwise: #54 lands without `admin:guestWeb`, its switch, its row and its tests (4-§12). What "Admin defined" then
    asks for (holding sign-ins at the first keyed start, or the blank page's colour) has no design in any part. It is
    designed, and given a unit of its own, before it is built.

**Awaiting the owner, but not questions of 0.6.0's build** (none holds a unit of §0.6):

- **3-H.15's offer.** A token sign-in written into `admin-sessions.json` holds the whole admin dashboard at the next
  watchdog restart, since the file is read and trusted at start (`accounts.js:408-418`). Unit H (#5) closes it for
  Accept and the token's export only. 3-H.15 offers the owner a unit of its own (keyed hashes, or token sign-ins kept in
  memory). It is not a unit of §0.6; until the owner takes it up, it stays among 3-H.15's findings.
- **4-§5.9.12's items 3-7**, suggested to Stagewatch for 2.20 and marked "not yet put to the owner". AGMessage 0.6.0
  assumes none of them. They are put to the owner before the request is handed over.
- **A fact, not a decision:** which iPadOS the owner's oldest Board iPad runs (D1), and whether any Board device of the
  owner's is below the page floor (4-Gaps, 5-§15.10). It is recorded before #20 sets the floor.

## 0.6 The global build order

Every unit of every part appears once. "Needs" lists the global numbers each unit depends on, as its part's "What can
move" and the unit's own text state them. Every number points to an earlier unit, except the two marked †.

- Every unit also needs #1, because of the CHANGELOG fence (§0.2). "1" is listed only where nothing else is.
- **In 0.6.0:**
  - **must:** the unit ships in 0.6.0;
  - **may slip:** the parts allow it to move to 0.6.x without touching another unit;
  - **conditional:** it lands in 0.6.0 only when its reading triggers before the close.
- **†** marks a dependency the parts state but this order cannot honour, because it closes a cycle. §0.8 C1 and C2 say
  how each is resolved.

## 0.7 Local ids, collisions and the global number

A unit's local id is the one its part uses. The global number is the one a commit uses (§0.2).

|---|---|
| 1 | 1 → #1 · 2 → #3 · 3 → replaced by #23, #24, #25 (Part 5 units 3a, 3b, 3c) · 4 → #37 · 5 → #39 · 6 → #40 · 7 → #41 · 8 → #42 · 9 → #43 · 10 → #44 · 11 → #45 · 12 → #46 · 13 → #47 · 14 → #48 · 15 → #49 · 16 → #50 · 17 → #51 · 18 → #53 · 19 → #54 · 20 → #55 (carried by Part 7 unit 20a) · 21 → #56 · 22 → #80 (the close) |

**The collisions, and how the global number resolves them:**

- **"Unit 22".** Part 1's close and Part 4's upload checks share it. Part 1's 22 is #80; Part 4's 22 is #58.
- **"Units 30, 31, 32".** Part 4 and Part 5 both use them:
  - Part 4's 30, 31 and 32 are the stage record (#67), the confidential mark (#68) and the close (#80);
  - Part 5's 30, 31 and 32 are the gate (#38), the header (#52) and the bounded first open (#57).
  - Part 5's 33 (#79) and 34 (the close, #80) are its own.
- **"Unit 3".** Part 1's unit 3 is replaced by Part 5's 3a, 3b and 3c (#23, #24, #25), as 5-§0 says. Every "needs 3"
  reads "needs 3a" (#23).
- **"Unit 20".** Part 1's unit 20 is carried whole by Part 7's 20a (#55), which says "(amends 20)". Part 7's 20b, 20c
  and 20d are #69, #70 and #71.
- **The close.** It is Part 1's "unit 22", Part 4's "unit 32" and Part 5's "unit 34". Part 7 and Part 6 call it "unit
  34", and Part 7 says "the splice settles the number". It is **#80**.
  - Part 4 §0 says every design "unit 22" reads "unit 32"; Part 5 §11 says it reads "unit 34". Neither replacement is
    applied, because #80 replaces both.
- **Additions, not units.** Part 7's "unit 9 (adds)" and "unit 14 (adds)" add to #43 and #48. Part 4's "unit 19,
  amended" is #54.
- **Letters that mean two things:**
  - **S** is the start-window unit (#4). S1-S16 are the stage readings (4-§12).
  - **D** is Part 5's compaction unit (#15). D1-D7 are the device matrix's rows (4-§5.15.1).
  - **W** is Part 5's words unit (#17). Part 6's draft units W1-W12 are not used (6-U.7).
  - **R1-R13** are Part 6's Windows readings (6-U7). "Readings 0-9" are Part 5's (5-§13.4).
  - **"Kind S"** was refused as a catalogue name (5-Critiques not taken).
- **Question numbers:**
  - the design's are 1-9, the stage's 10-20, Part 5's 21-33 and Part 6's 34-45;
  - Part 3 numbers its own A-C and 1-4;
  - the stage's readings are S1-S16, and the Board's questions B1-B6.
  - §0.5 says why "4" stays open.

## 0.8 Where the parts disagree, and how this plan resolves it

- **C1. A cycle: 20a needs T, T needs 25, and 25 needs 20.**
  - The statements:
    - Part 7 §11 says 20a needs "stage T (the device legs at `mobile: true`, the floor leg's init script,
      `docs/DEVICES.md`)".
    - Part 4 §11 says T needs 25, 26 and 27 ("a stand-in is a page picture"), and 25 needs 20 ("the simple view's
      controls").
    - Part 7 §11 repeats that "stage units 25 and 26 … need 20".
  - Part 7's own two statements close the cycle through Part 4's T, so the order of authority cannot settle it.
  - **The resolution:** 25 needs the simple view to exist. 20a needs only T's test harness. So #55 (20a) lands before
    #61 (25), and #64 (T) after #63 (27). What the units share is built by whichever lands first. That is how
    5-§11 already reads M and T, where M "stands alone" and "M and the stage addendum's T share the floor leg and
    `docs/DEVICES.md`":
    - #20 (M) lands first. It makes the floor leg's init script (`app/test/browser-smoke.js:117` holds the hook) and
      `docs/DEVICES.md` with 5-§15.10's rows and the matrix of 4-§5.15.1.
    - #55 (20a) makes the device legs: `mobile: true` (`false` today, `browser-smoke.js:118`), touch, and the three
      sizes of 4-§5.15.3. It runs its Board steps on them and adds its layout leg.
    - #64 (T) adds the Board-side checks of units 23-29, the stand-in steps, the ES2020 fence, the benches and its rows
      in `docs/DEVICES.md`.
  - No unit's scope is cut. Only who builds the shared harness first moves.
- **C2. A cycle: U18 needs "U16's immutable releases", and U16 needs U18** (6-U.7, "What can move").
  - **The resolution:** #77 (U18) lands before #78 (U16).
  - U18's check refuses any release that does not read `immutable: true` (6-U18, step 2), so before #78 it fails
    closed.
  - Nothing is lost by that. U18 installs only a release newer than the one installed, so its first real use is the
    first release after 0.6.0. #78 turns immutable releases on inside 0.6.0: "Release assets cannot be modified or
    deleted" and "Git tags cannot be moved"
    (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases).
- **C3. Part 5's unit 31 "may slip to 0.6.x without touching another unit"** (5-§11, the cut line).
  - Part 5's own "18 and 20 need 31", and Part 7's "20a needs … arch-ux 31 (header): this view is its simple branch",
    say otherwise.
  - Part 7 outranks Part 5, and #53 (18) and #55 (20a) cannot slip, so **#52 must land in 0.6.0**. §0.6 marks it so.
- **C4. Whether the port-holder message can read U8's busy line.**
  - 6-U8 says the folder pipe answers the busy line "for unit S's port-holder message", and that "Unit S's port-holder
    message and U14 read the busy line too".
  - 2-S.2 and 2-S.7 say only the folder-held words can. A copy refused at the port alone cannot name the pipe, which is
    named after the other copy's data folder.
  - The code bears Part 2 out: `holdDataFolder` names the pipe by a hash of `DATA_DIR` (`app/server.js:2453-2454`).
  - Part 6 outranks Part 2, but this is a claim about the code, and every part yields to the code. Part 2's reading
    governs for that sentence, and the rest of U8 stands.
  - A note at 6-U8 points here, and Part 6's text is not rewritten.
- **C5. (Withdrawn.)** Part 3's last owner bullet doubted the confirmation of 12 and 20. It now quotes it as
  `DECISIONS.md` records it, in the owner's words: "A board tablet can have a feature to tick to enable it to be
  downloaded." 4-§4.6.6 applies it (#61, #62).
- **C6. Part 3's "until unit S lands" words** (3-H.6, 3-H.13) never ship. #4 (S) lands before #5 (H), as 2-S.5 asks.
- **C7. Shift+right-click on On stage content.**
  - 5-§16.2's R6 keeps the browser's menu "always with Shift+right-click".
  - S14, which the owner kept ("Defaults"), and 4-§0 say that on an On stage seat's stage content Shift+right-click
    opens AGMessage's menu too, so "Save image as" is never offered.
  - The owner's answer outranks Part 5. A note at 5-§16.2 points here.
  - Firefox shows its own menu on Shift+right-click without firing `contextmenu`, so no page can cancel it
    (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/contextmenu_event; R6 notes "Firefox does it anyway").
    4-§4.6.6's "What cannot be prevented" names it.
- **C8. The close's number** is #80 (§0.7).
- **C9. A Part 7 replacement whose target text is gone.**
  - 7-§0.3 replaces 4-§5.9.2.2's "No code guest holds it: `GUEST_CAPS` (`server.js:699`) is unchanged". Part 4's
    revision 4 rewrote that sentence for S4, and it read "A code guest holds it only by the hall's setting …
    `GUEST_CAPS` (`server.js:699`) is unchanged".
  - That "unchanged" was S4's, and it stops being true once unit G (#21) narrows `GUEST_CAPS.board` to view and post.
    Part 4's sentence now says both: "S4 adds nothing to `GUEST_CAPS` (`server.js:699`); the board addendum's unit G
    narrows `GUEST_CAPS.board`", and a code guest holds `stage.web` only by the hall's setting.
- **C10. Part 3 asks Part 5 to drop a count.** 3-H.13 asks that 5-§15.4's "The eleven rights" read "The rights".
  - An earlier part is amending a later one, so it is not applied in place.
  - It does not contradict Part 5: #6 adds `audit.export` to `rbac.CAPS`, and the Accounts page draws its rights from
    `rbac.CAPS` (4-§0, `users.js:122`), so a fixed count would go stale. Read 5-§15.4 as "The rights".
- **C11. #76 (U15) archives stores that later-numbered parts' units make.**
  - `pages.json` (#50), `stage\` (#67), the confidential holds (#68), each hall's `guestWeb` (#54), and the Board's
    per-person clock and On stage switches (#69, #71).
  - It is placed after all of them, so the archive, continue and copy move each of them.
  - Two go further, and 6-U15 says both: under all three kinds the confidential holds (`pages.json`'s `holds`) are
    written into the new event's `pages.json`, since a hold belongs to a kept link and its confidential line may still
    be on that Stagewatch's frame (4-§5.11, 4-§5.14); and copy carries each hall's `guestWeb` with its lock
    (4-§5.9.2.2).
- **C12. Part 1 §11's "1, 2 and 3 stand alone"** is replaced by Part 5 §11's "1 and 2 stand alone. The lettered units
  each land after 1".
- **C13. The parts' commit subjects** (`unit Un`, `unit S`, `unit 3a`) give way to §0.2's global number.
- **C14. "The admin" in the owner's answers is one predicate, `theAdmin()`.**
  - The owner named the admin for the clock or countdown's lock ("Yes, the admin may lock"), B2's two switches ("An
    admin can choose"), B4's Got it clears ("Clearing the message is an admin option"), S4's `guestWeb` ("Admin
    defined") and the split ("Admin can choose to split"). 6-U15's Archive this event… is "for admin accounts and the
    token at the laptop", which is the same.
  - Each reads 7-§17.6's predicate: the host token, or an account whose role is `admin`, through the tunnel only where
    admins may sign in there. On a socket it is `theAdmin()` after `admin(ack)` (`server.js:1398`); over HTTP it is
    `theAdminReq(req)`: `isAdminReq` (`server.js:416-420`), then the token's cookie or the role (3-H.10.2).
  - A manager an admin granted `settings.manage` (`rbac.js:30`, `:105`) passes `admin(ack)` and `isAdminReq`
    (`server.js:688`, `:419`) and is refused each of these acts, with words and a test (4-§9 row 19, 3-H.12 "refused",
    6-U.8 U15, 7-§9 20b and 20d).
  - #7 (H3) builds the HTTP form for the split, and #76 (U15) uses it. #54 builds the socket form for `admin:guestWeb`,
    and #69 and #71 use it, so #69 needs #54 (§0.6).
  - The admin page's other acts keep `isAdmin` and `isAdminReq`, as 0.5.1 and the design have them (1-§2.4, design
    question 5).
  - The clock or countdown's choice, without its lock, is set where Chat view is (7-§17.3). That is the plan's
    reading of "the local and admin option", registered in §0.4.7.
- **C15. The Observer or Viewer row of the message menu.**
  - 5-§16.7 offered them Look; 4-§7.7, 4-§4.6.6 and 7-§0.3 said "no Look".
  - S2, which the owner kept, says observers and Viewer accounts see a picture shared in the chat as a card, without
    the picture, since the server withholds its link. S2 governs.
  - 5-§16.7's row now reads "no Look and no Download", 5-§16.8's matrix asserts `msg.look` absent for both, and a Viewer
    account's sockets join `ro:<key>` whatever their seat (4-§4.6.6), so a Viewer granted `hall.post`, who sits
    backstage, is withheld the link too (4-§9 row 26).

# Part 1: AGMessage 0.6.0: rooms within halls, people's screens, the Board's view (final design)

*`060/design.md`, 1398 lines, kept whole. Its headings carry the prefix `1-`; its units carry their global number, [#n] (Part 0 §0.3).*

Paths are relative to the repository's root, and `app/...` is the server and its pages. Line numbers are from the
current tree (0.5.1 at `cb564c0` plus the open 0.5.1 review edits). Each site is also named by its function, so it
can still be found if the lines move. Where a design and the code disagreed, the code was read and the code wins.

This design starts from the winning design ("data") and keeps its spine:

- side rooms live in their own map;
- side-room files are named `<HALL>.<ROOM>`;
- the migration writes nothing;
- every reader that means "a hall" is unchanged and fails closed.

It fixes every flaw the judges found in that design, and grafts the best ideas from the other two. §0.3 maps each flaw
to its fix.

---

## 1-§0. The decisions on one page

> **Amended by** 4-§0, 5-§0 and 7-§0.1, section by section below; Part 0's registers govern.

### 1-§0.1 The shape

> **Amended by** 4-§0, 5-§0 and 7-§0.1, at each subject's own section below; the units are Part 0 §0.6's.

- **A hall is its Main room, and today's store entry is that Main room.** The hall's key is the Main room's key, which
  is today's 6-character code. Every reader that means "a hall" therefore keeps working unchanged:
  - `store.rooms`, `get`, `has`;
  - the halls board, `/api/halls`, the context and the desk's notice count;
  - screens, Stagewatch links, peer links, desk results and accounts' `halls`.
- **A side room** (Legal, Media) is one more RoomStore entry, with its own op log, seq, ring, seats, lock and invites.
  - It sits beside its hall as `data/rooms/<HALL>.<KEY>.json|.log|.json.bak`.
  - In memory it lives in a second map, `store.side`, that only "any room" readers are changed to read. A reader that
    is missed sees no side room and answers "Room not found", which is fail closed.
- **A room's key and its guest code are two things.**
  - A side room's key is 8 characters. It is an address, never a credential.
  - Its guest code is 6 characters, made apart from the key, off by default, and renewable with **New code**.
  - A Main room's guest code is its key until someone presses New code. That is the 0.5.1 state, and it is said in the
    papers. New halls keep key = code at birth, so no test or page has to move.
- **Rights are checked per room, behind a fence.**
  - `rbac.can()` refuses `hall.view`, `hall.post` and `hall.files` when it is given a scope string.
  - Only `rbac.canIn(account, cap, scope)` answers those three. A call site that is not moved fails closed, even for
    an "every hall" account.
  - An account's side rooms are a new `rooms` field. `allHalls` never reaches a side room. The admin role reaches every
    room.
- **One socket holds one room.**
  - A room switch is a page navigation, so each page keeps one stream, one seq and today's resume protocol.
  - The switcher shows a dot on a room with news (unit 21).
- **Sending into another room is a new verb, `room:send`.**
  - It is allowed only when the sender may post where they are and the target's allow-list names their room.
  - The target room gets "↘ From Legal". The source keeps "↗ Sent to Main · delivered", which can be withdrawn.
  - Files keep to the room they were uploaded for, and only `room:send` (or `forward`) moves one across.
  - A file that came from another room never pops open on the Board's panel.
- **People's pages** get numbered takes, each confirmed by each page.
  - A take goes to the Board group (every page seated On stage in the Main room, accounts included) or to one person.
  - The person can dismiss it or minimise it into the On stage side bar.
  - A web take is reported "opened", never "on screen".
  - Web addresses are sealed at rest and named by host only.
- **The Board's simple view** is a view, not a right.
  - It is the default for an On stage seat, set per person by the admin, and applied live.
  - An account's view is on the account. A guest's view is in `data/pages.json`.

### 1-§0.2 New and changed stores

> **Amended by** 4-§5.11 (`pages.json`'s layers, `marks`, `holds`; the stage record's lanes), 7-§0.1 (§1.10: `views`, `pins`, accounts' `clock` and `onStage`), 6-U15 (events archived).

| Store | What | Lane |
|---|---|---|
| `data/rooms/<HALL>.<KEY>.*` | side rooms | the room store's own op log (the one exception, as today) |
| snapshot fields `guestCode`, `retired` | a room's guest code and its last three retired codes | written only by `store.compact` (no op, so never sent to a page) |
| `room.settings.codeOff` | whether the room's code admits guests | the room's op log (a `meta` op) |
| `settings.json` `roomSends` | which rooms may send into which | `settings`, existing |
| `accounts.json` `rooms`, `board`, `view` | an account's side rooms, its On stage halls, its chat view | `accounts`, existing |
| `data/pages.json` (new) | people's takes, their answers, guests' views | **`pages`**, new, in `saveLanes()` |

### 1-§0.3 What the judges found, and what this design does about it

| Flaw in the winning design | Fix here |
|---|---|
| `page:report` was in inputs.test's typed cases with no ack | `page:report` acks `{ok}` or a refusal (§5.3) |
| The admin entering every room was not specified at `join` | join checks `socket.data.isAdmin` first, and `rbac` makes the admin *role* a member of every room (§2.1, §3.3) |
| A side room's code was its permanent key: no New code, and visible in every member's URL | keys and guest codes are separate. New code retires the old code, voids its invites and keeps seated guests (§1.2, §2.2) |
| Switching Main's code off sent the Board's guests home | the confirm offers "Turn off" (seated guests stay until they leave) or "Turn off and send them out" (§2.2) |
| A 0.5.1 rollback silently turns codes back on | this cannot be prevented in 0.5.1. It is said in the CHANGELOG and README.txt, and the admin page's rollback note lists it (§1.8) |
| Help and stage sends were refused in side rooms (a narrowing) | both are allowed by the rights the person holds. Help is seen by the room and answered by the hall's crew, without its text (§2.5) |
| "Seen in Legal" carried a fact back from the target room | dropped. The source reads "delivered" only. `sentUpdate` stays, for Withdraw (§4.4) |
| Files are capability URLs | uploads are bound to the room and person they were made for (provenance), and incoming files never auto-open. Downloads stay capability URLs, which is said, and the owner is asked (§4.3, §12) |
| Accounts could never be Board | an account field `board: [halls]` seats an account On stage in that hall's Main room (§2.1) |
| The display refusal words were misquoted | the real words are quoted: "Your account may not drive this hall's screens." (§2.5) |
| `roomRef` was resolved by an HMAC over every room per send | an index `refs: Map<ref, key>` is kept on load, create and remove (§4.2) |
| Codes went into audit words | audit words name rooms by name and key, never a guest code, a text, a file name or a URL path (§2.7) |
| A file from Legal auto-opened on every Board panel | incoming `sentFrom` / `forwardedFrom` files never auto-open (§4.3) |
| A signed-in Viewer or Staff could read Main's code and join backstage | a signed-in socket is refused a code join. Codes are shown only by `mayKnowCode`. New code ends the residual for Main (§2.3) |
| No file provenance | `freshUploads` records the room and uid, and `buildMessage` checks them (§4.3) |
| `pages.json` held full web URLs in clear | `urlSealed` (secretbox) plus `host` (§1.10, §5.6) |
| The admin's reads of Legal were not audited | `room.read`: once per entry, watch or transcript, never on a resume (§2.7) |
| Lint sinks and iframe guard missing | `srcdoc`, `setHTMLUnsafe`, `createContextualFragment` and computed `['innerHTML']` refused, and one `createElement('iframe')` in `public/` (§5.6) |
| Guests may push only in a locked hall, with no console | kept, and asked of the owner. The console is gated on the join answer's `canPush`, not on `AS_ACCOUNT` (§2.6, §7.5) |
| An offline account's view could not be set | `account.view` on the Accounts page. Guests' views go through `admin:setView` (§6) |
| Room switching meant two tabs and no unread cue | navigation stays; `rooms:activity` lights a dot on the switcher (§3.4, unit 21) |
| halls.manage was given what the owner gave "the admin" | codes on/off, New code, allow-lists and removing rooms are the admin's. Making and renaming rooms is halls.manage's, like halls (§2.4) |
| The desk's notice skipped side rooms | it reaches every room of every hall, and still counts halls as "meetings" (§8) |

## 1-§1. Data model and persistence

### 1-§1.1 Halls and rooms

```
hall H7K2QA                       (no record of its own: it is its Main room)
├── Main   key H7K2QA  code H7K2QA (until New code)   data/rooms/H7K2QA.json .log .json.bak      — today's file, unchanged
├── Legal  key LGQ4MZP8 code K3TW9A (off by default)  data/rooms/H7K2QA.LGQ4MZP8.json .log .json.bak
└── Media  key MDR7VX2C code P8NB4E                   data/rooms/H7K2QA.MDR7VX2C.json .log .json.bak
```

- **A hall** is its Main room. Its key, name and createdAt are the Main room's. Renaming the hall renames its Main room
  (`hall:configure`, `server.js:1356-1363`, unchanged). There is exactly one Main room per hall. The file name makes
  that so: a stem without a dot is a Main room.
- **A room** is one RoomStore entry, unchanged from today's: seq, ring, op log, snapshot, `users`, `seen`, seats, lock.
  It gains a `hall` field, the key of its hall. A Main room's `hall` is its own key. The room's key stays in the
  `code` property (no rename, so no churn). In this paper "key" means `room.code`, and "guest code" means the code
  guests type.
- A hall has at most **20 side rooms**. This is a bound, not a governor: each one is a switcher button, an allow-list
  row and two files. A 21st is refused with words.

### 1-§1.2 Keys, guest codes, references

| Thing | Shape | Made by | Who may hold it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hall key = Main room key | 4-12 of `[A-Z0-9]`, in practice 6 (`makeRoomCode`, `server.js:74`) | `newRoom` (`server.js:541-545`) | anyone who reaches the hall, as today |
| Side room key | 8 characters, same alphabet: `makeRoomKey = customAlphabet('ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789', 8)` (new, beside `:74`). Passes `CODE_RE`, so validation stays one regex. Its file stem `<HALL>.<KEY>` never does | `newSideRoom` (new) | its members, the admin, and anyone who sees the hall's Set up. Never a credential: no lookup or join takes a key from a guest |
| Guest code | 6 characters, same alphabet. Unique among every live code, retired code and key | `newGuestCode()` (new): `do c = makeRoomCode() while (store.hasRoom(c) \|\| store.byCode(c) \|\| store.byRetired(c))` | people `mayKnowCode` allows (§2.3), and the guests who typed it |
| Room reference | `'r' + guard.mac(SECRET, 'room-ref:' + key, 16)`, 17 characters (`guard.mac`, `lib/guard.js:24-26`) | `roomRef(key)` (new) | anyone a send names that room to. It is not a credential: it never passes `CODE_RE` (17 characters, mixed case), so no join or lookup takes it |
| Message ids | unchanged (`server.js:75`) | | |

- **A room's guest code:**
  - A side room's is `room.guestCode`, set at creation.
  - A Main room's is `room.guestCode || room.code`. A migrated hall therefore keeps its code with nothing written.
  - Helper: `guestCodeOf(room)`.
- **Persistence.** `guestCode` and `retired` (at most three earlier codes) are top-level snapshot fields, written only by
  `store.compact`. A code change is never an op, so it never reaches `opsSince`, the ring or a resuming page.
- **The codes index.** `store.codes: Map<guestCode, key>` and `store.retiredCodes: Map<code, key>` are rebuilt at
  load and on every change.
  - When two rooms claim one code at load (a hand-edited file), the second gets no index entry, so its code admits
    nobody, and a console line names it.

### 1-§1.3 In memory: `lib/store.js`

| Change | Where |
|---|---|
| `this.side = new Map()` holds the side rooms by key. `this.rooms` keeps every Main room by hall key, as today. `this.codes` and `this.retiredCodes` are the indexes. The header comment says that `rooms`, `get` and `has` mean "a hall", and `room(key)` means "any room" | constructor `:28-33`; header `:2-18` |
| `SIDE_RE = /^([A-Z0-9]{4,12})\.([A-Z0-9]{4,12})$/` | beside `CODE_RE`, `:25` |
| `_blank(code, name, createdAt, { hall = code, guestCode = '', retired = [] } = {})` | `:70-72` |
| `file(room, ext)` takes a room. Its stem is `room.code` for a Main room and `room.hall + '.' + room.code` for a side room. `loadAll` builds the path from the stem before the room exists | `:37`; callers `:51`, `:75`, `:140`, `:177`, `:179`, `:204` |
| New: `room(key)`, `hasRoom(key)`, `allRooms()` (Main rooms then side rooms), `roomsOf(hall)` (Main first, then side rooms by `createdAt`), `isMain(r)` (`r.hall === r.code`), `byCode(code)`, `byRetired(code)` | after `:90` |
| `createIn(hall, key, name, { guestCode, settings })` makes a side room. It refuses unless `this.rooms.has(hall)` and `!this.hasRoom(key)`, sets the index, and compacts at once as `create` does | after `:97` |
| `setGuestCode(room, code)` moves the old code into `room.retired` (keeping the last 3), reindexes, and compacts at once. It returns the old code | new |
| `compact(key)` and `remove(key)` look the room up with `room(key)`. `compact` writes `guestCode` and `retired` when they are set; a Main room without them writes today's shape byte for byte. `compactAll()` and `unsaved()` cover `allRooms()` | `:172-188`, `:190`, `:197`, `:200-205` |
| `removeHall(hall)` removes the side rooms' files first, then the Main room's, so a crash part-way still leaves a whole hall. It returns the rooms it removed | new, after `:205` |

- **No new synchronous fs call.** The stems come from the existing `readdirSync` (`:47`). `lib/store.js` stays at 9 of
  its 10 (`test/resilience.test.js` guard-rail cap).
- `get`, `has`, `create`, `commit` and `opsSince` are unchanged. `commit` calls `compact(room.code)` (`:158`), which
  now finds side rooms through `room()`.

### 1-§1.4 Snapshots and the op log

- **No new op type.** An unknown op would be swallowed by a 0.5.1 replay with its seq consumed (`:83-86`), so none is
  added.
- **A side room's first snapshot** carries `settings: {codeOff: true}` and its `guestCode`. A Main room's snapshot only
  gains fields after New code.
- `seq` stays per room. A page holds one room, so `bump()` (`app/public/app.js:164-169`) needs no change.

### 1-§1.5 Loading (`loadAll`, `lib/store.js:44-68`)

1. A stem that passes `CODE_RE` is a Main room. It loads exactly as today, `onMigrate` included.
2. After every Main room, a stem that passes `SIDE_RE` is a side room. It loads only when its hall `m[1]` was loaded
   and its key `m[2]` is not already a loaded room. Otherwise a console line ("Not loaded: room LGQ4MZP8 — its hall
   H7K2QA is gone") is written, and the files stay on disk.
3. Any other stem gets a console line. Today it is skipped silently (`:49`).
4. `guestCode` and `retired` are read only when they pass `CODE_RE`, and then indexed (§1.2).

The load still runs with `compact: false` before the folder is held (`server.js:200-206`). `compactAll` still writes
only once this copy holds the folder and its port (`server.js:2482`).

### 1-§1.6 Removing

- `admin:deleteRoom` (`server.js:1429-1457`) takes any room (`store.room`).
- **A side room:**
  - its pages are told `kicked {reason: 'This room was closed by the admin.'}` and disconnected;
  - its files are purged if asked;
  - its key leaves every allow-list (`settings.roomSends`) and every account's `rooms` (`accounts.prune`);
  - one `room.remove` audit row is written.
- **A Main room:**
  - each side room is removed first, as above;
  - then today's steps run (Stagewatch, screens, pins, its link);
  - then `store.removeHall`;
  - accounts are pruned of the hall in `halls` and `board` (today they are left stale, `lib/accounts.js:307`);
  - `pages.forgetHall`;
  - **a peer link whose hall is gone fails closed**: `deskFor` answers `{link: null, desk: false}`, where today it
    falls back to the default desk (`server.js:2009`, against the rule at `:1287`);
  - one `hall.remove` row names its rooms and how many accounts were pruned.
- **Pruning accounts** of a key that no longer exists reaches nothing, so it causes no reconnect and no per-account
  audit row.
- `admin:resetRoom` (`:1419-1428`) resets one room, Main or side. Neither verb ever touches another hall.

### 1-§1.7 Migration of today's data: nothing is rewritten

| Data | 0.5.1 | After the 0.6 boot | Written? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rooms/<CODE>.json`, `.log`, `.json.bak` | one hall | the same hall, whose rooms are `[Main]`: the same key, guest code (= key), messages, files, seq, seats, lock and name | only by today's `compactAll` after the hold, in today's shape |
| op ring, resume | per room | per room | no |
| `settings.json` `hallStagewatch[code]`, `peerLinks[id].hall` | by hall code | the same keys name the same halls | no |
| `displays.json` | by hall code | unchanged | no |
| `accounts.json` `users[].halls` | hall codes | unchanged: the hall, its Main room and hall rights. `rooms`, `board` and `view` appear only when set | no |
| `desk-results.json` `link: 'hall:CODE'` | by hall | unchanged (`lib/deskresults.js:16`) | no |
| messages' `stage.link`, `proposal.link` | `hall:CODE` | unchanged, still followed after the restart | no |
| invites | `mac('invite:'+code+':'+role)` | unchanged: keyed by the guest code, which is the key | no |
| `audit.jsonl` | names halls by code | the same halls | no (a chain) |
| `settings.json` `roomSends` | — | absent means no room sends into another (fail closed) | only when set |
| `data/pages.json` | — | absent means every page shows its chat in its default view | only on a push, a guest's view or an answer |

The boot's "Session restored" line (`server.js:2483-2485`) goes into every room, side rooms included, once per room
(`test/resilience.test.js:484`). A 0.5.1 folder has no side rooms, so the line is identical.

### 1-§1.8 Rollback (a 0.6 folder opened by 0.5.1)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.1 (§1.8: "Kept and ignored" adds `clock` and `onStage`).

- **Main rooms** load as halls with every message.
- **Side rooms** are not loaded and are kept on disk (the stem fails `CODE_RE`). Going back to 0.6 brings them back.
- **Kept and ignored:** `pages.json`, `settings.roomSends` (0.5.1 rewrites `settings.json` whole and keeps unknown
  keys, `server.js:84-89`), and the accounts' `rooms`, `board` and `view` (unknown fields survive a load and a save).
- **Not kept:**
  1. A Main room's switched-off code admits guests again under 0.5.1. Back on 0.6, `codeOff` is still in the room's
     settings and is honoured again.
  2. A Main room's New code is lost. 0.5.1's compaction drops `guestCode`, so under 0.5.1 and after it the key admits
     again and the new code does not. The admin presses New code again.
  3. A file that only a side room uses can be removed by 0.5.1's reset or delete of any hall: 0.5.1's
     `uploadsInUse` scans only the rooms it loads.
- These three go in the CHANGELOG and README.txt ("do not go back to 0.5.1 during a show"), and in the admin page's
  About line.

### 1-§1.9 What is keyed by hall, by room and by person

| By **hall** (the Main room's key) | By **room** (its key) | By **person** |
|---|---|---|
| The Stagewatch link (`hallLinks`, `linkFor(room.hall)`, `settings.hallStagewatch`). Every room of a hall shows its countdown and sends there | messages, op log, seq, ring, snapshot | the chat view: `account.view`, or `pages.views['u:'+uid]` for a guest |
| Screens (`displays.json` `d.hall`, `halls{}.holding`) | seats, lock, invites (`room.settings.seats`, `lockRoles`; `guard.makeInvite(guestCode, role)`) | a take pushed to them, and their answer to it (`pages.json`) |
| Peer links and their nodes on the board | people present (`room.users`, `userRooms`), seen, typing | the account's side rooms and On stage halls |
| The halls board row (Main's last line, Main's help count, people in Main), the context (Main rooms only), desk results | guest code, `codeOff`, retired codes | |
| Accounts' `halls` (Main room and hall-level rights), `board` | the allow-list of rooms that may send in (`settings.roomSends[key]`) | |
| The Board group's take (`pages.json` `halls[H].board`) | help requests (they live in their room; §2.5), upload provenance, transcript, AI drafts, minutes | |

### 1-§1.10 New and changed stores, with their bounds

> **Amended by** 4-§0 and 4-§5.11 (two layers, `marks`, `holds`, `earlier`), 7-§0.1 (§1.10).

| Store | Shape | Lane | Bounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/rooms/` | side rooms beside their hall | the room store's op log | 20 side rooms per hall |
| `settings.json` `roomSends` | `{<TARGET key>: [<SOURCE key>…]}` | `settings` | 50 sources per target |
| `accounts.json` | `rooms: [side keys]`, `board: [hall keys]`, `view: ''\|'simple'\|'full'` | `accounts` | 200 rooms, 200 halls (as `halls`) |
| `data/pages.json` (new, `lib/pages.js`) | `{v:1, views:{'u:<uid>':{view, at}}, halls:{<HALL>:{seq, board: take\|null, people:{<personKey>: take}, answers:{<personKey>:{seq, state, at}}}}}`. Here `personKey` is `a:<accountId>` or `u:<uid>`, a take is `{seq, content, by, at}`, and a web take's content is `{kind:'web', host, urlSealed}` | **`pages`**: `new WriteLane(file, {delayMs: 100, keepBak: true, mode: 0o600})`, added to `saveLanes()` (`server.js:130`), so `flushLanes` and health cover it | views ≤ 5000 (the oldest go first); per hall ≤ 200 person takes and ≤ 500 answers. A new Board take also deletes the older takes and answers of everyone seated On stage then (they could never show again) |

- `lib/pages.js` reads with `readJsonWithBak` and writes only through its lane, so it has 0 synchronous fs calls (the
  cap for a new lib file).
- `pages.hold()`: nothing is written until the server holds the data folder. Until then `save()` only marks the store
  dirty.
- A record of the wrong shape is dropped, as `lib/displays.js:86` does.
- `codeOff` may travel to members in `meta` ops, because whether a code works is no secret to the room. The guest code
  itself and the allow-list never do: the code is a credential, and the allow-list names other rooms. This follows the
  precedent at `server.js:1945-1949`.

## 1-§2. Rights and membership

### 1-§2.1 `lib/rbac.js` (pure)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.1 (§2.1: the seat limit, `seatAllows`), 5-§0 (§2.3 and unit 5: `rbac.guestCaps`); 4-§0's stale citation `:799` → `:787` applied in place (Part 0 §0.9).

- **`ROOM_SCOPED`** = `new Set(['hall.view', 'hall.post', 'hall.files'])`.
- **The fence:** `can(account, cap, scope)` (`:75-82`) returns `false` for a `ROOM_SCOPED` cap whenever a scope string
  is given.
  - Today's body moves to an internal `hallCan`.
  - The no-scope question ("in any hall at all?") still answers, so `signedIn(cap)` (`lib/http-accounts.js:82`) is
    unchanged.
  - The probe `can({role:'tech', halls:['HALL01']}, 'hall.post', 'HALL01') === false` is a unit test.
  - A call site left on `can(…, 'hall.post', room.code)` for a side room would otherwise grant every `allHalls`
    account. The fence makes it refuse instead.
- **`effective()`** (`:57-65`) gains `rooms: Set(account.rooms)` and `board: Set(account.board)`.
- **`canIn(account, cap, scope)`**, where `scope` is `{code, hall, main}`:
  - a cap that is not room-scoped: `hallCan(account, cap, scope.hall)`. Screens, Stagewatch and nodes are the hall's;
  - a Main room: `hallCan(account, cap, scope.hall)`. Every Main-room answer is today's;
  - a side room: `e.caps.has(cap) && (account.role === 'admin' || e.rooms.has(scope.code))`. **`allHalls` does not
    reach a side room** (owner question 2). An admin-role account is a member of every room, through the tunnel
    included, whatever `isAdmin` says about the socket.
- **`seesHall(account, hall)`** is `hallCan(account, 'hall.view', hall)`: the hall's Main room and its hall-level parts.
  **`seesRoom(account, scope)`** is `canIn(account, 'hall.view', scope)`.
- **`roomRoleFor(account, scope)`** (`:161`) gives one of:
  - `'board'` in a Main room when `e.board.has(scope.hall)` and `canIn(post)`;
  - `'research'` with `canIn(post)`;
  - else `'observer'`.

  A string argument is read as a Main room, so `test/accounts.test.js:35-36` hold.
- **The escalation fence** (`:91-146`):
  - `mayChange`'s self-change list (`:94`) adds `'rooms' in change`, `'board' in change` and `'view' in change`. The
    refusal words stay, because `test/accounts.test.js` pins them.
  - `exceeds()` checks **rooms before** its `if (mine.allHalls) return false` (`:127`): any of `theirs.rooms` not in
    `mine.rooms` (unless the actor is an admin) is an excess. `board` halls are checked like `halls`.
  - `afterChange()` models `rooms` and `board` as lists and `view` as a value, as `Accounts.update` applies them.
  - `giveable()` keeps its exact shape (deep-equal at `test/accounts.test.js:84-86` and `:787`). A new
    `giveableRooms(actor)` returns `{all: isAdmin, rooms: [...]}`: a non-admin gives only rooms it holds itself.
  - `rightsView()` (`:164-167`) appends `rooms` and `board`.

### 1-§2.2 Each room's guest code: on, off, new

- **Stored in** `room.settings.codeOff`.
  - A Main room's code is on unless `codeOff === true`, which is today's behaviour.
  - A side room's code is on only when `codeOff === false`. A new room is for accounts until the admin switches its
    code on (deny by default).
- **Who switches it:** the admin only (`admin(ack)`, `server.js:1398`), as the owner asked. Owner question 5 asks
  whether project managers should too.
- **`room:update {code, codeOn: false, keepGuests}`** writes one `meta` op, then:
  - **`keepGuests: true`** ("Turn off"): seated guests stay. A seated guest whose Wi-Fi drops comes back within the
    8 s grace (`holdsSeat`, `server.js:283-289`). New guests are refused.
  - **`keepGuests: false`** ("Turn off and send them out"): every guest page in the room gets `kicked {reason: 'This
    room is for signed-in accounts now.'}` and is disconnected, and the op also clears the saved seats
    (`{codeOff: true, seats: {}}`). Accounts stay.
  - The admin page's confirm names the count: "3 guest pages are in with the code. [Turn off] [Turn off and send them
    out]".
- **`room:update {code, codeOn: true}`** turns on the same code.
- **`room:update {code, newCode: true}`** runs `store.setGuestCode(room, newGuestCode())`. Then:
  - the old code moves to `retired`;
  - invites, which are keyed by the current guest code, are void;
  - guests already in the room stay;
  - the dialog says "Guests in the room now stay. Anyone joining or reconnecting after a long break needs the new
    code."
- **Every switch** writes an audit row, `room.code`: `code off (3 guest pages kept)`, `code off (3 guest pages sent
  home)`, `code on`, or `a new code was issued`. The words never contain the code.
- **What reads it:**
  - **`GET /api/rooms/:code`** (`server.js:521-528`) resolves through `store.byCode`. A code that is off, retired or
    unknown answers exactly `{code, exists: false, name: '', locked: false}` and spends `lookupLock`. A switched-off
    code cannot be told apart from a wrong one.
  - **`join` for a guest** (§3.3):
    - a code that is on admits;
    - a code that is off or retired admits only a person who holds a seat in that room (`holdsSeat`);
    - otherwise the answer is "Room not found". It spends `joinLock` for an off or unknown code. For a retired code
      the words are the same but the lock is not spent, so a tunnel full of reconnecting guests sharing one `cf:IP`
      is not locked out.
  - **Invites** (`guard.checkInvite`, `lib/guard.js:76-81`) are made and checked with `guestCodeOf(room)`.
    `invitesFor(room)` (`server.js:1802-1806`) builds links with it. A side room's invites are `research` only.

### 1-§2.3 Guests, and who is told a code

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§2.3: On stage only by invite, account or the admin), 5-§0 (`rbac.guestCaps`), 7-§0.1 (§2.3: `GUEST_CAPS.board`, `mayKnowCode` On stage; its replacement applied in place, Part 0 §0.9).

- **One code admits a guest to one room**, with today's signed per-device identity (`lib/guard.js:61-73`).
- **Roles by room kind:**
  - Main: `board`, `research`, `observer`, as today.
  - Side rooms: `research` (shown as "Member") or `observer`. `board` in a side room is refused with "On stage seats
    are in the hall's Main room."
- **Rights in side rooms:** `GUEST_CAPS_SIDE = { research: ['hall.view', 'hall.post', 'hall.files'], observer:
  ['hall.view'] }`. A side room's Member has no `stage.send`. `GUEST_CAPS.board` is `['hall.view', 'hall.post']`. An admin's link (`rightsIn`, `server.js:924`) uses its own named set, `rbac.LINKED_CAPS`, which keeps today's `hall.files`.
- **An unknown role is refused, not downgraded** (`server.js:716-717`): "Choose On stage, Backstage or Observer." A
  missing role still means observer (the page's default), and `director` is still read as `board`.
- **A signed-in socket is refused a code join:** "You are signed in as Ana: open the room from your halls, or sign out
  to join with a code."
  - Otherwise a Viewer or Staff account could seat itself as a backstage guest with `stage.send` ("nobody widens their
    own rights").
  - The host token's admin has no account, so it is unaffected.
  - Not spent on `joinLock`.
- **`mayKnowCode(socket, room)`** decides who is told a guest code (the chips, `/api/halls`' `guestCode`, the join
  answer's `guestCode`, `room:settings`). It holds for:
  - the admin;
  - `halls.manage` (they hand codes out);
  - an account whose own rights in that room already cover what the code gives: `canIn` view, post and files there,
    and for a Main room also `stage.send` in the hall;
  - a guest, for the code they joined with.

  So Viewers and Staff are not shown Main's code. That is a behaviour change, written in the CHANGELOG (owner question
  8).
- **The residual, said in the papers:** until New code, a Main room's key *is* its code, and any account member reads
  the key in its URL, as in 0.5.1.
  - The admin page marks such halls: "This hall's code is also its address: anyone with an account in it can read it.
    Choose New code to separate them."
  - Halls made in 0.6 start the same way, so no page or test moves.
  - Side rooms never have this.

### 1-§2.4 Who sets rooms up

| Act | Who | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Make a side room, rename a room | `halls.manage` or the admin | `canManageHall()` (`server.js:1331`) |
| Code on, off or new; the allow-list; remove a room; reset a room | the admin | `admin(ack)` (`server.js:1398`) |
| An account's rooms, On stage halls, view | `users.manage` within `mayChange` (Accounts page) | `rbac.mayChange` |
| A guest's or an account's view from a hall or admin page | the admin | `admin(ack)` |

### 1-§2.5 Help, the stage, screens and nodes in side rooms

> **Amended by** 7-§0.1 (§2.5: `help:respond`'s On stage rule and account branch, unit G2).

- **Help** is allowed in a side room, with `hall.post` there. The request lives in its room.
  - On the halls board (§7.2), people who may read the room see it in full.
  - The hall's crew who are not in the room see `{hallName, roomName, category, from, state, by, at}` and no text, and
    may answer it. "The hall's crew" means anyone who may answer Main's help: `canIn(acct, 'hall.post', mainScope)` or
    the admin.
  - Its `helpUpdate` reaches the room's own pages, so "Ana is on the way" shows in Legal.
  - **`help:respond`** (`server.js:1313-1328`) uses `store.room`, and the account check becomes
    `canIn(acct, 'hall.post', scopeOf(r)) || canIn(acct, 'hall.post', mainScopeOf(r.hall))`.
  - The hall row's help count stays Main's (`board.hallRow` is unchanged), and the help strip counts by `hall`.
- **The stage:**
  - Every room of a hall shows the hall's countdown.
  - `stage:send`, `stage:targets` and `stage:propose` (`:1020-1090`) use `linkFor(room.hall)`, and `allowed()` decides
    as everywhere: an account needs `stage.send` in the hall, while a side room's guest has none.
  - `trackStageSend` and `trackProposal` keep the room's key. The followers (`:2027`, `:2050`, `:2112`) look it up with
    `store.room`.
  - The restart re-follow loops (`:2063-2073`, `:2093-2099`) iterate `store.allRooms()`, and the fallback at `:2067`
    becomes `linkFor(room.hall)`.
  - Desk results keep `hall:<HALL>` (`lib/deskresults.js:16`, `deskLinkOf` `:2131-2135`), unchanged.
- **Screens, nodes, hall settings:** these refuse a side room's key by construction, because `store.has` sees only
  halls. The real words are:
  - `display:list`: "Your account may not drive this hall's screens." (`:1099`)
  - `display:create`: "Your account may not add screens to this hall." (`:1146`)
  - `display:update`: "No such screen or hall, or not yours to change." (`:1157`)
  - `display:hallHolding`: "Your account may not set this hall's holding image." (`:1188`)
  - `nodes:link`: "No such hall." (`:1225`)
  - `hall:settings` and `hall:configure`: "No such hall." (`:1335`, `:1350`)

  Unit 6's tests hold each one. A page in a side room drives screens with its hall's key from the join answer's
  `hall`.

### 1-§2.6 Who may push to people's pages, and set views

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§2.6: `web` needs `stage.web`, S4; `canShow`), 7-§0.1 (§2.6: the seat limit cuts `canPush`).

- **`canPush(hall)`**, one of:
  - the admin;
  - an account with `display.control` in the hall (`rbac.can`, which stays hall-scoped);
  - a backstage (`research`) guest seated in the hall's Main room **while its roles are locked**, so that seat came
    from an invite.

  In an unlocked hall, anyone who types the code can sit backstage, so guests may not push there (owner question 1).
  `display.control`'s words on the Accounts page become "Change what a hall's screens and people's pages show".
- **View:** the admin (`admin:setView`), or `users.manage` on the Accounts page for accounts.

### 1-§2.7 Audit rows (`lib/audit.js`)

> **Amended by** 4-§0 and 4-§5.11 (new rows), 7-§0.1 (§2.7: `person.clock`, `person.onStage`), 6-U.7 (machine and event rows), 3-H.10 (`audit.archive`).

No row carries a guest code, a message's text, a file's name, a URL's path or query, or a token. Rooms are named by
name and key, halls by key (as today).

| Action | When | Target | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hall.create` | `admin:createRoom` over the socket (`:1413-1418`, unaudited today); `POST /api/rooms` as today | hall | name |
| `room.create` | `room:create` | room key | `Legal in Hall 2 (code off)` |
| `room.update` | renamed | room key | `name → Media` |
| `room.code` | on, off, new | room key | `code off (3 guest pages kept)` / `code on` / `a new code was issued` |
| `room.sendFrom` | allow-list changed | room key | `may send here: Main (Hall 2), Main (Hall 3)` |
| `room.reset` | `admin:resetRoom` (unaudited today) | room key | `messages and documents cleared, 4 files removed` |
| `room.remove`, `hall.remove` | deleted | room / hall key | name, rooms, files purged, `2 accounts updated` |
| `room.read` | the admin enters a side room on a page (a join without `since`), watches it, downloads its transcript or asks for its AI summary, when the admin's account does not list it (the host token never does) | room key | `entered as the admin` / `watched` / `transcript` / `minutes drafted by the AI` |
| `room.send` | a message or file sent into another room | target key | `a message (212 characters) from Legal (Hall 2) to Main (Hall 2)` / `a file (pdf, 2.1 MB) from …` |
| `room.withdraw` | a send withdrawn | target key | `a message sent from Legal (Hall 2), there 40 s` |
| `message.remove` | `admin:deleteMessage` (unaudited today) | room key | `a message by Kim (text)` |
| `seat.role`, `room.lock`, `room.link`, `room.unlink`, `seat.kick` | the room list's people controls (`:1466-1547`, unaudited today) | room key | `Kim: research → observer` / `roles locked (2 seats kept)` / `Gus may forward into Hall 3` / … |
| `minutes.post` | `admin:postSummary` (unaudited today) | room key | `minutes posted (pinned)` |
| `stagewatch.propose` | `stage:propose` (`:1057-1090`: the papers already say it is audited, `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:117-120`, and it is not) | room key | `asked the operator: a message (n characters) for the speaker's screen — proposal p12` |
| `user.create`, `user.update` | rooms, On stage, view | username | `rooms → Legal (Hall 2); board → Hall 2; view → simple` |
| `page.push` | one row per target | hall | `the Board (6 pages) → the clock` / `Ana Silva → a web page on vote.example.com` |
| `person.view` | a guest's view set by the admin | hall | `Rita (guest) → simple view` |

Not audited, with the reason:

- messages inside a room: they are the room's own record;
- a person's dismiss or minimise: their own act on their own page, shown to the pusher as status;
- reads such as `room:sendTargets` and `page:status`.

## 1-§3. Joining and sign-in

### 1-§3.1 Guests (`index.html`, `join.js`)

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§3.1 and §7.1: On stage only from an invite link).

- **The lookup:** they type a code, and `GET /api/rooms/:code` answers `{code, exists, name, locked, hallName, main}`.
  The two new keys go at the end. `hallName` is a name, never a code.
- **Roles:** the page offers On stage, Backstage and Observer for a Main room, and Member and Observer for a side room
  (`index.html:74-91`). It shows "Legal · Hall 2".
- **Copy:** "No hall or room has that code" (`join.js:114`).
- **Length:** six characters stay the rule (`join.js:111`, `index.html:99`).
- **A signed-in browser:** today, following a `?code=` link shows the code pane (`join.js:28`). It now says "You are
  signed in: open your halls, or sign out to join with a code", to match the server's refusal (§2.3).

### 1-§3.2 Accounts: one room goes straight in, several ask which

- **`GET /api/halls`** (`server.js:531-539`) keeps `halls` and each row's existing fields, and appends to each row:
  - `seat`: the server's `roomRoleFor` in Main;
  - `guestCode`: only by `mayKnowCode`;
  - `codeOn`;
  - `rooms: [{key, name, people, guestCode?, codeOn, seat}]`: the hall's side rooms the account may enter.

  It also appends a top-level `rooms` list, the side rooms the account may enter in halls it does not see, each with
  `hallName`.
- **`halls.js` `load()`** (`:18-32`) counts every room the account may enter:
  - **Exactly one**, with no other reason to stay (it may not manage halls or users, read the audit log, or administer):
    `location.replace` straight into it. This is "only one room set up".
  - **More than one:** the halls board is the question. Each hall's row lists its rooms as buttons, and a Legal-only
    account sees them under **Your rooms** (§7.2).
  - The hall page's "All halls" link carries `?stay=1`, so going back never bounces.
- **`hallHref`** (`halls.js:70-72`) uses the server's `seat`, not `can.post`, so a Board account opens with
  `role=board` and the reload-once at `app.js:109-114` stays a safety net.

### 1-§3.3 `join` (`server.js:707-816`)

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§3.3: `canWeb` with #54, then `canShow`, `over`, `earlier` with #60; `docs`), 5-§0 (§3.3: `forwardable`, windowed `history`), 7-§0.1 (§3.3: `clock`, `pins`, `onStage`, in the order #69, #70 and #71 land; `sends` false On stage).

- **Arguments:** the same keys as 0.5.1. `roomCode` is the room's **key** for `as: 'account'` and for the admin view,
  and the **guest code** for a guest. A page cached across the upgrade (static `maxAge` 5m, `:422`) therefore rejoins
  unchanged, because a migrated Main's key is its code. There is one new optional key, `viewOf` (§5.5).
- **An account:**
  - The room is `store.room(key)`.
  - The check is `socket.data.isAdmin || rbac.seesRoom(acct, scopeOf(r))`, with the admin first.
  - The refusal is "Your account has no access to this room — ask an admin" (`/no access/` still matches
    `test/accounts.test.js`). It does not spend `joinLock`, which is for code guessing.
  - The seat is `roomRoleFor(acct, scopeOf(r))`.
- **The admin view** (`adminView`): `store.room(key)`, unseated, as today.
- **A guest:**
  1. Refused when the socket carries an account (§2.3).
  2. The room is `store.byCode(code)`, else `store.byRetired(code)`.
  3. Admitted when the code is the room's live code and on, or when `holdsSeat(r, id, cleanName, cleanRole)`.
  4. Otherwise "Room not found", spending `joinLock` unless the code was retired.
  5. The role is read by room kind. The invite is checked with `guestCodeOf(r)`.
- **Every check that `store.has(room.code)` meant "the room still exists"** becomes `store.hasRoom`: `need()`
  (`:820`), `syncSeats()` (`:315`) and `leaveRoom()` (`:1640`, `:1650`). Without this, every side room is "Room gone".
- **The answer** (`:794-804`) keeps every field. `roomCode` stays what the page sent (a migrated Main's key, a side
  room's key, or the guest's code), so nothing new is disclosed. `roomName` is this room's name (for Main, the hall's,
  as today). New keys are appended **at the end**:

  ```
  hall        the hall's key when the person sees the hall (seesHall) or is the admin, else ''
  hallName    the hall's name
  main        whether this is the Main room
  guestCode   by mayKnowCode, else ''
  codeOn      whether this room's code admits guests
  rooms       [{key, name, main}]: this hall's rooms this person may enter (a guest: [])
  view        'simple' | 'full' (§6)
  page        the take this page shows now, with the person's answer, or null (§5.5)
  sends       whether room:sendTargets would list anything (the page offers To: only then)
  canPush     canPush(hall) (§2.6)
  now, tz     AGMessage's clock and zone, as displayState gives them (:1677-1682)
  ```

- **In a side room:** `stage` is `stagePayload(linkFor(r.hall))`, and `canSendToStage` and `canPropose` follow
  `allowed('stage.send')` there.

### 1-§3.4 One socket, one room

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§3.4: `rooms:activity` as a `Latest`; no presence line between rooms of one hall).

- A socket holds one room, one seat and one upload token, as today (`:673-674`, `:785-790`).
- **A room switch is a page navigation** to `/app.html?code=<key>&as=account`. Each page keeps one stream with no gaps
  it is not meant to see, and the client protocol (`app.js:98-185`) is unchanged.
- **Switching shows "X left"** in the room left, after the 8 s grace (`:1628-1651`). That is true: the person left.
- **Unread cues (unit 21):**
  - An account's or the admin's socket also joins the io rooms `watch:<key>` of the hall's other rooms it may enter.
  - `apply()` on an `add` that is not a system line emits `rooms:activity {key, seq, priority}` to `watch:<room.key>`.
    It carries no text, no name and no people.
  - The page lights a dot (🔥 for priority) on that room's switcher button. It keeps the last seq it saw per room in
    `localStorage` (in try/catch), against the join answer's `rooms[].seq`.
  - A dot, not a count: the seq counts operations, not messages.
- **Resume and seats** are unchanged, per room. The boot seat expiry (`:323`) iterates `store.allRooms()`.

### 1-§3.5 Every "any room" reader, moved in unit 4 (one line each)

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§3.5 and unit 4: the readers counted by a fence).

- `need()` `:820`, `syncSeats()` `:315`, `leaveRoom()` `:1640`, `:1650`: `store.has` → `store.hasRoom`.
- `join` `:720`, `myRooms` / `forward` `:936-946`, every `admin:*` room handler `:1400-1562`, `admin:linkRoom`'s target
  `:1503`, the transcript `:476`: `store.get` → `store.room`.
- `uploadsInUse` `:341`, the boot seat expiry `:323` and the restored line `:2483`: `store.rooms.values()` →
  `store.allRooms()`. If `uploadsInUse` misses side rooms, a Main room's reset deletes a file only a side room holds.
- `hallStageChanged` `:1933-1937` and `onStageState` `:1938-1944` emit `stage` to every room of `store.roomsOf(hall)`.
- Health `:488`: `rooms` keeps meaning halls, and `sideRooms` is appended.

## 1-§4. Cross-room messages and files

### 1-§4.1 The allow-list

- **`settings.roomSends = {<TARGET key>: [<SOURCE key>, …]}`**, set with `room:update {code, sendFrom: [keys]}` (the
  admin).
  - Each key must be an existing room, in any hall, and not the target itself.
  - The list is deduplicated and holds at most 50.
  - An unknown key is refused with words, never dropped.
  - One `saveSettings()` and one `room.sendFrom` row.
- **The picker** groups every room by hall. Each ticked row has a **"↔ and send back"** box that adds the reverse
  entry in the same save. Both lists' changes go in one row.
- **Removing a room** drops its key from every list, as a target and as a source.
- **Who sees the list:** only `room:settings` callers, who are the admin and `halls.manage`. It names rooms by name and
  key, never by code.

### 1-§4.2 The send path (new handlers in `server.js`, beside `forward`)

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§4.2: a file moves only from a room where the sender may download it), 5-§0 (§4.2: `cid`, `store.byRef`, `lib/handlers/rooms.js`), 7-§0.1 (§4.2: `room:send` refused On stage).

- **`refs: Map<ref, key>`** is filled on load, `createIn` and `remove`. `roomRef(key)` is computed once per room.
- **`room:sendTargets {}`** → `{ok, targets: [{ref, name, hallName}]}`: every room T whose list holds the socket's room
  S. It spends one `chatter` token and carries no key, code, people or seq.
- **`room:send`** has two forms:
  - `{to: ref, messageId}` sends an existing text or file of S;
  - `{to: ref, type: 'text'|'file', text, url, filename, caption, priority}` sends a new one.

The steps:

1. `need(ack)`, then one `writes` token, then `mayPost` in S. A file also needs `allowed('hall.files')` in S. The
   rights where the sender is decide: the allow-list is the admin saying that people who may post in S may post into T.
2. `T = store.room(refs.get(guard.str(to)))`, with T ≠ S. Otherwise "That room is gone."
3. Refused unless `(settings.roomSends[T.code] || []).includes(S.code)`: "This room may not send there — ask an admin."
   It is read on every request, so a list changed mid-show applies at once.
4. **The message.**
   - From `messageId`: copy S's text or file. Any other type is refused.
   - From the payload: `buildMessage(me, payload, {room: S})`, with `SENDABLE = {text, file}`. An action prompt or a
     help request is refused, fail closed. The file provenance of §4.3 applies.
5. **Into T:** `{…msg, id: new, from: {uid, name, role: me.role, acct?}, sentFrom: {roomName: S.name, hallName, ref:
   roomRef(S)}}`, then `apply(T, add)`.
6. **The copy in S:** `{…msg, id: new, sentTo: {roomName: T.name, hallName, ref: roomRef(T), id: <T's message id>}}`,
   then `apply(S, add)`. This is the owner's "Sent to <room>: …".
7. One `room.send` audit row. The answer is `{ok, id: <copy id>, seq, to: {name, hallName}}`, with no key or code.

T is written first, so a copy exists only for a message that is in T. "Delivered" is that fact: committed to T's log
and sent to T's pages. Nothing else of T (its seen receipts, replies, people, seq) ever comes back to S.

### 1-§4.3 What the target sees, replies and files

> **Amended by** 4-§0 (§4.3: provenance, privacy, no auto-open anywhere), 7-§0.1 (§4.3 and `forward`: refused On stage).

- **In T** the message shows "↘ From Legal · Hall 2", drawn where `forwardedFrom` is drawn (`app.js:576-585`), always
  with the sender's name. The join-time name check (`:751-757`) never ran for an outside sender, so this mark is what
  shows they are an outsider.
- **Replies stay in T** (`replyTo` is within one room).
  - **"Send back"** is offered on the message only when its `sentFrom.ref` is among T's own `room:sendTargets`, so it
    uses the same path and the same allow-list.
  - It opens the composer with To set to that room for one send.
  - The copy that lands back in S carries `replyTo` to S's copy (a lookup of `sentTo.id` in S's messages), so S sees
    the answer under its question.
- **Files.** The copy and T's message carry the same `/uploads/…` URL, so T's members download it (owner decision 5).
  - The URL is the capability, as today (`server.js:425-436`). That is said in SECURITY.md, and owner question 9 asks
    whether it is enough.
  - **Provenance (unit 13):** `freshUploads` (`:335`) becomes `Map<name, {at, room, uid}>`, filled from the upload
    token's `room` and `uid` (`:595`, from `req.agmUploader`, which today is never read).
    - `buildMessage(user, payload, {room})` (`:1808-1834`) accepts a file only when it is a fresh upload by
      `user.uid` for `room.code`, or when its URL is already in a message of that room.
    - Any other room's file URL is refused: "That file belongs to another room — send it from there."
    - A file therefore crosses rooms only by `room:send` (audited) or `forward` (between rooms one is in).
    - A file uploaded before a restart and not yet sent must be uploaded again; the orphan sweep would remove it within
      the hour anyway.
  - `uploadsInUse` scans every room, so a reset, a delete or the author's deletion of one copy removes the file from
    disk only when no room and no screen points at it.
  - **No auto-open:** a file that arrives with `sentFrom` or `forwardedFrom` never opens itself on the On stage panel
    (`app.js:408` gains `&& !msg.sentFrom && !msg.forwardedFrom`). Someone in the room opens or pins it.
- **Deleting:** the author may delete the copy in S (`delete`, `:873-882`). The message in T goes only by Withdraw
  (§4.4) or the admin.

### 1-§4.4 Withdraw (unit 15)

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§4.4: `sentUpdate` in the op table; "⊘ Withdrawn from Legal after 40 s"; `already`).

- **`room:withdraw {messageId}`**, on the copy in S:
  - its author (`from.uid === me.uid`) or the admin;
  - one `writes` token;
  - only while `sentTo.withdrawn` is unset and T still holds `sentTo.id`.
- **The steps:**
  1. `apply(T, {o: 'del', id})`.
  2. `systemMessage(T, 'Ana withdrew a message sent from Legal')`.
  3. `apply(S, {o: 'upd', id: copy, f: {sentTo: {...copy.sentTo, withdrawn: Date.now()}}})`.
  4. `removeUnused` for a file nothing else uses.
  5. One `room.withdraw` row.
- **The copy's line reads** "↩ withdrawn from Legal (it was there 40 s)". That is honest about it having been seen.
- **`apply()` emits events per known field only** (`:218-225`). A new `upd` field without its event would leave every
  S page with a gap in the numbers, and each would rejoin. So `apply()` gains
  `if ('sentTo' in op.f) io.to(room.code).emit('sentUpdate', {messageId, sentTo, seq})`, and the client's `applyOp`
  handles `sentTo` in resumed ops too.

### 1-§4.5 Limits

- The existing `writes` bucket (5/s, bursts of 15, per socket) covers `room:send` and `room:withdraw`. Each request has
  one target, with today's text and file caps.
- No new per-room governor, because there is no measured cause ("measured, then governed"). A pair limit is left for
  later, to be measured first.
- `test/inputs.test.js` fuzzes each new handler by itself (§9).
