## 1-§5. Pushed screens on people's pages

### 1-§5.1 Content kinds (`lib/pages.js` `cleanPage(c, facts)`, pure, fail closed)

> **Amended by** 4-§0 and 4-§5.9.3 (`doc`, `image`, `snippet`; `chat {layer}`; `sourceOk`), 5-§0 (§5.1: the `brand` kind goes, owner answer 31).

| Kind | Clean shape | Refused when |
|---|---|---|
| `chat` | `{kind:'chat'}`: back to the chat; it closes any layer | — |
| `stage` | `{kind:'stage'}`, drawn from the `stage` payload the page already receives | the hall has no Stagewatch (`!linkFor(hall).base`): "This hall has no Stagewatch linked — link one in Set up." |
| `clock` | `{kind:'clock'}`, in AGMessage's time and zone (`now`, `tz`) | — |
| `holding` | `{kind:'holding', image?}`: the image given, else the hall's holding image, else the hall's name faint on black | an image that is not one of ours (`guard.validUploadUrl` + `IMAGE_EXT`, the rule of `lib/displays.js:41`), or one in no message of a room of that hall the pusher may read |
| `blank` | `{kind:'blank'}`: black (owner question 4). The controls appear on a touch | — |
| `brand` | `{kind:'brand'}`: the AGMessage mark (`.brand-mark`, `styles.css:66-71`, enlarged) and the hall's name. No new asset | — |
| `web` | `{kind:'web', url, host}` | §5.6 |

- An unknown kind, or a field of the wrong type, is refused with words that list the kinds. Nothing is defaulted
  (unlike `lib/displays.js:47`, `:52`, `:55`).
- `describePage(c)` gives the words for the console and the audit: `back to chat`, `Stagewatch`, `the clock`,
  `a holding slide`, `blank`, `the AGMessage holding page`, `a web page on <host>`. A web take is never named by more
  than its host.
- Screens (`/d/`) are unchanged: `lib/displays.js` `KINDS` and `test/displays.test.js:27` still refuse `iframe` and
  web content, and a screen is never sent `chat`.

### 1-§5.2 Targets

> **Amended by** 4-§0 and 4-§5.9.1, 4-§5.9.10 (the Board by invite and account; two layers).

- **`to: 'board'`** is the Board group: every page seated `board` in the hall's Main room.
  - That is code guests On stage and accounts with the hall in `board`.
  - It is standing state, so a Board page that joins, reconnects or comes back after a restart gets the current take.
  - "Board" includes presenters seated On stage (owner question 3). The console names every page it reached.
- **`to: {uid}`** is one person: `a:<accountId>` (every device of the account) or `u:<uid>` (that device's guest).
  - The pusher may name only a person seated now in a room of the hall that the pusher may read. Otherwise "not in this
    hall now", which also hides who is in a room the pusher cannot read.
  - The take reaches every seated page of that person in any room of the hall (`seatsOf` over `roomsOf(hall)`), and
    the admin's support view of them (`viewOf`, §5.5).
- **Which take a page shows:** each hall numbers its takes with one counter, `pages.halls[H].seq`. A page shows the
  highest-numbered take addressed to it: its person's, or the Board's when it is seated `board` in Main. Latest wins,
  and `chat` is how a screen is handed back.

### 1-§5.3 The numbered take and its confirmation (the displays model, `lib/displays.js:163-204`)

> **Amended by** 4-§5.9.1 (two layers), 5-§0 (§5.3: `cid`, `Latest`, `lib/handlers/takes.js`, person-first words; the marks ◷ and ○ applied in place, Part 0 §0.9).

- **`page:push {code: <hall key>, to, content}`** → `{ok, seq, results: [{key, name, ok, status}]}`.
  - The steps:
    1. `canPush(hall)`.
    2. One `writes` token.
    3. `cleanPage`.
    4. `pages.take(...)`. A Board take supersedes the older person takes and answers of those seated On stage now.
    5. A targeted `page:take` to each target socket. **It is never a room op or a room broadcast**: ops go to everyone
       in the room (`:210-232`).
    6. One `page.push` row per target.
    7. `pagesChanged(hall)`.
  - The answer's status is **"… sending"**, never "shown" (the rule of `test/displays.test.js:184`).
- **`page:take {seq, content, by, hallName, holding, now, tz, answer}`** goes from the server to the page. A web take's
  URL is opened in memory and sent to its targets only. It carries no key or code.
- **`page:report {seq, state, words}`** goes from the page to the server. **It acks** `{ok: true}`, or `{ok: false,
  error}` for a refused report, so inputs.test's typed case is answered.
  - It spends one `chatter` token.
  - It is ignored from `adminView` sockets and from unseated sockets.
  - It counts only for the seq that socket's person is shown now, never an older one.
  - `state` must be one of `shown | hidden | opened | failed | dismissed | minimised`. `words` pass `cleanText(160)`.
- **Visible or it did not happen.** The page reports `shown` only while `document.visibilityState === 'visible'`.
  Otherwise it reports `hidden`, and reports again on `visibilitychange`.
- **Runtime reports** are `pages.live: Map<hall, Map<socketId, {key, seq, state, words, at}>>`. They are never saved,
  and a socket that disconnects is dropped.
- **`Pages.status`** (pure) is per person or Board group, over every page they have open in the hall, against the
  current seq. Never colour alone:

| Mark | Words |
|---|---|
| ✓ | on screen / on all 6 Board pages |
| ◐ | 1 page not in view (asleep or another app) |
| ◇ | opened — AGMessage cannot see inside a web page (web only, never ✓) |
| ▭ | minimised to On stage at 14:02 |
| ○ | closed by Ana at 14:02 — on chat |
| ◷ | sending — on 2 of 4 pages |
| △ | could not show it: the image did not load |
| ✕ | no page open |

- **`page:status {code}`** → `{ok, board: {seq, showing, mark, words, pages}, people: [{uid, name, room, seq, showing,
  mark, words}]}`.
  - Only `canPush` may ask.
  - People are listed from the rooms of the hall that the asker may read (for a guest pusher, Main).
- **`pages:changed {}`** is a signal with no content, coalesced to once per 150 ms like `displaysChanged`
  (`:1719-1729`). It is sent only to sockets in the hall's rooms whose `canPush` held at join. Consoles read
  `page:status` again, so latest wins.

### 1-§5.4 Dismiss, minimise, restore

> **Amended by** 4-§5.9.1, 5-§0 (§5.4: Show it again within 10 s; ✕ and ▭ kept, owner answer 32), 7-§0.1 (§5.4: ⛶ only where the Fullscreen API is).

- The layer has **✕ Back to chat** and **▭ Minimise**, 48 px, in words as well as icons. **Escape minimises; it never
  dismisses.** A **⛶ Full screen** button is the person's own gesture: a push cannot enter the Fullscreen API.
- **Back to chat** reports `dismissed`.
  - The server saves `answers[key] = {seq, state: 'dismissed', at}`.
  - It sends `page:take {…, answer: 'dismissed'}` to **every** page of that person in the hall, so their phone and
    tablet both go back to chat.
  - A reload or a restart does not bring the same take back. A newer take (a higher seq) shows again.
- **Minimise** reports `minimised`. The take moves into the "📺 On stage" side bar (`#docPanel`, `app.html:118-144`) as
  a card at its top:
  - "▶ Stagewatch" shows the live countdown text;
  - "🕐 Clock" shows a small clock;
  - "🌐 vote.example.com" shows the host;
  - "🖼 Holding", "■ Blank" and "AG AGMessage" show a label.

  Each card has **Show again**, which reports `shown` again and clears the answer. The collapsed rail reads "📺 On
  stage • 1". The panel opens itself once for this (`setStageCollapsed(false)`, `app.js:1219`). It no longer forces
  itself open on a document while a pushed screen is minimised.
- **Observers and Viewer accounts** have no panel today (`styles.css:176-186`). The panel's rail is shown when the page
  holds a minimised take (`body[data-pushed]`), so a minimise always has somewhere to go.
- Answers are not audited (§2.7). The pusher sees them as status.

### 1-§5.5 A page that reconnects, and the admin's support view

> **Amended by** 4-§5.9.1 (two layers).

- **The join answer's `page`** is `{seq, content, by, at, hallName, holding, answer: 'dismissed'|'minimised'|null}` for
  the take the page shows now, or `null`.
  - `dismissed`: nothing is shown.
  - `minimised`: the card is in the bar.
  - Otherwise the layer is drawn without animation, and the page reports.
- No backlog: only the newest take is sent. A Wi-Fi blip or a watchdog restart brings the tablet back to exactly what
  it showed (`pages.json` is flushed by `flushLanes` at stop and crash, `:132-135`).
- **A role change** to or from `board` (`admin:setRole`, `:1466-1485`) sends `page:take` again when the take that page
  is shown changes.
- **The support view:** `admin.js` `openUserView` (`:372-384`) passes `viewOf=<uid>` from the row. An `adminView` join
  with `viewOf` gets that person's `page` and `view`, and receives their `page:take` and `view`. It never reports.

### 1-§5.6 The web page (unit 19)

> **Amended by** 4-§0, 4-§5.9.9 and 4-§5.9.2.2 (`stage.web`; S4's `guestWeb`), 4-§11 (unit 19, amended: #54).

- **The address** (`pages.webUrl`, on the server, and again in the page before the frame's `src` is set):
  - a string, read with `guard.str`, of at most 2048 characters, that `new URL()` parses;
  - protocol exactly `https:`. `http:` would be mixed content under HTTPS or the tunnel. `javascript:`, `data:`,
    `blob:` and `file:` are refused;
  - no username or password;
  - a hostname that is not AGMessage itself: `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`, `os.hostname()`, this machine's
    addresses (`tlsmod.lanAddresses()`) and the running tunnel's host. A frame of AGMessage with `allow-same-origin`
    would own the parent page;
  - kept as the normalised `href`.
- **The server never fetches it.** A header check would be server-side request forgery into the venue network, and it
  would not see what the tablet sees.
- **At rest:** `pages.json` holds `{host, urlSealed}` (`secretbox.seal`). The full address goes only to the target pages
  and to the pushers' console (`page:status`). It never goes to the halls board, the context, the AI's brief, the
  server's console or an audit row, which name the host only.
- **The CSP, on the hall page only:**
  - `lib/guard.js` exports `CSP_HALL`, which is `CSP` (`:178-191`) with `frame-src 'self' blob: https:`.
  - `pageHeaders` (`:193-201`) sets `CSP_HALL` when `req.path === '/app.html'`, and the strict CSP everywhere else.
    The static route and its caching stay as they are, and no synchronous call is added.
  - Every other page keeps `frame-src 'self' blob:`: index, halls, users, admin, the screen page and the transcript.
    `frame-ancestors 'self'` and `X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN` are unchanged.
  - `test/server.test.js:53-62` gains both assertions.
- **The frame** is made in one place, `framePage(url)` in `public/pagelayer.mjs`:
  - `sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"`: no forms (owner question 6), no popups, no top navigation of either
    kind, no modals, no downloads;
  - `referrerpolicy="no-referrer"`, because the hall page's URL carries `code=` and `invite=`;
  - `allow=""`, `credentialless` where the browser supports it, and `title="Web page from <host>"`.
  - The page refuses an address whose origin is its own (a second check).
  - A strip outside the frame reads "A web page chosen by Ana (example.com). Don't type passwords here." with
    **Open in a new tab** (`target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"`, in AGMessage's own chrome) and **Back to
    chat**.
- **What can be known:** a refused frame (the site's `X-Frame-Options` or `frame-ancestors`) still fires `load`, and
  the parent cannot read inside it. So:
  - a loaded web take reports `opened` and reads "◇ opened";
  - with no `load` in 15 s, it reports `failed: the page did not load`;
  - the Board member can always go back to chat.
- **The operator's preview:** the console's web field has **Preview**, which frames the same address with the same
  `framePage` on the operator's own screen before it is pushed. The admin page offers **Open in a new tab** instead,
  since its CSP stays strict.
- **postMessage:**
  - The listener at `app.js:1666-1671` gains `e.source === window.parent && e.origin === location.origin` (unit 2).
    Today a framed site would be the first frame able to trigger it.
  - `admin.js:399` posts with `location.origin`, not `'*'`.
- **The lint fence:** `agm/no-unescaped-html` (`app/eslint-rules/no-unescaped-html.js`) also refuses:
  - assigning `srcdoc`, as a property or through `setAttribute`;
  - `setHTMLUnsafe(`;
  - `createContextualFragment(`;
  - a computed `el['innerHTML']`.

  `test/lint-rules.test.js` gains one refused shape for each. A source guard in `test/resilience.test.js` holds that
  `createElement('iframe')` appears exactly once in `public/`, inside `framePage`.

### 1-§5.7 The other kinds' renderer

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§5.7: `pagelayer.mjs` gets plain values and no socket), 4-§5.9.11.

- They are drawn by a new module, `app/public/pagelayer.mjs`, loaded with `import()` on the first take, as
  `pdf.min.mjs` is (`app.js:1044`).
  - It is linted as a module with `agm/no-unescaped-html` (`eslint.config.mjs:91`), and does not share `app.js`'s
    global scope.
  - It exports `render(box, content, ctx) → Promise<{state, words}>` and `card(content, ctx)`.
  - Everything is built with the DOM API and `textContent`.
- **`stage`:** time, title, next and the message strip. It shows `--:--` when stale, unlinked, without a key or refused,
  by `display.js`'s rule (`:165-198`).
- **`clock`:** the server's offset and zone (`display.js:202-217`).
- **`holding`:** an `<img>` whose `onload` / `onerror` decide `shown` or `failed`. A failed take leaves the layer
  black, never the picture before it.
- `display.js` is unchanged in 0.6.

### 1-§5.8 Nothing reaches the stage by surprise, and nothing is lost

> **Amended by** 7-§0.1 (§5.8: 👍 Got it on the take layer's 🔥 strip).

- **A 🔥 priority message** in the room shows as a strip at the bottom of any layer, with its sender, text and **Open
  chat**. Other new messages add "2 new" on the layer's bar, so the Support Team can always reach the Board.
- **A draft is never lost.** A take never moves focus from an open input. It waits for blur, at most 3 s, and the
  composer keeps its text under the layer.
- **The layer** is `#pageLayer`: `position: fixed; inset: 0`, above the sticky header (z 10), below the toasts
  (z 9999), with `role="dialog"` and `aria-label` naming its kind. It is never a modal `<dialog>`, which would cover the
  toasts.

## 1-§6. The Board's simple view

> **Replaced by** 7-§17.2, 7-§17.3, 7-§17.5 and 7-§17.6 (7-§0.1); before that amended by 4-§0 and by 5-§0 and 5-§15.5, which 7-§0.2 replaces item by item.

- **What it is:** a display mode of the same page, in the same Main room, on the same socket, with the same `join` and
  the same seq. Nothing about rights or the room changes. It is `body[data-view="simple"]` (CSS keyed the way
  `styles.css:1086-1092` hides an observer's controls), plus a few JS guards. The server's checks never read it.
- **What it shows:**
  - the hall's name and the countdown chip;
  - the Main room's feed, with every Support Team message, show-desk notices and "From Legal" sends;
  - the Board's large type (`styles.css:463-491`, with the mis-scoped `body[data-role="director"]` half rewritten);
  - action prompts with large answer buttons;
  - help requests and the Help button;
  - files (tap to open in the On stage panel);
  - the quick-note composer (`#directorCompose`, text + 🔥 + Send);
  - the On stage side bar (documents, pinned files, minimised takes);
  - zoom;
  - the pinned strip, read-only.
- **What it hides:**
  - reply, react, forward, Send to…, pin, delete, ⧉, 🖥 and 📝;
  - reaction rows and seen lines;
  - presence lines;
  - the People panel;
  - typing;
  - "To:" and the room switcher;
  - the "Reply with text" `prompt()` (`app.js:707`), which blocks a stage tablet;
  - the right-click menu.
- **How it is chosen:**
  1. `account.view` for an account, or `pages.views['u:'+uid]` for a guest, when set;
  2. else `'simple'` for a seat `board` in a Main room;
  3. else `'full'`.

  It arrives in the join answer's `view`.
- **How it is changed:**
  - **The Accounts page:** a **Chat view** select (By seat / Simple / Full) beside **On stage (Board member)**.
    `PATCH /api/users/:id {view}` goes through `mayChange` (nobody sets their own).
    - `accountChanged(id, what)` (`:1784-1786`) sends `view {view}` live to that account's sockets when `what` is
      exactly `view`, instead of ending them. Every other change still ends the sockets, as rights changes must.
    - The page says so beside Save.
  - **The admin page and the hall page's People panel** (admin only): **View** (By seat / Simple / Full) sends
    `admin:setView {roomCode, socketId, view}`.
    - For a guest it sets `pages.setView(uid, view|null)` and writes `person.view`.
    - For an account it calls `accounts.update(id, {view})` and writes `user.update view → simple`.
    - Either way the server emits `view {view}` to every page of that person (and their support view). It is applied
      live, with no reload, and kept across reloads and restarts. A guest's view follows the device.
- **Still part of the Main room:** the smoke checks that a simple Board page's `allMessages` holds the Support Team's
  messages (`test/browser-smoke.js:262`). It also counts visible controls, as it does for the Viewer at `:546-564`.

### 1-§7.7 Right-click and the buttons, in step (unit 3)

> **Replaced by** 5-§16 (5-§0: unit 3 becomes 3a, 3b, 3c, #23-#25); rows added by 4-§7.7 and 7-§17.1.

- **One list per surface** draws both the buttons and the menu, so they cannot drift.
  - A new classic script, `public/menus.js`, defines only `AGM.menu(items, at)`. It is a fixed-position menu built like
    `.fwd-menu`, with arrow keys, Escape, focus return, and ContextMenu / Shift+F10.
  - `app.html` and `admin.html` load it before their scripts.
- **The action functions:** each page keeps its own `messageActions(msg, ctx)`, `personActions(user, ctx)`,
  `roomActions(room, ctx)` and `takeActions(take, ctx)`. Each returns `[{id, label, icon, when, run}]`, and the same
  list draws the buttons and the menu.
- **Delegated handlers:** one listener each on `#feed`, `#pinnedList`, `#peopleList` and the admin page's tables, keyed
  by `data-id` and `data-action`. This also fixes today's pinned clones, which lose their stage, propose, screen and
  help handlers (`app.js:791-853`), before any new per-message control arrives.

| On | Buttons | The same in right-click / ⋯ |
|---|---|---|
| A message | Reply · React · Forward / Send to… · Pin · Show on screens · Send to Stagewatch · Delete (own) | the same |
| A "Sent to" line | Withdraw | the same |
| A message from another room | Send back | the same |
| A person (People panel) | ⋯ | Show on their screen ▸ · View ▸ (admin) · Role (admin) · Log out (admin) |
| The Board chip | click | the same menu |
| A room button (switcher, halls board) | open | Open · Open in a new tab |
| An On stage card | Show again · Remove | the same |
| A room (admin list, Set up) | Watch · Code · New code · May send in · Rename · Reset · Delete | the same |

- The simple view has no context menu.
- The smoke compares each menu's items with the visible buttons of the same element, for every seat and view.

## 1-§9. Tests

> **Amended by** 2-S.3, 3-H.12, 4-§9, 5-§9, 6-U.8, 7-§9 (and 7-§0.1 on unit 20's row); 4-§0's stale citation and coverage gate applied in place (Part 0 §0.9).

The rule for each unit:

- its first test is written first and **fails on the tree before it**;
- the fixtures named below change on purpose, in the same commit;

## 1-§12. Risks, what is left for later, and the owner's questions

> **Amended by** 4-§12, 5-§12, 7-§12; 6-U.9 (the risk "Upgrade mid-show" gains U5 and U8) and 6-U.10.

### 1-Risks

- **A future reader of "a room" that calls `store.get` misses side rooms.** It fails closed ("Room not found"), never
  open. A new call that checks room rights with `rbac.can` fails closed through the fence. The store's comment and
  unit 6's hall-only tests make a mistake in the other direction visible.
- **The migrated-Main residual:** until New code, a Main room's key is its code, as in 0.5.1. It is marked on the admin
  page and said in the papers.
- **Rollback to 0.5.1** (§1.8): a Main room's code switched off or renewed works again, and a file only a side room
  uses can be removed. This is said in three places.
- **Files are as private as their links.** `/uploads/:name` serves anyone with the URL, the tunnel included
  (`server.js:425-436`). Provenance stops re-posting, not copying a link. A private room raises the stakes (owner
  question 9).
- **"The Board" is whoever sits On stage in the Main room**, presenters included: invited guests, Board accounts and
  those the admin seats, in open halls too (`addendum-stage.md` §5.9.2.1, owner answer 10). An open hall's code guest
  takes no On stage seat and shows nothing, where today any guest with the code may sit On stage (`index.html:74-78`).
- **A web page cannot be confirmed.** Many sites refuse framing, and a venue offline shows nothing. "Opened", the
  operator's preview, the 15 s failure and Back to chat are the honest ceiling. A framed site can read what is typed
  into it, and the strip says so.
- **A change to an account's rooms or On stage halls reloads every page of that account.** That is today's rule for
  rights changes, and the Accounts page says so. A view-only change never reloads.
- **Presence noise:** switching rooms by navigation posts "left" after the grace, as switching halls does.
- **Staff no longer see Main's code.** A crew that relied on Staff handing it out must ask a tech, a project manager or
  the admin (owner question 8).
- **Upgrade mid-show:** pages cached across the restart rejoin with 0.5.1's join shape, which still works. Until they
  reload, their Screens list misses `displays:changed {}`, and a cached signed-in page that had joined by code is
  refused. The CHANGELOG says to upgrade between shows.

### 1-Left for later

- One page holding several rooms, and unread counts rather than dots.
- Seen receipts across rooms, deliberately left out so that no fact of the target room crosses back.
- Action prompts and help requests sent across rooms.
- Per-room download checks on `/uploads` (guests and screens carry no cookie).
- Web takes on `/d/` screens (the `brand` kind goes, owner answer 31).
- A Board chip on the halls board's rows.
- A per-room-pair limit, once a flood is measured.
- Framing Stagewatch's own page.
- A guest identity that lasts across devices.
- Renaming the Main room's label.
- Retiring today's per-guest admin link (`admin:linkRoom`) once allow-lists have been used in a show.

### 1-Questions only the owner can answer

> **Answered in** Part 0 §0.4.3, and §0.5 for the "4".

1. **May backstage code guests push to people's screens?** The design allows it only where the Main room's roles are
   locked (invite-vetted seats), and always for accounts that may drive screens and for the admin.
2. **Do "every hall" accounts (project managers, senior techs) enter every hall's Legal and Media rooms?** The design
   says no: a side room is only for those it is given to, and for the admin.
3. **Is "the Board" everyone seated On stage (presenters too, as the join page has it), or should board members get a
   seat of their own?**
4. **Is a "blank page" black or white?** The design uses black, which is kind to a lit stage.
5. **Should project managers also switch room codes, renew them, and set who may send into a room?** The design keeps
   these to the admin, as you wrote. Making and renaming rooms is open to project managers, as halls are.
6. **May a pushed web page use forms (a voting page)?** The design allows scripts but not forms, popups or navigation.
7. **Should AI drafts be available in rooms like Legal?** They send that room's recent messages to the AI provider. The
   design keeps them available, as in every hall today.
8. **Staff accounts are no longer shown Main's guest code** (with it they could sit backstage with stage rights). Is
   that right for your crews?
9. **Is a file in a private room protected enough by its unguessable link**, readable by anyone who holds it, through
   the tunnel too? Or should downloads be checked per room? That is a larger change, because guests and screens carry
   no cookie.

answers of 2026-10-27 to every question left open, of which 29, 34 and 35 reach this addendum. Evidence class: the
owner's report and answers, read against `start-agmessage.bat`, `make-shareable-copy.bat`, `app/server.js`,
`app/supervise.js`, `app/lib/resilience.js` and `app/test/version.test.js` on `main` at `89104d8`; Microsoft's

## 2-S.1 What the window said, and what it means

The window showed the banner (`start-agmessage.bat:6-16`), then `The system cannot find the path specified.`, then
`Server stopped. Press any key to close this window.` The browser still opened on a working AGMessage.

- **It is not a second server.** A second copy that found one running would have said so in its own words:
  - `Port 3023 is already in use. Close the other AGMessage window, or set PORT to another number.` (`server.js:2441`);
  - or `AGMessage is already running on this data folder (…). Use that window, or give this copy a folder of its own.`
    (`server.js:2458`).
- **It is cmd failing to find Node.** `The system cannot find the path specified.` is cmd's own message when
  `"%~dp0node\node.exe"` (`start-agmessage.bat:29`) does not exist next to the .bat. cmd then sets `ERRORLEVEL` to 3
  (the system's "path not found").
- **The .bat misreads cmd's 3 as AGMessage's 3.** `:32` sends code 3 to `:stopped`, because 3 is AGMessage's own
  `EXIT.CONFIG` ("can't start as configured", `lib/resilience.js:16`). So a copy that never started reads "Server
  stopped", and nothing says why.
- **Why the page worked anyway.** `:20` opens `http://localhost:3023` after 2 s whether or not this copy starts. Whatever
  already listens on 3023 answers: an AGMessage left running from an earlier start, possibly an older version. The owner
  may be using that copy without knowing. Its version is at `http://localhost:3023/api/health` (`version`, `build`;
  `server.js:486`) and on the admin page.
  - From 0.6.0, on a PC where AGMessage is installed, what answers on the installed node's port is most likely that
    node, which serves from boot (answer 35). S.2's banner line and port-holder words then name it.
- **Why `node\node.exe` was missing**, most likely first:
  - The .bat was started from inside the zip. Explorer's zip view copies only the file that is opened to a temporary
    folder, so `node\`, `app\` and `bin\` are not beside it. The CI artifact makes this likely, because GitHub wraps the
    portable zip in a second zip.
  - It was started from a checkout of the repository, which has no `node\` (it is fetched by `tools/fetch-runtime.ps1`).
  - A security product removed or quarantined `node\node.exe`.
- **The guide does not warn of it.** `README.txt:7` and `:17` say "Unzip"; neither says "Extract All, then run the
  .bat from the extracted folder".

## 2-S.2 The design

> **Amended by** 3-H.6 (the opener's `/admin` line is unit H's, #5); 6-U.10's corrections are already in this text.

- **A preflight in the .bat, before anything is opened or started.**
  - **It first reads the install record:** `Version` under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage`, the one record the installer
    writes (`addendum-install.md` U12), with `"%SystemRoot%\System32\reg.exe" query`, never a bare `reg`. No record is
    the common case, and then nothing is said.
    - When the record is there, the banner says "AGMessage <Version> is installed on this PC and starts with Windows.
      This window starts a separate portable copy."
  - It checks `node\node.exe`, `app\supervise.js`, `app\server.js` and `app\node_modules` beside the .bat (`%~dp0`).
  - A missing one is named in words, with the likely cause:
    - When the .bat's folder is under `%TEMP%`: "AGMessage was started from inside the zip. Close this window, right-click
      the zip, choose Extract All, and run start-agmessage.bat from the extracted folder."
    - Otherwise: "This copy is missing node\node.exe. Download the portable zip again and Extract All. If it keeps going
      missing, your antivirus may be removing it."
    - When the install record is there, either ends "To use the installed AGMessage: Start → AGMessage → Open
      AGMessage."
  - The .bat then pauses and exits with a code of its own (2), and opens no browser.
- **The codes the .bat reads are AGMessage's alone.**
  - The preflight means cmd's "path not found" 3 can no longer reach `:32`.
  - `:stopped` is split in two:
    - code 0 reads "Server stopped. Press any key to close this window.";
    - code 3 reads "AGMessage did not start — the reason is above. Press any key to close this window." The reason
      is the server's own words (`server.js:2441`, `:2458`, and the port's holder below), the watchdog's
      (`supervise.js:62`, `:70`), or, once U1 lands, a folder or key that cannot be used, which in the portable channel
      is exit 3 with words (`addendum-install.md` U1).
- **The browser opens on this copy, and only once it is serving.**
  - The .bat's timed opener (`:20`) goes. The .bat sets `AGM_OPEN=1` for the watchdog.
  - The server opens `http://localhost:<PORT>` once `front.listen` has called back (`server.js:2480`).
    - It is opened once per start of the .bat: never on a watchdog restart (`RESTARTS`, `server.js:154`), never in
      tests, and never when `AGM_OPEN` is unset.
    - **It is the portable channel's alone.** It is opened only when `AGM_RUNS` is absent or `portable`
      (`addendum-install.md` U1). Any other value, `task` included, never opens, whatever `AGM_OPEN` holds (S.2.1).
    - It uses `spawn(<SystemRoot>\explorer.exe, [url], {windowsHide: true, detached: true, stdio: 'ignore'})`:
      `explorer.exe` by its absolute path under `%SystemRoot%`, never its bare name (U11's fence); an argument array, no
      shell, inside the `child_process` fence (`eslint.config.mjs:18-25`). It runs on Windows only. With `SystemRoot`
      unset, nothing is spawned and one console line says so.
    - A failure to open is one console line, and the copy keeps serving.
    - **Unit H adds one line to it:** when the audit log has a question at start, the opener opens `/admin` instead
      (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.6). That line and its test (H.12's `opener` row) are H's.
- **A port in use says who holds it.**
  - On `EADDRINUSE` (`server.js:2440-2444`), the server reads `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/health` once, with a 1 s
    timeout, before it exits.
  - The read is loopback only and sends no token. From loopback the answer is the host's detail (`server.js:487`). The
    words take `version`, `build` and, where the answer has it, `install.runs` (the admin health's `install` block,
    `addendum-install.md` U.7), and nothing else. The answer only chooses words; nothing is decided on it.
  - **In the portable folder** (exit 3, as today):
    - "The AGMessage installed on this PC (0.6.0, build …) is serving on port 3023. Open it from Start → AGMessage →
      Open AGMessage, or set PORT to another number to run this copy beside it." when the answer says `install.runs`
      is `task`;
    - "AGMessage 0.5.1 (build …) is already running on port 3023. Use its window, or close it and start this copy
      again." when the answer is AGMessage's otherwise;
    - "Another program is using port 3023. Close it, or set PORT to another number." otherwise.
  - **In the installed node** the same read chooses the installed node's own words (S.2.1).
  - **U8's busy line joins the folder-held words, not these.** U8 answers its busy line on the folder pipe
    (`addendum-install.md` U8). A copy refused at the folder (`server.js:2458`) knows that pipe's name, so its words can
    say how busy the running copy is. A copy refused at the port alone cannot: the pipe is named after the other copy's
    data folder (`server.js:2453-2454`), which it does not know. That line and its test are U8's.
- **The banner says which copy is starting.** The .bat's first lines name its own folder ("from C:\Tools\AGMessage"). The
  server's first line already names the build (`server.js:2492`).
- **`setlocal enabledelayedexpansion` goes** (`start-agmessage.bat:2`). Nothing in the .bat uses `!var!`, and with it on
  a folder whose name holds `!` loses that character from `%~dp0`, which is the same "path not found".
- **The CI artifact and the guide say Extract All.** This is the portable zip's; the installer is one file, and its
  release-notes words are U13's (the Smart App Control words).
  - `README.txt`'s steps (`:17-21`) gain "Extract All first (right-click the zip). Running the .bat from inside the zip
    does not work."
  - Its troubleshooting (`:126-133`) gains the new messages, word for word.
  - The release notes in the release job (`ci.yml:188`, `gh release create --notes`) gain the same line.
  - The package job's artifact is said to be a zip around the zip, in `README.md`'s Build section.

### 2-S.2.1 Which channel each part is for (answers 34 and 35)

The installed node runs `node.exe app\launch.js serve` as a startup task under LocalService, in session 0, with no
window (`addendum-install.md` U.5, U12). A process there shows nothing to the person at the screen:

- "Services cannot directly interact with a user as of Windows Vista", and "All services run in Terminal Services
  session 0" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/interactive-services);
- a task's message box "will be displayed if the task is activated and the task has an interactive logon type", and a
  task run as LocalService is `TASK_LOGON_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, not an interactive one
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/principal-logontype).

So nothing in unit S that opens or draws runs there. Each part is for one channel, and the installed node's words go
where U3 puts them.

| Part of unit S | The portable folder | The installed node: what it shows instead, and whose unit |
|---|---|---|
| The install-record line | Yes, on a PC where AGMessage is installed | — |
| The preflight (`node\node.exe`, `app\…`) | Yes | No .bat (U13). The installer lays the files, and U16's life cycle checks each against `SHA256SUMS.payload`. A `node.exe` removed afterwards stops the task and every Start menu item, since each is a `node.exe` run (U13), so nothing of AGMessage's can say why: Task Scheduler's last result for `\AGMessage\Server` is where it shows (the IT sheet, U.9), and lab 4 reads Smart App Control's case |
| The split `:stopped` | Yes: code 0 and code 3 in words | No window. Under `task` the watchdog's 0, its give-up and a configuration refusal end the task with 0 after writing why, and a held port or folder exits 75 and is retried (U1, U12). The words reach `server.log`, the admin page and "This laptop" (U3), and Start → AGMessage → AGMessage status and Open AGMessage show the log's tail (U12, U13) |
| The browser opener | Yes: `AGM_OPEN`, after listen, once per start of the .bat | Never from the server (S.2). **Open AGMessage** in the Start menu, run as the person in their own session, opens `http://localhost:<PORT>` when the installed build answers, and otherwise says what it found: the state, the log's tail and what to do (U.3, U13). It opens the browser the same way, `explorer.exe` by its absolute path (U11), with its own copy of the call, since `launch.js` requires `node:` built-ins only (U11) |
| The port-holder message | Yes: on the console, exit 3 (S.2) | The same read, its own words. An answer that is AGMessage's is another copy, since the server task runs one instance (`MultipleInstancesPolicy` `IgnoreNew`, U12): "Another copy of AGMessage, 0.6.0 (build …), holds port 3023. Close its window: AGMessage takes the port back on its next try." Otherwise: "Another program is using port 3023. AGMessage tries again; AGMessage status names the program's process." Both are said on the console, which U3 tees into `server.log`; the exit is U1's 75, and `status` names the holder's pid (U12) |
| The banner's folder line | Yes | "This laptop" names the serving build and how it runs (U3), and the admin health's `install` block its folder (`dir`, U.7) |
| Extract All (the guide, the release notes) | Yes: the zip | The installer is one file. Its words in the release notes are U13's |
| The clean copy (S.6) | Yes | `make-shareable-copy.bat` is not installed (U13). What is handed on is the installer itself |
| The bundle start in CI (S.3) | Yes: the zip | U16's life cycle installs, starts the installed node and reads its health |

## 2-S.3 Tests

> **Amended by** 3-H.12 (the `opener` row is unit H's); the "On an installed PC" row runs in #78's job (Part 0 §0.6).

| Unit | Test | Fails today because |
|---|---|---|
| S | **A source test** (`test/startbat.test.js`, every platform) reads `start-agmessage.bat` as text: no `enabledelayedexpansion`; the install record read through `%SystemRoot%\System32\reg.exe` and no bare `reg`, before the preflight's words; the preflight's `if not exist` lines come before any `start` and before `:run`; no `start … http` line remains; code 0 and code 3 reach different words; CRLF line endings throughout (cmd misreads LF-only labels) | the timed opener and the shared `:stopped` exist |
| S | **The .bat run on Windows** (the `test-windows` job): a copy of the .bat in a throwaway folder with no `node\`, run with `cmd /c … < nul`, exits 2, says "missing node\node.exe". Under a folder inside `%TEMP%` it says "started from inside the zip". The runner has no install record, so no "installed" line is said | the .bat exits 3 with "Server stopped" |
| S | **The browser opener** (`test/server.test.js` style): with `AGM_OPEN=1` and a stubbed opener, the server calls it exactly once, after listen, with `http://localhost:<PORT>`; not on a restart (`RESTARTS=1`); not without `AGM_OPEN`; **not with `AGM_RUNS=task`, or any value but `portable`, with `AGM_OPEN=1`**. The spawned file is `<SystemRoot>\explorer.exe` (a stubbed `SystemRoot`); with `SystemRoot` unset nothing is spawned and one line is said | no opener exists |
| S | **The port in use**: a fake health server on the port answers `{version:'0.5.1', build:'…'}`, so a second server exits 3 with "AGMessage 0.5.1 … is already running on port …". Answering `install: {runs: 'task'}` as well gives "The AGMessage installed on this PC … is serving on port …". A plain TCP listener gives "Another program is using port …". **With `AGM_RUNS=task`**, the AGMessage answer gives "Another copy of AGMessage … holds port …" and the listener "Another program … AGMessage tries again", on the console (the exit code is U1's test). None sends a header with a token | the message names no holder |
| S | **The bundle starts** (the `package` job, after the zip is built): the zip is extracted to a throwaway folder; `node\node.exe app\supervise.js` is started there with `PORT` set and no `AGM_OPEN`; `/api/health` answers within 30 s with the build CI stamped; then it is stopped. This is the first time CI runs the shipped bundle rather than the checkout | the job builds the zip but never runs it |
| S | **On an installed PC** (run in U16's elevated job once U13 is in; the words are S's): after the install, the zip's .bat run from a throwaway folder names the installed build in its banner, and exits 3 with "The AGMessage installed on this PC … is serving on port …". With a portable copy started first on the installed node's port, the installed node's `server.log` says "Another copy of AGMessage … holds port …", and the node serves once the copy is stopped | no installer exists |

> **Amended by** Part 0 §0.6: unit S is #4, after #1 and before #5 (H) and #36 (U8).

## 2-S.6 Found beside it: the "clean copy" is not always clean

Found by the audit review (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.15) and read in the code. It is the portable folder's alone
(S.2.1).

- **The fault:** `make-shareable-copy.bat:6` always copies into one fixed folder, `..\AGMessage-Portable-Windows-clean`.
  `:11` copies with `robocopy /E` and no `/PURGE`, so files already in that folder stay.
  - A clean copy that was then started once (to test it) holds its own `app\data`: accounts and their password hashes,
    sessions, `secret.key`, the audit log and settings.
  - Making the clean copy again leaves all of it in place, and the window still says "The copy has no meeting history,
    files, keys or settings."
- **The fix (in unit S):**
  - Each copy goes to a new folder named with the time (`AGMessage-Portable-Windows-clean-<yyyymmdd-hhmm>`). The .bat
    refuses a folder that already exists, so nothing is ever merged.
  - After the copy, it refuses and deletes the copy if anything is found under `app\data` or `app\uploads` but the empty
    folders and `.gitkeep`. That is `build-portable.ps1:43-46`'s rule, in the .bat's words.
  - It says "Done" only after that check.
- **Its test:** S.3's Windows run gains a case. Run the .bat twice, with a file planted under the first copy's
  `app\data` between the runs. The second copy is a new folder, it holds no planted file, and the first is untouched.

## 2-S.7 Risks, left for later, and corrections

- **Risks:**
  - The opener runs as the person in their own session, as the .bat's `start` did. The installed node's server never
    calls it: it runs in session 0, where nothing it opened would be seen (S.2.1). `AGM_OPEN` is set only by the .bat,
    and the opener checks `AGM_RUNS` as well.
  - The installed node cannot say why it does not start when `node.exe` itself is gone (S.2.1's preflight row).
  - The port-holder words come from the holder's own answer. A program that answers as AGMessage chooses which words
    are said, and nothing more.
- **Left for later:**
  - a second copy offering itself on the next free port;
  - a tray icon instead of the console window, and, for the installed node, a status app in the signed-in user's session
    (left for later in `addendum-install.md` U.10 too).
- **No owner question is left here.** The final's "should this go out as 0.5.2 now … or wait for 0.6.0?" is answered by
  29: 0.6.0 (Owner's answers).
- **Corrections to the final (2026-10-26):**
  - S.1 cited `start-agmessage.bat:30` for the `node.exe` line; it is `:29` (`:30` is `set CODE`), as
    `addendum-install.md` U.10 found.
  - S.2 said the health read's "public fields name the version and build only (`server.js:486`)". From loopback the
    answer is the host's detail (`server.js:487`); the words take only the fields S.2 names.
  - S.2's opener spawned `explorer.exe` by its bare name. It is spawned by its absolute path (`addendum-install.md`
    U.10, U11's fence).
  - S.5 said S "can go first, before unit 1" and "can ship in a 0.5.2". Both are withdrawn: answer 29, and the
    CHANGELOG fence.

*`060/addendum-audit-hmac.md`, 1503 lines, kept whole. Its headings carry the prefix `3-`; its units carry their global number, [#n] (Part 0 §0.3).*

Requester: the owner's list (2026-10-26), "Switch the audit chain to HMAC"; the owner's answers to this addendum's
three questions the same day (A–C below); and the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 to every question left open: this
addendum's 1–4, and 29, 34, 35, 38 and 45 where they reach the audit log. Evidence class: the owner's list and answers,
read against `app/lib/audit.js`, `app/lib/secretbox.js`, `app/lib/resilience.js`, `app/lib/tls.js:130-150`,
`app/lib/rbac.js`, `app/lib/guard.js`, `app/lib/accounts.js:401-441` (the token's sign-ins), `app/lib/displays.js:64-75`,
`app/server.js`, `app/supervise.js:32`, `app/lib/http-accounts.js:38-86,114,272-283`, `app/public/users.js:30-40,206-239`,
`app/public/users.html:39-48`, `app/public/admin.html`, `app/public/admin-plus.js`, `app/test/accounts.test.js:411-437`,
`start-agmessage.bat`, `tools/build-portable.ps1`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:145-189` and `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:115-135` on
`main` at `89104d8`; libuv's `src/win/fs.c` (v1.x); and `addendum-install.md` (U12–U15) for the installed shape and the
event archive.

Reviews: three of the first draft (forgery, life cycle, code), run against a model of these rules; then two of the second
version (security, fidelity). The second pair found four attacks that read △, ✓ or "genuine" where they must not: a
token sign-in written into the data folder could Accept (H.8); the claim for data-folder writers did not hold in the
portable layout (H.1); a bundle re-signed with any key passed the verifier (H.9.5); a whole log removed across a move read
△ or ✓ (H.6). That version answered them and the rest of what held; what was not taken is at the end. This version adds
the owner's answers of 2026-10-27: questions 1–4 take the plan's defaults, and answer 45 adds the archive point and the
split (H.10, unit H3). H.10 has had no review of its own yet.

Measured (Node 22.22, the review container; scripts in `bench-export/` beside this file):

- **The keyed check:** 56,000 lines take 0.31 s today and 0.60–0.67 s keyed (parse, exact round trip, HMAC,
  constant-time compare), about 11 ms per 1,000-line slice, inside the 250 ms and 300 ms fences. Those fences now seed a
  keyed chain too. A typical line grows by 62 bytes (338 to 400), so the file rotates about 18 % sooner. The export adds
  nothing to a line.
- **Ed25519 (`node:crypto`):** 67 µs to sign one entry, 124–135 µs to verify one (56,000: 6.9 s); one signature over a
  manifest 0.07 ms. A key built from a 32-byte HKDF seed is the same key every time.
- **A file:** SHA-256 of a 21.9 MB log file 58 ms in one call, on the calling thread; deflate level 6 on the thread pool
  282 ms, to 3.2 MB (6.9×, synthetic lines: real ones will differ); CRC-32 7 ms, on the calling thread.
- **WebCrypto (Node's, standing in for a browser's):** one 23 MB digest 130 ms; 56,000 per-line digests 3.7–3.9 s;
  56,000 Ed25519 verifies 13–16 s; it verifies `node:crypto`'s signatures.
- **The verifier's structure pass** (parse, exact round trip, `seq`, `prev`): 56,000 lines 368 ms.
- **OpenSSL 3.0.13** verifies a `node:crypto` Ed25519 signature with `pkeyutl -verify -rawin`, and refuses it once one
  byte is added.
- **Not measured:** the 500 MACs at open (H.6, estimated from the check's rate); reading the last log at another path
  (H.5, once at a start whose log changed); the verifier's table of 56,000 entries in a browser (H.9.5); the split
  (H.10), which is renames on one volume, one signature and one check, each of whose costs is above; and the check's look
  at each archive (two small reads and a `stat` per file, H.10.4).

Section and unit numbers are placeholders until the splice. The export (H.9) and the archive point (H.10) each moved the
later sections one higher: `addendum-startup.md:109` names this file's H.13 for the clean-copy finding, which is H.15
here, and reads H.15 at the splice.

## 3-H.1 What the chain proves today, and what a key adds

> **Amended by** 6-U.9 (this part's line citations of `addendum-install.md` read by section, applied in place, Part 0 §0.9).

- **Today** each entry carries `h = SHA-256(canonical(e))`, and `canonical` includes `prev` (`audit.js:32-33`), from 64
  zeros (`GENESIS`, `:28`). The check finds an edited, removed or reordered line. While the server runs it also finds the
  newest entries removed (`:216-218`).
- **What it cannot show** (`audit.js:10-11`, `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:125-127`):
  - the whole chain written again, because SHA-256 needs no secret;
  - the newest lines, or the whole file, removed while the server is stopped.
- **With a key** (H.2) and records kept in the key folder (H.5), **a change to the data alone** cannot pass unseen.
  Whoever edits, restores, copies in or removes files in the data folder, without running AGMessage code they changed,
  cannot:
  - write an entry that checks;
  - relabel entries as another machine's, or as this machine's own keyless run;
  - remove the newest entries, remove the whole log, or put another log in its place while AGMessage is stopped, also
    across a move to a new folder (H.5, H.6).

  Each shows at the next start (console, health) and in the check, until the person at the AGMessage laptop accepts it
  with its token. The acceptance is itself an entry.
- **That is not the same as "anyone who can write the data folder".** In the portable layout `app\data` sits in the
  AGMessage folder beside `app\lib`, `app\server.js`, `node\node.exe` and `start-agmessage.bat`
  (`tools/build-portable.ps1:28-31`), under the same rights; on a USB stick formatted FAT or exFAT there are no rights at
  all. Whoever can write `app\data` there can usually change the code or the start script too, and then AGMessage says
  whatever they make it say (an edited `lib\audit.js` can read ✓).
  - One such change leaves a trace a person can see. A start script that sets `AGM_KEY_DIR` to a key folder of the
    writer's own makes their rewritten log check under their key. But the banner then shows another key id and signing
    key, and prints the key folder (H.9.1), and the sealed Stagewatch and AI keys no longer open. Comparing the banner's
    signing key with the show's paperwork at each start (README.txt, H.13) catches it.
  - Nothing inside AGMessage can catch changed code.
- **Off this machine** (H.9): an export is checked anywhere without the HMAC key, against a fingerprint the auditor got
  from the laptop's paperwork, not from the export (H.9.5). A signature by this machine's key covers every byte of the
  bundle and the laptop's own verdict. The keyed entries' MACs are still checked only on the laptop, and the export carries
  what that check said.
- **What it still cannot show**, said in `docs/ACCOUNTS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `README.txt` and the header of `audit.js`:
  - anything done by someone who can change AGMessage's code, its Node or its start script, controls this Windows account,
    or administers this machine. In the portable layout that is anyone who can write the AGMessage folder, which holds
    `app\data`. They can run code that holds the machine key and the records (`secretbox.js:3-6`), and so the signing key
    (H.2);
  - a whole-machine image restored, with the key, the records and the data all from one moment;
  - which person acted, when the actor can write the data folder. They can add an account or a session to
    `accounts.json` or `sessions.json`, which are read as plain JSON (`accounts.js:316-326`), and act through the server
    as anyone; the entries those acts cause are genuine. The token's sign-ins in `admin-sessions.json` are the same
    (`accounts.js:408-420`), which is why Accept asks for the token itself (H.8);
  - the earlier entries of a log first seen keyed on this machine. This includes the 0.5.1 entries at the first keyed
    start (answer C), a folder moved in, and a log written before the key was replaced. They are linked but not checked,
    and nothing here vouches that the newest of them are all there. They are △ until accepted;
  - the newest entries removed after a crash, between their fsync and the head's save. That window is 200 ms normally,
    and longer while a head save fails, which health names.
- **Where the claim holds as written:** the code where only an administrator can change it and the data elsewhere. That
  is the installed shape, which is in 0.6.0 (answers 34 and 35): the program in Program Files, and data and keys in
  `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`, served in session 0 (`addendum-install.md` U.0). That addendum makes the folder with SYSTEM
  and Administrators in full control and the server task's SID (`NT TASK\AGMessage-Server`) allowed to modify (`addendum-install.md` U12's machine folder). Its `keys\` folder
  must then be readable and writable only by the account AGMessage runs as, administrators aside; that addendum's units
  carry the line (H.13). A portable folder stays as described above.

## 3-H.2 The keys

> **Amended by** 6-U.9 (a citation by section, applied in place); 6-U.10 ("one key per machine" installed, already in this text).

- **Three keys, derived, never stored:**
  - `secretbox.derive(label)` = `Buffer.from(crypto.hkdfSync('sha256', machineKey(), '', label, 32))`.
    `hkdfSync` returns an ArrayBuffer ([Node](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/crypto.html#cryptohkdfsyncdigest-ikm-salt-info-keylen)).
  - The labels are allow-listed, and any other label throws:
    - `'agmessage audit entry v1'` gives Ke, for entries;
    - `'agmessage audit head v1'` gives Kh, for the records;
    - `'agmessage audit sign v1'` gives the 32-byte seed of the signing key, for exports (below).
  - The machine key itself never keys a MAC and never signs. It still keys AES-GCM for sealed values, as today
    (`secretbox.js:41`).
- **Its id:** `kid = createHash('sha256').update('agmessage audit key id\n').update(Ke).digest('hex').slice(0, 16)`.
  - The draft's `'…' + K` gave every machine the same kid. `hkdfSync` returns an ArrayBuffer, and a string turns it into
    `[object ArrayBuffer]`. Checked on Node 22: two random machine keys gave one kid, `a09873a45662b4b7`.
- **The signing key (Ed25519):** `secretbox.signingKey()` gives `{privateKey, publicKey, spki, fingerprint}`.
  - The private key is `crypto.createPrivateKey({key: Buffer.concat([PREFIX, seed]), format: 'der', type: 'pkcs8'})`,
    where `PREFIX` is the fixed 16 bytes `302e020100300506032b657004220420`. That is the PKCS#8 form of an Ed25519 private
    key ([RFC 8410 §7](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8410#section-7)), and it is the same prefix
    `generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')` exports (checked on Node 22).
  - Node 24.15 added `format: 'raw-private'` for this
    ([Node](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/crypto.html#cryptocreateprivatekeykey)). It is not used, because
    `engines` allows 24.11 (`app/package.json:19-21`) and the format is marked "Active development".
  - Signing is `crypto.sign(null, bytes, privateKey)` and checking is `crypto.verify(null, bytes, publicKey, sig)`. The
    algorithm "is required to be `null` or `undefined` for Ed25519"
    ([Node](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/crypto.html#cryptosignalgorithm-data-key-callback)).
  - It is pure Ed25519, with no context string, because that is the form both OpenSSL 3.0's `pkeyutl` and WebCrypto
    check (H.9.5). The key signs nothing but the `SHA256SUMS` of an export (H.9.3) or of an archive (H.10.3), which
    keeps it apart from any other use. Each of those lists the file that names its kind (`manifest.json` or
    `archive.json`), and the verifier requires that kind, so one is never read as the other.
  - It is derived when an export signs and is not kept between exports.
  - **`fingerprint`** = SHA-256 of the public key's SPKI DER (44 bytes), 64 lower-case hex characters, shown in 16 groups
    of 4 (`fe97 b845 a378 6ffd …`), always all 16 where a person compares it (the banner, Health, the verifier).
    `openssl pkey -pubin -outform DER | sha256sum` gives the same value. The first 16 characters are its short form in
    audit rows and headers, which are ids, not something a person checks a key against.
- **Why derived rather than stored.** The plan wants a signing key that is never replaced on its own, so that a bundle
  signed today and one signed next month carry the same key unless the machine key itself changed.

| Where the signing key could live | Exposure | Never replaced on its own | Chosen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Derived from `machine.key` (label above) | whoever reads `machine.key` | by construction: it changes only when the machine key does, and the log already records that (`audit.rekey`, H.4) | **yes** |
| `generateKeyPairSync('ed25519')` once, private key sealed in `<keyDir>/audit-sign.json`, as `tls.json` is (`tls.js:146`) | the same: the sealing key is `machine.key`, beside it | needs H.2's publish rules again: a link-exclusive write, and never a new key on a read error. `tls.js:141-147` makes a new certificate on any failure, which is the pattern to avoid | no |
| A plain private key file beside `machine.key` | the same, plus a second secret file to keep | as above | no |

  A stored pair adds a file that can go missing on its own. A key folder restored without it would sign with a new key,
  and nothing in the log would say why. Derivation has neither problem, and `lib/secretbox.js` stays at 3 synchronous
  calls.
- **One key per Windows account on a machine** (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage\machine.key`). A folder moved to another
  laptop or another account goes on under that one's key, with `audit.rekey` (H.4). Its exports carry that one's
  fingerprint.
  - **Installed (answer 35), one key per node:** `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\keys\machine.key`, whichever Windows account
    signs in. The import carries the show user's `machine.key` and `audit\` there as files, so the chain, its records and
    the signing key go on unchanged, and it checks the chain before it finishes (`addendum-install.md` U14's verify). The copies
    left in the show user's profile are removed once the import is verified (answer 42's default).
- **The machine key is never replaced.** Today `secretbox.js:28-35` makes a new key on any read error and overwrites the
  file, which would end the chain's history and lose the sealed keys.
  - **A missing file (ENOENT):** the new key is written whole and fsynced to a temporary file (`writeFileAtomic`). It is
    then published with `fs.linkSync`, which fails if the file already exists. So the file is either absent or whole.
    EEXIST means another first start made it, and that key is read instead. The temporary file is removed.
  - **A link refused for any other reason** (EPERM or ENOTSUP where the key folder's drive cannot hold a hard link, as
    FAT and exFAT cannot; EXDEV): this run has no key, and the words name the code and the folder: "the key folder
    <path> cannot publish the machine key (EPERM): it needs an NTFS drive". The default folder (`%LOCALAPPDATA%`) is on
    the system drive; only `AGM_KEY_DIR` points elsewhere.
  - **Any other read error** (EBUSY, EACCES), or a file that is not 32 bytes: this run has no key.
    - `seal()` throws a named error.
    - The 0.2 migration (`server.js:91-97`) waits for a run that has a key.
    - `contextToken()` (`:103-107`) keeps a new token in memory for this run.
    - A key the admin saves is refused with the reason.
    - `open()` returns `''`, as today.
    - An export is refused (H.9.4).
  - `secretbox.js` stays at 3 synchronous calls (`readFileSync`, `linkSync`, `unlinkSync`; the write is inside
    `writeFileAtomic`). Its reason (`test/resilience.test.js:422`) becomes "the machine key, read once, or made once and
    published whole".
- **No key: a keyless run.**
  - The log keys this run with a random in-memory key and writes `audit.keyless` first, with the error code.
  - It also writes a marker, `keyless-<l>.json`, into the key folder's `audit\` (H.5), best effort since that folder may
    be what failed. The next run tells its own keyless run from entries dressed as one by that marker (H.4).
  - The console, health (`audit.attention`) and the check say so.
  - `write()` never throws, so sign-ins go on (`docs/ACCOUNTS.md:130`). A later run reads this range as a span (H.4).

## 3-H.3 The entry

- **A keyed entry** adds two fields and is written in this order: `{seq, at, actor, action, target, words, ip, prev, l,
  k, h}`.
  - `l` is the log's id: 32 random hex characters, chosen when the log is first keyed and carried by every keyed entry
    of it. It names the log wherever its folder goes (H.5).
  - `k` is the kid.
  - `h = HMAC-SHA256(Ke, canonical2(e))`, where
    `canonical2(e) = JSON.stringify({v: 2, seq, at, actor: {t, id, name}, action, target, words, ip, prev, l, k})`.
- **Nothing is added for the export.** H.9.2 weighs a plain hash or a signature in each entry and takes neither.
- **A legacy entry** (no `l` or `k`) keeps `canonical` and SHA-256 exactly as AGMessage 0.5.1 and earlier wrote it.
  Nothing on disk is rewritten.
  - Whether `k` is present decides which rule applies. `v: 2` only keeps the two canonical forms from ever being the
    same bytes.
- **A line is whole** only when all of these hold. Anything else is "line N is not a whole entry" (✕).
  - It is exactly `JSON.stringify` of what it parses to.
  - It has exactly the written keys, in the written order: nine for a legacy entry, eleven for a keyed one, and `actor`
    exactly `t, id, name`.
  - Each field has its type.
  - `k` is 16 and `l` is 32 lower-case hex characters.

  So a repeated key (`JSON.parse` keeps the last value, while a person or another tool reads the first), an extra field,
  reordered `actor` keys or an upper-case kid is never read as an entry.
- **The rules that need no key live in one pure file**, `app/verify/auditrules.js`: whole lines, links, legacy hashes,
  H.4's runs, and the bundle's path set (H.9.5). `lib/audit.js` requires it, and the export ships it to the auditor
  (H.9.5), so the laptop and the verifier cannot drift.
- **Compared in constant time:** the hex format is checked first, then `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on the 32-byte values,
  for entries and records. A computed MAC never goes into `why`.
- **`write()` makes keyed entries only.** `hashOf` stays exported, with `macOf(e, Ke)` beside it.

## 3-H.4 Runs, boundaries and spans

These rules are applied both by `open()` (H.6) and by the check (H.7). Every rule here but the MAC is also the
verifier's (H.9.5).

- **A run** is a stretch of consecutive entries with the same `k`, or with none.
- **The key changes only at a boundary entry under the new key.** The boundary's `target`, which the MAC covers, names
  the run before it as `<kind>:<first entry>`, for example `plain:1` or `3fa2c1d0e9b8a7f6:812`.

| Boundary | Ends | Words (this machine's, from its own records) |
|---|---|---|
| `audit.keyed` | plain entries from entry 1 (`;first` is added when this machine had never keyed a log, H.5) | with `;first`: "the log is keyed from here on (key 9c01…), from this first start of AGMessage 0.6.0 on this laptop; entries 1–811 have plain hashes, as AGMessage 0.5.1 and earlier wrote them, and nothing vouches for them until they are accepted". Without: "the log is keyed from here on (key 9c01…); entries 1–811 have plain hashes and came to this laptop with no record of them: from an AGMessage that does not key its log (0.5.1 or earlier), or changed by anyone who could write the folder". The version is `BUILD.version` |
| `audit.rekey` | a run under a key this machine does not hold | with no keyless marker for that key id: "entries 812–1630 carry key id 3fa2… (their own claim), a key this machine does not hold: keyed on another computer or Windows account, or written by anyone who could write the folder; this machine cannot check them". With this machine's marker for it: "entries 1631–1700 were written here while this machine had no machine key (EBUSY, 14:02 on 25 Oct): linked, and not checkable" |
| `audit.unkeyed` | plain entries after keyed ones | "entries 1631–1700 have plain hashes after entry 1630: written by an AGMessage that does not key its log (0.5.1 or earlier, a rollback), or by anyone who could write the folder" |
| `audit.keyless` | opens a keyless run (written under the run's in-memory key) | "this run has no machine key (EBUSY): its entries are linked, and cannot be checked after a restart" |

- **The one change of key with no boundary is a change to plain**, since 0.5.1 and earlier cannot write a boundary. That
  plain run must end at an `audit.unkeyed` that names it.
- **Every entry under this machine's key is MAC-checked** wherever it stands.
- **Breaking these rules is ✕.**
  - A middle line relabelled with a made-up kid (`deadbeef…`, its words changed, `h` kept) is ✕: the next entry is no
    boundary naming it. The draft read it as ◇.
  - Relabelling the newest entries, with their `h` kept, is ✕ too.
- **A span** is a stretch of entries that are not under this machine's key.
  - **Its kind and words are this machine's.** They come from what this machine holds: whether the entries carry a `k`
    at all, whether that key id is this machine's, and the keyless markers in its key folder (H.5). A span's own entries
    are what is not vouched for, so a boundary inside them (an `audit.keyless` or `audit.keyed` under a key this machine
    does not hold) is structure only: it is held to the rules above, and its words are quoted as its claim, never used.
    So entries appended while AGMessage was stopped, opened by a made-up `audit.keyless`, read "carry key id deadbeef…
    (their own claim), a key this machine does not hold", never "this run had no machine key".
  - **Every span is △ until an `audit.accept` names it (H.8), and ◇ once accepted. There is no exception** (answer C).
    The plain range a 0.5.1 log brings to its first keyed start is a span like any other. `;first` changes only its
    words, which tell the person at the laptop whether this is the expected upgrade or a plain log arriving where one
    was already keyed.
  - A span with no boundary after it is ✕ (entries added behind the running server's back).
- **A chain that begins after entry 1** (the live log after a split, or an archive that continues an earlier one, H.10)
  begins at an archive point, `audit.archive`, under this machine's key. The point's target names the run it stands in
  (`9c01ab23cd45ef67:812`), so these rules start there, and a later boundary may name that run by a first entry the chain
  no longer holds. Any other chain that begins after entry 1 is ✕, as today: "entries 1 to 36000 are missing"
  (`accounts.test.js:436`).

## 3-H.5 The records outside the data folder

They live in `<keyDir>/audit/` (`secretbox.keyDir()`). The folder is injected in tests (H.12).

| File | Holds | Written |
|---|---|---|
| `head-<l>.json` | `{v: 1, log, path, kid, seq, h, run, held, at, mac}`. `seq` and `h`: the newest entry on disk and fsynced. `run`: the first entry of this machine's run that entry stands in (H.4), so an archive point can name it when the run began in an older file (H.10.1). `held`: findings whose own entry (`audit.cut`, `audit.head`) is not on disk yet, oldest first; at most 16, then one item `{kind: 'more', n}` that reads ✕ until those entries are on disk (H.7) | through the lane `auditHead`, which the log owns: after every fsynced `_put()`, latest wins, 200 ms; at once at `open()`; and by `flush()` |
| `latest.json` | `{v: 1, log, path, seq, at, mac}`: the log this machine wrote last, and where | with each head save, through the same lane |
| `folder-<id>.json` | `{v: 1, folder, path, log, at, mac}`: the log this file path last held | at `open()`, when it changes |
| `keyed.json` | `{v: 1, since, log, mac}`: this machine has keyed a log. Its only effect is `;first` in H.4's words | once |
| `keyless-<l>.json` | `{v: 1, log, runs: [{kid, from, at, code}]}`, the newest 16 runs this machine made without its key (H.2). No `mac`: there was no key to make one, and whoever can write the key folder holds the key anyway | at a keyless run's start, best effort |

- **No signing key file.** The signing key is derived (H.2), and AGMessage keeps no copy of an export (H.9.3).
- **No record of a split.** The head names the newest entry, so never an archived one; each archive is pinned by the
  keyed entry that made it (H.10.6). The head's `run` is the one field the archive point needs.
- **`mac`** = HMAC(Kh, JSON of the record's other fields in the order shown). The log's id and path are inside it.
  - A record that fails its MAC, or is not JSON, is kept aside: copied to `<name>.changed-<time>.json` through
    `writeFileAtomic`, after the lock. This is said (H.6).
- **Reads happen at `open()` only**, through `readOr` (`audit.js:35`), which now also hands back the error's code: the
  same call, so `lib/audit.js` stays at 11 synchronous calls in its text. Writes go through `writeFileAtomic` and the lane.
  - **Only ENOENT means a record is absent.** Any other error (EBUSY, EACCES: a backup tool or antivirus holding it)
    makes this run △ "the head record could not be read (EBUSY)" (H.6), and that record is not written this run, so its
    evidence is never overwritten from a tail that may have been cut. While the head cannot be read, the head lane stays
    off for the run and health names it (`head.error`).
  - Its reason (`resilience.test.js:426`) and `docs/ANALYSIS.md:94-98` add "the records outside the data folder, read
    once at open".
- **`<id>` = `resilience.placeId(dir, name)`:** SHA-256 of `fs.realpathSync.native(dir)`, joined with `name` when one is
  given, lower-cased on Windows, as 16 hex characters. The directory is real by then (the constructor makes it,
  `audit.js:64`), so a first start with no log file yet gives the same id as every later one.
  - The record's id is `placeId(dirname(file), basename(file))`. It names the log file, not the folder, so two logs in one
    folder (`accounts.test.js:362`) have two records; a junction, a `subst` drive or a short name gives one id.
  - **The data-folder lock** (`server.js:2453`) holds 0.5.1's pipe name (SHA-256 of `path.resolve(DATA_DIR)`, lower-cased
    on Windows) and, when it differs, `placeId(DATA_DIR)`'s. So a 0.5.1 copy and this one on one `AGM_DATA_DIR` still
    refuse each other, and two paths to one folder are one folder. A realpath that fails falls back to `path.resolve`,
    with one console line.
  - `lib/resilience.js`'s cap goes from 10 to 11 (`resilience.test.js:421`). The guard rail's pattern is widened to
    count `fs.realpathSync.native(`, which today it does not see.
- **The head is found by the log's id, not by the path.**
  - The zip unpacks to `AGMessage-Portable-Windows-<version>` (`build-portable.ps1:20,50`). So a portable upgrade, a
    moved folder or a changed USB drive letter means a new path, and the log keeps its head anyway.
  - `audit.moved` records the move: "this log was last written at <path>".
- **The log this machine wrote last** (`latest.json`). At `open()`, when this log is not `latest.log`, the file at
  `latest.path` is read once (its newest entry; when it holds none, its newest rotated file's, as the constructor does,
  `audit.js:71`) to see whether it still holds that log.
  - Gone (ENOENT), or another log there: a finding (H.6). A log removed, or swapped for another, is found also across a
    new path, where the head (found by an `l` the new log does not carry) and the folder record (of a path never used)
    see nothing.
  - Still there: not a finding. Two copies of AGMessage on one machine, each with its own log, are allowed.
  - Read failing otherwise: △, as any record (above).
  - This is one read of up to 20 MB, only at a start whose log is not the last one written. Not measured.
- **The head covers only what is durable.** `_put()` sets `onDisk` after `fsyncSync` succeeds; today `:145-146` set it
  before. The head reads `onDisk`, so a failed fsync never lets it claim an entry that a power cut can take away.
- **Stop and crash:**
  - `flushLanes()` calls `audit.flush()` first. That puts the waiting entries on disk, then flushes the head lane.
    The other lanes follow.
  - Today `server.js:132-135` runs in the reverse order, and the head lane's timer dies with the process, so entries
    written at a stop were never in a head.
  - `saveLanes()` lists `['auditHead', audit.headLane]` for health.

## 3-H.6 Opening the log

> **Amended by** Part 0 §0.6: unit S (#4) lands before unit H (#5), so the "until unit S lands" words here never ship (§0.8 C6).

`open()` (`:97-108`) runs after the folder lock and before any entry. It no longer returns early when nothing is torn
(`:100`).

1. **Keys.** `derive` runs inside a try. With no key, the run is keyless (H.2).
2. **The tail**, from the bytes the constructor already read. They are kept until `open()`: at most 20 MB, for about a
   second at start. From them it takes:
   - the newest entry;
   - the first entry of the tail's run, and its kind;
   - the newest keyed entry and its `l`;
   - the entry at the head's `seq`, when it is in that file;
   - the newest `audit.export.sent`, for Health's "Last export" (answer 3, H.11).

   These come from a backward scan by line, not a parse of every line. When the head's entry lies in an older file, the
   check compares it.
   - **The rows the list shows are checked here, once.** The newest 500 lines `_load` keeps (`audit.js:75-85`) are held
     to H.3's whole-line rule, and those under this key are MAC-checked. Each keeps a `mark` for the list (H.11). That is
     500 MACs at start, under 6 ms at the check's measured 11 ms per 1,000 lines (parse included); not measured on its
     own.
3. **A torn fragment** (`:65-68`):
   - its bytes are kept aside as `audit-torn-<time>.bin` (through `writeFileAtomic`), then cut;
   - the words give its size;
   - when it is longer than one entry can be (about 4 KB escaped), they add "more than a half-written line: whole
     entries may have been in it". Step 4 sees any entry it held.
4. **The records against the tail.** Each disagreement is written as `audit.cut` or `audit.head`, and is a finding of the
   check from then on (H.7). Until its entry is on disk it is also in `held`.

| Found | Entry, mark | Words (ranges by `missing()`, `:37`) |
|---|---|---|
| the head's `seq` is beyond the tail | `audit.cut`, ✕ | "entries 1201 to 1630 are missing: this machine recorded entry 1630; the log ended at entry 1200" |
| the entry at the head's `seq` has another `h` | `audit.cut`, ✕ | "the log forked: this machine's entry 1100 is not the log's entry 1100" |
| this path's record names a log whose head says it was last written here, and that log is not here | `audit.cut`, ✕ | "this folder held another log (1630 entries, the newest at 14:02 on 25 Oct); it is not here" |
| this log is not the one this machine wrote last, and that one is not where it was written (`latest.json`, H.5) | `audit.cut`, ✕ | "the log this machine wrote last (1630 entries, at C:\AGMessage-Portable-Windows-0.5.1\app\data, 14:02 on 25 Oct) is not there; this is another log" |
| entries under this machine's key, and no head for this log (ENOENT) | `audit.head`, ✕ | "this machine keyed this log and has no record of it: the head record outside the data folder is missing" |
| the head fails its MAC or is not JSON | `audit.head`, ✕ | "the head record outside the data folder was changed: kept aside as head-….changed-….json" |
| the head is under another kid | `audit.head`, △ | "this log's head is under a key this machine no longer holds (3fa2…, entry 1630): the key was replaced" |
| a record could not be read (any error but ENOENT, H.5) | `audit.head`, △ | "the head record could not be read (EBUSY): this start could not compare the log with it, and entries from here on are not vouched for until a start that can" |

   - A log that moved is not lost: its head names its new path, and this path's record simply moves on.
   - An entry at the head's `seq` with the head's `h` but not under this key is a changed entry: ✕ at the check, never
     held and never accepted.
5. **The tail's kind**, classified only after step 4 and only from this machine's records (H.4), gives the boundary H.4
   asks for:
   - plain from entry 1: `audit.keyed` (`;first` when there is no `keyed.json`);
   - plain after keyed entries, found from the newest keyed entry, also when more than 500 lines follow it:
     `audit.unkeyed`;
   - a key this machine does not hold: `audit.rekey`, its words chosen by whether a keyless marker names that key id;
   - this machine's key: nothing. After a crash a few durable entries may follow the head; they check by MAC.
6. **Then** `audit.repair` (step 3) and `audit.moved` are written. The head (with `held`), `latest.json`, the folder
   record and `keyed.json` are saved at once, except a record that could not be read (H.5).

- **Order:** boundary, then `audit.cut` or `audit.head`, then `audit.repair`, then `audit.moved`. The boundary comes
  first because H.4 needs it directly after the run it names. So on a 0.5.1 log with a torn line: the cut, then
  `audit.keyed`, then `audit.repair`.
- **Visible without pressing Check.** Each is a system row in Accounts → Audit log (`users.js:206-222`), with its mark.
  Each finding is also one console line at start and a line in health (`audit.attention`).
- **The first start asks** (answer C). At the first keyed start on a 0.5.1 log, `audit.open()` (`server.js:2489`) runs
  before the banner. The banner's token block (`:2499-2502`) is followed by the question, so it sits beside the token
  that answers it:

  ```
    Audit log:   entries 1–811 have plain hashes, as AGMessage 0.5.1 and earlier wrote them; anyone who
                 could write this folder could have rewritten them. If this log has been in your hands,
                 accept them: http://localhost:3023/admin → Health → Accept, and type the token above.
                 Until then the log reads △. Nothing waits for this.
  ```

  - Admin → Health, signed in with the token at the laptop, opens with the same question and the Accept button (H.8).
    Signed in as an admin account, it shows the question and where to answer it, with no button. The Accounts page reads
    △ and names where to go.
  - Nothing waits for the answer: sign-ins, takes and sends go on. Only the log's mark is △. That is answer 4's
    default, since its "Admin defined" is read as the stage's S4 **(to confirm: S4, not A4)**, H.15.
  - **The browser opens on the question.** When `AGM_OPEN` is set (unit S) and `audit.attention()` is not empty after
    `audit.open()`, the opener opens `http://localhost:<PORT>/admin` (`server.js:421` redirects it to `/admin.html`)
    instead of `http://localhost:<PORT>`. This is unit H's line in unit S's opener: at the splice `addendum-startup.md`
    S.2 gains it, and S.3's opener test gains "with a △ seed, the stubbed opener gets `/admin`". Until unit S lands, the
    question is in the black window and on Admin → Health, and README.txt says so.

## 3-H.7 The check

`_verify()` (`audit.js:186-220`):

- **Snapshots** `onDisk` and the head, with `held`, when it starts, as `expect` does (`:188`). The re-run after a
  rotation (`:215`) takes a new snapshot. A check given an export's file handles (H.9.4) reads through them, stops at the
  export's row, and never re-runs.
- **Per line:** whole (H.3), linked (`:208-209`), then its own rule: this key, MAC; plain, SHA-256; another key, linked
  but not checked. Then the run rules (H.4).
- **After a split** the walk starts at the live log's first line, an archive point, and names every archive, each looked
  at but not re-read (H.10.4).
- **The findings come from the chain itself.**
  - Each `audit.cut` and `audit.head` entry is a finding, with the id `e<seq>` (its own entry's seq). Those entries are
    MACed, so they can be neither forged nor removed unseen.
  - Each span is a finding, with the id `s<from>-<to>`.
  - `held` adds only findings whose entry is not on disk yet. They read as findings and cannot be accepted until their
    entry is on disk; beyond 16, one `more` item stays ✕ (H.5).
  - Each `audit.accept` covers exactly the ids its target lists (H.8). A finding no later accept names is open.
- **At the end:**
  - the entry at the head's `seq` carries this key, checks, and has the head's `h`;
  - the in-run `expect` holds, as today (`:216-218`);
  - each open finding is reported.

  The check goes on past acceptable findings, so the Accept dialog can list them all. It stops at the first broken entry,
  as today.
