**Revision 3, what changed for the owner** (each from a finding upheld against the code, §12 has the readings):

- **A confidential line on the speaker's screen stays there.** Stagewatch's frame comes back into AGMessage and was
  passed on whole: screens drew it in their strip, every room's page and the halls board were sent it, and the AI's
  brief quoted it. While a confidential line is on the frame, every reader but the rooms where it is in use gets
  nothing of it (§5.14). The line goes only to a hall's own Stagewatch, never a shared one, only over an encrypted link,
  and its words now say what Stagewatch does with it: every output, its public frame (readable on the venue network
  without the PIN), its triggers and its saved settings (§5.9.10, S6).
- **Downloads cannot be reached around the ticket.** A file's address opened in the browser no longer saves it
  (`GET /uploads/` never answers `attachment` and refuses navigations); a file cannot be moved by someone who may not
  download it into a room where they may; a Viewer account never downloads, whatever its seat; observers are never sent
  a document take; and a demoted page is cut off from file links by the server, not by its own reload (§4.6.3, §4.6.6).
- **The operator's information stays up.** A researcher's push no longer replaces or takes down a web page or
  document the operator put over the Board's chat; it goes to the Board's side bar instead (§5.9.1). A side room reaches
  the Board only when it is on the Main room's allow-list, typed quotes included (§5.9.2.2).
- **A take shown by mistake can be withdrawn**, not only taken down: it leaves Earlier too, and its Download ends
  (§5.9.7).
- **Hidden things never shown, closed further:** Word's hidden text (which mammoth 1.13.0 would have drawn), hidden
  slide shapes, Markdown comments and "very hidden" sheets; a Board seat's Look uses the Board's drawing; a file with
  hidden parts is never shown with Download ticked (§5.10.3).
- **The confidential mark is one record per file**, read by every check, and set by the backstage team (or by whoever
  shares the file, as they share it); the AI never receives a confidential file's name, and status words name it only
  to people seated where it is in use (§5.14, §5.12, §5.9.3).
- **On stage links** leave the address bar once used, and the admin can issue a new one without changing the code; a
  Board tablet that remembered On stage falls back to Observer, and unlocking a hall keeps its On stage seats (§5.9.2.1).
- **`stage.show` now governs everyone's information pushes**, Tech and Senior included: revoking it stops them (§5.9.2.2).
- **The request to Stagewatch** keeps the owner's two asks; the other three, and two new ones, are listed as suggested,
  not yet put to the owner (§5.9.12).

**Revision 4, what changed for the owner** (the answers of 2026-10-27):

- **A locked hall's backstage guests can show web pages when the admin allows it** (S4, "Admin defined"): a switch on
  the admin page's Roles & invites panel, per hall, off by default, audited, and turned off when the hall is unlocked
  (§5.9.2.2).
- **Every stage feature works on the Board's mixture of devices** (answer 22). An iPad too old to open documents
  (before iPadOS 16.4) is shown a picture of the place, or what the sender sees, in place of the document, and says
  so; quotes, pictures, web pages, Earlier, Download and the no-save measures work there as anywhere. A device matrix in
  `docs/DEVICES.md`, a smoke leg that takes away what older devices lack, a syntax fence on AGMessage's own page code,
  and a walk on the owner's devices before 0.6.0 is tagged (§5.15, unit T).
- **No 0.5.2** (answer 29): units L and V ship in 0.6.0 (§11).
- **The readings S1 to S16 are the owner's defaults** (§12); only the reading of "4" waits for the owner's word.

**The design's sections, as amended:**

- **§2.3 (guests):** in a Main room, **an On stage (`board`) seat comes only from an On stage invite link, an account
  given the hall's `board`, or the admin**, whether the hall's roles are locked or open. A code guest who asks for On
  stage without the link joins as an observer with words (§5.9.2.1). Backstage and Observer stay open to the code in an

- **§4.3's provenance** gains the file's name, its kind and its source: `freshUploads` is `Map<name, {at, room, uid,
  name, transferOnly, from?}>` (`from`, a picture's source, §5.9.8), and `buildMessage` takes a file's name from the
  upload's record, or from the room's earlier message holding the same URL, never from the client (§4.6.3). A file's
  confidential mark is its own record in `pages.json` (§5.14).
- **§4.3's "Files are as private as their links"** narrows: the link stays the capability for those a room shows it to,
  but an observer seat is never given a file message's link or a document take, opening a link in the browser saves
  nothing, and a download is a server act with a ticket (§4.6.6). Design question 9
  ("should downloads be checked per room?") is answered in part: the download act is checked per seat; reading a file
  a page was shown stays a capability.
- **§5.1** gains the kinds `doc`, `image` and `snippet` (§5.9.3). `chat` gains `layer`. `holding`'s image rule becomes
  `sourceOk` (§5.9.5), and a confidential picture is never a holding image (§5.14).
- **§5.2 (targets):** "the Board" is everyone seated On stage in Main, which is now invited guests, Board accounts and
  guests the admin seated there; an open hall's code no longer reaches it.
- **§5.2 to §5.5 and §1.10** gain a second layer: information over the show (§5.9.1). The `pages.json` shape changes
  before anything writes it, so nothing migrates.
- **§5.6 (the web page, unit 19):** `web` needs **`stage.web`**, a new hall-scoped right that lands with the kind in
  unit 19 (§5.9.9). A code guest holds no `stage.web` of its own: a locked hall's backstage guest shows web pages only
  while the admin's setting for that hall is on (S4, off by default), and an open hall's code guest never (§5.9.2.2).
- **§6 (the simple view):** "files (tap to open in the On stage panel)" becomes "files as cards; a tap opens one with
  Look in the person's own side bar; no Download, except on a take shown with Download ticked (§4.6.6)". A `doc` take in
  the simple view has its page box and zoom at 48 px.
- **§7.3 (the Accounts page)** names `stage.show` and `stage.web` in the rights list; it draws every right from
  `rbac.CAPS` already (`users.js:122`, `lib/http-accounts.js:208`), so the list follows the table.
- **§7.4 (the admin page):** the Invites panel shows the **On stage link** for an open hall too (today it shows links
  only when locked, `admin-plus.js:198-201`, "Open: anyone with the code can join in any role."), with **New On stage
  link**, which voids the old one without changing the code (§5.9.2.1); and, under the lock, **Backstage guests may
  show web pages**, off by default and disabled while the hall is open (S4, §5.9.2.2).
- **§4.2 and §4.3 (`room:send`, `forward`):** a file moves only from a room where the sender may download it (§4.6.6).
- **The architecture and UX addendum's R6** gains a second exception: on an On stage seat's stage content (the layer,
  `#docDisplay`, the feed's pictures), Shift+right-click opens AGMessage's menu too, so the browser's "Save image as" is
  never offered there (§4.6.6).
- **§7.5**: the Board chip and a reduced People tab for `canShow`; the console gated on `canPush || canShow`; the
  composers' words (§4.6.2). **§7.7** gains the rows of §7.7 below, and the catalogue of the architecture and UX
  addendum (§16.7, a draft beside this one) gains the facts and rows listed there.
- **§2.7** gains the rows `upload.refused`, `stagewatch.send`, `file.mark`, `file.download`, `room.invite` and
  `room.guestWeb`, words for `page.push` (a withdrawal included), "n takes ended" in `room.reset`, "guests' web pages
  off" in `room.lock`, "a confidential file … confirmed" in `room.send`, and "confidential text included" in
  `room.read` (§5.11).
- **§8** gains §5.12 and §5.13. **§9**, **§10**, **§11** and **§12** gain the rows below.
- **The `userState:push` relay** (unit 2's key allow-list) carries `doc` between one person's own devices, and from the
  person to the admin's support view, never from the support view to the person (§4.6.3, unit 26).
- **The units.** Three units carry letters, as the start-window and audit-chain addenda's do: **unit L** (a line for the
  speaker's screen) and **unit V** (the vendored libraries), which stand alone, and **unit T** (the Board's devices,

## 4-§4.6 Files to transfer, and files shown on the stage

### 4-§4.6.1 Two acts, not one

Today they are one act. The research File pane's button reads "Send to stage" (`app.html:108`, hint "Files render
directly on the directors' panel", `:99`). It posts a `file` message into the hall's chat (`app.js:1595-1618`), the
message reaches everyone in the hall, and every live Board and research page opens it on its own panel (`app.js:408`,
`if (!silent && msg.type === 'file' && HAS_STAGE) openDocInPanel(...)`). No download link exists on any page
(`renderFileBody`, `app.js:645-676`, draws "📄 name" with no `href`). So a file meant only for download still takes over
the Board's panel, and a file meant for the Board can be saved only through the browser's own image menu.

From 0.6.0 they are two acts with two verbs:

| Act | Verb on the wire | What it makes | Where it goes | Who sees it open |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **📎 Share for download** (a transfer) | `message {type:'file'}` (today's), or `room:send {type:'file'}` into another room (§4.2) | a file message in the room's chat | this room, or another room by its allow-list | nobody, by someone else's act. Backstage seats may 👁 Look or ⬇ Download; On stage seats Look; observers see the card (§4.6.6). The admin's support view mirrors what the person opens, never the reverse (§4.6.3) |
| **📺 Show the Board** / **📺 Show Ana** | `page:push {content: {kind: 'doc' \| 'image' \| 'snippet' \| 'web'}}` (§5.3, §5.9) | a numbered take on the information layer (§5.9.1), never a chat message | the Board group, or one person (for `canShow`, one person seated On stage, §5.9.2) | the targets, over their chat or in their side bar, confirmed page by page |

- **A file message is a transfer.** Nothing else marks it: no `purpose` field is added. A take is a stage push. The two
  never stand for each other.
- **A transfer never opens on anyone's panel.** The rule at `app.js:408` is removed, not narrowed. The §4.3 condition
  (`!msg.sentFrom && !msg.forwardedFrom`) becomes moot with it.
- **A stage push is never a download** on the target's page, unless the pusher ticks **Let them download it** on a
  whole-file push (`doc` with `download: true`; owner answers 12 and 20 as confirmed). Then that item, and only that
  item, offers ⬇ Download to every target that may download it, Board tablets included; observers and Viewer accounts
  never. A quote or a page picture is never a download, and a file whose reader found hidden parts is never shown with
  Download ticked (§5.10.3). §4.6.6 has who may download and what is enforced on the server.
- **What a push hands over.** A `doc` take hands over the whole file. A page, a region or "what I see" is drawn into a
  new picture on the pusher's page and hands over that picture only. A quote hands over its words only. A whole image
  pushed as it is *is* the file, with its metadata; "without its metadata" re-draws it first (§5.9.8).
- **Transfer between rooms** ("for users to download") is `room:send` of a file message (§4.2-4.3). It lands in the
  target room as a download card with "↘ From Legal". It never opens itself there either. Only someone who may download
  the file where it is may move it (§4.6.6), so a seat that may not download cannot carry a file to one that may. A
  confidential file needs a confirmation to cross (§5.14).

### 4-§4.6.2 The words

"Stage" means three things in 0.5.1: the Board's chat ("Type a message to the stage…", `app.html:64`), the On stage
panel (`:118-144`) and Stagewatch's speaker screen (`stage:send`, "Sending to the stage is for the backstage team.",
`server.js:1023`). From 0.6.0 each has its own word, and a button names who will see it:

| Thing | Button | Words after the act |
|---|---|---|
| A file shared for download | **📎 Share for download** | "Shared in Main — the backstage team can download it; the Board can open it." |
| A take (heading: **Send to stage**) | **📺 Picture of p. 12** / **📺 Document at p. 12**, then **Show the Board** / **Show Ana** following To: (§5.9.7) | "Showing the Board… · Take down", then the console's mark (§5.3) |
| A line on the speaker's Stagewatch screen | **📝 Ask the operator** / **🖥 Send now**, chosen per send (§5.9.10) | as today (`renderStageLine`, `app.js:287-300`) |
| A chat message | **Send** | — |
| An action prompt | **❓ Ask the Board** (was "Send to stage", `app.html:91`); in a side room **❓ Ask Legal** | — |
| Saving a file | **⬇ Download** (§4.6.6) | "⬇ Downloading Board pack.pdf…", then "✓ Board pack.pdf reached this browser" or "The download did not start — try again." |
| Opening a file for oneself | **👁 Look** (Board) / **👁 Preview** (research). Observers have no panel (`styles.css:176-178`) and see the card only | — |
| The mark | **🔒 Confidential** (a switch beside 🔥 Priority; on a file, ⋯ → **🔒 Mark confidential** / **Remove the mark**) | "Marked confidential: it goes only where it is in use, or where you send it." |

- The research text placeholder becomes "Type a message to the Board…" in a Main room and "Type a message to Legal…" in
  a side room, which has no Board (§2.3).
- `stage:send`'s refusal (`server.js:1023`) becomes "The speaker's screen is for the backstage team."; its system line
  (`:1035`) "… sent to the speaker's screen: “…”"; its context event (`:1038`) "research sent a message to the speaker's
  screen (…)". `test/showbus.test.js:702-703` and `test/resilience.test.js:337` pin the event's words and change on
  purpose (unit L).
- The rights' words (`lib/rbac.js:15-27`, `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:24-36`):
  - `hall.files` "Share files for download, or forward one into a hall" (`lib/rbac.js:18` and `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:28`
    both say "and push them to a hall" today);
  - `stage.show` "Show files, pages and quotes to the people on stage";
  - `stage.web` "Show web pages on people's pages (the Board's or one person's)";
  - `display.control` as §2.6 has it.
- The roles' words (`lib/rbac.js:32-51`, `docs/ACCOUNTS.md:15-19`): Project manager, Senior tech and Tech add "the
  Board's pages"; Staff "Their halls: messages, files, and information for the Board's pages"; Viewer unchanged.
- No test pins the 0.5.1 button words (grep over `test/`); the smoke's new steps pin the new ones.

### 4-§4.6.3 What changes in today's code

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§4.6.3: the File pane, 📎 in the Message row; the origin line's ⤴, applied in place), 7-§0.3 (§4.6.3: 📺 Shown to you in the simple view; pins for the room or for me; `forward` and `room:send` refused On stage).

- **The upload** (`server.js:561-597`) is one path for both acts, with §4.3's provenance, the file's name and its kind:
  `freshUploads` becomes `Map<name, {at, room, uid, name, transferOnly}>`, `name` being `cleanText(originalname, 120)`.
  Its answer already carries `size` (`:596`) and appends `transferOnly`. The checks of §5.10.3 (archives, image sizes,
  macros) apply to the types the stage can show; a transfer-only type gets its first-bytes check only (§4.6.7).
- **The file message** (`buildMessage`, `server.js:1808-1834`):
  - `filename` is the server's: the upload record's `name` for a fresh upload, or the `filename` of the room's earlier
    message holding the same URL. The client's `filename` is ignored (today it is kept, `:1821`), so a re-post cannot
    rename a file ("Final approved budget.pdf"), and a name never carries an extension the file does not have.
  - It appends `size` and `transferOnly` (when true). Its confidential mark is not stored on it: delivery adds
    `confidential` from the file's one record (§5.14).
    `fs.existsSync` (`:1818`) becomes `fs.statSync(…, {throwIfNoEntry: false})`, which answers both "is it there" and
    its size, so `server.js` stays at its 16 synchronous calls (`test/resilience.test.js`).
  - `forward` (`:943-968`) and `room:send` copy `size` and `transferOnly` with the file; the confidential mark is the
    file's own record, not the message's (§5.14).
  - **Moving a file needs the right to download it where it is.** Today `forward` checks only the target room
    (`rightsIn(dst)`, `:954-956`), so a code guest seated as an observer in a locked hall and backstage in an open one
    (one device identity, `userRooms`, `:948`) could forward the first hall's files into the second and download them
    there. From 0.6.0 `forward` and `room:send` of a file need `mayDownload` in the source room (§4.6.6: the admin, or a
    backstage seat that is not a Viewer account), as well as `mayPost` and `hall.files` there (design §4.2 step 1).
    Otherwise: "Files are moved by the backstage team." Text still forwards as today.
- **Reading a file** (`GET /uploads/:name`, `server.js:425-436`) keeps `nosniff` and the sandbox CSP, with four
  changes:
  - `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600` (`:434`) becomes **`private, no-store`** for every upload, so no device
    keeps a copy in its HTTP cache (RFC 9111 §5.2.2.5, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111#section-5.2.2.5). A
    reload fetches pictures again; no measurement this round of what that costs on venue Wi-Fi (unit 26's bench records
    the bytes per reload of a busy hall).
  - **Never `attachment` on `GET`.** Today `:433` sends `attachment` whenever the type is not `inline` (`docx`, `xlsx`,
    `pptx`, `xls`, `lib/guard.js:204-217`), so opening such a file's address saves it with no ticket and no
    `file.download` row. Every `GET` answer is `inline`.
  - **Navigations are refused** (404) by Fetch Metadata (https://www.w3.org/TR/fetch-metadata/): a request with
    `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate`, or `Sec-Fetch-Dest` of `document`, `iframe`, `frame`, `embed` or `object`. Without it, a
    PDF's address opened in the address bar would give the browser's own viewer, with its Save. AGMessage's own readers
    are unaffected: pdf.js and the readers fetch (`Sec-Fetch-Dest: empty`), and screens draw pictures with `<img>`
    (`image`); no AGMessage page navigates to `/uploads/` (grep over `public/*.js`). A request with no `Sec-Fetch-*`
    headers (an older browser) is served, and SECURITY.md says so; the browsers' support is MDN's compatibility data,
    not tried on the Board's devices until the walk (§5.15).
  - A **transfer-only** file is never answered on `GET` (404): nothing in AGMessage reads it, so only a download ticket
    reaches it (§4.6.7).
- **Download** is a ticketed act, never a `GET` (§4.6.6). The `?dl=1&as=` route of revision 1 is dropped: the name is
  the message's, which the server already holds.
  - `file:download {messageId}` or `{seq}` (a take with `download: true`) over the socket → `{ok, ticket, name, size}`.
  - `POST /uploads/:name/download` with the form field `t` → `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<ASCII
    stem>.<ext>"; filename*=UTF-8''<RFC 5987 stem>.<ext>`.
  - `<ext>` is always the stored file's (an allow-listed extension, `multer`'s `fileFilter`, `:557`). The stem is the
    message's `filename` stem with Windows' reserved characters (`\/:*?"<>|`), trailing dots and spaces removed; a
    trailing `.<ext>` of its own that differs from the stored one is dropped ("Agenda.cmd" for a `.txt` saves as
    "Agenda.txt").
  - The download streams from disk (`res.sendFile`): no `blob:`, no 25 MB held in the page's memory, and the true name
    survives where today's header cuts it to ASCII (`:433`). No synchronous call is added.
- **What an observer's page is given** (§4.6.6): a file message without its `url`, in its live events and in its join
  history, and never a document take (§5.9.3), so it holds no link to a file it could save but a picture shown to it.
- **The file card** (`renderFileBody`, `app.js:645-676`), per seat (§4.6.6's table):
  - "📎 Board pack.pdf · PDF · 2.1 MB" (the kind from the extension table, the size when the message has it), "🔒
    Confidential" before the name when marked, "📦 … · download only" for a transfer-only type. An image keeps its
    inline picture, drawn from the bytes fetched `no-store` into an object URL that is revoked when the card leaves the
    page (§4.6.6); an observer's card has no picture.
  - **⬇ Download** for the admin and the backstage seats that are not Viewer accounts, in the full view.
  - **👁 Look** (Board) / **👁 Preview** (research) opens it in the person's own panel. It reports nothing and pushes
    nothing, except to the person's own devices through `userState:push 'doc'` (`app.js:896`). Not offered for a
    transfer-only type.
  - **📺 Show the Board ▸** for `canShow` (§5.9.2). **⧉ Show on screens** as today (`app.js:455-459`), never for a
    confidential or transfer-only file.
- **The relay of `doc`** (`syncPeer`, `server.js:971-980`): today it runs both ways between a person and the admin's
  support view of anyone with the same name, so the support view can open a file on a person's panel
  (`app.js:1811-1818`). From 0.6.0 `doc` is relayed between sockets of the same uid, and from a person to an `adminView`
  socket; an `adminView` socket's `doc` is relayed to nobody. Unit 26's test holds it, beside unit 2's key allow-list.
  The admin page "shows" a person something only through a take (§5.5), which is confirmed.
- **Pinning** stays the room's pin (`server.js:864-871`). A pinned transfer stays in the panel's pinned list
  (`refreshDocPinnedList`, `app.js:1172-1204`), whose entries open with 👁 Look, never on anyone else's panel.
- **The On stage panel** (`#docPanel`, `app.html:118-144`) has two readers from now on:
  - **On a Board page, "📺 On stage"**, top to bottom:
    - the take cards (§5.4): a minimised information take, a take that arrived in the side bar (§5.9.1), a minimised
      show take; each with **Show again · Remove**, and **⬇ Download** on a take shown with Download ticked;
    - **Earlier**: the last information takes addressed to this person in this hall (§5.11), each opened with Look;
    - one item drawn in `#docDisplay`, with its origin line: "From Ana · p. 12 · ⤴ Show again" for a take, "You opened
      this" for a Look. A Look never removes a take's card;
    - the pinned files.
    - Empty state: "Nothing on stage. What the backstage team shows you appears over the chat or here; ▭ Minimise keeps
      it here."
  - **On a research page, "👁 Preview — the Board does not see this"**: the researcher's own file, paged, zoomed and
    picked from (§5.9.6). A take addressed to this researcher (by `canPush`, §5.9.10) is a card above the Preview,
    marked "sent to you". Empty state: "Nothing in your preview. Open a file to page through it, then show the Board a
    picture of a page, the document, what you see, or what you pick."
  - Observers have no panel. A take minimised by an observer is a card on the rail (§5.4) with **Show again** only.
  - `openDocInPanel`'s `fromPush` branch (`app.js:881-883`, the 75 % split) goes, since nothing pushes into the panel.
- **The research File pane** (`app.html:95-110`):
  - A dropped file opens in the Preview **from the local copy** (`File.arrayBuffer()` to pdf.js's `getDocument({data})`
    and to the worker): instant, private, and no upload. Nothing reaches the server until the researcher acts.
  - **📎 Share for download** (with §7.5's To:) uploads it and posts it. Its 🔥 Priority and 🔒 Confidential sit beside
    it and apply to the share.
  - **Show the Board**, two buttons side by side, neither hidden behind the other (owner answer 11):
    - **📺 Picture of p. 1** draws the Preview's current page into a picture and uploads that alone (§5.9.8). For an
      image it reads "Show this picture"; for a spreadsheet, Word, Markdown or text file, "Show what you see" (sent as
      data, §5.9.4).
    - **📺 Document at p. 1** uploads the whole file and shows it opened at the Preview's place; the Board pages through
      it. **☐ Let them download it** sits under this button only.
  - The caption becomes the take's `note` (`cleanText(200)`; the input's `maxlength` 200, today 120 at `app.html:104`).
  - The hint becomes "Max 25 MB. Share puts it in the chat for download; Show puts a picture of a page, or the document,
    on the Board's pages."
  - A file previewed from the local copy is on this device only: `userState 'doc'` carries a `messageId`, so another of
    one's own devices cannot follow it until the file is shared.

### 4-§4.6.4 How 0.5.1 messages are read

- A 0.5.1 file message is a transfer: a download card without its size. It never opens itself. Nothing is rewritten.
- A 0.5.1 pinned file stays in the pinned list, opened with Look.
- It can be shown on the stage from its ⋯ (§5.9.5 rule 2). A 0.5.1 archive never had the upload checks, so `sourceOk`
  runs them on the first `doc` take that names it (§5.10.3).
- An observer joining after the upgrade is given 0.5.1 file messages without their links too: the withholding is at
  delivery, not in the stored message.
- **Rollback** (adds to §1.8):
  - Stage-only files (§5.11) are in no message, so 0.5.1 neither counts nor removes them (its `removeUnused` takes
    message files only, `server.js:347-357`). They stay on disk, unused, and 0.6 names them again from `pages.json`.
  - The other half: 0.5.1's `uploadsInUse` (`:338-345`) does not read takes, so under 0.5.1 a reset or a delete can
    remove a message file that a 0.6 take names. Back on 0.6 that take reports "the file could not be read".
  - Under 0.5.1, observers are given links again, there are no download tickets, a file's address saves an Office
    file again (`attachment` on `GET`), the confidential mark is ignored (it lives in `pages.json`, which 0.5.1 does not
    read), and a transfer-only file is unreachable (0.5.1's `GET` refuses an extension it does not list,
    `server.js:428-429`; a protected `.docx` is served as a Word file, which no reader opens). The numbered On stage
    links fall back to number 0, so a link replaced under 0.6.0 admits again under 0.5.1 until the code is changed.
    `data/stage/` is not read, and a hall's `guestWeb` (S4) means nothing to 0.5.1, which has no web kind. The
    CHANGELOG says each.

### 4-§4.6.5 Every reader

| Reader | A transfer (a file message) | A stage push (a take) |
|---|---|---|
| The hall page's feed | the file card, per seat (§4.6.3, §4.6.6) | never in the feed. The pusher's toast and console; the Board chip (§7.5) |
| The simple view (§6) | the card; a tap opens it with Look; no ⬇ | the layer, or the side bar; Earlier; ⬇ on a take shown with Download ticked |
| Right-click / ⋯ (§7.7) | the file message's row | the take card's Show again · Remove; the Preview's list (§5.9.7) |
| The admin page's room view (`admin.js:315`) | "📎 name — caption" with ⬇ Download | People rows show the person's current takes, both layers (§7.4) |
| The transcript (`server.js:1836-1887`) | "📎 *name* (shared for download) — caption", 🔒 when marked | the stage record, interleaved by time (§5.13, owner answer 19) |
| The minutes (`admin:summary`, `server.js:1548-1553`) | the thread's line (`lib/ai.js:32`); a confidential file without its name (§5.14) | the stage record's lines, each quote with its text; a confidential item without its text, file name or page (§5.13, S9) |
| The halls board (`lib/board.js:26`) | "📎 name — caption", "📎 🔒 name" when marked | nothing (§5.3) |
| The audit (§2.7) | `room.send` across rooms, as §4.2; `file.mark`; `file.download` for a confidential file | `page.push`, with no file name and no text (§5.11) |
| The context (`lib/context.js:6`) | nothing (no document names) | nothing |
| The AI's brief | `shared "name" for download: caption` (`lib/ai.js:32`); "shared a confidential file" when marked | §5.12 |
| Stagewatch | nothing | only a line, when asked (§5.9.10) |
| Screens (`/d/`) | ⧉ as today, never a confidential or transfer-only file | never. A take is never sent to a screen |
| Stagewatch's frame as AGMessage passes it on (the `stage` payload: the join answer, rooms' `stage` events, screens' strip, the halls board; the AI's brief) | — | the frame's message, except while it is a confidential line: then nothing of it but to the rooms where the item is in use, which read "🔒 a confidential line" (§5.14) |

### 4-§4.6.6 Who may download, and what a Board tablet keeps (owner answers 12 and 20)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§4.6: the no-save measures hold on a Shown to you thumbnail and a Look, on every device row).

The answers, as confirmed: a Board tablet offers no download and keeps no copy **by default**; the sender's "Let them
download it" tick on a whole file applies to Board tablets, for that item only; quotes and page pictures are never
downloads; observers and Viewer accounts never download.

**Who may download what:**

| Seat | A file shared for download | A whole file shown with "Let them download it" | A quote or a page picture |
|---|---|---|---|
| The admin | ⬇ | ⬇ | never |
| Backstage (`research`): accounts and code guests, a side room's Members | ⬇ | ⬇ | never |
| On stage (`board`), either view | 👁 Look only | ⬇, on that take's card and layer bar only | never |
| Observer (`lib/rbac.js:161`) | the card only: no link, no picture, no Look, no ⬇ | a `doc` take is refused for an observer target (§5.9.3); a picture or a quote is drawn | never |
| A Viewer account, whatever its seat (a Viewer granted `hall.post` sits backstage, `roomRoleFor`) | the card only, as an observer's (S2): no link, no picture, no Look, no ⬇ | never ⬇ | never |

`mayDownload(socket, room)` is this table in one pure function in `lib/pages.js`: the admin; or a `research` seat whose
account, if any, is not a Viewer; or, for a take with `download: true`, a target seated `board`. Every download ticket,
the ⬇ buttons and the catalogue's `download` fact (§7.7) read it, and so do `forward` and `room:send` of a file
(§4.6.3).

**What the server enforces** (not hidden buttons):

- **An observer's page never holds a file message's link, nor a document's, and nor does a Viewer account's** (S2).
  Observer sockets, and a Viewer account's sockets whatever their seat, join an io room of their own, `ro:<key>`, at
  join. `apply()`'s `add` (`server.js:210-216`) sends a file message twice: whole to
  `io.to(key).except('ro:'+key)`, and without `url` to `ro:<key>`, as `emitUsers` already splits a broadcast
  (`server.js:253-259`). The join answer's `history` and `ops` (`:793-797`) pass through the same `withoutUrl` for an
  observer seat and a Viewer account. Only file messages are sent twice. A `doc` take is refused for a target seated observer (§5.9.3); a
  picture shown to an observer hands over that picture only.
- **A seat change does not wait for the page.** `admin:setRole` (`server.js:1466-1485`) changes `seat.role` in place and
  only emits `roleChanged`, after which the page reloads itself (`app.js:202`); a page that ignored the event would stay
  in the whole stream. From 0.6.0 the server joins or leaves `ro:<key>` for each socket of that seat in the same tick as
  the change, before the emit, so the next file message is split by the new seat whatever the page does. An account's
  change already closes its sockets (`accountChanged`).
- **A download needs a ticket the socket is given only for a seat that may download.** `file:download {messageId}` (a
  file message of this socket's room) or `{seq}` (a take with `download: true` addressed to this socket's person, or to
  the Board group it sits in, current or in Earlier), one `chatter` token:
  - refused for an observer seat, and for a Viewer account whatever its seat: "Downloads are for the backstage team.";
  - refused for an On stage seat on a message: "On stage tablets keep no copies — ask the backstage team to show it to
    you with Download ticked.";
  - refused for a take without `download`: "This was shown without Download.";
  - refused past **4 live tickets for this socket or 8 for this person**, checked before the global bound, so one page
    cannot push other people's tickets out: "Finish the downloads already started first.";
  - otherwise `{ok, ticket, name, size}`. The ticket is 18 random bytes, kept in a bounded map (at most 1,000 live,
    the oldest going first) as `{upload name, filename, uid, address, socket id, until: now + 60 s}`.
- **The download itself** is `POST /uploads/:name/download` with the form field `t` (a route-level
  `express.urlencoded({extended: false, limit: '1kb', parameterLimit: 2})`; `form-action 'self'` already allows it,
  `lib/guard.js:178-191`). The ticket is taken out of the map on first use, and must name this file, this address
  (`guard.clientIp(req)` against the socket's) and an unexpired time. Then `res.sendFile` with the attachment headers of
  §4.6.3, `no-store`, `nosniff` and the sandbox CSP. A ticket that is unknown, spent, expired or for another address or
  file is answered **204 No Content**, so the hall page stays where it is (a 204 leaves the document view as it was,
  RFC 9110 §15.3.5, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-15.3.5; browsers' handling of 204 and attachment
  navigations is in the web platform tests,
  https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/navigation-api/ordering-and-transition/navigate-204-205-download-then-same-document.html).
  - **Every outcome but the attachment is 204**, the body parser's own refusals included: a `t` sent twice (an array),
    a body over 1 KB or more than two fields would otherwise reach the global handler, whose JSON 400 or 413
    (`server.js:602-607`) the form would show in place of the hall page. The route has an error handler of its own that
    answers 204 for each, tested shape by shape.
- **Attempts are not facts.** The page builds the form with the DOM (no HTML string), submits it, and waits: the server
  emits `file:sending {ticket}` to the socket that asked when the headers go and `file:sent {ticket}` when the stream
  ends. The page reads "⬇ Downloading Board pack.pdf…", then "✓ Board pack.pdf reached this browser"; with no
  `file:sending` in 5 s, "The download did not start — try again." Whether the browser then saved it is the browser's;
  the words say "reached this browser", not "saved".
- A confidential file's download writes one `file.download` row (§5.11) when its stream ends (`file:sent`), never when
  the ticket is issued: a ticket not spent is not a download. Other downloads are not audited: they are a person reading
  what their room already shows them, and the room's record is the record of the file.

**What a Board tablet keeps** (nothing AGMessage writes or offers):

- Every upload is served `private, no-store` (§4.6.3), and the readers fetch with `fetch(url, {cache: 'no-store'})`, so
  no response lands in the browser's HTTP cache. pdf.js reads PDFs by range requests into memory (§5.9.8), which
  `no-store` also keeps out of the cache.
- Pictures (a feed card's, a Look's, an `image` take's) are drawn from the fetched bytes through an object URL that is
  revoked when the card leaves the page or the take closes (`URL.revokeObjectURL`,
  https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/revokeObjectURL_static); mammoth's `blob:` pictures and the
  readers' are revoked with the document they belong to; a pdf.js document is destroyed when it closes (§5.10.2).
- AGMessage's pages register no service worker and use no Cache Storage or IndexedDB (grep over `public/*.js`: none),
  and `localStorage` holds a name, a role, a theme and seen numbers, never a file.
- No ⬇ link and no save action in AGMessage's menus on an On stage seat, except on a take shown with Download ticked. On
  stage content (the layer, `#docDisplay`, the feed's pictures) has AGMessage's own menu in place of the browser's
  (`contextmenu` handled, as §7.7's catalogue does everywhere), **Shift+right-click included** (but for Firefox, below; an exception to the
  architecture and UX addendum's R6, which otherwise leaves the browser's menu there), pictures are `draggable="false"`
  (dragging an image to the desktop saves it), and `-webkit-touch-callout: none` stops iOS's long-press "Save to Photos"
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/-webkit-touch-callout); Chrome on Android fires `contextmenu` on a
  long press, so the same handler keeps its "Download image" away (rows D4 and D5 of §5.15 walk it). The take layer has
  these measures on **every** seat it is drawn on, observers' included, not only On stage. Text stays selectable: iOS's
  Speak and Translate need it, and copying words is as retyping (below). Printing hides the layer and the panel:
  `@media print` replaces them with "What is shown on stage is not printed.", since a print to PDF is a copy (S14).
- **What cannot be prevented**, said in SECURITY.md and README.txt: a screenshot, a screen recording or a photo of the
  screen; a desktop browser's developer tools, which read the page's memory and can `fetch` any link the page was given
  (the navigation guard of §4.6.3 stops only the address bar, links and frames); a browser that sends no Fetch Metadata;
  the browser's own "save page" for what the page still shows; copying or retyping the words; Firefox's own menu on
  Shift+right-click, which Firefox shows without firing `contextmenu`, so no page can cancel it
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/contextmenu_event). "Keeps no copy" means
  AGMessage writes none and offers none, not that a person cannot make one.

### 4-§4.6.7 Files to transfer only (owner answer 18)

Files to transfer accept more types than the stage can show. AGMessage reads their first bytes at upload and never
opens, draws, previews, parses, shows or sends them to the AI; they reach a person only through a download ticket.

| Type | First bytes checked at upload | Reference |
|---|---|---|
| `zip` | `50 4B 03 04` | WHATWG MIME Sniffing, archive patterns, https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#matching-an-archive-type-pattern |
| `mp4`, `m4a`, `mov` | an ISO base media `ftyp` box at bytes 4-7 (a QuickTime file that starts otherwise is refused with the mismatch words) | https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#signature-for-mp4 |
| `mp3` | `ID3`, or an MPEG audio frame header | https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/#matching-an-audio-or-video-type-pattern |
| `wav` | `RIFF`, four bytes, `WAVE` | the same |
| `odt`, `ods`, `odp` | a zip whose first entry is `mimetype`, stored, holding the type's own string (read at its fixed offset in the first 4,096 bytes, as today's check reads, `server.js:582-587`) | ODF 1.2 Part 3 §3.3, https://docs.oasis-open.org/office/v1.2/os/OpenDocument-v1.2-os-part3.html |
| `docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx` protected with a password | the Compound File header `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1` instead of a zip's, **and** a directory that holds the streams `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` and none of `WordDocument`, `Workbook`, `PowerPoint Document`, `Macros` or `_VBA_PROJECT_CUR`. The header alone would admit any compound file: a Word 97 `.doc` with an AutoOpen macro renamed `Agenda.docx` would pass as "download only" | [MS-CFB] §2.2 and §2.6, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-cfb/ ; [MS-OFFCRYPTO] (an encrypted package's `EncryptionInfo` and `EncryptedPackage` streams), https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_file_formats/ms-offcrypto/ |

- **In code:** `lib/guard.js` gains `TRANSFER_TYPES` beside `UPLOAD_TYPES` (`:204-217`): the extensions that are only
  ever transfers, each with its magic. A password-protected `docx`, `xlsx` or `pptx` is not an extension of its own but
  a second shape of three `UPLOAD_TYPES` keys, decided per file: **`lib/cfbcheck.js`** (new, 0 synchronous calls) reads
  the compound file's header, the FAT sectors it names and the directory's chain with `fs.promises` at their offsets,
  at most 64 KB read in all, and answers whether the directory holds the two encryption streams and none of the five
  others; a directory it cannot read within the bound is refused with the mismatch words. `uploadType` (`:229-233`)
  returns `{ext, mime, transferOnly}`; a transfer-only file's `mime` is `application/octet-stream`, whatever it is. The
  `multer` filter (`server.js:557`) admits both tables. `extOf` reads extensions of 1 to 5 characters (`:224-227`), so
  the list stays within that.
- **Served:** only to a download ticket, as `attachment`, `application/octet-stream`, `nosniff`, the sandbox CSP and
  `no-store`. `GET` answers 404 (§4.6.3): by its extension for a `TRANSFER_TYPES` file, and, for a `docx`, `xlsx` or
  `pptx`, by its first 8 bytes read with `fs.promises` at each `GET` (the compound-file header is the transfer-only
  shape). Reading the bytes, not a record, keeps the answer right after a restart, for a side room's file not loaded
  (design §1.5), and with no state to drift. `sourceOk` and `display:take` read the same verdict, cached by name.
- **Never:** Look, Preview, Show, ⧉ screens, a take's source (`sourceOk` refuses it: "That file is for download only:
  AGMessage does not open it."), the AI's document text. The card says "download only".
- **Not taken:** RTF (it carries OLE objects that Office opens), executables, scripts, HTML and SVG, as today.
- **The archive check of §5.10.3 does not run on a transfer-only zip or ODF file:** AGMessage never inflates it. A zip
  bomb harms only a machine that extracts it, as an email attachment would. SECURITY.md says so.
- **The size cap stays 25 MB** (`server.js:556`, "Files can be up to 25 MB."), so most video is too large. A larger cap
  for media is left for later, to be measured first (disk, the upload buckets, venue Wi-Fi).
- **`STAGE_TYPES` and `TRANSFER_ONLY`** (§5.9.3): `TRANSFER_ONLY` lists `TRANSFER_TYPES`' keys. The test holds that no
  key is in both `TRANSFER_TYPES` and `UPLOAD_TYPES`, that every `UPLOAD_TYPES` key is in `STAGE_TYPES`, and that a
  `docx`, `xlsx` or `pptx` in the protected shape is transfer-only per file (its upload answer, its message, `GET`'s
  404, `sourceOk`'s refusal), while the same extension as a zip is a stage type.

---

## 4-§5.9 A researcher pushes to the stage

### 4-§5.9.1 Two layers: the show, and information over it (amends §5.2-§5.5 and §1.10)

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (the show layer without `brand`, owner answer 31, applied in place), 7-§0.3 (§5.9.1 and §5.9.10: a Board member's typed line arrives `side`).

With one layer, a researcher's quote would replace the clock the show operator left up through Q&A, which is exactly
when research is needed; or the researcher would be refused until they found the operator. Neither is instant, and the
first undoes the operator's choice from backstage. So a page holds two layers:

- **The show layer:** `stage`, `clock`, `holding`, `blank`. Only `canPush` pushes it.
- **The information layer:** `doc`, `image`, `snippet`, `web`. `canPush` or `canShow` pushes it, and `web` also needs
  `stage.web` (§5.9.2). A web page is information whoever sends it: the operator's voting page draws over the clock, and
  Back to chat returns to the clock.
- **`chat`** hands back both layers. `{kind: 'chat', layer: 'info'}` hands back the information layer only; it is all
  `canShow` may send of `chat`.

The rules:

- **Which take a page draws.** Within each layer, §5.2's rule: the highest-numbered take addressed to the page, its
  person's or the Board's (when seated `board` in Main). The information take is drawn over the show take. With no
  information take (none, dismissed or minimised), the show take is drawn; with neither, the chat.
- **Over blank.** `blank` is the operator's "keep this tablet dark". An information take over it is held: blank's touch
  controls read "1 from backstage", and a touch shows it. It reports `hidden` with "held under blank".
- **What is under.** The take drawn underneath reports `hidden` with words ("under a quote"), never `shown`: visible or
  it did not happen. The console reads "🕐 clock ◐ under a quote · ❝ Ana's quote ✓ 6/6".
- **Supersede, per layer** (§1.10, §5.3 step 4). A Board information take deletes the older person information takes,
  and their answers, of those seated On stage; a Board show take, the older person show takes. A quote to the Board never
  removes a clock pushed to one Board member. `chat` of both layers to the Board clears both.
- **Whose information stays up.** Each information take records whether its pusher held `canPush` for it (`by.op`).
  With one rule for everyone, a Staff researcher's quote, or the Board chip's Take down, would replace the voting page
  the operator put over the Board's chat during a vote, which is the undoing from backstage this section exists to
  prevent. So a `canShow` push whose target's current information take (the Board's, or that person's) was pushed by
  `canPush` is refused when it arrives `over`: "The operator is showing a web page — ask them, or send it to their side
  bar." It is accepted with `arrive: 'side'`, which draws in the side bar beside the operator's take and supersedes
  nothing. Between two `canShow` pushers, and for `canPush`, the latest wins as above.
- **Answers, per layer.** `answers[personKey] = {show: {seq, state, at}, info: {seq, state, at}}`. Back to chat on an
  information take returns to the show take beneath it. Show again, Minimise and Escape (§5.4) act on the layer drawn on
  top.
- **How a take arrives** (information only): `page:push {…, arrive: 'over' | 'side'}`, default `over`.
  - `over`: the layer of §5.8, over the chat.
  - `side`: an open card in the On stage side bar, drawn in `#docDisplay`; the panel opens itself once
    (`setStageCollapsed(false)`, `app.js:1219`) and never widens to 75 %. It reports `shown` with "in the side bar". For
    routine information that should not cover the chat.
  - A show take always arrives over.
- **Earlier.** When an information take is superseded, handed back or answered with Back to chat, it joins the hall's
  Earlier list (§5.11). A page is told the entries addressed to it and draws them in its side bar. Opening one is a Look:
  no report, no new take. A take that is **withdrawn** (§5.9.7) leaves Earlier too.
- **On the wire.**
  - `page:take` gains `layer` (`'show' | 'info'`), `arrive` and `confidential` (§5.14), and `{withdrawn: seq}`, on
    which a page destroys that take's reader, revokes its object URLs and drops it from its cards and Earlier.
  - The join answer's `page` stays the show layer's take, as designed. **`over`** (the information layer's take, the
    same shape) and **`earlier`** (`[{seq, content, by, at}]`, at most 10) are appended after `canShow` (§5.9.2), which
    unit 24 appends after unit 19's **`canWeb`**.
  - `page:status` gives each target `{show: {seq, showing, mark, words}, info: {seq, showing, mark, words, arrive}}`,
    and the number of its pages that joined without `docs` (§5.15.2).
  - `page:report` counts for the current seq of either layer for that socket's person.
- **In `pages.json`** (§1.10's shape, changed before anything writes it): `halls[H] = {seq, board: {show, info},
  people: {<personKey>: {show?, info?}}, answers: {<personKey>: {show?, info?}}, earlier: [...], files: {...}}`. Person
  takes stay at most 200 per hall, counting both layers; answers at most 500.

### 4-§5.9.2 Who is a researcher, and the rights (owner answer 10)

A researcher is whoever sits **backstage** (`research`) in a hall: code guests who chose Backstage, and accounts that
may post there (`roomRoleFor`, `lib/rbac.js:161`). There is no "Support Team" seat in the code; the owner's Support Team
and researchers are this seat.

The owner's answer: "Board pages should be more secure and not available to guests in an open hall. Web pages need
rights of their own." Confirmed: a code guest in an open hall can neither take an On stage seat nor show anything, and
presenters who join by code need an invite link.

#### 4-§5.9.2.1 On stage seats come from an invite, an account, or the admin

- **Today:** in a locked room, a board or research seat needs the admin's invite link or a seat already held, else the
  guest joins as an observer with a note (`server.js:740-743`, "This meeting needs an invite link for that role — you
  joined as an observer."). In an open room any code guest may sit On stage (`index.html:74`, `join.js:108-119`).
- **From 0.6.0**, `join`'s check (`:740`) holds for `board` in every Main room, locked or open:
  `(cleanRole === 'board' || (r.settings.lockRoles && cleanRole !== 'observer')) && !isAdmin && !checkInvite(…) &&
  !holdsSeat(…)` → observer, with the note "On stage seats need the invite link — you joined as an observer." A locked
  room keeps today's words for a research seat.
- **Seats are kept across a restart** for On stage in an open hall too: `syncSeats` (`server.js:314-321`) returns today
  unless the room is locked (`:315`); it now also saves an open Main room's `board` seats (only those: research and
  observer seats in an open hall come from the code and need no keeping). So an invited Board tablet, or one the admin
  seated, comes back to its seat within `BOOT_SEAT_MS` of a restart (`holdsSeat`, `server.js:283-289`), as a locked
  room's does today.
- **Unlocking keeps them.** `admin:lockRoles` writes `seats: on ? seatsNow(r) : {}` (`server.js:1491`), so unlocking a
  hall today wipes every saved seat. From 0.6.0 unlocking keeps the `board` seats of `seatsNow(r)` and drops the rest,
  so an On stage tablet is not sent to Observer by the next restart after an unlock.
- **The admin may still seat a code guest On stage** from the People list (`admin:setRole`, `server.js:1466-1485`): an
  invite by another route, written as `seat.role` (§2.7). The owner kept it (S5, "Defaults").
- **The join page** (`index.html:70-94`, `join.js:85-120`): the On stage option is shown only when the page came from
  an On stage invite link (`?role=board&invite=…`, read at `join.js:97-101`). Otherwise the role group shows Backstage
  and Observer, and under it "On stage seats come with an invite link from the backstage team." A remembered
  `agm.role` of `board` (`join.js:90-92`) falls back to **Observer** when On stage is not offered, with the same words:
  Backstage would pre-select a Board tablet into a seat that downloads, shows and sends to the speaker's screen
  (owner answers 10 and 20). The submit check beside
  today's locked one (`:115`): `role === 'board' && !invite` → "On stage seats need the invite link you were sent. Join
  Backstage or as an Observer, or ask the backstage team." A page cached across the upgrade still offers On stage; the
  server's note answers it.
- **The admin's Invites panel** (`admin-plus.js:186-215`) shows the **On stage link** for an open hall too, with "Open:
  anyone with the code joins Backstage or as an Observer; On stage needs this link." (today "Open: anyone with the code
  can join in any role.", `:201`). `admin:invites` (`server.js:1494-1498`) already answers in an open hall.
- **The link is not left lying about, and can be replaced.** Today the invite stays in the address for good:
  `join.js:117-119` carries it into `/app.html?…&invite=…` and `app.js:16` reads it from there, so it sits in the
  browser's history of a venue's shared iPad; and `guard.makeInvite` (`lib/guard.js:76-78`) is a fixed MAC of the code
  and the role with no expiry, so only a new code voids it (design §2.2). From 0.6.0:
  - after a successful join the hall page drops `invite=` and `code=` from its address with `history.replaceState`, and
    keeps the invite in `sessionStorage` (in try/catch) for its own rejoins in that tab;
  - the MAC covers a number per hall and role (`invite:<guest code>:board:<n>`, `n` in the room's settings, 0 when
    absent; number 0 is MACed as today, `invite:<guest code>:board`, so today's links keep working until the first
    change); **New On stage link** on the Invites panel adds one
    to `n`, voids the old link without changing the code, keeps the seats already held, and writes a `room.invite` row
    (no link in it). Backstage links get the same number and button.
- **On the upgrade**, a Board tablet that joined an open hall with its code rejoins as an observer with the note, since
  0.5.1 saved no seats in an open hall (`:315`). The CHANGELOG and README.txt say: send the On stage link to presenters
  and board members before the show.

#### 4-§5.9.2.2 The rights: `stage.show` and `stage.web`

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§5.9.2.2: unit G narrows `GUEST_CAPS.board`, now said in this section; Part 0 §0.8 C9); Part 0 §0.8 C14 (`admin:guestWeb` behind `theAdmin()`); S4 is §0.5's open question.

`canPush(hall)` (§2.6) needs `display.control`, which Staff accounts lack (`lib/rbac.js:49`). Yet a Staff researcher's
file opens on the Board's panel today, and so does an open hall's backstage guest's. This addendum keeps the account's
reach under a right of its own, on the information layer only, and ends the open hall guest's (owner answer 10):

- **`stage.show`**, a new hall-scoped cap: "Show files, pages and quotes to the people on stage" (`doc`, `image`,
  `snippet`, and `{chat, layer: 'info'}`).
  - In `CAPS` (`lib/rbac.js:15-27`) and `HALL_SCOPED` (`:29`).
  - In the presets of manager, senior, tech and **staff** (`:32-51`). Viewer never. Revocable per account
    (`effective`, `:57-65`).
  - **It governs every account's information pushes**, through `canPush` as through `canShow`: a Tech with
    `stage.show` revoked is refused `doc`, `image`, `snippet` and `{chat, layer: 'info'}` even though `display.control`
    makes `canPush` hold. Otherwise the right's words would mislead whoever revokes it. Nothing changes until it is
    revoked, since the presets hold it. The admin, and a locked hall's backstage guest (owner question 1), are
    unchanged.
  - **Staff gain more than 0.5.1 gave them.** In 0.5.1 a Staff member's shared file opened in the Board's side panel
    (`app.js:408`); with `stage.show` it can also be drawn over the Board's chat, and a typed quote can be shown. The
    CHANGELOG says so, and the owner kept it (S13, "Defaults").
- **`stage.web`**, a new hall-scoped cap: "Show web pages on people's pages (the Board's or one person's)" (`web`, and
  the link of a web quote's source, §5.9.9).
  - In `CAPS` and `HALL_SCOPED`; in the presets of **manager, senior and tech** (the holders of `display.control`, who
    push web pages in the design); **not staff, not viewer**. Grantable and revocable per account.
  - It lands with the `web` kind in **unit 19**, which this addendum amends: a `web` take needs `canPush(hall)` and
    `allowed('stage.web')` (`server.js:700-705`), or `canShow` with `stage.web`.
  - **A code guest holds it only by the hall's setting** (S4; the owner: "Admin defined"). S4 adds nothing
    to `GUEST_CAPS` (`server.js:699`); the board addendum's unit G narrows `GUEST_CAPS.board`. For a code guest, `allowed('stage.web')` (`server.js:700-705`) holds exactly while
    the guest sits `research` in the hall's Main room, that room's roles are locked (`settings.lockRoles`) and its
    `settings.guestWeb` is `true`. Wherever this addendum says a pusher holds `stage.web`, a code guest holds it so,
    Open the source of a web quote (§5.9.9) included. An open hall's code guest shows nothing (above); a side room's
    Member guest, an On stage guest and an observer never hold it.
  - **Off by default.** No hall has `guestWeb` until the admin turns it on, a hall made before 0.6.0 included, so until
    then a locked hall's backstage guest pushes every show kind and every information kind but `web`.
  - **Where the admin sets it:** the admin page's 🔒 Roles & invites panel (`admin.html:68-74`,
    `admin-plus.js:186-215`), under "Board and research seats need an invite link": ☐ **Backstage guests may show web
    pages on people's pages**, with "Off by default. Guests who joined Backstage with the invite link may then show web
    pages, as accounts with the Web pages right do." It is offered on a hall's Main room only, and disabled while the
    roles are open, with "Lock the roles first: in an open hall, code guests show nothing."
  - **The verb:** `admin:guestWeb {roomCode, on}`, behind `admin(ack)` (`server.js:1398`: the laptop's token, or an
    account with `settings.manage`, `:688`) and then `theAdmin()`: the token, or an account whose role is `admin`
    (`addendum-board.md` §17.6). A manager an admin granted `settings.manage` is refused with "Only an admin may let
    backstage guests show web pages.", and on that manager's admin page the switch is drawn disabled with those words.
    Refused for a side room ("This is set on the hall's Main room.") and for an open hall (the words above). It writes
    `{o: 'meta', settings: {guestWeb}}` through `apply`, which the room's op log keeps (`meta` merges settings, `lib/store.js:122-125`), so a restart keeps it; writes one `room.guestWeb` row
    (§5.11); and in the same tick emits `pages:rights {canWeb}` to each backstage guest socket of the Main room, so the
    console's web entries and the Board chip's Web page… appear or go without a reload.
  - **Unlocking turns it off.** `admin:lockRoles` with `on: false` (`server.js:1486-1493`) writes `guestWeb: false` in
    the same `meta` op, and its `room.lock` row (design §2.7) adds "guests' web pages off". Locking again leaves it
    off, as for a new hall: a lock keeps whoever sits backstage then, code guests who joined by the bare code while the
    hall was open included (`server.js:1491`, `:292-299`), so a switch kept across an unlock would reach guests the
    admin never chose.
  - **Turned off, the next push is refused** with "Web pages from backstage guests are off in this hall — ask the
    admin." A web page a guest is showing stays up until someone takes it down: the admin's answer says how many ("1
    web page a guest showed is still up"), and the panel offers **Take it down**, `{chat, layer: 'info'}` from the
    admin.
  - **A new event** (answer 45, the install addendum's U15): continue and copy carry `guestWeb` with the hall's lock;
    fresh starts without it.
- **`canShow(facts, kind, to, arrive)`**, pure, in `lib/pages.js`, over facts the server gathers: `canPush`, the
  socket's seat and room, whether it is an account, the account's `stage.show`, `stage.web`, `post` and `files` where it
  sits, whether the sending room is on the Main room's allow-list, and who pushed the target's current information take.
  It holds when:
  1. `canPush` holds: every kind, any target, either layer, either arrival; for an account, the information kinds with
     `stage.show` (above); `web` with `stage.web` (a code guest's by the hall's setting, above); or
  2. **an account seated `research` in a room of this hall**, with `canIn(post)` where it sits, the target `board` or
     one person seated `board` in the Main room, and:
     - `stage.show` in the hall for `doc`, `image`, `snippet` and `{chat, layer: 'info'}`, with `canIn(files)` where it
       sits for `doc` and `image`;
     - `stage.web` in the hall for `web` and `{chat, layer: 'info'}`;
     - **from a side room, that room on the Main room's allow-list** (`(settings.roomSends[Main] || []).includes(room)`,
       design §4.1), for every kind, typed quotes and take-downs included: a room that may not post one line into Main's
       chat (design §4.2 step 3) does not draw over every Board tablet either;
     - `arrive: 'side'` when the target's current information take was pushed by `canPush` (§5.9.1);
     - for `{chat, layer: 'info'}`, an `ifSeq` naming the current take, pushed by `canShow` (§5.9.7).
  3. Otherwise it is refused with words, each tested:
     - "Showing the Board is for the backstage team." (not seated backstage here);
     - "In an open hall, showing the Board needs an invite link or an account — ask the admin." (a code guest of an open
       hall, any kind);
     - "Only the people on stage can be shown this." (a target not seated `board`);
     - "Your account may not share files here, so it shows quotes only." (`doc` or `image` without `files`);
     - "Web pages on the stage need their own right — ask an admin." (`web` without `stage.web`, for `canPush` and
       `canShow` alike); for a locked hall's backstage guest while the hall's setting is off, "Web pages from
       backstage guests are off in this hall — ask the admin.";
     - "Showing files, pages and quotes on the stage needs its own right — ask an admin." (an information kind without
       `stage.show`, for an account through `canPush` or `canShow`);
     - "This room may not send to the Main room's Board — ask an admin." (a side room off Main's list);
     - "The operator is showing a web page — ask them, or send it to their side bar." (in the console's words for the
       kind; an `over` push, or a take-down, over the operator's information take).
- **What `canShow` never does:** push or hand back the show layer (§5.9.1). The show operator's choice stays, and the
  information is drawn over it.

| Who | Seat | `canPush` (§2.6) | `canShow` | `web` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The admin | — | every kind | — | yes |
| Tech, Senior, Manager (presets hold `display.control`, `stage.show`, `stage.web`) | research | every kind | — | yes |
| Tech with `stage.show` revoked | research | the show layer only | none | as granted |
| Backstage code guest, Main room, roles locked (an invite) | research | every kind (§2.6, owner question 1); `web` only with the hall's setting | — | only while the admin's setting is on (S4, off by default) |
| Backstage code guest, Main room, roles open | research | none | none: "In an open hall, showing the Board needs an invite link or an account" | never |
| Staff account (`stage.show`), seated backstage in a room of the hall | research | none | `doc` `image` `snippet`, to the Board or a person On stage, over (unless the operator's information is up) or in the side bar; from a side room only when it is on Main's list | only when granted `stage.web` |
| Staff with `hall.files` revoked | research | none | `snippet` only | when granted |
| An account with `revoke: ['stage.show']` and no `stage.web` | research | none | none | — |
| Staff with `hall.post` revoked, or a Viewer granted `stage.show` or `stage.web` | observer (`rbac.js:161`) | none | none: the seat is checked | none |
| Member code guest, a side room | research | none | none (`GUEST_CAPS_SIDE`, §2.3) | never |
| On stage code guest (an invite) or Board account; observers | board, observer | none | none | none |

- The join answer appends **`canWeb`** (a `web` take would be accepted from this socket) with unit 19 as amended, and
  unit 24 appends after it **`canShow`** (a boolean: rule 2 holds for some kind), then `over` and `earlier` (§5.9.1;
  §3.3).
- **The console for `canShow`** (amends §7.5): Screens & pages loads when `canPush || canShow`.
  - The Board chip shows: "Board · 🕐 clock ◐ · ❝ Ana's quote ✓ 6/6". Its menu, and right-click on it, hold **Take
    down** (`{chat, layer: 'info'}` with the current take's `ifSeq`, offered only while that take was pushed by
    `canShow`; otherwise disabled with "The operator put this up — ask them.") and, with `canWeb`, **Web page…**.
  - A reduced People tab lists the people seated On stage only.
  - `page:status` and `pages:changed` (§5.3) reach `canShow` sockets as well as `canPush` ones. A `canShow`-only asker is
    told a web take's host only, never its address, and a confidential take in the in-use voice of §5.9.3.
- The Accounts page names `stage.show` and `stage.web` in the rights list (it lists `rbac.CAPS`, `users.js:122`);
  `giveable()` (`:153-158`) and `rightsView()` (`:164-167`) carry them like any cap; a change of either is a `user.update`
  row whose words name the right (`describe`, design §7.3).

### 4-§5.9.3 The new kinds (`lib/pages.js` `cleanPage`, pure, fail closed)

| Kind | Clean shape | Refused when |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` | `{kind:'doc', url, name, at?, download, note?, standin?}`: the whole file, drawn by the same reader as the Preview, as a Board or observer seat draws it (§5.10.1), opened at `at` (`{page}` PDF, `{slide}` PPTX, `{sheet}` spreadsheet, `{block, page?, approx?}` DOCX, `{line}` text and Markdown). The Board may page on; a device that cannot open documents draws its `standin` instead (§5.15.2) | the file fails §5.9.5; its type is not in `STAGE_TYPES` (below) or it is transfer-only; `at` of the wrong type or out of range (`page` and `slide` 1-9999, as screens take, `lib/displays.js:52`; `sheet` ≤ 64; `block` and `line` 1-999999; `approx` a boolean, and only with a DOCX `page`); **the target is a person seated observer**: "Observers are shown pictures and quotes, not documents." (a document hands over the whole file, which owner answer 20 keeps from observers); a `standin` that fails §5.15.2's rules |
| `image` | `{kind:'image', url, from?, note?}`: a picture, fitted, with zoom. `from` names what it is a picture of: `{url, at}` of a file, checked by §5.9.5 and stored as `{name, room?, at}`; or `{local: true, name, at}` for the researcher's own copy | not an image upload (`guard.validUploadUrl` + `IMAGE_EXT`, `lib/displays.js:28`); it fails §5.9.5; `from.url` fails §5.9.5; over the take's pixel bound (§5.10.3) |
| `snippet` | §5.9.4 | §5.9.4 |
| `web` (§5.6) | unchanged; the normalised `href` keeps its fragment (`#id`, `#:~:text=…`, §5.9.9) | §5.6; without `stage.web` (§5.9.2.2) |

- **There is no `region` on the wire.** A region of a page or an image, and "what I see", is drawn into a new picture on
  the pusher's page (§5.9.8): a cropped image would otherwise hand every target the whole original, its EXIF and GPS
  included.
- **`STAGE_TYPES`** (frozen, in `lib/pages.js`): `pdf png jpg jpeg gif webp txt md csv xlsx xls docx pptx`. It is checked
  in `cleanPage` and again in `docview.open`. **`TRANSFER_ONLY`** lists the transfer types of §4.6.7. A test holds that
  every key of `guard.UPLOAD_TYPES` is in `STAGE_TYPES` and every key of `guard.TRANSFER_TYPES` in `TRANSFER_ONLY`, so a
  type added for transfer is never parsed on the Board's devices unasked.
- `name` is the server's (§4.6.3): the upload record's or the room's message's, never the client's. A local copy's name
  is the client's, and every reader says so ("her copy of").
- `note` is the researcher's line above the take: `cleanText(200)`, optional.
- `download` is `true` only when sent as `true`; anything else is `false`. It is ignored for every target that may not
  download (§4.6.6).
- `confidential` is the server's (§5.14): set from the file's record (`isConfidential(name)`) for a `doc`, for an
  `image` or snippet whose `from` names a file, and for a stage-only upload recorded with a confidential `from` (§5.9.8);
  or `true` when the pusher sends `true`. A client never clears it.
- **The cleaners' rules:** an array's length is checked before it is iterated; every result is a fresh object, never a
  spread of the client's; numbers are finite integers in their range; an unknown key is ignored, a known key of the
  wrong type refuses the whole take.
- **`describePage(c, {voice, inUse})`** has two voices. The console (pushers, `page:status`) may name the file; the
  audit and the server's console never name a file, quote a text or carry a URL path (§2.7). A DOCX page read from Word's
  own breaks is "p. 12"; otherwise "≈ p. 12" (§5.10.4). A confidential item adds "🔒" in the console and "a confidential
  …" in the audit. **To an asker not seated in a room where the item is in use**, a confidential item is "🔒 a
  confidential item": no file name, page or words, since `page:status` and `pages:changed` reach every `canShow` socket
  in the hall, a Media researcher's among them. The AI's voice (§5.12) is always that one.

| Kind | Console | Audit |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` | `Board pack.pdf at p. 12` / `Minutes.docx at ≈ p. 3` | `a PDF at p. 12` / `a Word document at ≈ p. 3` |
| `image` of a page | `Ana's picture of Board pack.pdf, p. 12` | `a picture of a PDF page (p. 12)` |
| `image` of part of an image | `Ana's picture of part of Stage plan.png` | `a picture of part of an image` |
| `image` of a local copy | `Ana's picture of her copy of Board pack.pdf, p. 12` | `a picture of a PDF page (p. 12), from a local copy` |
| `snippet` | `❝ a table cell from Q3.xlsx, 'Sheet1'!C4` | `a quote (a table cell, 18 characters) from a spreadsheet` |
| `snippet`, typed or pasted | `❝ a quote typed by Ana (42 characters)` | `a quote (typed, 42 characters)` |
| `snippet` from the web | `❝ a quote from vote.example.com` | `a quote from a web page on vote.example.com` |
| a confidential `snippet` | `🔒 ❝ a paragraph from Legal advice.docx, p. 3` (seated where it is in use); `🔒 a confidential item` (anyone else) | `a confidential quote (a paragraph, 310 characters) from a Word document` |
| `{chat, layer: 'info'}` | `the information taken down` | `the information taken down` |

  A source in a side room adds its room: `from a spreadsheet in Legal` (rooms are named by name, §2.7). A push sent from a
  side room adds `, sent from Legal` in both voices. An arrival in the side bar adds `, in their side bar`.

### 4-§5.9.4 The snippet: carried as data, never HTML

`{kind:'snippet', unit, title?, text? | items? | table? | blocks?, from?, note?, cut?, more?, confidential?}`, cleaned
by **`cleanSnippet`** in `lib/pages.js`. Every string is read with `guard.str`; a field of the wrong type refuses the
whole take; nothing is defaulted.

| Field | Rule |
|---|---|
| `unit` | one of `word` `sentence` `line` `item` `paragraph` `cell` `row` `column` `range` `slide` `selection` `view` `text`. Anything else: "Choose what to send: a word, sentence, line, item, paragraph, cell, row, column, range, slide, selection, what you see or text." |
| what it carries | `word` `sentence` `line` `paragraph` `selection` `text` carry `text`; `item` carries `items`; `slide` carries `title` and `items`; `cell` `row` `column` `range` carry `table`; `view` (what I see in a DOM reader) carries `blocks`. Exactly one body. A mismatch: "A row is sent as a table." |
| `text` | `guard.cleanBlock`, at most **1,200** characters |
| `items` | at most **20** strings of **300**; `ordered` (boolean) and `start` (1-9999) optional |
| `title` | `cleanText(120)`: a heading path ("Capex › ¶ 3") or a slide's title |
| `table` | `{rows, head, side, ref?, focus?}`: `rows` at most **25 × 10** strings of **200**; short rows padded with `''`; `head` and `side` 0 or 1 (the first row or column holds labels); `ref` `cleanText(64)` (`'Q3'!B2:D9`, "rows 4-9"); `focus` `[r, c]` inside the table |
| `blocks` | at most **12** of `{kind: 'p' \| 'h' \| 'li' \| 'quote', text}` or `{kind: 'table', table}`, each by the rules above |
| `from` | `{url, at}` for a file (§5.9.5; the server drops `url` and sets `name`, the side room and the mark), `{local: true, name, at}` for the researcher's own copy (`name` `cleanText(120)`, said as theirs), `{web: href}` for a web page (§5.6's rules; kept as `{host, urlSealed}`), or absent ("typed by Ana") |
| `at` | `page` `slide` 1-9999, `sheet` ≤ 64, `block` `line` 1-999999, `lines: [a, b]` (a range of lines, `a ≤ b`), `ref` ≤ 64, `heading` ≤ 120, `approx` (a boolean, with a DOCX `page` only, §5.10.4) |
| `cut` | `true` only when the researcher chose "Send the first 1,200 characters" or "Send the first 25 rows × 10 columns"; with a table it needs a full-sized table (25 rows or 10 columns) |
| `more` | with `cut` and a table only: `{rows, cols}`, integers 0-1,048,576, the researcher's count of what was left out. The card reads "… 40 more rows not shown" |
| `confidential` | `true` only when sent as `true`; the server sets it from a confidential source whatever is sent (§5.14) |
| the whole | at most **4,000** characters across every string: the stage is read at a glance |

- **Never cut by the server.** Over a bound, the take is refused with words: "Too big for the stage: narrow it to 25
  rows × 10 columns", "Too long for the stage: 1,200 characters at most (this is 1,860)". The bar says the same before
  sending (§5.9.7), and offers the cut as the researcher's own choice, for text and for tables.
- **Characters** in these bounds are counted as code points (`Array.from`), so no count splits a surrogate pair. (Lines
  for Stagewatch are cut in UTF-16 units, unit L.)
- **`guard.cleanBlock(s)`** (new, beside `cleanText`, `lib/guard.js:33-36`): `str`, then `\r\n`, `\r`, U+2028 and U+2029
  to `\n`; a tab to a space; every other `\p{Cc}`, the bidi overrides and isolates of `UNSAFE_TEXT`, U+061C ARABIC LETTER
  MARK, U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, U+2060 WORD JOINER and U+FEFF dropped; trailing spaces per line trimmed; three or more
  line breaks to two; then trimmed. It never cuts. `cleanText` destroys line breaks, which a paragraph or a list needs.
  U+061C also joins `UNSAFE_TEXT` for `cleanText` (`lib/guard.js:33`, which lacks it today).
- **A cell is sent with its labels.** A picked cell goes as the 2 × 2 table of its corner, its column label, its row label
  and its value, with `focus: [1, 1]`, unless the researcher turns **with labels** off. A column goes with its label cell.
  The labels are the sheet's header row and label column, which the researcher marks once per sheet in the grid; by
  default the sheet's frozen panes, else row 1 and column A. The bar shows them before sending: "C14 · Revenue (row 4) ·
  Q3 (col C)". A finance sheet's title rows would otherwise be shown as a cell's header, a false label on stage.
- **What is and is not a fact.** The server checks that a file source exists and may be shown (§5.9.5). It cannot check
  that the quote is in it, because it never parses a document. So the card always says who quoted it, in their voice:
  "Quoted by Ana · Board pack.pdf, p. 12". The quote is Ana's claim; the Board page's `shown` is the fact.
- **At rest.** A quote's words sit in `pages.json` and the stage record (§5.13) in clear, as the room's own messages sit
  in its file (`data/rooms/*.json`), from the same people; a confidential quote too (§5.14 says the mark is not
  encryption). A web address is sealed (§5.6) because an address can carry a sign-in token in its query.

### 4-§5.9.5 Where a stage file may come from (`sourceOk`)

A `doc` or `image` URL, an `image`'s `from.url`, a snippet's `from.url`, and (amending §5.1) a `holding` image, must be
one of:

1. **a fresh upload by this pusher** (`uid`), made with an upload token whose room is the hall's Main room, or a side
   room that is on Main's allow-list (`settings.roomSends[Main]`, §4.1) and where the pusher may post with files;
2. **a file in a message of the hall's Main room**;
3. **a file in a message of a side room** of the hall that the pusher may read and that is on Main's allow-list;
4. **a file this hall's `pages.json` records** (`files`, a current take or Earlier), when its recorded `room` passes
   rule 2 or 3 for this pusher.

Then:

- **Never a transfer-only file** (§4.6.7): "That file is for download only: AGMessage does not open it."
- **A confidential file** passes only where §5.14 lets it: in use in **every room where the take will be drawn** (Main,
  for the Board; for one person, each room where that person is seated, since a person take reaches every seated page
  of theirs, design §5.2), or with `confirm: true` from someone who may download it in a room where it is in use, after
  which each of those rooms is in use. A confidential picture is never a `holding` image.
- **The refusal names the room only to someone who may read it:** "That file belongs to Legal, which may not send into
  the Main room — send it there first, or ask an admin." Otherwise §4.3's words: "That file belongs to another room —
  send it from there."
- **The allow-list decides which rooms reach the Board.** A file, the pictures made of it and the quotes picked from it
  are held to Main's list by their source; every push from a side room, a typed or pasted quote and a take-down
  included, is held to it by `canShow` (§5.9.2.2). Words a person has copied can still be typed in a room that is on the
  list; §12 says so.
- **No source URL travels for a quote or a picture.** A snippet's or an `image`'s `from`, in `pages.json` and in
  `page:take`, is `{name, room?, at}`, never `url`. A quote never hands the Board the file; a picture hands over only
  itself.
- **The checks a file has not had** run here: a 0.5.1 archive gets §5.10.3's archive check, and an image gets the
  pixel check, both async and cached by name (§5.10.3).

### 4-§5.9.6 The researcher's Preview, and what can be picked

The Preview is the research page's panel (§4.6.3). Its readers move out of `app.js` into `public/docview.mjs`
(§5.10.1), which the Board's layer and side bar also use for `doc` takes, so the researcher and the Board see one
drawing (the Board's without hidden parts, §5.10.3). Which drawing a reader uses is decided by the seat it is on, never
by the caller: a Board or observer seat's Look, Earlier and takes all draw without hidden parts.

**The place, and "what I see":**

- **A page box** replaces the PDF's read-only chip (`app.js:1097-1105`): a number to type, ‹ ›, "of 48", PageUp and
  PageDown. It shows the slide for PPTX, the sheet tabs for spreadsheets (`app.js:985-1026`), the line for text, and
  **the page for Word** ("p. 12 of 30", or "≈ p. 12 of ≈ 30", §5.10.4).
- **Zoom** for PDF and images: −, Fit width, Fit page, +, and pinch. Today the panel only fits the width; A−/A+ scale
  message text (`app.js:66-81`).
- **The place is kept.** A resize, a collapse or a splitter release rebuilds the PDF today (`rerenderCurrentDoc`,
  `app.js:1250-1262`) and does not restore the scroll (inferred from the code, not observed). The reader keeps
  `{page, zoom, offset}` and returns to it.
- **Find.** A find box searches the reader's text (the text that today feeds the AI, §5.10.1) and moves the page box to
  each match. The PDF text layer is built only for pages in view, so the browser's own find misses the rest.
- **What I see**: in a PDF, the page with the most visible area (the page box's) and, when zoomed, its visible rectangle;
  in an image, the visible rectangle; in the other readers, the visible blocks or the visible range of cells, hidden
  ones left out.

**What each type offers:**

| Type | The place | What I see is sent as | Units | How the pick is read | Not offered, and why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PDF | page N | a picture of the page or its visible rectangle (§5.9.8) | word, line, selection; paragraph, item, cell, row, column in a **tagged** PDF; paragraph and item in an untagged one marked "≈ best guess"; a region | pdf.js `TextLayer` over the canvas, built for pages in view only; `page.getStructTree()` maps a marked-content span to its P, LI, TD, TH or TR. Both are in the vendored 4.10.38 (`class TextLayer`, `getStructTree`), and the span's id and the struct tree's content id are the same string, `p<page ref>_mc<n>` (the text layer's from `getPageObjId()`, which returns `` `p${ref}` ``; the struct tree's `` `p${pageObjId}_mc${mcid}` ``, both in `vendor/pdf.*.min.mjs`). Looked up with `CSS.escape` inside the page's container, since two documents can share ids. Untagged lines by baseline | cells in an untagged PDF: "Tables in this PDF cannot be read as cells — send the region as a picture" |
