| Image (png, jpg, gif, webp) | — | the visible rectangle, as a new picture | a region, as a new picture; the whole image as it is, or "without its metadata" | a rectangle drawn on an overlay, nudged by the arrow keys and typed numbers | text (no OCR); an animated GIF crops to its first frame |
| Text (txt) | line N | the visible lines as text | word, sentence, line, paragraph, selection | one element per line (`data-line`); a paragraph is a run of non-blank lines | — |
| Markdown (md) | line N | the visible blocks | word, sentence, line, item, paragraph, cell, row, column (pipe tables), selection | the in-house block parser; inline marks shown as text; raw HTML read by `parseInert`'s text rule (§5.10.1): HTML comments (`<!-- … -->`), `<style>`, `<script>`, `<template>` and elements marked `hidden`, `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` dropped, the rest as plain text | an HTML comment or hidden element, which a Markdown renderer would not show (owner answer 13) |
| CSV | row N | the visible range as a table | cell, row, column, range | the grid (§5.10.2) | — |
| Spreadsheet (xlsx, xls) | sheet, A1 | the visible range as a table, with `ref`, hidden rows and columns left out | cell, row, column, range | the grid; `'Sheet'!B2:D9` from `encode_range` | hidden sheets (SheetJS's `Hidden` 1, and 2, "very hidden", alike), rows and columns: drawn dimmed and marked "hidden" in the researcher's Preview (S15), never pickable, never on the Board's pages (owner answer 13); a formula with no saved value is marked "formula — no saved value", never a blank |
| Word (docx) | heading › ¶ N, **p. 12** (≈ where Word's own breaks are missing, §5.10.4) | the visible blocks (`view`) | word, sentence, item, paragraph, cell, row, column, selection; a picture in it (png, jpg, gif, webp) as a picture | mammoth's HTML, parsed by `parseInert` (§5.10.1) into blocks, each with its page from `wordpages.js`; hidden runs removed before mammoth reads the part (§5.10.2) | **line** (reflowed text has no stable line; sentence takes its place); a picture in EMF or WMF ("a picture this browser cannot show"); hidden text (`w:vanish`, `w:specVanish`), anywhere, the researcher's Preview included; tracked deletions and comments, which mammoth leaves out |
| Slides (pptx) | slide N | the slide's outline | word, item, paragraph, cell, row, column (slide tables), the whole slide (`slide`); a picture in it as a picture | the in-house outline reader (§5.10.2): title, bullets by level, tables, pictures | a picture of the slide as designed (export it to PDF); presenter notes, which are never read (owner answer 13); a shape, picture, table or group marked hidden (`p:cNvPr hidden="1"`), never read; a hidden slide (`show="0"`) is marked and never on the Board's pages. Today pptx has no preview at all (`app.js:1028-1037`) |
| A web page (§5.6 Preview) | the address and its fragment | — | — | — | anything inside the frame: a parent cannot read a cross-origin frame's document or selection. Paste instead (§5.9.9) |
| A transfer-only file (§4.6.7) | — | — | — | never opened | everything: "This file is for download only." |

- **Word and sentence** use `Intl.Segmenter` (word-like segments; sentences), so CJK text and a tap on a word work.
- **Every pick is built from the reader's block model** (§5.10.1), never from `Range.toString()`, which drops block
  boundaries. A native selection counts only when `previewRoot.contains(range.commonAncestorContainer)`.
- **Tables are never picked by native selection.** The grid keeps `{r0, c0, r1, c1}`: tap or the arrow keys pick a
  cell, shift-tap or a drag a range, a header picks its row or column. A merged cell is placed through an occupancy grid,
  so "column C" is the grid's column C.
- **Hidden parts and invisible text.** A pick, "what I see" and the AI's text leave out hidden sheets, rows and
  columns, hidden slide shapes, Word's hidden text, Markdown comments and slides' notes. Text a PDF draws invisibly
  (render mode 3) stays pickable: it is how a scanned PDF carries its words (S15). The bar shows exactly what will
  be drawn on the Board (§5.9.7), which is the guard against text nobody saw. Whether a PDF's optional content that is
  switched off still reaches pdf.js's text layer is not verified (§12 Gaps).

### 4-§5.9.7 Picking and sending

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (§5.9.7: `previewActions(pick)` is the catalogue's kind `pick`; R6's Preview exception).

- **A highlight made first is honoured.** Any selection, tap or drag makes a pick. The bar then offers, as chips with
  their sizes, the units that hold it: "Selection · Sentence · Paragraph 240 ch". The default is the smallest that covers
  the highlight, else the unit last used. Choosing a unit first, then tapping, stays as a shortcut for a finger on an
  iPad. The pick is shown with the CSS Custom Highlight API (an outline on the block where the browser lacks it).
- **One list, two surfaces** (§7.7). `previewActions(pick, ctx)` returns one flat list, which the bar draws as chips and
  the right-click menu as rows: **Copy** · each unit that holds the pick · **Picture of this page** (PDF and images) ·
  **What I see** · **The document at this place** · **▸ to a person**. On touch the menu opens from ⋯ or a second tap on
  the highlighted pick; a long-press stays the browser's own selection gesture, which "Selection" and pasting need.
- **The bar** reads `📺 [Show the Board ▾] [Paragraph ▾ | Picture of p. 12 | Document at p. 12] [over their chat ▾ | in
  their side bar] [🔒] [＋ the speaker's screen] [Show]`, with an optional note. The button names the target as To:
  changes ("Show Ana"). **☐ Let them download it** appears with the Document choice only, and is disabled when the
  reader found hidden parts in the file (§5.10.3). Both the picture and the
  document are offered side by side for every page (owner answer 11); neither is a default behind a ▸. The bar remembers
  the researcher's last choice on this device (`localStorage`, in try/catch).
- **The bar shows what will go before it goes**: the snippet drawn exactly as `pagelayer.render` will draw it (§5.9.11),
  with its size ("a column, 6 cells"); for the document, "the whole file (2.1 MB), opened at p. 12 — the Board can page
  through it"; for a picture, "this page only, as a picture (about 0.8 MB)". Over a bound: the refusal of §5.9.4 with
  **Send the first 1,200 characters** or **Send the first 25 rows × 10 columns**. Above a glance budget (measured on a
  tablet and a phone of the device matrix, D2 and D6, in unit 27's bench, before it is fixed): "Long for the stage — the
  Board will scroll", which never refuses.
- **When a target cannot open documents** (`page:status` counts the target's pages that joined without `docs`,
  §5.15.2), the Document choice reads "the whole file, opened at p. 12 — 2 of 6 Board pages are older devices: they get
  a picture of p. 12 in its place", and the page draws and uploads that picture as the take's `standin` (a PDF or an
  image), or sends what it sees as data (the other types), with no step of the researcher's.
- **When someone else's push is fresh.** When the target shows another pusher's information take under 15 s old, the bar
  says "The Board is reading Ben's quote (8 s) — Replace · Show a person instead", from `page:status`. Between two
  `canShow` pushers it informs and refuses nothing. Over the operator's information take (§5.9.1) the bar offers only
  "in their side bar", with "The operator is showing a web page — this goes to their side bar."; the server refuses an
  `over` push there anyway.
- **A confidential source** lights 🔒 in the bar and cannot be switched off there; a push that would draw it in a room
  where the file is not in use asks "This file is confidential to Legal. Show it in the Main room? It will be in use
  there." (naming each room, for a person seated in several) and sends `confirm: true` on yes (§5.14).
- **The steps and their words:**

| Step | Words |
|---|---|
| a page being drawn | "Drawing p. 12…" |
| the picture or the document being uploaded | "Uploading the picture (0.8 MB)…" / "Uploading the document (2.1 MB)…" |
| the upload's rate reached (`429`, `server.js:564`) | "Sending in 2 s…", then up to three tries 2 s apart, then the server's words |
| the take sent | "… sending — on 0 of 6 pages" (§5.3) |
| every page reported | "✓ on all 6 Board pages" / "✓ in the side bar on all 6 Board pages" |
| the take could not be drawn | the page's `failed` words (§5.9.11) |
| a line with it (§5.9.10) | "📝 waiting for the operator" / "🖥 on the speaker's screen", then its acknowledgement |
| refused | the server's words |

- The feed's ⋯ on a file message offers **📺 Show the Board ▸ A picture of p. 1 · A picture of a page… · The document…**
  ("…a page…" asks the number, as the screens' PDF offer does, `app.html:165-170`). **The document…** opens the same
  short bar the Preview's Document button has: the page (p. 1 by default), **☐ Let them download it**, the arrival and
  Show; the People tab's "Show them ▸ the document" opens it too. So Download can be ticked from every place a document
  can be shown (owner answer 12), not only from the Preview. From the Preview, ⧉ Show on screens fills its page number
  from the page box.
- **Take down, not Undo.** The toast's action is **Take down** for 10 s: `page:push {code, to, content: {kind: 'chat',
  layer: 'info'}, ifSeq: <seq>}`. It hands back the information layer only while this take is still current there; else
  it is refused with "Ben's quote is up now — yours was already replaced." It never re-sends older content, which could
  pop a quote the Board had already closed back onto every page. (For show takes, §7.5's Undo stands.)
- **Withdraw, for a take shown by mistake.** Taking a take down leaves it in Earlier, and with Download ticked every
  Board page keeps offering ⬇ there; a stage-only upload belongs to no message, so only a Main reset would remove it.
  **Withdraw** (`page:withdraw {code, seq}`, one `writes` token), offered beside Take down in the toast for its 10 s and
  then on the take in the console, is for its pusher, `canPush` holders and the admin. It removes the take from the
  current takes and from Earlier, sends `page:take {withdrawn: seq}` to each target (the page destroys the reader and
  revokes its object URLs), voids the `{seq}` download tickets and refuses new ones ("This was withdrawn."), starts its
  stage file's wait (§5.11), adds a `withdrawn` entry to the stage record (what was shown stays recorded, §5.13) and
  writes a `page.push` row "… withdrawn". Its words: "Withdrawn from 6 Board pages — it is no longer under Earlier.";
  a page that was offline is told at its next join, since the take is no longer in what the join answer carries.

### 4-§5.9.8 A page as a picture, or the document (owner answer 11)

The owner's answer: "Both as options." The researcher chooses per push between a picture of exactly what they see and
the live document the Board can page through.

| | **Picture of p. 12** | **Document at p. 12** |
|---|---|---|
| What the Board gets | that page, or the visible rectangle, as a new picture; nothing else of the file | the whole file, opened at p. 12; the Board pages, zooms and finds |
| Kind | `image` with `from: {url, at}` | `doc` with `at` |
| Light on the device | about 0.5-2 MB, no pdf.js | each Board device fetches and parses the file |
| Exactly what the researcher saw | yes | the same drawing (`docview`), at the Board device's size |
| Download | never | only with **Let them download it** (§4.6.6) |
| For DOCX, XLSX, Markdown, CSV, text | no picture: "What I see" goes as data (`view` or a table snippet), redrawn on the Board, since DOM readers are not rasterised (below; S10) | yes |

- **Drawing a picture:** pdf.js renders the page, or the visible rectangle through an offset viewport, into a canvas
  whose long edge is 2,048 px, never over 4,096 px a side or 5,242,880 pixels, the cap pdf.js's own viewer sets on iOS
  and Android (`compatParams.set("maxCanvasPixels", 5242880)`, `web/pdf_viewer.mjs:4132` of the 4.10.38 package; an A4
  page at 2,048 px is about 3 MP). Then `toBlob` as PNG (text and line art) or JPEG 0.9 (a scan, chosen when the page is
  one image).
- **A region of an image, or what I see of it:** `createImageBitmap(img, sx, sy, sw, sh, {imageOrientation:
  'from-image'})`, a canvas, `toBlob`, after the pixel check of §5.10.3. Re-encoding through a canvas strips EXIF, GPS
  included. "Without its metadata" draws a whole image the same way.
- **Uploading it:** `POST /api/upload` with the page's existing token (`app.js:1555`, `server.js:561-597`) and a form
  field **`from`**, the source it was drawn from (`m:<messageId>` of this room, or `s:<seq>` of a take of this hall). A
  PNG passes today's magic check. It is a fresh upload by the pusher for this room, so §5.9.5 rule 1 admits it (in
  Main, or a side room on Main's list). The server records the source in the upload's `freshUploads` entry and, when
  that source's file is confidential, marks the new picture in the file record **when it is stored**, before any take
  names it, so it is never an unmarked fresh upload that its uploader could share or put on a screen. A page that leaves
  `from` out uploads an unmarked picture: the mark on derived content holds for AGMessage's own page, not against
  someone who rewrites it (§5.14 "What it does not do").
- **Again without a second upload:** the page keeps `{source, page, rect, scale} → url` while the stage file's wait runs
  (`UPLOAD_ORPHAN_MS`, §5.11), and draws and uploads again when a push is refused because the file is gone.
- **The document's reader** on the Board passes `{disableStream: true, disableAutoFetch: true}` to pdf.js, since pdf.js
  stops pre-fetching only when streaming is off too ("NOTE: It is also necessary to disable streaming, see above, in
  order for disabling of pre-fetching to work correctly", `disableAutoFetch` in `getDocument`'s parameters,
  `types/src/display/api.d.ts:203-211` of the 4.10.38 package), so Express's Range answers fetch only what is drawn, and
  `no-store` keeps each range out of the cache (§4.6.6).
- **No measurement this round** of the render-plus-upload time on venue Wi-Fi, of how fast a researcher pages against
  the upload buckets (`Bucket(0.5, 4)` per connection, `server.js:693`; `Bucket(0.5, 8)` per address, `:331`), or of a
  25 MB document's parse on a Board tablet. Unit 27's bench records them on the rig's laptop and the device matrix's
  D2 and D4 (§5.15); a bucket
  changes only if that is measured to matter.
- **DOM readers are not rasterised:** no library that draws a page's DOM into a picture is vendored, and none is added
  this round. Their "what I see" goes as data (`view`, §5.9.4), which the Board redraws at its own size; the owner took
  that as the answer for these types (S10, "Defaults").

### 4-§5.9.9 A web page, and pasting

- **A web page** is §5.6's `web` take, on the information layer, with the same address rules, the sealed address and
  host-only words, offered only with **`stage.web`** (§5.9.2.2): to `canPush` holders who have it, to accounts
  seated backstage that have it, and to a locked hall's backstage code guests while the admin's setting is on (S4).
- **At a place.** The normalised `href` keeps its fragment. An `#id` scrolls inside the frame. A text directive
  (`#:~:text=start,end`) is applied only to a top-level, user-started navigation ("If document's node navigable has a
  parent, return false" and "If is user involved is false, return false", URL Fragment Text Directives §3.5.4, "check if
  a text directive can be scrolled", https://wicg.github.io/scroll-to-text-fragment/; its editor's note says Chrome also
  allows a same-origin initiator), so the frame does not highlight it; the Board member's **Open in a new tab** does.
  The strip above the frame shows the directive's own words, decoded (in `try`) and cleaned with `cleanBlock` to 300:
  "Look for: ❝ net revenue rose … in Q3". Nothing is fetched.
- **A highlight inside a web page cannot be read** (§5.9.6). The honest path is **❝ Quote**, a new research composer
  tab beside Message, Action prompt and File:
  - a box to paste into, or to type. It reads the `paste` event's `clipboardData`, which works over plain HTTP too:
    MDN marks `Navigator.clipboard`, `Clipboard` and `ClipboardItem` "Secure context" and `ClipboardEvent` not
    (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Clipboard_API);
  - tab-separated text (what Excel and Sheets put on the clipboard) becomes a table snippet;
  - `text/html` is read only for its structure (table rows and cells, list items), through `parseInert` (§5.10.1), so
    no image or frame in it loads. `<style>`, `<script>`, `<noscript>`, `<template>`, `<head>` and any element with
    `hidden` or an inline `display:none` or `visibility:hidden` are dropped. The structure is kept only when its cells'
    text, joined, equals the `text/plain` flavour with whitespace normalised; otherwise the `text/plain` flavour alone is
    used, so no text the person did not see on the page arrives;
  - **From:** a file in this room (▾), a web address, or nothing ("typed by Ana");
  - **🔒** for the person's own mark (a typed or pasted quote's mark is theirs, §5.14);
  - then the same bar and target as §5.9.7.
  - It is also the path for a document open in Word or Excel on the researcher's own machine and never uploaded.
- **Open the source.** A quote from the web carries its address to the target pages (in `page:take`, sealed at rest)
  **only when the pusher holds `stage.web`**, since it is a web page offered on the Board's devices. The Board's card
  then offers **Open the source**, which opens it in a new tab with a text directive built from the quote's first and
  last words, when the address has no fragment of its own. Without `stage.web`, the source line names the host only and
  carries no link.
- **Screen capture** of what the researcher sees (`getDisplayMedia`) is left for later (§12): it needs HTTPS, a prompt
  every time, and on iOS Safari 27.

### 4-§5.9.10 Targets: the Board, one person On stage, the presenter's Stagewatch screen

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§5.9.1 and §5.9.10: May send to people On stage).

- **The Board** (§5.2 `to: 'board'`): everyone seated On stage in the Main room, presenters with a page included. From
  0.6.0 that is invited guests, Board accounts and guests the admin seated there (§5.9.2.1). The default target. Board
  members and presenters share one seat (design question 3 keeps the design's default, the owner's "Defaults" of
  2026-10-27), so a quote meant for the speaker reaches every board member, and the reverse; One person On stage
  reaches one of them.
- **One person On stage** (§5.2 `to: {uid}`): the To list names each person seated On stage. `canShow` reaches no one
  else. Others in the hall (observers, researchers, the operator) are `canPush`'s targets, as §5.2 has them; an observer
  is shown pictures and quotes, never a document (§5.9.3).
- **A presenter who reads only Stagewatch's speaker screen** gets **one line of plain text**, and nothing else. The
  bar's **＋ the speaker's screen** adds it. It is shown only when the hall has a Stagewatch and the pusher holds
  `stage.send`, and it is **off on every push** until ticked:
  - Its words say where it shows: "＋ Also on the speaker's screen — every Stagewatch output, NDI and its viewer page
    show it" (Stagewatch's message rides the public frame, `src/Timer.Core/SnapshotJson.cs:66` at `855e8b6`).
  - It is disabled until there is something to send: the line is `stagelines.flatten(content)` (unit 29), a snippet's
    text in one line ("Revenue Q3: £4.2m", "Q3: Revenue £4.2m · Costs £3.9m", with the marked labels) or, for a `doc` or
    `image`, the researcher's note. Never a file name, address or page unless typed.
  - **The line is the push's own words, built by the server.** `stage:send` and `stage:propose` take `text` from the
    client today (`server.js:1025`, `:1062`). With `withTake`, the server builds the line itself from the stored take
    (`stagelines.flatten` over its content, or its `note`) and refuses a `text` that differs from it: "The line must be
    the push's own words." Otherwise any line, sent within 60 s of any push, would reach every Stagewatch output with
    no text kept anywhere (below). The bar shows the server's line before it goes; a person who wants other words sends
    a line of their own without `withTake`, which the room's record quotes as today.
  - **Through the operator or at once, chosen per send** (owner answer 16): ticked, ＋ shows two choices,
    **📝 Ask the operator** (`stage:propose`) and **🖥 Send now** (`stage:send`), each offered when its path is open:
    `canPropose` (`link.desk && link.key && !link.deskRefusal`, `server.js:801`, `:1051`) and `canSend`
    (`server.js:800`, `:1051`). A choice whose path is closed is shown disabled with its reason ("The show desk is not
    connected" / "Sending at once needs Stagewatch's key"). The choice is preset to the person's last one on this device
    (`localStorage`, in try/catch), and the first time to Ask the operator when the desk can take it. Under 🖥 the words
    say what it does: "Replaces what the speaker's screen shows now, the operator's message included, and cancels its
    waiting acknowledgement" (Stagewatch's `SetMessage`, `src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:703-722` at
    `855e8b6`, the cancel at `:707`), which the researcher cannot otherwise see. No new key goes on the wire: the page
    calls the verb of the chosen path.
  - The bar counts characters: 500 sent now, about 377 through the desk (`lineFor`), "reads at a glance up to about 60"
    (an estimate from Stagewatch's layout, not measured).
  - **A confidential item** (§5.14) may go, by either path as the sender chooses (owner confirmation of answer 16: "if
    the speaker screen is part of the room, yes it can"). One rule, held on the server, in this order:
    1. **The item is in use in the hall's Main room**, whose stage the speaker's screen is (a Board take makes it so,
       with its confirm). A person take to someone seated in Legal makes Legal in use, not Main, so its line is refused:
       "This is confidential to Legal: show it in the Main room first." The owner kept this reading (S7,
       "Defaults").
    2. **The hall has a Stagewatch of its own.** `linkFor` falls back to the shared default link
       (`linkFor = (code) => hallLinks.get(code) || stageLink`, `server.js:1921`), so halls without their own link share
       one Stagewatch, and `linkFor(room.hall)` can be another hall's speaker's screen. A confidential line goes only when
       `hallLinks.has(hall)`, or when `roomsUsing(link)` (`:1923`) lists no room of another hall; otherwise: "This hall
       shares its Stagewatch with another hall: a confidential line is not sent there." ＋ is then disabled with those
       words.
    3. **The link is encrypted** (an `https:` base, its certificate pinned, `lib/tls.js`). Today's line rides in the
       request's path (`POST /api/message/<text>/…`, `lib/nodes.js:705`) and a proposal in its body, both in clear over
       `http:`. Otherwise: "This hall's Stagewatch link is not encrypted: a confidential line is not sent."
  - **Its words say what Stagewatch does with it**, read at `855e8b6`: it shows it on every output; it publishes it in
    its public frame (`SnapshotJson.cs:66`), which anyone on the venue network may read without the PIN ("reading the
    public frame doesn't", `docs/NODES.md:105`; the viewing code is optional, `docs/FEATURES.md:177`); it fires its
    message trigger to its integrations (`FireTrigger(TriggerEvent.Message, "speaker", text)`, `MainViewModel.cs:711`);
    and it keeps the text in its settings on disk (`_store.Update(… MessageState.Text = text)`, `:712-717`, which
    schedules a save, `src/Timer.Core/SettingsStore.cs:69-72`), and in its journal when no acknowledgement is asked
    (`:710`; AGMessage asks one). The ＋ then reads "🔒 Confidential — every output of this hall's Stagewatch shows it
    (the speaker's screens, NDI, its viewer page); anyone on the venue network can read it from Stagewatch, which also
    keeps it and passes it to its triggers." The owner approved the line for the people at the speaker's screen, and
    kept this reading of the rest (S6, "Defaults"): either path, an encrypted link and these words, until Stagewatch
    2.20 (§5.9.12).
  - **The room's record carries no quote.** The line goes with `withTake: <seq>`, a take this person pushed in the last
    60 s. Then the system line reads "Ana sent a line (17 characters) to the speaker's screen with a push" (or "asked the
    operator for a line (17 characters) …"), with no text (today it quotes 120 characters, `server.js:1035`, `:1085`,
    and observers and the transcript read it, `:1841`). The message's `proposal` keeps `lineMac` (`guard.mac` of the
    line) instead of `line`, and `notOurs` (`server.js:2107`) compares the MAC of the desk's line with it after a
    restart, so the follow still knows its own proposal. The words are kept where the record of what was shown is: the
    stage record's entry for the take gains `line` (§5.13), which the admin's transcript shows and the AI is given unless
    the item is confidential.
  - **While a confidential line is on Stagewatch's frame, AGMessage passes none of it on** (§5.14).
  - Its receipt and the speaker's acknowledgement follow today's record (`server.js:1028-1037`, `renderStageLine`), and
    the step words show them (§5.9.7).
- **What Stagewatch would need to show more** is §5.9.12. AGMessage 0.6.0 sends it nothing new but this line, through
  today's two paths.

### 4-§5.9.11 The take on the target's page

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§5.9.11: the layer's bar draws the person's secondary object in the simple view).

§5.3 (the numbered take, `page:report`, visible or it did not happen) and §5.4 (Back to chat, Minimise, Escape
minimises) apply, per layer (§5.9.1). What each new kind reports:

| Kind | `shown` when | `failed` words |
|---|---|---|
| `doc` | its place (page, slide, sheet, block) has drawn and the page is visible; on a device that cannot open documents, its `standin` has drawn, with "as a picture: this device cannot page through the document" (§5.15.2) | "the file could not be read" / "this device could not draw the page" / "the file took too long to read" / "this device cannot open documents — ask for a picture" (no `standin`) |
| `image` | `onload` and `decode()` have resolved | "the picture did not load" / "too big for this device" |
| `snippet` | laid out and fitted, on the next frame, while visible; a card longer than the screen reports `shown` with "longer than the screen: it scrolls" | "this page could not load the stage view — reload" (the module did not load) |

- **Ready before the first take.** A Board page imports `pagelayer.mjs` and `docview.mjs` with `import()` 2 s after
  its join answer is drawn (`script-src 'self'`), and the heavy readers after its first `doc` take, so the first quote
  on venue Wi-Fi is not held up by an import. Not `<link rel="modulepreload">`, which Safari has only from 17, nor
  `requestIdleCallback`, which Safari lacks (§5.15.2): a timer and `import()` work on every row of the device matrix.
  `docview.mjs` imports pdf.js with `import()` inside `try`, as `loadPdfJs` does today (`app.js:1041-1047`), never
  statically, so a device that cannot parse pdf.js loses documents only.
- **A second check in the page.** `pagelayer` and `docview` refuse a take whose `url` is not `/uploads/<UPLOAD_NAME>` of
  a `STAGE_TYPES` extension, as §5.6 checks a web address again in the page. It reports `failed`.
- **Drawn from memory** (§4.6.6): every file a take names is fetched `no-store`; pictures are drawn through object URLs
  revoked when the take closes; a `doc`'s pdf.js document is destroyed when it closes.
- **The no-save measures** of §4.6.6 (AGMessage's menu, Shift+right-click included; `draggable="false"`;
  `-webkit-touch-callout: none`; print hidden) apply to the take layer on every seat it is drawn on.
- **Drawn** by `pagelayer.mjs` (§5.7) with `textContent` only:
  - on a dark ground by default; the hall's countdown chip stays in the layer's bar, beside ✕ Back to chat and
    ▭ Minimise;
  - a snippet as `<blockquote>`, `<ol>` / `<ul>` or `<table>`; `white-space: pre-wrap`; `dir="auto"` on each paragraph
    and cell; the largest type that fits, in at most 12 steps between 28 px (20 px under 600 px wide,
    a phone) and 12 vw; numeric-looking cells
    right-aligned by a pattern on the strings; the `focus` cell outlined and bold, never colour alone; a cut table ends
    in "… 40 more rows not shown"; a table wider than the screen scrolls sideways inside its card, its label row
    and column kept in view;
  - a source line under it: "Quoted by Ana · Board pack.pdf, p. 12" / "Quoted by Ana · Minutes.docx, ≈ p. 3" / "Quoted
    by Ana from her copy of Board pack.pdf" / "Quoted by Ana · vote.example.com · Open the source" (with `stage.web`) /
    "Typed by Ana"; a side room's file adds "(Legal)"; a confidential item begins "🔒 Confidential ·";
  - an `image` fitted, with its line "Ana's picture of Board pack.pdf, p. 12";
  - a `doc` through `docview.mjs` (the Board's drawing, chosen by the page's seat, §5.10.1), at its place; **⬇ Download
    only when `download` is true** and this seat may download (§4.6.6), never otherwise.
  - **`image` and `doc` take zoom:** pinch, double-tap and + / − with pan; a `doc` also has its page box. The controls are
    48 px in the simple view. The bar suggests "What I see" when a whole page would draw its text under about 16 px on
    the target (an A4 page on a 10-inch tablet draws body text near 7 pt).
- **The cards** (§5.4), in the side bar: "📄 Board pack.pdf · p. 12", "🖼 Ana's picture · p. 12", "❝ Revenue Q3 £4.2m"
  (the first 40 characters), "🔒" first when confidential, each with **Show again · Remove**, and ⬇ where the take was
  shown with Download.
- **The status marks** of §5.3 are unchanged; their words take the console voice of §5.9.3.

### 4-§5.9.12 A request to Stagewatch for 2.20 (owner answer 17; to hand over)

> **From AGMessage 0.6.0, for Stagewatch 2.20: what a messenger node needs on the speaker's screens.**
>
> **Today** (read at `855e8b6`). A node can put one plain-text line under the
> countdown, coloured by urgency, with "Got it" on a Production licence, read back by its receipt and `messageAck`. It
> has no verb for a picture or a table, and its line has the operator's slot: it replaces whatever the speaker's screen
> shows and cancels that message's waiting acknowledgement (`SetMessage`,
> `src/Timer.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:703-722`, the cancel at `:707`). It is drawn on every output and published
> in the public frame (`src/Timer.Core/SnapshotJson.cs:66`), which reading needs no PIN (`docs/NODES.md:105`); it fires
> the message trigger (`MainViewModel.cs:711`) and is kept in the saved settings (`:712-717`,
> `src/Timer.Core/SettingsStore.cs:69-72`). `{NEXT}`, `{TIME}` and the rest in its text are rewritten
> (`Placeholders.Render`, `src/Timer.Core/CueLadder.cs:200-217`), and a long line shrinks nothing but the whole screen
> (`MessageText` at a fixed `FontSize="100"`, `src/Timer.Output/OutputWindow.xaml:82-88`).
>
> **Asked** (the owner's two asks, answer 17), in order of need:
>
> 1. **Messages a node owns.** A node's message has a slot of its own: it neither replaces the operator's message nor
>    cancels its acknowledgement; a node clears only what it sent; the operator sees every node's message and can clear
>    any. Its receipt names the node's message, so the node can say "on the speaker's screen" truthfully.
> 2. **A card on the speaker's screens only.** A picture (PNG, JPEG or WebP, known by its SHA-256, at most 2,048 px on
>    its long edge) or a short table (at most 25 × 10 cells of plain text, with a header row and a focus cell), drawn on
>    the speaker's confidence screens and role screens Stagewatch chooses, **never on NDI, the audience output or the
>    public viewer frame**, with a "Got it" acknowledgement and a clear, as messages have. AGMessage's hello already
>    lists the cap `documents` (`app/lib/nodes.js:109`, AGMessage's `docs/NODES.md:8`), which nothing in Stagewatch's
>    `src/` reads at `855e8b6`. How the bytes travel is Stagewatch's to choose; AGMessage can serve a picture by its
>    hash to a node key.
>
> **Also suggested by AGMessage, not yet put to the owner** (each marked so before hand-over; none is assumed):
>
> 3. **Where a message shows.** Per message, the outputs it reaches: speaker screens only, or every output. AGMessage
>    sends confidential lines only with the sender told that every output shows them; with this, it could offer
>    "speaker screens only".
> 4. **A literal flag**, so a node's text is never read for `{…}` tokens. Until then AGMessage turns `{` and `}` into
>    `(` and `)`.
> 5. **Wrapping and fitting** of a long message on the output window, instead of a fixed size.
> 6. **The message in the request's body**, not its path (`POST /api/message/<text>/…` today, which lands in any log
>    of request lines).
> 7. **A confidential node message**: kept out of the public frame and of the saved settings and the journal, and not
>    fired to triggers; shown on the speaker's screens and given to the operator's frame only.
>
> **Not asked now:** a way to frame an AGMessage page in a Stagewatch window.
>
> **How AGMessage would prove it:** a receipt per card and per node message; the speaker's acknowledgement per item; a
> test that the public frame and NDI carry neither; a test that a node's message leaves the operator's and its
> acknowledgement in place.

AGMessage 0.6.0 assumes none of this: it sends one line through today's two paths (§5.9.10). Items 3 to 7 are marked
"not yet put to the owner" until the owner says otherwise. Revision 2 cited a "Show Bus §12" for window grants, a
Stagewatch `docs/WHATS_NEXT.md:165-167` and Show Bus `documents` and `media` caps at `docs/SHOWBUS.md:1114-1117`; none
of them exists on disk (Stagewatch's `WHATS_NEXT.md` is 103 lines at `855e8b6`, and every `SHOWBUS.md`, AGMessage's 228
lines, Stagewatch's 210 and Patterns' 212, ends at §11), so the request no longer cites them.

## 4-§5.10 Libraries, notices, and reading files safely

### 4-§5.10.1 What runs where

- **In the page, never on the server.** Documents are parsed only by the browser of the person looking: the researcher's
  Preview, and the target's page for a `doc` take. Snippets and pictures need no parser on the Board's device. The server
  reads only bounded metadata at upload, or at a file's first take (§5.10.3), and a transfer-only file's first bytes.
- **New files** (no build step):
  - `public/zipcore.js`: a classic script, also loadable by `require`: the central-directory reader and its bounds
    (entries, sizes, ratios, overlap, ZIP64 records, encryption, `vbaProject.bin`), pure over bytes. The server's
    `lib/zipcheck.js` requires it and reads the file's tail with `fs.promises`; the worker loads it with
    `importScripts`. One check, two callers, so the verdicts cannot drift; a parity test feeds every fixture through both
    callers' byte readers.
  - `public/wordpages.js`: a classic script, also loadable by `require`, pure over strings: Word's page breaks from
    `word/document.xml`, `word/styles.xml` and `docProps/app.xml` by a tag scanner (no DOM, so it runs in the worker and
    under `node --test`), and their mapping onto the reader's blocks (§5.10.4).
  - `public/docworker.js`: a classic worker. `importScripts` of `zipcore.js`, `wordpages.js`, SheetJS and mammoth. It
    runs the zip check and inflates parts through `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` and a counting stream that aborts
    at the bound; scans every XML part for `<!DOCTYPE` and `<!ENTITY` before any parser sees it, SheetJS's, mammoth's
    and `wordpages.js`'s included; reads spreadsheets; converts DOCX with mammoth and reads its page breaks; and hands
    PPTX parts back as XML strings. Each task runs under `readInWorker(source, task, ms)`'s wall clock, after which the
    worker is terminated.
    - **mammoth is given a copy of the file without its hidden runs.** Its browser build opens only
      `convertToHtml({arrayBuffer})` (`browser/unzip.js`, which the 1.13.0 package's `browser` field puts in place of
      `lib/unzip.js`, whose `options.file` the bundle does not have), so the parts cannot be handed to it one by one.
      `zipcore.js` gains `repack(bytes, replaced)`, pure over bytes: every entry's local header and compressed bytes are
      copied as they are, the replaced entries are written stored (method 0) with their CRC-32, and a new central
      directory follows, all inside the zip check's bounds. The worker replaces `word/document.xml`,
      `word/footnotes.xml` and `word/endnotes.xml` with the same parts, every hidden run removed (§5.10.2), and hands
      mammoth the repacked copy, so mammoth never sees hidden text. Unit 23's tests feed hidden fixtures through it and
      assert the text is absent from the drawing, the picks and `text()`.
    - **Pictures leave the worker as bytes.** mammoth's `convertImage` in the worker returns a placeholder `src`
      (`agm-img:<n>`) and hands the picture's bytes back as a transferred `ArrayBuffer`; the page checks its size
      (§5.10.3), makes the object URL itself and revokes it with the document. A `blob:` URL made inside the worker
      belongs to the worker's environment, and when it lapses once the worker is terminated is not defined (File API
      §8.3.3, "Lifetime of blob URLs", https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/, defines the clean-up for a document only, with
      the editor's note "This needs a similar hook when a worker is unloaded."), so the page could not rely on drawing
      it after the 15 s `terminate()`, nor count and revoke it, and the smoke could not see it.
  - `public/docmodel.mjs`: pure readers into one block model, `{kind: 'p'|'h'|'li'|'quote'|'code'|'table'|'img', text,
    level?, list?, rows?, src?, alt?, at, page?, pageApprox?, hidden?}`: CSV, Markdown blocks, text decoding (BOM
    sniffed; `TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true})`, else windows-1252), the occupancy grid, the PPTX outline over the
    worker's XML strings (`DOMParser`, which workers lack, so on the page), and **`parseInert(html) → {blocks}`**, the
    one place HTML is parsed (§5.10.3). The readers that need no `DOMParser` run under `node --test`.
  - `public/docview.mjs`: the drawing, the page box, zoom and find, the text layer, the grid, the pick, and
    `open(box, source, {at, seat}) → {place(), goto(at), visible(), pick(unit), text(), destroy()}`. `seat` is the page's
    own seat (`research`, `board` or `observer`; the admin's support view reads as `research`), never the caller's
    choice: only `research` draws hidden rows and columns dimmed and makes the text selectable for picks; every other
    seat gets the Board's drawing, for a take, a Look or an Earlier entry alike. `source` is `{url}` (fetched
    `no-store`, §4.6.6) or `{file}` (a local `File`). `text()` is the AI's document text, capped as
    today (80 pages, 60,000 characters, `app.js:1053-1062`), hidden parts left out, a DOCX's pages marked "— p. 12 —"
    (or "— ≈ p. 12 —") so a draft can cite them, run only on a research seat, and never for a confidential file
    (§5.14).
  - `lib/zipcheck.js` and `lib/imagesize.js` (§5.10.3).
- **`img` blocks:** a picture in a DOCX (its bytes handed back by the worker, above, not base64) or a PPTX is drawn,
  is not pickable as text, and is offered as a picture when it is png, jpg, gif or webp. Its object URL, made by the
  page, is revoked with the document (§4.6.6). Inline formatting (bold, italic, links) is dropped from the drawing, and
  an XLSX loses `sheet_to_html`'s styling: unit 23 and the CHANGELOG say so.
- **`app.js` loses** `buildDocPreview` and its renderers (`app.js:931-1148`), `loadPdfJs` (`:1042`, which the smoke's
  `test/browser-smoke.js:252` calls and which moves to `docview.mjs`), and with them two `sanitizeHtml → innerHTML`
  sinks (`:978`, `:1001`). `sanitizeHtml` (`:914-929`) goes once no caller is left.

### 4-§5.10.2 The libraries

| Library | Version | Licence | Where it runs | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| pdf.js | **4.10.38, its legacy build** | Apache-2.0 | the page and the screen page; its own worker | The vendored modern build calls `Promise.withResolvers` without a polyfill (30 calls in `vendor/pdf.min.mjs`, 11 in the worker; only `Promise.try` is polyfilled), which needs Safari and iOS 17.4, Chrome 119 or Firefox 121 (MDN's compatibility data, `javascript/builtins/Promise.json`, https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data), so older iPads fail on today's panel and screens alike. The same version's legacy build is vendored instead (unit V; answer 22 keeps older iPads among the Board's devices), compiled for Chrome 103, Firefox ESR and Safari 16.4, the document floor of §5.15.2: its `legacy/build/pdf.min.mjs` and `pdf.worker.min.mjs` each define it (`{target:"Promise",stat:!0},{withResolvers:function withResolvers(){…}}`, read in the 4.10.38 package in the scratch folder), and unit V's test holds it. `isEvalSupported: false` and `enableXfa: false` (as today, `app.js:1052`); scripting off; no annotation layer, so no live link; `maxImageSize: 16777216` (its default is no limit); lazy `getPage` past the first pages instead of every page up front (`app.js:1092`; measured on a 300-page pack before and after, on the bench); **one worker for the page's life and `destroy()` on the document it leaves**, as `display.js:76-104` does (`app.js` never destroys one today); **a deadline per document** (20 s to the first page drawn): on expiry the loading task and the shared `PDFWorker` are destroyed, a new worker is made, and the take reports `failed`. The worker's own response carries `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (§5.10.5). The text layer's `.textLayer` rules are copied from 4.10.38's `web/pdf_viewer.css` with its Apache notice |
| SheetJS Community Edition | 0.20.3, kept | Apache-2.0 | `docworker.js` | vendored from `cdn.sheetjs.com` only (npm's `xlsx` is frozen at 0.18.5, before CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363 were fixed); `XLSX.read(ab, {type: 'array', dense: true, sheetRows: N, cellFormula: false, cellHTML: false, bookVBA: false})`; `sheet_to_json(ws, {header: 1, raw: false, defval: ''})`, strings only; `!merges`, hidden rows, columns and sheets passed as data, a sheet's `Hidden` of 1 or 2 ("very hidden") read alike as hidden. `sheet_to_html` is never called again |
| mammoth | **1.11.0 → 1.13.0** | BSD-2-Clause | `docworker.js` | 1.12.2 closes a prototype pollution that could set `externalFileAccess`; 1.12.3 a backtracking denial of service from crafted documents, and its NEWS recommends a separate thread with a timeout. **It draws hidden text**: nothing in its `lib/` reads `w:vanish` or `w:specVanish` (grep over the 1.13.0 package), so a hidden run comes out as ordinary text. Tracked deletions and moves are left out (`w:del` and `w:moveFrom` in its body reader's ignore list, `lib/docx/body-reader.js:727-732`), and comments are dropped unless a style map names them. So `docworker.js` removes, from the parts it repacks for mammoth (§5.10.1), every `w:r` whose run properties carry `w:vanish` or `w:specVanish` (not `w:val="0"` or `"false"`): set directly, through its `w:rStyle`, or through its paragraph's `w:pStyle` run properties, each style followed through `w:basedOn` at most 10 deep, and `w:docDefaults`. A hidden mark it cannot resolve (a chain past 10, a style it cannot find) fails closed: the Board's drawing refuses the file with "This Word file has hidden text AGMessage could not leave out — show a picture or a quote.", and the researcher's Preview says the same. The vendored bundle's `DOMParser` is xmldom's (pure JavaScript), and its `document.createElement` calls sit only in feature-detected promise schedulers, so it very likely runs in a worker; unit 23's first test settles it. If it does not, the Board's pages never parse a DOCX: a `doc` take of one is refused with "Show a picture or a quote; Word files reach the Board as downloads", and the researcher's Preview runs it on the page behind the zip check. `convertImage` writes `blob:` URLs. Its HTML goes to `parseInert`, never assigned. It drops `w:lastRenderedPageBreak` (its body reader's ignore list, `"w:lastRenderedPageBreak":!0` in `vendor/mammoth.browser.min.js`) and draws a page break (`w:br w:type="page"`) as nothing unless a style map names it, so page numbers come from `wordpages.js` (§5.10.4), not from mammoth |
| In-house | — | the project's | `zipcore.js`, `wordpages.js`, `docworker.js`, `docmodel.mjs`, `lib/zipcheck.js`, `lib/imagesize.js`, `lib/cfbcheck.js` | the zip reader, RFC 4180 CSV (quotes, CRLF, a sniffed `,` `;` or tab, BOM), the Markdown block parser (ATX headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, fences, pipe tables; HTML comments and hidden raw HTML dropped), the PPTX outline (`p:sldIdLst` order, `show="0"` hidden, `p:sp` titles and `a:p` bullets by `lvl`, `a:tbl` tables, pictures through the slide's rels, `p:grpSp` recursed, a shape, picture, frame or group whose `p:cNvPr` carries `hidden="1"` skipped with all it holds, `ppt/notesSlides` never read), Word's page breaks and hidden runs, the image header reader, the compound-file directory reader, the block model and the grid |

- **pdf.js 6 is left for later** (§12): two majors, and pdf.js's FAQ lists its current legacy build for Chrome 125,
  Firefox ESR and Safari 18 ("Which browsers/environments are supported?",
  https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/Frequently-Asked-Questions#faq-support), which would leave every iPad before
  iPadOS 18, the matrix's D2 among them (§5.15), without documents.
- **JPEG 2000 images in today's PDFs.** The vendored 4.10.38 worker compiles an embedded OpenJPEG with
  `new WebAssembly.Module` and has no JavaScript fallback for it; JBIG2 is decoded in JavaScript (`class Jbig2Image` in
  `vendor/pdf.worker.min.mjs`) and is not affected. The worker's response carries the page CSP today (`script-src
  'self'`, no `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, `lib/guard.js:178-191`), so JPEG 2000 images are probably left undrawn today, on the
  panel and on screens (inferred from the code). §5.10.5 gives that one response `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` (owner answer 15);
  unit 23's fixture records the fact before and after.
- **Notices.** No vendored library's licence ships today: there is no `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` file, the mammoth bundle
  carries no licence text, and the CycloneDX SBOM is npm only (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:148`). Unit V adds, after
  PlayMap's pattern:
  - `app/public/vendor/VENDOR.json`: per file, its package, version, build, licence, source URL and SHA-256;
  - `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` and `licenses/<id>/` at the root, shipped by `tools/build-portable.ps1`;
  - the manifest's components appended to the SBOM in CI;
  - `test/vendor.test.js`, which fails on a vendor file not in the manifest, a hash that differs, or an entry with no
    licence or notice. It would have caught the stray 3.11.174 worker.

### 4-§5.10.3 Refused, and the bounds

**Refused or never done:**

- **Macros:** `.docm`, `.xlsm`, `.pptm` are outside the allow-list (`lib/guard.js:204-217`). A `.docx`, `.xlsx` or
  `.pptx` that carries a `vbaProject.bin` part is refused at upload, at no extra cost to the zip check: "That file
  carries macros. Save it without them, or as a PDF." Legacy `.xls` may carry VBA; SheetJS never parses it
  (`bookVBA: false`). A downloaded `.xls` opened in Excel is a transfer-side risk; whether Windows marks a file from a
  LAN address for Office's macro block is not verified (§12). A password-protected Office file is never opened, so its
  macros are the opener's to block (§4.6.7).
- **Formulas are never computed.** The cached value the authoring application saved is shown; it can be stale. A formula
  with no cached value is marked, never shown as a blank.
- **External references** (linked workbooks, `attachedTemplate`, `r:link` images) are never fetched; their cached values
  show. **Hyperlinks** are never live on stage, in a quote or in a reader.
- **XML with a DTD:** any part containing `<!DOCTYPE` or `<!ENTITY` is refused before any parser sees it, the in-house
  readers', mammoth's xmldom and SheetJS's alike (the worker's scan, §5.10.1). OOXML parts never need one.
- **HTML is parsed in one place.** `parseInert(html)` in `docmodel.mjs` is the only `template.innerHTML` in the new
  modules, with a disable comment saying why; it walks the inert template into plain objects and strings and returns no
  DOM node. Nothing parsed is ever adopted into the live page, where a `<meta http-equiv=refresh>` would navigate a
  Board tablet and a `<style>` would apply (`style-src 'unsafe-inline'`). The DOCX walk and the Quote tab both call it.
- **Hidden things are never shown on the Board's pages** (owner answer 13: "Hidden things never shown."), whole files
  included. On every seat but `research`, `open(…, {seat})` never draws hidden sheets (very hidden included), rows or
  columns, only "3 hidden rows not shown"; never reads slides' notes; never draws a hidden slide or a hidden shape;
  never draws a Markdown comment or hidden raw HTML; and Word's hidden text never reaches the drawing on any seat,
  since it is removed before mammoth reads the file (§5.10.2). The researcher's own Preview draws hidden rows and
  columns dimmed and marked so they know what the file holds, and never lets them be picked (S15).
- **A file with hidden parts is never shown with Download ticked.** A document take hands over the whole file, so a
  budget workbook's hidden "Salaries" sheet would be one Unhide away on every tablet that downloads it. When the
  researcher's reader finds hidden sheets, rows, columns, slides or shapes, or Word's hidden text, the bar's ☐ Let them
  download it is disabled with "This file has hidden parts: Download would hand them over. Share a copy without them for
  download instead." The server never parses the file, so this is the page's guard; it is said so in SECURITY.md.
- SVG stays refused; embedded OLE objects and media are never drawn; pdf.js scripting and XFA stay off.

**Bounds** (bounds, not governors: each is a ceiling on one input, refused with words):

| Where | Bound | Words |
|---|---|---|
| Server, at upload, a zip-magic type the stage can show (`lib/zipcheck.js` over `zipcore.js`: reads the End of Central Directory, the ZIP64 records and the central directory with `fs.promises`, inflates nothing) | at most 2,000 entries; declared total ≤ 200 MB, any entry ≤ 100 MB, each entry's ratio ≤ 200:1, ZIP64 sizes held to the same bounds; no encrypted entry; no two entries whose ranges overlap (Fifield's construction); `[Content_Types].xml` present; no `vbaProject.bin`; a central directory over 1 MB refused unread | "That file is packed in a way AGMessage will not open. Share it as a PDF." The numbers are set at four times the largest real board-pack files measured in unit 22 (the owner's own, or Office's samples), and written in the test |
| Server, at upload, every image (`lib/imagesize.js`, new: PNG IHDR, GIF's screen, WebP's VP8, VP8L and VP8X, and JPEG by a marker walk to SOF0-15 with `fs.promises.read` at segment offsets, at most 64 segments or 1 MB read) | ≤ 100 MP; a size that cannot be read is refused | "That image is too large to show." / "That image cannot be read." |
| Server, `sourceOk`, every `image` take and every image `doc` take (the same reader, cached by name; a 0.5.1 message's image included) | ≤ 40 MP, provisional, until the decode limit of the device matrix's oldest rows (D1, D2, §5.15) is measured in unit 22's bench and written in the test | "Too large for the Board's devices — send a region." |
| Server, `sourceOk`, a zip-type `doc` take with no check on record (a 0.5.1 file) | the upload's archive check, cached by name | as at upload |
| The page, before any canvas | `naturalWidth × naturalHeight` within the same bound | "too big for this device" |
| `docworker.js` | 15 s wall clock, then `terminate()` | "This file took too long to read, so it is not shown." (on a backstage seat: "⬇ Download opens it in its own application.") |
| pdf.js, per document | 20 s to the first page drawn, then a new worker | "the file took too long to read" |
| A spreadsheet | `sheetRows` 5,000 per sheet | "Showing the first 5,000 rows." |
| A text file | 20,000 lines drawn | "Showing the first 20,000 lines." |
| Word's page scan (`wordpages.js`) | inside the worker's 15 s; `w:basedOn` chains followed at most 10 deep | pages marked approximate ("≈") when the scan stops short |
| A rendered page | 2,048 px long edge, ≤ 4,096 a side, ≤ 5,242,880 pixels (pdf.js's own mobile cap, §5.9.8) | — |
| An upload | 25 MB, every type (`server.js:556`) | "Files can be up to 25 MB." |

- Memory is not contained by a worker (it shares the tab's renderer); the zip check and the pixel bounds are what bound
  it.
- The 5,000-row and 20,000-line numbers are the readers' first draw, measured on the rig's laptop and the device
  matrix's D2 and D4 in unit 23 before they are fixed; "no measurement this round" until then.
- A refused upload writes `upload.refused` (§5.11).

### 4-§5.10.4 Word page numbers (owner answer 14)

The owner's answer: "Page numbers would be preferable to have as well." A browser has no Word layout engine, and none is
vendored; the pages come from what Word itself wrote into the file.

**What the file holds:**

- **`w:lastRenderedPageBreak`**: "this position delimited the end of a page when this document was last saved by an
  application which paginates its content" (ISO/IEC 29500-1 §17.3.3.13, quoted at
  https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.lastrenderedpagebreak). Word writes
  one where it last broke a page, and a hard page break gives rise to one in the right position (python-docx's
  `Run.contains_page_break`, https://python-docx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/text.html). It moves only when Word saves
  again, depends on printer, page size and margins
  (https://python-docx.readthedocs.io/en/latest/_modules/docx/text/pagebreak.html), is never written by tools without a
  layout engine (python-docx says so of itself, the same page), and is not always where the page broke ("you cannot rely
  on the position of the w:lastRenderedPageBreak", Eric White of Open-XML-PowerTools,
  https://www.ericwhite.com/blog/?p=4043); one report finds them at column breaks too
  (https://lightrun.com/answers/mwilliamson-python-mammoth-wlastrenderedpagebreak-).
- **Explicit breaks**: `w:br w:type="page"`; `w:pageBreakBefore` on a paragraph or inherited through its style
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.pagebreakbefore); and a section
  break whose `w:type` is `nextPage` (the default when absent), `oddPage` or `evenPage`, carried in the `w:sectPr` that
  ends the section (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.wordprocessing.sectiontype).
- **`docProps/app.xml` `<Pages>`**: "the total number of pages of a document if applicable"
  (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/documentformat.openxml.extendedproperties.pages).

**How `wordpages.js` reads them** (pure, over the strings the worker already inflates and scans for a DTD):

1. From `word/styles.xml`: the paragraph styles whose `w:pPr` carries `w:pageBreakBefore` (not `w:val="0"` or
   `"false"`), following `w:basedOn` at most 10 deep.
2. A first scan of `word/document.xml` collects the section types in order (each `w:sectPr`'s `w:type`, `nextPage` when
   absent). A second scan walks the body's paragraphs at any depth (`w:p`, inside `w:tbl` cells too) in order, keeping
   for each its text (`w:t`, with `w:tab` and `w:br` as spaces; `w:delText`, `w:instrText` and the hidden runs that
   `docworker.js` removes left out, as mammoth never sees them) and two counts at its start: Word's rendered breaks so
   far, and explicit breaks so far.
3. **The basis:**
   - **`word`** when the file has at least one `w:lastRenderedPageBreak`: a paragraph's page is 1 + the rendered breaks
     before it, and a paragraph holding one spans two pages. Explicit breaks are not added, since Word's own carry them.
     If `<Pages>` is present and differs from rendered breaks + 1, the basis is **`word-stale`**.
   - **`breaks`** otherwise: 1 + the explicit breaks before it. Pages that only filled up are not counted, so these are
     lower bounds. An odd or even page section break counts one.
4. **Mapped onto mammoth's blocks** by text, in order: each block's normalised text (whitespace collapsed, trimmed) is
   matched with the next paragraph of the scan whose normalised text equals it, or begins with its first 40 characters,
   looking at most 50 paragraphs ahead; empty paragraphs are skipped, as mammoth skips them by default
   (`ignoreEmptyParagraphs`, https://github.com/mwilliamson/mammoth.js/blob/master/README.md). A block with no match
   takes the page of the block before it and is marked approximate.
5. **Printed numbers:** the page is the document's physical page, counted from 1, as a PDF's page box counts. Where a
   section restarts numbering or uses another format (`w:pgNumType` with `w:start` or `w:fmt`), the page box adds "the
   printed page numbers differ here".

**What is said where:**

| Basis | Page box (Preview and Board) | Source line on the Board, the console, the transcript | Audit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `word`, block matched | "p. 12 of 30" | "Minutes.docx, p. 12" | `at p. 12` |
| `word-stale`, `breaks`, or a block not matched | "≈ p. 12 of ≈ 30", and its title "Word's last saved layout is missing or out of date: pages are approximate" | "Minutes.docx, ≈ p. 12" | `at ≈ p. 12` |

- **How the Board is told:** the take carries the pusher's page and `approx` (§5.9.3, §5.9.4); a `doc` take's Board
  reader runs the same scan over the same file and shows the same pages. The server never parses the file, so the page
  is the pusher's claim, as the quote is (§5.9.4).
- **`text()`** marks page starts ("— p. 12 —" or "— ≈ p. 12 —"), so the AI's draft can cite a page as `REPLY_SYSTEM`
  asks (`lib/ai.js:73`).
- **Not done:** laying a Word document out again in the browser; pages for Word files saved by tools that write no
  rendered breaks beyond the explicit ones.
- **Not verified:** how close Word's rendered breaks sit to the real breaks in the owner's own board packs. Unit 23's
  bench compares, for the owner's DOCX files, the page box with Word's own page for ten picked paragraphs each, and the
  result is written in the fixture README.

### 4-§5.10.5 The PDF worker's own CSP (owner answer 15)

- **`CSP_PDF_WORKER`** in `lib/guard.js` is `CSP` (`:178-191`) with `script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'`.
  `pageHeaders` (`:193-201`) sets it only when `req.path` is exactly one of the pdf.js worker files `VENDOR.json` lists
  (unit V; today `/vendor/pdf.worker.min.mjs`), never by prefix. Every page, the screen page and pdf.js's own main
  module keep `CSP`.
- **Why that response:** a worker loaded by URL takes the CSP delivered with its own script, not its page's; only a
  `data:` or `blob:` worker inherits the page's
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API/Using_web_workers#content_security_policy). The hall
  page and the screen page load the worker by URL (`app.js:1045`, `display.js:83`).
- **What it allows:** compiling and running WebAssembly in that worker, not `eval`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/script-src). Supported
  from Chrome 97, Firefox 102 and Safari 16, iOS included (MDN's compatibility data,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/http/headers/Content-Security-Policy.json). A Board device older
  than that still leaves JPEG 2000 images undrawn; the page draws without them.
- pdf.js keeps `isEvalSupported: false` (§5.10.2), so nothing in the worker uses JavaScript `eval`.

## 4-§5.11 Rights, audit rows, stores and lifetimes

> **Amended by** 5-§0 (`brand` leaves the rights table, applied in place).

**Rights** (adds to §2.4 and §2.6):

| Act | Who | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Share for download | `hall.post` and `hall.files` in the room | `mayPost`, `allowed('hall.files')` (`server.js:825-835`), unchanged |
| Look | anyone seated `research` or `board` who reads the room, and the admin | the link, given to those seats only (§4.6.6) |
| Download a transfer | a `research` seat in the room that is not a Viewer account, or the admin | `file:download {messageId}`, `mayDownload` (§4.6.6) |
| Download a take's whole file | a target that is neither seated observer nor a Viewer account, when the take has `download: true` and is not withdrawn | `file:download {seq}` |
| Move a file to another room (`forward`, `room:send`) | `mayDownload`, `mayPost` and `hall.files` where it is; `hall.post` and `hall.files` where it goes | §4.6.3 |
| Show `doc`, `image`, `snippet` | `canShow` (§5.9.2), or `canPush`; for an account, `stage.show` either way | then `sourceOk` (§5.9.5) and §5.14 |
| Take the information down | `canPush` (an account with `stage.show`); `canShow` only over a take `canShow` pushed, with its `ifSeq` | §5.9.1, §5.9.7 |
| Withdraw a take | its pusher, `canPush` holders, the admin | `page:withdraw` (§5.9.7) |
| Show `web` | `canPush` or `canShow`, with `stage.web`; a locked hall's backstage code guest while the hall's setting is on (S4) | §5.6, §5.9.2.2 |
| Let a locked hall's backstage guests show web pages, or stop them | the admin | `admin:guestWeb` (§5.9.2.2) |
| Show `stage`, `clock`, `holding`, `blank`; `chat` of both layers | `canPush(hall)` | §2.6 |
| A line on the speaker's screen | `stage.send` | `allowed('stage.send')`, unchanged |
| Mark a file confidential | when sharing it, whoever shares it; later, a backstage seat with `hall.files` in a room where it is in use, or the admin | `file:mark` (§5.14) |
| Remove the mark | who marked it, or the admin | `file:mark {on: false}` |
| An On stage seat (a code guest) | an On stage invite, a held seat, or the admin's `admin:setRole` | `join` (§5.9.2.1) |
| A new On stage (or Backstage) link | the admin | `admin:newInvite` (§5.9.2.1) |

**Audit** (adds to §2.7; no row carries a file name, a quote's text, a URL path, a guest code or a token):

| Action | When | Target | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| `page.push` | an information push, a take-down or a withdrawal, one row per target | hall | `the Board (6 pages) → a PDF at p. 12` / `Ana Silva → a picture of a PDF page (p. 12)` / `the Board (6 pages) → a quote (a table column, 6 cells) from a spreadsheet in Legal, in their side bar` / `the Board (6 pages) → a confidential Word document at ≈ p. 3, confirmed` / `the Board (6 pages) → the information taken down` / `the Board (6 pages) → a PDF at p. 12, withdrawn` |
| `upload.refused` | the archive, macro or image check refuses an upload | hall | `a docx: 12,000 parts (bound 2,000)` / `a docx with macros` / `a png of 400 MP (bound 100)` |
| `stagewatch.send` | `stage:send` (today unaudited; §2.7 audits `stage:propose` only) | room key | `a line (n characters) on the speaker's screen, sent now` / `…, with a push` / `…, a confidential line` |
| `room.reset` | as §2.7, and | room key | `…, 3 takes ended, the stage record cleared` |
| `room.send` | as §2.7, and | target key | `a confidential file (pdf, 2.1 MB) from Legal (Hall 2) to Main (Hall 2), confirmed` |
| `file.mark` | the mark set or removed | room key | `a pdf in Legal (Hall 2) marked confidential` / `a pdf in Legal (Hall 2): the confidential mark removed` |
| `file.download` | a confidential file's download stream ended (`file:sent`) | room key | `a confidential pdf downloaded in Legal (Hall 2)` |
| `room.invite` | a new On stage or Backstage link | room key | `a new On stage link (the old one no longer admits)` |
| `room.guestWeb` | the hall's setting turned on or off (S4) | hall | `backstage guests may show web pages` / `backstage guests may no longer show web pages (1 shown now stays until taken down)` |
| `room.lock` | as §2.7, and | room key | `roles unlocked, guests' web pages off` |
| `room.read` | as §2.7, and | room key | `…, confidential text included` when the admin chose it (§5.13) |

Not audited, with the reason: a download of a file that is not confidential (a person reading what their room already
shows them), a refused download ticket (a page's own button, refused with words), a Look or a Preview (one's own panel),
a pick (nothing leaves the page), an Earlier entry opened (a Look).

**Stores** (adds to §1.10's `pages.json`, §5.9.1's shape):

- **A file message** gains `size` and `transferOnly` (when true). Nothing is rewritten: a 0.5.1 message has neither.
  Its confidential mark is not stored on it: delivery adds `confidential` from the file's record (below, §5.14).
- **`pages.json` `marks: {<upload name>: {by, name, at}}`**, new, at the top level beside `views` and `halls`: the
  confidential mark, one record per file, whichever rooms and halls hold it. Bounded by the files on disk; a file's
  record goes when `removeUnused` removes the file.
- **`pages.json` `holds: {<link id>: {mac, messageId, proposals}}`**, new: a confidential line held back from the readers
  of a Stagewatch's frame (§5.14), no text; at most one per link, dropped with its link.
- **A take's content** may now be a snippet: at most 4,000 characters of strings plus structure, about 6 KB as JSON.
  With 200 person takes and 20 Earlier entries per hall, a hall's worst case is about 1.3 MB. Unit 27's bench measures
  the lane's save of a `pages.json` with 50 such halls; a further bound lands only if that is measured to matter.
- **`halls[H].earlier: [{seq, to, content, by, at}]`**, new: at most **20** per hall, the oldest going first; a page is
  told the 10 newest addressed to it (`to: 'board'` when seated `board` in Main, or its person key).
- **`halls[H].files: {<upload name>: {at, room, uid, name, confidential?}}`**, new: the stage files, uploads that a take
  of this hall named. It keeps the record `freshUploads` holds only in memory and only for the hour, so rule 4 of §5.9.5,
  the take's name and the mark survive a restart.
  - Written when a take naming a fresh upload is accepted.
  - **In use** while a current take or an Earlier entry names it: `uploadsInUse` (`server.js:338-345`) also counts every
    `url` that `pages.json`'s current takes and Earlier entries name, and every `files` entry still inside its wait.
  - When nothing names it any more, its `at` becomes now; after `UPLOAD_ORPHAN_MS` (`server.js:61`) it goes to
    `removeUnused`, which still keeps it if a message, screen, holding image or take names it. So a file superseded at
    minute 59 of its upload's hour is not removed at minute 60 by the upload's own sweep (`:358-362`), and a second push
    within the wait reuses it.
  - **The boot sweep** (new): after the load and the hold, once, `removeUnused` over `files` entries past their wait. It
    reads only names AGMessage recorded, so a file of a side room not loaded (§1.5) or any other file in the folder is
    never touched. It also removes `data/stage/<HALL>.json` and its `.bak` for a hall that no longer exists.
  - **A hall removed takes its stage files with it.** `admin:deleteRoom` purges only `fileNamesOf(r.messages)`
    (`server.js:1433`, `:1455`), and the boot sweep reads only names still recorded, so a forgotten hall's pictures
    (pictures of confidential pages among them) would stay on disk for good. `pages.forgetHall` (design §1.6) returns
    the hall's `files` names, and the removal always passes them to `removeUnused`, with or without "purge files" (they
    were never a message anyone could keep).
  - At most **200** per hall; the oldest not in use goes first. With 200 in use, a new stage file is refused: "This
    hall's stage holds 200 files — take some down."
- **The stage record** (§5.13), new: `data/stage/<HALL>.json` per hall, at most 500 entries, through a `WriteLane` per
  hall that is in `saveLanes()`, made with `mode: 0o600`.
- **What a clear leaves behind.** `WriteLane` keeps the old file as `.bak` on every write (`writeFileAtomic`,
  `lib/resilience.js:85-88`), so after a reset `pages.json.bak` and `data/stage/<HALL>.json.bak` would still hold the
  quotes the reset cleared, until the next write. `WriteLane` gains `clearBak()`: the next write keeps no `.bak` and
  removes the old one after its rename. A Main reset, a side room's reset and a withdrawal call it on the lanes they
  change. A hall removed closes its stage lane (pending writes dropped) before its `.json` and `.json.bak` are
  unlinked.
- **Download tickets** (§4.6.6): in memory only, at most 1,000, 60 s each; a restart voids them.
- **`settings.guestWeb`** (S4): on the hall's Main room, in its op log beside `lockRoles` (`meta`,
  `lib/store.js:122-125`).
- **A new event** (answer 45): the install addendum's U15 archives `stage\` and `pages.json` with the event. Continue
  and copy carry each hall's `guestWeb` with its lock; copy carries no take, Earlier entry, stage file, record or mark,
  as U15 has it. `pages.json`'s `holds` go into the new event's `pages.json` under all three kinds: a hold belongs to a
  Stagewatch link, which every kind keeps, and its confidential line may still be on that Stagewatch's frame (§5.14).
- **What ends a take** (amends §1.6 and §2.7's `room.reset`):
  - **A reset of the Main room** ends every information take of the hall, clears its Earlier list and its stage record:
    `page:take {chat, layer: 'info'}` to each target, the `files` entries' waits started, "n takes ended, the stage
    record cleared" in the `room.reset` row. **A reset of a side room** ends the information takes and Earlier entries
    sourced from it, and drops its entries from the stage record. The show layer is left as it is.
  - **The author's delete** of a file message (`server.js:873-882`) ends the takes and Earlier entries that name its
    URL, when no other message of the hall holds it.
  - **The admin's delete** (`admin:deleteMessage`, `:1458-1464`) of such a message asks "On the Board's pages now — take
    it down too?"; yes ends them as the author's delete does.
  - **A withdrawal** (§5.9.7) ends that take, removes it from Earlier, and starts its file's wait.
- **`lib/zipcheck.js`, `lib/imagesize.js`, `lib/cfbcheck.js` and `lib/stagerecord.js`** have 0 synchronous calls each
  (the cap for a new lib file). `server.js` stays at 16 (§4.6.3).
