## 4-§5.12 The context and the AI's brief

- **The context and the Show Bus:** nothing of a take, a transfer's name, a snippet's text, a page number or a mark.
  That keeps `lib/context.js:6` ("no message text, no document names") and `docs/SHOWBUS.md:128`. A test reads
  `GET /api/context` and the body a mock Stagewatch receives at `POST /api/peers/context` (`lib/nodes.js:749`) while a
  quote is on the Board's pages, and finds neither its words nor its file's name.
- **The AI's brief:**
  - Stagewatch's frame reaches the brief through `briefFor` (`server.js:1664-1667`), whose `showBrief` writes `; on the
    speaker screen: "<message>"` (`lib/context.js:157`), and `ai:draft` and `ai:options` both send it. While a
    confidential line is on the frame, `briefFor` gets the view without it (§5.14), so no draft or options request
    carries it.
  - The thread's file lines read `shared "name" for download: caption` (`lib/ai.js:32`); a confidential file's line
    reads `shared a confidential file`, with neither its name nor its caption (§5.14). Takes are not messages, so they
    are never in the thread.
  - The document text is the researcher's Preview, as today (`docForAi`, `app.js:907-911`; `lib/ai.js:79-93`), from
    `docview`'s `text()`, hidden parts left out, DOCX pages marked. **Never a confidential file's**: the page leaves
    `docForAi` empty for it, and `ai:draft` (`server.js:998-1009`, which takes `docText` from the client, `:1001`) gains
    `docFrom`: `{messageId}` of a file message in this room, `{seq}` of a take of this hall (for a take's stage-only
    file), or `{local: true}`. A `docText` without `docFrom`, or whose named file is confidential, is refused with "This
    file is marked confidential: its text is not sent to the AI." Whenever `docFrom` names a file, `docName` is the
    server's record of it, never the client's (today it is the client's, `:1007`). A local copy's mark is the page's to
    keep, and a page that rewrites itself can send any text as `{local: true}`: the check holds for AGMessage's own page
    (§5.14 "What it does not do").
  - New, one line, only when the drafter's socket is in the **Main room** and holds `canShow` or `canPush`: "On the
    Board's pages now: ❝ a table cell from Q3.xlsx, 'Sheet1'!C4", in the console's words. A snippet's text is added only
    when **this drafter pushed it** ("— Revenue Q3: £4.2m"), never another pusher's, whose source the drafter may not
    read. **A confidential take of any kind** reads "On the Board's pages now: a confidential item — not sent to the
    AI", with no file name, page or words, as the thread's line and the minutes withhold a confidential file's name. A
    side room's draft never
    carries it (§8: "nobody on stage reads it").
  - The minutes read the stage record as §5.13 says: every entry with its text, a confidential one without its text,
    its file name or its page.
  - The AI never pushes. A draft stays text that a person sends.

## 4-§5.13 What was shown, in the transcript and the minutes (owner answer 19)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§5.13: a Board member's typed line recorded as any take).

The owner's answer: "Yes" to recording what was shown to the Board (who, which file and page, a quote's text), and
"Right" to the reading that a confidential item is recorded with its mark and its text never goes to the AI provider.

- **The stage record** (`lib/stagerecord.js`, new, pure apart from its lane): one entry per accepted take of the hall,
  both layers, every target, and per take-down:
  `{seq, at, by: {name, role}, to: 'board' | {name}, sentFrom?, layer, kind, what, text?, line?, from?, confidential?,
  seen?, withdrawn?}`.
  - `what` is `describePage`'s console voice (§5.9.3): the file's name and page, "≈" where approximate; a web take's host
    only, never its address (§5.6).
  - `text` is a snippet's words in reading order (cells joined by " · ", rows by line breaks), at most 4,000 characters
    as the snippet is; absent for other kinds.
  - `line` is the line sent with the take to the speaker's screen (`withTake`, §5.9.10), as the server built it, with
    "sent now" or "asked the operator"; absent when none was sent.
  - `withdrawn` is the time a withdrawal (§5.9.7) took it off; the entry stays, since what was shown was shown.
  - `seen` is written once, when every target page has reported or 10 s after the take, whichever comes first:
    `{shown, of, standin?}` ("✓ on 6 of 6 Board pages" / "on 4 of 6 within 10 s" / "✓ on 6 of 6, 2 as a picture",
    §5.15.2). Visible or it did not happen: the record says
    what the pages reported, nothing more.
- **Where it lives:** `data/stage/<HALL>.json`, per hall, at most **500** entries, the oldest going first (the
  transcript says "12 earlier entries are no longer kept"). Each hall's file goes through a `WriteLane` of its own, made
  when the hall's first entry is written and listed in `saveLanes()` (flushed at stop and crash, named in health). It is
  loaded after the hold with `fs.promises`, like the boot sweep. The lane writes with `mode: 0o600`, as the `pages`
  lane does. A hall removed closes its lane and takes its file and `.bak` with it; a Main reset clears it and its `.bak`
  (`clearBak()`, §5.11); a side room's reset drops the entries sent from it. Worst case a full hall's file is about
  2.5 MB; unit 30's bench measures the lane's save of one before the bound is fixed.
- **The transcript** (`renderTranscriptHtml`, `server.js:1836-1887`; served by `/api/admin/transcript/:code`,
  `server.js:474-482`): the Main room's transcript interleaves the hall's entries with its messages by time; a side
  room's interleaves the entries sent from it. Each entry is built with the same `esc()`: "📺 14:02 — Ana (backstage)
  showed the Board (6 pages): ❝ a table cell from Q3.xlsx, 'Sheet1'!C4 — “Revenue Q3 £4.2m” · ✓ on 6 of 6", with "🖥
  line: …" when one was sent and "withdrawn 14:03" when it was.
  - **Who reads it.** The route admits whoever `isAdminReq` accepts (`server.js:416-421`): the laptop's token, and any
    account with `settings.manage`, on any device. Revision 2 called it "the admin's, on this machine"; it is not. So the
    answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store` (it sets none today), and a **confidential entry carries its text only on
    the laptop itself** (`guard.isHostMachine(req)`) or when the admin ticks **Include confidential text** on the room
    view, which adds `?confidential=1` and is written in the `room.read` row ("…, confidential text included").
    Otherwise a confidential entry reads "🔒 Confidential — Board pack.pdf, p. 12 (its words are shown on the AGMessage
    laptop, or with Include confidential text)": its mark, file and page, as owner answer 19 asks, without its words.
  - The route becomes `async` to read the record; it writes `room.read` as §2.7 has it.
- **The minutes** (`admin:summary`, `server.js:1548-1553`; `ai.summarise`, `lib/ai.js:110-121`): `summarise` takes the
  record's lines beside the thread, as `[14:02] Ana showed the Board: a table cell from Q3.xlsx, 'Sheet1'!C4 — "Revenue
  Q3 £4.2m"`, and an entry with a line adds `; on the speaker's screen: "…"`. **A confidential entry goes as `[14:05]
  Ana showed the Board a confidential item (its name and words not sent to the AI)`**, with neither its text, its
  line, its file's name nor its page: a file's name can itself be confidential ("Redundancy plan — K. Smith.docx").
  The transcript keeps the name and page (above). The owner kept this (S9, "Defaults").
  `SUMMARY_SYSTEM` (`lib/ai.js:105-108`) adds "and what was shown to the Board". Posted minutes
  (`admin:postSummary`, `server.js:1554-1561`) are the AI's text, as today.
- **Not in the room's feed:** a take stays out of the room's record and its readers (§4.6.5); only the transcript and the
  minutes read the stage record. The audit still names the act without its content (§5.11).

## 4-§5.14 The confidential mark (owner answer 16)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (§5.14: an On stage seat shares no file, so it never marks one).

The owner's answer: "Files, especially confidential, can only be sent to the rooms in use or selected", and, confirmed,
"if the speaker screen is part of the room, yes it can, as they would be the people who need to see it."

- **Every file already goes only where a person sends it:** a file is accepted in a room only as a fresh upload there or
  a file already in a message there, and crosses rooms only by `room:send` or `forward`, one chosen room at a time
  (design §4.3, unit 13). The mark adds the rest.
- **One record per file.** Revision 2 wrote the mark on every message holding the file's URL, as `upd` ops room by
  room, and then on `pages.json`: a screen already showing the file kept it, a stop between two rooms' commits left one
  copy unmarked (so it could be forwarded and put on screens with no confirm), and a side room that did not load
  (design §1.5) kept copies the scan never saw. From revision 3 the mark is **`pages.json` `marks[<upload name>] = {by,
  name, at}`** (§5.11), written first, and every check reads **`isConfidential(name)`**: `sourceOk`, `forward`,
  `room:send`, `display:take`, `display:hallHolding`, `file:download`, `ai:draft` and the stage line. Messages are not
  rewritten. **Delivery decorates**: a file message reaches a page (live, in the join's `history` and `ops`) with
  `confidential` added from the record, as an observer's is given without its `url` (§4.6.6); `fileMark {name,
  confidential}`, latest wins and unnumbered (it changes no room's log, so no page is left with a gap in its numbers,
  design §4.4), tells every page of every room holding the file to redraw its cards; the halls board, the transcript,
  the admin's room view and the AI's thread line read the record too.
- **What carries it:** a file (its record); a take, a picture or a quote from it (the server sets the mark from the
  source's record, whatever the client sent; a picture drawn from it carries the upload's `from`, §5.9.8, and is marked
  in the record when it is stored); and a typed or pasted quote, or a local copy, that its pusher marks. A client may add
  the mark, never remove it.
- **Who sets it:**
  - when sharing or showing: **🔒 Confidential** beside 🔥 Priority, off by default; whoever shares the file may mark
    it, an On stage seat included;
  - later, from ⋯ on the file: someone **seated backstage** (`research`) with `hall.files` in a room where it is in use,
    or the admin. An On stage guest holds `hall.files` (`GUEST_CAPS.board`, `server.js:699`), so with the rule of
    revision 2 any On stage tablet could mark every file of the hall, and only it or the admin could lift the mark;
  - **Remove the mark**: who marked it, or the admin. Otherwise "Only Ana or an admin can remove the mark." (S16).
- **The verb:** `file:mark {messageId, on}`, one `writes` token. The server writes or removes the file's record (the
  `pages` lane), then emits `fileMark` to the rooms holding the file and writes one `file.mark` row. **Marking refuses
  while the file is on a screen or is a holding image** ("Take it off screen 2 and the hall's holding image first: a
  screen is seen by whoever stands near it."), naming each, so a mark never leaves a confidential file on show where
  §5.14's table forbids it.
- **Where it shows** (an icon with its word, never colour alone): the file card ("🔒 Confidential · Board pack.pdf"); a
  take's card, layer bar and source line on the Board; the console and Earlier; the pinned list; the admin page's room
  view; the halls board's line (`lib/board.js:26`, "📎 🔒 name"); the transcript; the audit's words.
- **In use:** the rooms where a message holds it, and the hall's Main room while a current take or an Earlier entry
  names it. **Any act that puts it in a room where it is not in use needs `confirm: true`**, from someone who may
  download it (§4.6.6) in a room where it is in use; the page asks first, naming the room (S12); the room is then
  in use. A take is in use only when it is in use in **every** room where it will be drawn: for one person, each room
  where that person is seated.

| Act | Rule | Refused with |
|---|---|---|
| Share it in this room | this room is in use | — |
| `room:send` or `forward` into another room | `mayDownload` where it is (§4.6.3), and `confirm: true` | "This file is marked confidential: confirm to send it to Legal. It will be in use there." |
| Show it on the Board (`doc`, a picture of it, a quote from it) | in use in Main, or `confirm: true` | "This file is marked confidential: confirm to show it in the Main room. It will be in use there." |
| Show it to one person | in use in every room where that person is seated, or `confirm: true` | the same, naming each room |
| A line on the speaker's screen (§5.9.10) | in use in the hall's Main room; the hall's own Stagewatch (not one another hall shares); an encrypted link; the words say what Stagewatch does with it | "This is confidential to Legal: show it in the Main room first." / "This hall shares its Stagewatch with another hall: a confidential line is not sent there." / "This hall's Stagewatch link is not encrypted: a confidential line is not sent." |
| ⧉ Show on screens, a hall's or a screen's holding image, the `holding` take | never: screens are seen by whoever stands near them | "A confidential file is never shown on screens: anyone near them can see it." (`display:take`, `server.js:1107-1112`; `display:hallHolding`, `:1185-1189`; `sourceOk` for `holding`) |
| The AI provider | never its text; in the thread, the "now" line and the minutes, neither its name, its page nor its caption | "This file is marked confidential: its text is not sent to the AI." (§5.12) |
| The context, the Show Bus | never (they carry no file names anyway) | — |
| Download | as any file (§4.6.6), plus a `file.download` row when the stream ends; a document shown to the Board may carry the Download tick, and Earlier keeps the item for Board members seated later (S8) | — |
| Stagewatch's frame while the line is on it | below | — |

- **The frame's message while a confidential line is on it.** Stagewatch's frame comes back into AGMessage, and its
  `message` (`stageView`, `lib/nodes.js:252`, up to 500 characters) is spread into every `stagePayload`
  (`server.js:1925-1930`): the join answer (`:799`), each room's `stage` event (`onStageState`, `:1941-1947`), every
  screen's `display:state` and `display:stage` (`:1677-1682`, `:1939`), whose page draws it in its strip
  (`public/display.js:174`), the halls board through `hallParts` (`:1746`), and the AI's brief (`briefFor`,
  `:1664-1667`, `lib/context.js:157`). Design §1.9 has every room of a hall show its countdown, and design §5.7's
  `stage` take draws the strip on people's pages. So a confidential line sent to the speaker's screen would come back
  to the hall's foyer screens, to rooms where the file is not in use, to every halls-board watcher and to the AI
  provider. From 0.6.0 **`viewFor(link, audience)`** is the one way `link.view` reaches a reader (`stagePayload`,
  `displayState`, `hallParts`, `briefFor`), and each link keeps a **hold**:
  - **set** when a confidential line is sent at once, or proposed. A send holds the first frame message that differs
    from the one on the frame before it (its `messageId` from the receipt's `refs.messageId`, `readReceipt`,
    `lib/nodes.js:292-303`, where Stagewatch gives one). A proposal holds **every** new frame message from the moment
    it is proposed until the desk's answer is read (the follow, `trackProposal`): the operator may approve it edited,
    so no text match is trusted. A refused or expired proposal ends that part of the hold.
  - **kept** by the held message's `guard.mac` (never its text) and `messageId`, and **released** when the frame's
    message differs from both: a new message, or the operator's clear.
  - **while held**: screens, the halls board, the context and the AI's brief get `message: ''`; pages of a room where
    the item is in use get `message: '🔒 a confidential line'`; every other room `''`. `messageAck` and `messageAckBy`
    stay, since they carry no text, so the sender still reads the speaker's acknowledgement.
  - **kept across a restart**: the hold is written through the `pages` lane (`pages.json` `holds[<link id>] = {mac,
    messageId, proposals}`, no text), so a restart while a confidential line is up still withholds it from the first
    frame. A hold whose link is gone is dropped. A new event carries it, since the link is kept (§5.11, answer 45).
- **What it does not do:** it is not encryption (the file on disk and its link are as any file's); a person who reads it
  can retype or photograph it; a message that talks about it is not marked; a local copy's mark and a typed quote's are
  the page's to send, since the server never sees the file. **The mark on derived content and the AI check hold for
  AGMessage's own page**: a picture uploaded without its `from`, or document text sent as a local copy, by someone who
  rewrites the page or copies the words, is not caught, and SECURITY.md says so. What Stagewatch does with a line once
  it has it is Stagewatch's (§5.9.10, §5.9.12).
- **Rollback:** 0.5.1 ignores the mark (§4.6.4): `pages.json` is not read, so under 0.5.1 a marked file is an ordinary
  one.

## 4-§5.15 The Board's devices (owner answer 22)

> **Amended by** 5-§0 and 5-§15.10 (unit M's rows, its floor leg's removals), 7-§0.3 and 7-§17.7 (the chat view's rows, the layout leg); who builds the shared legs: Part 0 §0.8 C1.

The owner's answer: "Board will use a mixture of devices." As `DECISIONS.md` reads it: iPads on current and older
iPadOS, Android tablets, and phones (iOS and Android); every Board feature works on each, with a test matrix and
fallbacks, and nothing is tuned to one device. This section is that answer for the stage: what an On stage or observer
seat draws, keeps from saving and downloads. The Board's chat view (the wake lock, a long press, `<dialog>`) is the
board addendum's; its rows join the same matrix and the same walk.

### 4-§5.15.1 The matrix

| Row | Device | Browser | Why it is a row |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | an iPad on an iPadOS before 16.4, the oldest the owner's devices run | Safari | below the document floor (§5.15.2): the stand-in, and everything else as on any row |
| D2 | an iPad on iPadOS 16.4 to 16.7 | Safari | the oldest that opens documents. It has no `<link rel="modulepreload">` (Safari 17) and no `Promise.withResolvers` (Safari 17.4), so the timed import and pdf.js's legacy build are what it runs |
| D3 | an iPad on the current iPadOS | Safari | the newest WebKit |
| D4 | an Android tablet | Chrome, current | a long press fires `contextmenu` |
| D5 | an Android tablet | Samsung Internet, current | a second Blink browser (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/browsers/samsunginternet_android.json), with menus and downloads of its own |
| D6 | an iPhone on the current iOS | Safari | a phone's width; the board addendum's Shown to you tab |
| D7 | an Android phone | Chrome, current | a phone's width and a long press |
| CI | the smoke's Chrome and Edge, with the device legs of §5.15.3 | — | every push |

- A walked row records the model, the OS and browser versions and the date: "current" is whatever the device ran that
  day, written down. A row the owner has no device for reads "not walked", which is a fact in the paper, never a pass.
- **What each row walks:**

| Feature | Checked on every row | On D1, below the floor |
|---|---|---|
| A quote | a word, a paragraph, a cell with its labels and a 25 × 10 table: drawn, fitted, ✓ reported | the same |
| A picture | a page picture and a region: drawn; pinch, double-tap and + / − zoom with pan; ✓ | the same |
| A web page | the frame, its "Look for" strip, Open in a new tab | the same |
| A PDF document | the page box, paging, zoom, find; a JPEG 2000 page drawn; the first page of a 25 MB pack, timed | its stand-in, with its words |
| A DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, Markdown or text document | drawn without hidden parts; Word's page numbers | CSV, Markdown and text drawn, since they need no inflating; DOCX, XLSX and PPTX as their stand-in |
| Earlier and Look | an Earlier entry, and a Look at a picture | the same; a document's Earlier entry draws its stand-in, and a Look at a document reads "This device cannot open documents — ask the backstage team to show you a picture." |
| ⬇ Download | on a take shown with Download ticked: the file reaches the device's downloads under its name, and the page stays (the 204 of §4.6.6) | the same: a form POST needs no parser |
| No save | a long press on a picture offers no save; a drag leaves it in place; where `contextmenu` fires, AGMessage's menu opens | the same |
| Many takes | 20 takes in a row, then Back to chat: the tab still draws, and nothing reloads it | the same |
| Asleep, then back | a take sent while the device slept is drawn at its next join, as the current take or under Earlier | the same |

### 4-§5.15.2 The floor, and what a device below it does

- **The document floor is Safari 16.4 (iOS and iPadOS 16.4), Chrome 103 and Firefox ESR.**
  - pdf.js 4.10.38's legacy build is compiled for "Chrome >= 103", "Firefox ESR" and "Safari >= 16.4" (`ENV_TARGETS`,
    https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/v4.10.38/gulpfile.mjs#L81-L90, which its Babel step takes as its targets,
    `:97`).
  - It keeps a class static block (`class PDFWorker{static#_s=0;…static{if(i){…GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc||=…` in
    `legacy/build/pdf.min.mjs` of the 4.10.38 package), which Safari parses from 16.4 (MDN's compatibility data,
    `static.initialization_blocks`, https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/javascript/classes.json). Below
    16.4 the module does not parse at all.
  - `docworker.js` inflates Office parts with `DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` (§5.10.1), which arrived at the same
    versions: Chrome 103, Firefox 113, Safari 16.4
    (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/DecompressionStream.json). So one probe stands for both.
- **Not taken: an older pdf.js for devices below the floor.** 3.11.174's legacy build predates the fix of
  CVE-2024-4367 ("<= 4.1.392" affected, "4.2.67" patched, with the workaround "Set the option `isEvalSupported` to
  `false`", https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/security/advisories/GHSA-wgrm-67xf-hhpq), and two pdf.js versions would
  double what is vendored and tested. A picture of the place reaches those devices instead.
- **The page knows before it is asked.** At join the hall page tries `new DecompressionStream('deflate-raw')` inside
  `try` and sends **`docs: true`** only when it succeeds. No user agent is read, and no syntax is probed: the page's
  CSP has no `'unsafe-eval'` (`lib/guard.js:178-191`), so `new Function` cannot test one. The server keeps it per socket
  (`socket.data.docs`; anything but `true` is `false`). A device that passes the probe yet fails pdf.js's `import()`
  reports `failed` with "this device cannot open documents — ask for a picture" and joins without `docs` for the rest
  of its session (kept in `sessionStorage`, in try/catch).
- **A document's stand-in** (`standin` on a `doc` take, cleaned by `cleanPage`, one of two shapes):
  - for a PDF or an image, `{url}`: a picture of the take's place that the pusher's page draws and uploads as §5.9.8
    draws a page picture, with `from` naming the same file. It is checked as an `image` take is (`sourceOk`, the pixel
    bound), takes the source's confidential mark, and is a stage file named by the take (§5.11);
  - for the other types, `{snippet}`: what the pusher sees at that place, as "What I see" sends it (`view` blocks or a
    table, §5.9.4), cleaned by `cleanSnippet`, hidden parts left out;
  - attached by the pusher's page when `page:status` says a target page joined without `docs`, and only then, so no
    picture is uploaded for nothing (the bar says so before it goes, §5.9.7);
  - a page without `docs` draws the stand-in with "As a picture of p. 12: this device cannot page through the
    document" and reports `shown` with those words; a page with `docs` never draws it. With no stand-in (a page that
    joined after the push), it reports `failed` with "this device cannot open documents — ask for a picture", and the
    pusher's console offers **Send them a picture of p. 12**: a person `image` take to each such page's person, drawn
    over the Board's take on their pages only (§5.9.1);
  - ⬇ Download on a take shown with Download ticked is offered as on any device: it needs no parser;
  - the console's mark reads "✓ 6/6 (2 as a picture)", and the stage record's `seen` counts the stand-ins (§5.13).
- **Everything else works below the floor**, and the walk holds it: quotes and tables (`pagelayer.mjs` draws with
  `textContent` and CSS), pictures (`HTMLImageElement.decode()`, Safari 11.1,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/HTMLImageElement.json), zoom (Pointer Events, Safari 13,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/PointerEvent.json), web pages (§5.6's frame), Earlier,
  Download and the no-save measures.
- **AGMessage's own page code parses on every row.** Every page script parses as ES2020 today (measured: espree from
  `app/node_modules`, `ecmaVersion: 2020`, over `app/public/*.js` at `89104d8`; `admin-plus.js` parses as ES2017), and
  ES2020's newest syntax parses in Safari from 14 (BigInt; optional chaining and `??` from 13.1;
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/javascript/builtins/BigInt.json,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/javascript/operators/optional_chaining.json).
  `eslint.config.mjs` sets `ecmaVersion: 2020` for `app/public/**` (its page blocks, `:87-91`, set none today, so ESLint
  reads the newest syntax): a class field, a static block, `||=` or a top-level `await` in the hall page,
  `pagelayer.mjs`, `docview.mjs`, `docmodel.mjs` or `docworker.js` fails the lint. Built-ins are not syntax: the floor
  leg (§5.15.3) and the walk hold those. The vendored files are outside the lint (ignored, `eslint.config.mjs:30`),
  which is why pdf.js sets the floor.
- **Older devices' other gaps, each with its fallback:**
  - `<link rel="modulepreload">` arrived in Safari 17, and Safari has no `requestIdleCallback`
    (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/html/elements/link.json,
    https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Window.json): the timed `import()` of §5.9.11;
  - Fetch Metadata arrived in Safari 16.4
    (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/http/headers/Sec-Fetch-Mode.json): a device without it is
    served, as §4.6.3 says, so on D1 a file's address typed into the address bar opens it. D1's row in
    `docs/DEVICES.md` and SECURITY.md say so;
  - `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` from Safari 16 (§5.10.5) is under the floor, so every device that opens documents draws JPEG
    2000;
  - **a long press:** iOS never fires `contextmenu` on one (`contextmenu_event`, `safari_ios` false,
    https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/Element.json), so `-webkit-touch-callout: none` (iOS
    Safari from 2, https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/css/properties/-webkit-touch-callout.json)
    keeps "Save to Photos" off a picture there. Chrome on Android fires `contextmenu` on a long press (the architecture
    and UX addendum's touch rules), and the layer's handler opens AGMessage's menu in place of "Download image".
    Whether Samsung Internet does the same is D5's walk.
- **Phones** (D6, D7): the side bar is the board addendum's 📺 Shown to you tab; a quote's type floor is 20 px under
  600 px wide, and a table wider than the screen scrolls sideways inside its card (§5.9.11); the zoom controls and the
  page box are 48 px, as in the simple view. A phone may be remote, through the tunnel on mobile data (answer 33): a
  quote or a picture costs its own bytes, a document its file (by ranges for a PDF, §5.9.8). No measurement this
  round; unit T's bench records a document take's bytes and time to a phone through the tunnel.
- **Nothing is tuned to one device:** no user agent is read anywhere in the stage's code; each fallback is chosen by a
  probe or by what failed, and its words say what this device does.

### 4-§5.15.3 How it is proven

- **On every push, in the smoke (Chromium):**
  - **device legs:** the Board-side checks of units 23 to 29 run again with `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` at
    `mobile: true` (`false` today, `test/browser-smoke.js:118`), at 1180 × 820, 820 × 1180 and 390 × 844, with
    `Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled`;
  - **the floor leg:** an init script (`Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument`, `browser-smoke.js:117`) removes
    `DecompressionStream`, `requestIdleCallback` and `Promise.withResolvers` before the page loads, so it joins without
    `docs`. A document take then draws its stand-in with its words and reports ✓; without one, `failed` and the
    console's Send them a picture; quotes, pictures, web pages, Earlier, ⬇ Download and the no-save checks pass as on
    any leg. It cannot take away syntax the browser parses, which is what the walk and the ES2020 fence are for.
- **In the lint:** `ecmaVersion: 2020` for `app/public/**` (above).
- **On the owner's devices, before 0.6.0 is tagged** (unit 32): every row walked, or "not walked" where the owner has
  no such device (a fact in the paper, never a pass), and recorded in **`docs/DEVICES.md`** (new): each row's device,
  versions and date, and each feature ✓ or the fallback seen. A ✕ is a defect, fixed before the tag, or a fallback
  that the row and the device's own words then name. The page floor's words (`addendum-arch-ux.md` §15.10) are not
  such a fallback: a Board device of the owner's below that floor is a ✕ that holds the tag until the floor is lowered
  for it or the owner retires it from the Board (owner answer 22). The board addendum's rows (the wake lock, a
  long press, `<dialog>`) join the same paper.
- **The benches** that named "a Board iPad" run on the rows they now name: D1 and D2 for the image decode limit (unit
  22), D2 and D4 for parse times (units 23 and 27), D2 and D6 for the glance budget (unit 27); and unit T's on a phone
  through the tunnel.

## 4-§7.7 Right-click and the buttons (adds rows to §7.7's table)

> **Amended by** 5-§0 and 5-§16.7 (its rows are the catalogue's kinds), 7-§0.3 (§7.7: no Send to ▸ On stage; 📌 Pin for me; the pin door).

| On | Buttons | The same in right-click / ⋯ |
|---|---|---|
| A file message | 👁 Look / 👁 Preview · ⬇ Download (`mayDownload`) · 📺 Show the Board ▸ (a picture of p. 1 · a picture of a page… · the document…, which opens the short bar with ☐ Let them download it) · ⧉ Show on screens · ↗ Forward / Send to… (`mayDownload`) · 📌 Pin · 🔒 Mark confidential / Remove the mark · 🗑 Delete (own) | the same, per seat (below) |
| A transfer-only file | ⬇ Download (`mayDownload`) · ↗ Forward / Send to… (`mayDownload`) · 📌 Pin · 🔒 · 🗑 Delete (own) | the same |
| A message (§7.7's row) | "Send to Stagewatch" reads 🖥 Send now · 📝 Ask the operator | the same |
| A pick in the Preview | the bar's chips (`previewActions`): Copy · each unit that holds it · Picture of this page · What I see · The document at this place · ▸ to a person | the same; on touch from ⋯ or a second tap |
| An On stage card (either layer) | Show again · Remove · ⬇ Download (a take shown with Download) | the same |
| A take in the pusher's console (the pusher, `canPush` holders, the admin) | Take down (`canShow`: its own pushes only) · Withdraw · Send them a picture (a page that cannot open documents, §5.15.2) | the same; the toast offers Take down and Withdraw for 10 s |
| An Earlier entry | Look | the same |
| The Board chip, for `canShow` | click | Take down · Web page… (with `canWeb`) |
| A person On stage, in the People tab, for `canShow` | ⋯ | Show them ▸ (a picture of a page, the document… with the same short bar and its Download tick, what I see, a quote; a web page with `canWeb`) |
| The admin's 🔒 Roles & invites panel, on a hall's Main room | ☐ Backstage guests may show web pages (S4; disabled while the roles are open) · Take it down (after turning it off over a guest's web page) | — (an admin page control) |

- The layer keeps §5.4's **✕ Back to chat** and **▭ Minimise**; a card says **Remove**, one word for one act. On an On
  stage seat, AGMessage's menu replaces the browser's on stage content, Shift+right-click included, and holds no save
  (§4.6.6).
- The simple view has no context menu (§7.7), and its file card opens with a tap (Look).

**The catalogue** (the architecture and UX addendum's `public/catalog.js`, §16.2 and §16.7) changes with it:

- **Facts** (`f`) gain `canWeb` (the join answer's; for a code guest it follows `pages:rights`, S4), `docs` (this
  device opens documents, §5.15.2), `download` (`mayDownload`: the admin, or a `research` seat that is not a Viewer
  account) and `files` where it sits (for the mark); `role` and `view` already decide the rest.
- **A. A message:** Download and Forward / Send to ▸ of a file show only with `f.download`; "🔒 Mark confidential /
  Remove the mark" joins the keep group (a `research` seat with `files`, or the admin; Remove disabled with "Only Ana or
  an admin can remove the mark."); Look is absent for an observer.
- **B. A file:** Download as A.
- **C. A person:** "Send to stage ▸" offers a web page only with `canWeb`.
- **J. A pushed take:** Download on a `doc` with `download`, for every seat but an observer or a Viewer account, Board
  seats included (owner confirmation of answers 12 and 20). In the pusher's console: Take down · Withdraw, and Send
  them a picture for a page that cannot open documents. Without `f.docs`, a document's card opens its stand-in.
- **L. The Board chip:** Web page… shows only with `canWeb`.
- **M. A pick:** "Picture of this page" and "The document at this place" side by side; "＋ a line on the speaker's
  screen" with its two choices (§5.9.10).
- **The message menu by seat:** On stage (full view): respond, keep, Look, Send to ▸ **for text only**, Delete own, no
  Download. **Observer or Viewer: Copy, and Send to ▸ for text only, where they may post elsewhere; no Look, no
  Download.** A file is moved only by a seat that may download it (§4.6.3).
- **Every new verb:** `file:download` → `msg.download`, `file.download`, `take.download` (no longer `local`); `file:mark`
  → `msg.confidential`, `file.confidential`; `page:withdraw` → `take.withdraw`; `admin:newInvite` → the Invites panel's
  New On stage link.

## 4-§9. Tests (adds to the table; the rule for each unit is unchanged)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.3 (the revision 3 test's words, applied in place).

| Unit | What its tests prove | Red first because… |

## 4-§10. Papers (adds to the list; each line moves in the unit that changes its subject)

- **`README.md`:** a **Files** bullet ("📎 Share for download, or 📺 Show the Board: two acts"); a **From the backstage
  team** bullet (a picture of a page or the document, what they see, or a picked word, line, item, paragraph, cell, row
  or column, a quote, a web page, each over the Board's chat or in their side bar, confirmed by each page, with a line
  on the speaker's screen through the operator or at once when asked); the information drawn over the show; **On stage
  seats come from an invite link**; **downloads are for the backstage team, and a Board tablet keeps no copy unless
  Download is ticked**; **🔒 Confidential**; **hidden things (hidden sheets, rows, columns, slides, shapes, Word's hidden
  text, presenter notes) are never shown on the Board's pages**; **what was shown to the Board is recorded in the
  transcript and the minutes**; Word page numbers; files to transfer of more types; **the stage works on iPads old and
  new, Android tablets and phones**, and an iPad too old to open documents is shown a picture of the place.
- **`README.txt`:** the research steps (Preview, the page box, a pick, a picture or the document, Show); the Board's
  steps (Look, the side bar, Earlier, Minimise, ⬇ on a take shown with Download); before the show: send the On stage
  link to presenters and board members, and make a new one after a shared device was used, and walk the Board's devices
  as `docs/DEVICES.md` lists them; what an older iPad shows in place of a document; the admin's Backstage guests may
  show web pages switch, off by default; Withdraw for a take shown by mistake; what a Board tablet keeps and what cannot
  be prevented (§4.6.6); `:199-201`, the libraries' versions, replaced by "see THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md".
- **`CHANGELOG.md`** 0.6.0, the behaviour changes:
  - no file opens itself on anyone's panel; showing the Board is a take, not a chat file, as a picture of a page or as
    the document, chosen per push;
  - a Download for the backstage team, by a ticket the server issues per seat; **observers and Viewer accounts no longer
    download, and no longer see pictures in the chat** (the server withholds their links); **Board tablets download
    nothing unless the sender ticked Download on a whole file**; uploads are served `no-store`;
  - a file's name is the uploaded file's, never the poster's;
  - **On stage seats come from an invite link, an account or the admin, in open halls too**: an open hall's Board
    tablets must rejoin with the On stage link after the upgrade; an open hall's code guests no longer reach the Board's
    pages (0.5.1 opened their files there);
  - two new rights: `stage.show`, which Staff, Tech, Senior and Manager accounts hold on upgrade, and `stage.web`, which
    Tech, Senior and Manager accounts hold on upgrade; code guests push web pages only in a locked hall whose admin
    turned it on (off by default);
  - information is drawn over the clock and the other show takes, and never replaces them;
  - the support view no longer opens a file on a person's panel;
  - the action prompt's button reads "Ask the Board";
  - lines to Stagewatch keep `{…}` as `(…)`, are cut on characters, and name departments as Stagewatch does; a line sent
    with a push leaves no quote in the room's record, and goes through the operator or at once as the sender chooses;
  - the confidential mark; a confidential line goes only to a hall's own Stagewatch over an encrypted link, and while
    it is on the speaker's screen AGMessage's screens, the halls board and the AI do not show or receive it; the
    transcript and the minutes record what was shown to the Board;
  - opening a file's address in the browser no longer saves or shows it; only a seat that may download a file may move
    it to another room; Viewer accounts never download; Board tablets and observers keep their file links only while
    their seat allows;
  - Staff accounts can now draw information over the Board's chat and show typed quotes, which 0.5.1's side panel did
    not; a researcher's push no longer replaces the operator's information, and a side room reaches the Board only from
    the Main room's allow-list;
  - Withdraw, beside Take down; New On stage link; the On stage link leaves the address bar after joining; unlocking a
    hall keeps its On stage seats; a remembered On stage role falls back to Observer;
  - hidden things never shown: Word's hidden text, hidden slide shapes, Markdown comments and very hidden sheets left
    out, and no Download for a file with hidden parts;
  - files to transfer: zip, mp4, m4a, mov, mp3, wav, ODF and password-protected Office files, download only;
  - Word documents show page numbers ("≈" where Word's own layout is missing); JPEG 2000 images in PDFs draw;
  - pdf.js 3.11.174's worker removed; pdf.js 4.10.38's legacy build (older iPads); mammoth 1.13.0;
  - the stage on the Board's devices: a device too old to open documents (before iOS and iPadOS 16.4, or Chrome 103) is
    shown a picture of the place, or what the sender sees, in the document's place; the stage's modules are imported
    after the join instead of preloaded; AGMessage's page code is held to ES2020;
  - refused at upload: oversized archives, macro parts in Office files, huge or unreadable images;
  - the readers' visible changes: CSV as a grid, PPTX as an outline, Word and Excel without their inline styling;
  - §4.6.4's rollback items.
- **`docs/ACCOUNTS.md`:** `:28`'s `hall.files` words; the `stage.show` and `stage.web` rows (`:24-36`); the roles' words
  (`:15-19`); who may show what (§5.9.2.2's table), and that `stage.show` governs every account's information pushes;
  that a locked hall's backstage code guests show web pages only while the admin's setting for the hall is on; who may
  download and who may move a file (§4.6.6's table, Viewer accounts never); who may mark a file confidential and who may
  remove the mark (§5.14); "A code guest's rights come from where they joined" gains "On stage needs an invite link,
  which the admin can replace"; the audit list (`:115-121`) gains `page.push`'s words (withdrawn included),
  `upload.refused`, `stagewatch.send`, `file.mark`, `file.download`, `room.invite`, `room.guestWeb`, `room.lock`'s
  "guests' web pages off" and `room.read`'s "confidential text included".
- **`docs/DISPLAYS.md`:** People's screens (unit 18's section) gains the two layers, `doc`, `image` and `snippet`, the
  arrival in the side bar, Earlier, the source rule and §5.9.11's table; screens never show a confidential or
  transfer-only file.
- **`docs/DESIGN.md`:** documents are parsed only in the page, in a worker with a time cap where the library allows;
  archives and images are checked before anyone opens them; HTML is parsed in one place and never adopted; a quote is
  data, never HTML; a download is a ticketed server act and a `GET` never saves; an observer is never given a file's
  link; hidden things are never shown on the Board's pages, Word's hidden text removed before mammoth reads the file;
  Word pages come from Word's own breaks; the confidential mark is one record per file, read by every check; a
  confidential line on Stagewatch's frame is held back from every other reader (`viewFor`); each device's fallback is
  chosen by a probe or by what failed, never by its user agent, and the document floor is the one pdf.js's legacy build
  sets.
- **`docs/NODES.md`:** `:12`'s "Send to stage" row is renamed "The speaker's screen", with the braces, the cut on
  characters, the department cut, the choice per send, a confidential line's words, and the textless record of a line
  sent with a push; a line saying what AGMessage has asked Stagewatch for 2.20 (§5.9.12).
- **`docs/SHOWBUS.md`:** the context carries nothing of a take or a mark (beside `:128` and `:156`).
- **`SECURITY.md`** ("The design, briefly", `:34-50`):
  - downloads are a server act: a ticket per seat, single use, 60 s, bound to the person, the address and the file, at
    most 4 per page and 8 per person; observers are never given a file's link, and Viewer accounts never download;
    uploads are served `no-store`, never as `attachment` on `GET`, and a navigation to one is refused by Fetch Metadata
    (a browser that sends none, an iPad before 16.4 among them, is served, as before);
  - **On stage by invite**: an On stage seat needs the invite link, in open halls too; the link leaves the address bar
    after joining, and New On stage link voids it; `stage.show` and `stage.web` are rights of their own; a code guest
    shows web pages only in a locked hall whose admin turned it on;
  - a Board tablet keeps no copy and offers no download unless a sender ticked Download, and what cannot be prevented
    (screenshots, developer tools, the browser's own save, retyping);
  - "not offered" is not "not reachable" for a seat that was shown a file: its link is the capability;
  - a downloaded file's extension is always its own; a page, region or "what I see" is a new picture, and a whole image
    keeps its metadata unless re-drawn; a downloaded copy stays on the device that saved it;
  - files to transfer only: never opened, parsed or shown by AGMessage, first bytes checked, served only as
    `attachment`, `application/octet-stream`, `nosniff`, at most 25 MB; a zip is not inflated by AGMessage, so open it as
    an email attachment would be opened;
  - the archive, macro and pixel checks; macros, formulas, external references and links;
  - the PDF worker alone may run WebAssembly (`'wasm-unsafe-eval'` on its own response);
  - the confidential mark: where it keeps a file, that it is not encryption, and that the mark on derived content and
    the AI check hold for AGMessage's own page, not against someone who copies or rewrites it;
  - a file with hidden parts is never shown with Download ticked, which is the researcher's page's guard (the server
    never parses a document);
  - the stage record holds quotes' words, confidential ones included, in clear in `data/stage/` (mode 0600), as rooms'
    messages sit in `data/rooms/`; the transcript shows confidential words only on the laptop or when the admin asks;
  - the stage files' lifetime and the boot sweep; a line on the speaker's screen is seen on every Stagewatch output, is
    readable from Stagewatch's public frame on the venue network, and is kept by Stagewatch; a confidential one goes
    only to a hall's own Stagewatch over an encrypted link, and is held back from AGMessage's other readers.
- **`docs/ANALYSIS.md`:** the vendor manifest fence, `parseInert` and the refused shapes, the new pages in the guard
  rail, the inputs keys, the gate, `ecmaVersion: 2020` for the pages, and the smoke's device legs and floor leg.
- **`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`** and **`licenses/`** (new), shipped by **`tools/build-portable.ps1`**.
- **`docs/DEVICES.md`** (new, unit T): the device matrix (§5.15.1), the floor and each fallback (§5.15.2), and the
  walk's record per row, kept for each release.
- **`CLAUDE.md`:** "Where things live" gains `public/zipcore.js`, `public/wordpages.js`, `public/docmodel.mjs`,
  `public/docview.mjs`, `public/docworker.js`, `lib/zipcheck.js`, `lib/imagesize.js`, `lib/stagerecord.js`,
  `public/vendor/VENDOR.json`, the notices and `docs/DEVICES.md`. The house words gain **a transfer** (a file shared for
  download), **show the Board** (a take on people's pages), **the information layer** (what is drawn over the show), **a
  quote** (a snippet: picked text or cells, carried as data), **a download ticket** (the server's single-use leave to
  download one file), **confidential** (a mark that keeps a file where it is in use or sent), **the stage record** (what
  was shown, for the transcript and the minutes), **the device matrix** (the Board's devices every stage feature is
  walked on, `docs/DEVICES.md`) and **a stand-in** (what a device that cannot open documents draws in a document's
  place).

## 4-§12. Risks, left for later, the owner's answers, and the one open question (adds to §12)

### 4-Risks

- **A quote is the researcher's claim.** The server never parses, so it cannot check that the words are in the file, or
  that a Word page is right. The card names who quoted it and from where, in their voice; the audit names the act.
- **Words can be carried by hand.** Every push from a side room is held to Main's allow-list (§5.9.2.2), but a Legal
  member who is also seated in a room on the list, or who tells someone there, can type Legal's words onto the Board's
  pages. The audit row names the act and the room it came from.
- **Whoever sits On stage reads what is pushed.** From 0.6.0 that is invited guests, Board accounts and those the admin
  seats, in open halls too; an invite link passed on admits whoever holds it, as today in a locked hall. New On stage
  link voids it without changing the code (§5.9.2.1), and a new code voids every invite (design §2.2).
- **"Not offered" is not "not reachable" for a seat that was shown a file.** A Board tablet that Looks at a transfer or
  is shown a `doc` holds its link; opening it in the address bar saves nothing (§4.6.3), but a desktop browser's
  developer tools can `fetch` it, and a browser that sends no Fetch Metadata is served. An observer is never given a
  file message's link or a document. A picture or a quote hands over nothing else.
- **A download ticket is the download.** Whoever holds a ticket within its 60 s, at the same address, gets the file
  once. Behind a shared NAT or the tunnel's address, a stolen ticket would work; the ticket never leaves the socket that
  asked and the form that spends it.
- **A `doc` take parses on the Board's device**, with today's parsing risks bounded by §5.10.3. A picture or a quote
  parses nothing there.
- **A whole image keeps its metadata** (EXIF, GPS) unless it is sent "without its metadata". A region or a page is
  always re-drawn.
- **A downloaded copy stays on the device that saved it,** a venue's shared tablet included; a Board tablet saves one
  only when a sender ticked Download.
- **Word's pages are approximate even when Word wrote them**: its rendered breaks are not always where the page broke,
  and depend on the printer and fonts of the machine that last saved the file (§5.10.4).
- **Picks in untagged PDFs are guesses.** Paragraphs and items are marked "≈ best guess"; cells are not offered; a
  multi-column page can interleave text in content order. Office's PDF export can include tags (an option, not verified
  as its default).
- **A line on the speaker's screen sent at once replaces the operator's message**, cancels its acknowledgement, and is
  seen on every Stagewatch output, NDI and its viewer page, a confidential one included; Stagewatch also publishes it in
  its public frame, fires its triggers with it and saves it (§5.9.10). Hence off by default, the choice made per send
  with words under 🖥, a confidential line only to the hall's own Stagewatch over an encrypted link with words that say
  all of this (S6, which the owner kept).
- **The hold on Stagewatch's frame matches what it can see.** A confidential line is held back from AGMessage's other
  readers by its MAC and `messageId`, and every new message is held while a confidential proposal waits; an operator
  who retypes the line by hand at Stagewatch's own desk, outside the proposal, is not caught.
- **Transfer-only files are as safe as their source.** AGMessage checks their first bytes only; a zip bomb or a
  malicious media file harms the machine that opens it.
- **The confidential mark is a rule about where AGMessage sends a file, not encryption.** Retyping, photographing and
  talking about it are outside it.
- **Behaviour changes on upgrade:** a Share no longer appears on the Board's panel; research must press Show. Open
  halls' Board tablets must rejoin with the On stage link. Observers and Viewers lose downloads and the pictures in the
  chat. Board tablets have no Download, except on a take shown with Download ticked. Observers and On stage seats no longer forward files. Staff accounts gain
  `stage.show`, which reaches further than 0.5.1's side panel (over the chat, typed quotes); Tech, Senior and Manager
  accounts gain `stage.show` and `stage.web`. A file's address opened in a browser no longer saves it. The admin's
  support view no longer opens files on a person's panel. The CHANGELOG says each.
- **Formula values are what the author's application last saved,** and may be stale.
- **The Board's devices are a mixture** (answer 22), walked once, before the tag (§5.15). A model or browser version
  that appears after the walk is not proven until its row is walked again. Below the document floor a device is shown
  a picture of the place, not the document, and a page that joins after the push has no stand-in until it is sent a
  picture. `Intl.Segmenter` (Safari 14.1), the Highlight API (Safari 17.2, with its outline fallback), a form POST's
  attachment on iOS, `filename*` on iOS and Fetch Metadata's `Sec-Fetch-Mode` (Chrome 76, Firefox 90, Safari 16.4,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/http/headers/Sec-Fetch-Mode.json) are taken from the browsers'
  tables until the walk. The smoke runs Chrome and Edge, with device legs that emulate a size and touch, not WebKit.

### 4-Left for later

- pdf.js 6 (its WebAssembly decoders or their JavaScript fallbacks, `standardFontDataUrl`, `cMapUrl`), once no row of
  the device matrix is below its legacy build's Safari 18 (§5.10.2).
- Screen capture of the researcher's own view (`getDisplayMedia`): HTTPS, a prompt each time, Region Capture on desktop
  Chromium only, iOS from Safari 27. To be asked with the venues' HTTPS.
- ODT, ODS and ODP on the stage (the zip core can learn ODF's stored `mimetype`); they are transfer-only in 0.6.0.
- A larger upload cap for video and audio, once disk, buckets and venue Wi-Fi are measured.
- A ticketed read of every file (not only its download), so a seat shown a file holds no lasting capability; it needs
  every reader, the screens included, to fetch with a header.
- The AI finding the passage that answers the Board's question, offered as a pick the reader checks against its own
  block model before it is sent.
- UTF-16 text exports (Excel's "Unicode text"), which `isText`'s NUL refusal turns away (`lib/guard.js:220-223`).
- A picture of a DOCX, XLSX, CSV, Markdown or text view (S10 keeps "What I see" as data).
- The Board's current take drawn on the researcher's panel (the console gives its words and marks today).
- A local Preview followed by one's other devices (a file in no message has no `messageId`).
- "The speaker now" as a target matched to Stagewatch's current speaker by name, once presenters have a seat of their
  own (design question 3 kept its default; the board addendum leaves that seat for later).
- `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` on the hall page, with one policy for `parseInert`, once every row of the device
  matrix enforces it; until then it would guard only some of the Board's devices
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/require-trusted-types-for).
- A lint of Web APIs (built-ins, not only syntax) against the device matrix's floor, once a tool's coverage of the APIs
  §5.15 names is checked.
- Everything of §5.9.12, on Stagewatch's side.

### 4-Gaps (not measured, not verified)

- Parse time and memory for a 25 MB XLSX, DOCX or PDF on the rig's laptop and the device matrix's rows; the 300-page
  `getPage` loop; render plus upload of a 2,048 px page on venue Wi-Fi; paging against the upload buckets; the lane's
  save of a full `pages.json` and of a full stage record; the image decode limit and glance budget on the matrix's rows;
  the bytes a reload fetches with `no-store`, and a document take's bytes to a phone through the tunnel. Each has its
  unit and its bench above.
- Whether mammoth's browser bundle runs in a worker (very likely, from its xmldom parser and guarded schedulers; unit 23
  settles it). How it hands over hidden text is no longer a gap: 1.13.0 reads no `w:vanish`, leaves out `w:del` and
  `w:moveFrom`, and drops comments without a style map (read in its package), so hidden runs are removed before it reads
  the file (§5.10.2).
- Whether a PDF's optional content that is switched off still reaches pdf.js 4.10.38's text layer (and so a pick); unit
  23 adds a fixture with a hidden layer and records what a pick and `text()` hold before the Board's drawing relies on
  it.
- Where real password-protected Office files put their compound-file directory, and so whether 64 KB is enough (unit
  26's fixtures, from Office's own "Encrypt with password" on the owner's files).
- How near Word's rendered breaks sit to the real page breaks in the owner's own DOCX files (unit 23's bench).
- Whether JPEG 2000 draws under `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` on the matrix's iPads (D2, D3). (That pdf.js 4.10.38's legacy build
  defines `Promise.withResolvers` was read in its package: both `legacy/build/pdf.min.mjs` and `pdf.worker.min.mjs`
  define it.)
- Whether the venue's Stagewatch links are `https:`; a confidential line is refused over `http:` (§5.9.10).
- Whether ZIP64 appears in the owner's machine-written Office files, and the real sizes behind the archive bounds
  (unit 22's fixtures from the owner's own files).
- The Windows mark-of-the-web zone for files downloaded from a LAN address, and so Office's macro block.
- Whether iOS Safari takes a form POST's attachment into its downloads, honours `filename*` for a non-Latin name, and
  keeps the page on a 204 (D2, D3 and D6 of the walk).
- Which iPadOS the owner's oldest iPad runs (D1), whether any of the owner's devices is below Safari 16.4 or Chrome
  103, and whether Samsung Internet fires `contextmenu` on a long press (D5): the walk.
- Stagewatch's receipt words for `message`, and whether it refuses an identical message as changing nothing.

## 4-Critiques not taken

- **Web pages kept off `stage.show`, or under a separate `stage.web`** (security 5): not taken in revision 1, **taken in
  revision 2** by the owner's answer 10. `web` needs `stage.web`, a right of its own, for every pusher.
- **Locked-hall guests narrowed to `canShow`** (security 6's recommended branch): not taken. §2.6 and owner question 1
  keep them in `canPush`, without `web` unless the admin's setting for the hall allows it (S4); the draft's table row
  is corrected instead, and the two layers stop any information push from touching the show.
- **Undo as a server verb that re-issues a stored take** (security 3): taken in another form. Re-pushing older content
  is itself a defect (it re-shows what the Board closed, stage-ux 5), so Undo becomes Take down with `ifSeq`, which needs
  no content back.
- **`proposal.line` kept only in the server's follow record** (security 12): taken in another form. The restart
  re-follow compares lines (`notOurs`, `server.js:2107`), so the message keeps a MAC of the line rather than nothing.
- **PDF invisible text left out of picks** (security 15): not taken. Render mode 3 is how a scanned PDF carries its
  OCR words; the bar's exact preview is the guard.
- **U+200C and U+200D dropped by `cleanBlock`** (security 17): not taken for those two. They join letters in Persian and
  Indic scripts and build emoji sequences; U+061C, U+200B, U+2060 and U+FEFF are dropped.
- **Snippet text sealed at rest** (security, missing): not taken; the reason is written in §5.9.4, and §5.14 says the
  confidential mark is not encryption either.
- **A list of the accounts that gained `stage.show` on upgrade** (security, missing): not taken as a new page. Every
  Staff, Tech, Senior and Manager account gains it, and Tech, Senior and Manager `stage.web`, which the CHANGELOG says in
  one line; the Accounts page shows it per account.
- **Trusted Types as an owner question** (security, missing): moved to left for later; it is an engineering choice.
- **Two copies of the zip check with a parity test** (consistency 8): taken in another form. One core,
  `public/zipcore.js`, is shared by the server and the worker, and the parity test stays for the two byte readers.
- **"The map is `'p' + spanId`"** (consistency 30): corrected, not taken as stated. `getPageObjId()` already returns
  `` `p${ref}` ``, so the span's id and the struct tree's are the same string (§5.9.6); the gap is closed.
- **"The speaker now" matched by name** (stage-ux 34): left for later. Matching a Stagewatch speaker's name to a seat is
  a guess while presenters and board members share one seat (design question 3 kept its default); the To list names
  each person On stage.
- **Pages of a server file pushed as `doc` by default, to spare the upload bucket** (stage-ux 10's first option): taken
  in another form by the owner's answer 11. Neither is a default: the picture and the document sit side by side, the
  bar keeps the researcher's last choice, and the page retries a refused upload with words.
- **A Word layout engine for exact page numbers**: not taken. None runs in the browser within the vendored set, and
  Word's own breaks with "≈" where they are missing answer the owner's "preferable" (§5.10.4).

Revision 3 (the security and fidelity critiques of revision 2), one line each:

- Security 2, only 📝 for confidential lines until Stagewatch 2.20: not taken (owner: "options for both"); S6, which the
  owner kept.

# Part 5: AGMessage 0.6.0, addendum: speed and stability, modules, the experience, and right-click menus

*`060/addendum-arch-ux.md`, 2429 lines, kept whole. Its headings carry the prefix `5-`; its units carry their global number, [#n] (Part 0 §0.3).*

Paths are relative to the repository's root, and `app/...` is the server and its pages. Line numbers are from the tree
at `4483f08` (0.5.1, unit 4.7); `main` at `89104d8` carries the same `app/`. Each site is also named by its function.
Where this addendum and the code disagreed, the code was read and the code wins.

The owner's asks, verbatim:

- (C) "Consider the latest gaming, messaging, sever, and communication software coding and architecture for speed and
  stability."
- (D) "Consider abstraction and modularity."
- (E) "Research and implement user experience and ease of workflow. Use your enabled design skills and plugins to create
  a simple but rich and efficient service."
- (F) "Make good use of right click menu's"

**This revision (2026-10-27)** applies the owner's answers to this addendum's questions 21–33 (Owner's answers, below):

- 21, 23–28 and 30–32 take the plan's defaults;
- 22 (a mixture of Board devices) adds §15.10 and unit M. They join this addendum's parts to the stage addendum's
  answer to 22: its §5.15 matrix, its smoke legs, its ES2020 fence and its walk (unit T there, in its revision 4 of
  2026-10-27);
- 29 (no 0.5.2) puts every lettered unit in 0.6.0;
- 33 (remote phones in unknown numbers) lands unit 32 without waiting for a reading, and adds unit X (for the unknown
  count) and a new reading 7.

The code it adds to the record was read on `main` at `89104d8`, whose `app/` is the same tree. §13.3.8, §15.10, units M
and X and reading 7 have had no review of their own yet.

The evidence class is the owner's list and answers, the code read at `4483f08` (and at `89104d8` for this revision),
measurements on a VM, a browser walk, and web research:

- **Measured** on a 4-vCPU Linux VM (ext4 on virtio; Node 24.22.1, socket.io 4.8.4, engine.io 6.6.11, ws 8.22.0). The
  server was started as `app/test/helpers.js:18-37` starts it, on a throwaway data folder; the pages were real
  socket.io-client pages in worker threads; CPU was read from `/proc/<pid>/stat`, and one run was `--cpu-prof`'d.
  **Only rows recorded in `060/bench/fanout-results.jsonl` are quoted as numbers.** A row the record does not hold is
  marked "not reproduced", and reading 0 (§13.4) reruns the bench with a fixed count before any unit quotes it.
- **Walked** in headless Chromium at phone (390×844, 2×, touch), tablet (1024×768, touch) and desktop (1440×900) sizes,
  in both themes, one browser context per person: a Board presenter, a Board member, a researcher, an observer, the
  admin.
- **Judged** with the design skills' methods: heuristics with severities 0-4, journey maps per persona, an interface
  inventory, a copy deck, and WCAG 2.2 AA in five layers.
- **Researched** from games, messengers, Socket.IO, Node, browsers and accessibility practice, 2024-2026, each source
  cited where it is used. For this revision:
  - the browsers' versions are MDN's compatibility data (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data), read file by file
    and cited where each is used;
  - the tunnel's limits are Cloudflare's own pages;
  - mobile addressing is the IETF's RFCs.
- **Reviewed** by three critiques of the draft (a design council, engineering, scope against the final stage addendum).
  Each upheld defect was checked against the code or the research before it was fixed; the few not taken are listed at
  the end.
- **Not run** on the show laptop (Windows, with Defender), on a Board member's device, or through a Cloudflare tunnel.
  Every number that needs one names its reading (§13.4) or its walk (§15.10) and what it triggers. File-system numbers
  here are lower bounds for the laptop.
- The scripts are in the scratch folder's `060/bench`, `060/mod`, `060/ux` and `060/menus-bench`. None ships.

The rules this addendum keeps: no feature without a job; no limit or governor without a measured cause and a
deterministic test; no rewrite where a move will do; removing a cost beats governing it.

## 5-§13. Speed and stability

### 5-§13.1 What 0.5.1 already does as games and messengers do (kept)

- **Sequence numbers and resume.**
  - There is a per-room seq, a ring of 2,000 ops and `opsSince` (`lib/store.js:7-11`, `:23`, `:163-169`), with the
    page's `bump` and `rejoin` (`app/public/app.js:94-169`).
  - This is the Discord gateway's resume from the last sequence number
    (https://docs.discord.com/developers/docs/topics/gateway).
  - Measured after a watchdog restart: 100 of 100 pages that had missed nothing resumed with ops (135 bytes, 2-3 ms).
    The boot's "Session restored" op (`server.js:2487`) keeps the ring covering the gap.
- **Latest wins for state.**
  - The halls board is ticked at 300 ms (`server.js:1740-1767`) and memoised per seq (`lib/board.js:49-61`).
  - Screens are coalesced at 150 ms (`:1714-1729`).
  - Stagewatch's view is published only when it changes (`lib/nodes.js:574-581`).
  - This is the snapshot model: send the newest state, never a backlog
    (https://gafferongames.com/post/state_synchronization/).
- **Interest management.** There is an io room per hall, a board filtered per watcher (`:1749-1761`), and a screen told
  only its own take. Slack sends presence only for the users on screen (https://slack.engineering/real-time-messaging/).
- **Crash-only recovery.**
  - The pieces are the op log, atomic snapshots, the watchdog's exit codes and backoff (`app/supervise.js`,
    `lib/resilience.js:12-60`), and `guardHandlers` (`server.js:644-665`)
    (https://www.usenix.org/conference/hotos-ix/crash-only-software).
  - Measured: a kill is back to "is running" in 2.3-2.8 s, and every page is back without a reload.
- **A slow page is bounded by the heartbeat** (`pingInterval` 10 s, `pingTimeout` 8 s, `:617-618`: 18 s). Measured with
  a page whose reads were paused while four senders posted 16 messages/s of 1.5 KB: it was cut after 17.3 s, and RSS rose
  96 → 118 MB, then stayed flat.

### 5-§13.2 What was measured

"Recorded" means the row is in `bench/fanout-results.jsonl`. "Printed" means the script printed it and no file kept it;
reading 0 records it again.

| # | Finding | Measured | Where | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
