### 5-§13.3 What 0.6.0 adopts

#### 5-§13.3.1 One latest-wins primitive (unit C)

- **`lib/latest.js`**, pure: `new Latest({name, delayMs, flush, merge, schedule})`, with `mark(key, value)`,
  `flushNow()` and `stats()`.
  - **At most one flush per `delayMs`.** A mark after a quiet window flushes on the next turn (a zero-delay timer), so
    a single change is sent at once. Marks inside the window fold into one flush at its end, with `merge(prev, next)`
    (default: the newer). So a burst costs at most two frames per window.
  - `flush(map)` gets every key marked since the last flush. A flush callback skips keys whose room no longer exists.
  - `schedule` is `{setTimeout, clearTimeout}`, injected. Its timers are `unref()`'d where they can be, as today's
    screens timer and board interval are (`server.js:1728`, `:1767`).
  - `stats()` is `{marks, flushes}`. Health appends `latest: {board, screens, people, seen, …}`, so the laptop shows
    what coalescing saves, as `WriteLane.coalesced` does for saves.
- **It never drops.** No volatile emit is used: the last change is always delivered, and the heartbeat bounds a slow page
  (§13.1).
- **Its users:**
  - the two that exist, moved onto it: the board (300 ms; today a 300 ms interval polling a flag, `:1762-1767`) and
    screens (150 ms, `:1714-1729`);
  - new: people (100 ms, §13.3.2) and seen (1,000 ms, §13.3.3);
  - from their first commit: `pages:changed` (150 ms, §5.3, unit 17) and `rooms:activity` (500 ms, §3.4, unit 21).
- **Why one:** four hand-written variants of one rule would become six. One tested primitive keeps "latest wins, never a
  backlog" true in every new frame.
- **The fence (o):** `test/resilience.test.js` counts `setTimeout(` and `setInterval(` over `handlerFiles()` (server.js
  and `lib/handlers/*`), each with its reason, as it counts synchronous calls. The count is set at unit C's commit; a new
  hand-written tick moves it, with its words.

#### 5-§13.3.2 No per-message deflate, and the people list once per window (unit C)

- **Deflate off:** `server.js:619` reads `perMessageDeflate: false`. HTTP long-polling keeps `httpCompression`
  (engine.io's default). Socket.IO ships deflate off because it "is known to add a significant overhead in terms of
  performance and memory consumption" (https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-options/). With it off, one pre-built frame is
  written to every socket of a broadcast (F1).
- **The people list:** `emitUsers` (`:253-259`) marks the room on a `Latest` of 100 ms.
  - The flush keeps today's split: one broadcast without links, and the admins' own copies.
  - `join` (`:809`), `admin:setRole` (`:1481`) and `leaveRoom` (`:1632`) only mark.
- **The two land together.** Deflate off alone puts the join storm on the wire (290 MB at 200 pages, recorded).
- **Measured** (`fanout.js` against the tree and the variant copies `bench/app-*`; recorded rows only):

| Pages, 10 messages/s | CPU per message | CPU per delivery | Delivery p50 / p99 | RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100, today → deflate off | 16.2 → 2.8 ms | 162 → 28 µs | 10.2 / 24.1 → 2.2 / 6.4 ms | 253 → 118 MB |
| 100, `serverNoContextTakeover` (so the threshold works) | 5.3 ms | 53 µs | 2.7 / 7.3 ms | 268 MB |
| 200, today → deflate off | not usable today (the idle baseline overlapped the storm's tail) → 4.0 ms | → 20 µs | 15.2 / 30.9 → 2.8 / 6.5 ms | 531 → 126 MB |
| 25 | not reproduced | | | |

| Join storm | Server CPU | People-list bytes parsed | On the wire | RSS |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 pages, today | 2.73 s | 27.8 MB | 1.0 MB | 211 MB |
| 100 pages, deflate off | 0.41 s | 35.0 MB | 37.2 MB | 116 MB |
| 200 pages, today | at least 4.13 s | at least 49 MB (the count stopped 1.5 s after the last join's answer) | 2.1 MB | 503 MB |
| 200 pages, deflate off | 1.24 s | 279 MB | 290 MB | 124 MB |
| deflate off, people coalesced | not reproduced | | | |

- **The middle setting was measured and refused:** with `serverNoContextTakeover` a delivery still costs 53 µs, and RSS
  is 268 MB at 100 pages.
- **The trade-off this owns:** a first open of a large hall goes uncompressed (1.37 MB at 5,000 messages, against
  112 KB). On the venue LAN that is milliseconds; through the tunnel to a phone on mobile data it is not.
  - Remote phones do join that way, in numbers nobody knows (owner answer 33). So unit 32 bounds the first open in
    0.6.0, with no reading first.
  - Its 200 messages are about 55 KB at F8's size per message (computed from F8's printed 1.37 MB for 5,000, not
    measured).
- **Tests:** a handshake answers no `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`. During 30 joins, each page receives at most
  `ceil(elapsed / 100 ms) + 1` `users` frames over the joins' span, and its last holds all 30 people.
- **Before the papers quote a number,** reading 0 reruns the bench with the fixed count (§13.4).

#### 5-§13.3.3 Seen receipts: one frame per room per second (unit C)

- The `seen` handler (`server.js:905-914`) updates `room.seen`, which is already latest per person, and marks the room
  on a `Latest` of 1,000 ms.
- The flush emits one `seen {seen: [{uid, name, role, seq}…]}` per room, holding the entries changed since the last
  frame.
- The page (`app.js:255`) applies the batch, then calls `refreshSeenLines` once. The join answer's `seen` (`:803`) is
  unchanged. A page cached across the upgrade reads the new frame as one with no `uid`, and ignores it.
- **Cause:** N² frames per message when messages are sparse (F3), each refiltering every page.
- **The trade-off:** a receipt after a burst may show up to 1 s later; a lone message's receipts go at once (the
  leading flush).
- **Test:** 20 pages report within one second; each page receives at most two `seen` frames in it, whose entries
  together hold the 20.

#### 5-§13.3.4 A send never vanishes and never doubles (unit Q)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§13.3.4: Got it leaves `self`; `pin:mine` is `hold`; `message {also}` is `now`).

**The client: `public/outbox.js`** (a classic script, `AGM.outbox`), loaded by app.html, admin.html and halls.html. Every
write goes through it, in its catalogue entry's mode (§16.2):

- **`hold`: what a person wrote or answered.** `message` of every type (text, file, action prompt, help), `room:send`
  and `forward` (through Send to ▸), `actionResponse`, and `help:respond`.
  - Each send gets a `cid` of 16 random bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues`, as base64url (22 characters).
    `crypto.randomUUID()` is not used: it exists only in secure contexts, and a page on the venue LAN over plain HTTP is
    not one.
  - It draws a local echo marked "◷ sending" (an answer: the chosen option marked ◷).
  - It is held while the page is disconnected or not yet joined, and sent after the join answer. After a reconnect it is
    sent again with the same `cid`, until it is answered.
  - On ok, the echo becomes the server's message, matched by `cid` on the broadcast, in the resumed ops or in the
    history.
  - On a refusal, the text stays and the server's words show, with **Retry** and **Edit**.
  - **No time limit.** A held item is sent when the connection is back, however long it waited. It carries `heldMs`,
    the page's own monotonic count since it was written (at most 24 h), and the server keeps it on the message as
    `held` (whole seconds). Every reader then sees "written 14:02 · sent 14:06 (offline)", the halls board's help strip
    included, so a five-minute-old "Sound" request reads as one. The sender is not asked first, however long the wait
    (owner answer 27).
  - **A reload keeps it.** Held items are kept in `sessionStorage` (in `try`), keyed by the room and the person's uid.
    After a reload (the page's own, after `account:changed` or `roleChanged`), items for this room and this uid come
    back as "◷ waiting" echoes and are sent with their `cid`. Items for another uid are discarded, never sent as someone
    else. `kicked` clears them. They never outlive the tab.
  - **A file is held in memory only.** A reload drops it, and its echo says "Not sent — choose the file again". An upload
    refused because its token was reissued at a join (`server.js:785-790`) or its provenance was lost in a restart
    (design unit 13) is uploaded once more.
- **`now`: what a person does to something.** Pin, react, delete, withdraw, `page:push`, `display:take`, `stage:send`,
  `stage:propose`, and the admin's acts.
  - It is disabled while offline: "Not connected — AGMessage is reconnecting."
  - It waits 5 s for the ack, else "No answer — check the connection."
  - It is sent again with the same `cid` only when the connection dropped while it was in flight.
- **`self`: what a person does on their own page.** Back to chat, Minimise, Show again, Remove, Got it. It acts at once.
  Its `page:report` is queued, latest wins per seq and layer, and sent after the join answer.
- **`local`: nothing on the wire.** Look, Download, Copy, Open in a new tab, text size, theme.

**The server:**

- **`buildMessage`** (`:1808-1834`) keeps `cid`, read with `guard.str`: at most 40 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; any
  other shape is refused with words. An absent `cid` is allowed, so a page cached across the upgrade still sends. It
  keeps `heldMs` as `held`: an integer 0-86,400,000 ms, else refused ("That message's wait could not be read").
- **The store keeps `byCid`**, in `_apply` beside `byId` (`lib/store.js:100-127`), so the one writer keeps every index:
  - `add` maps `uid:cid` to `{id, seq}`;
  - `del` and `reset` keep a tombstone: the message's `id` and, when it had one, its `uid:cid`;
  - the snapshot keeps the newest 500 tombstones as `gone`, so a restart keeps them (0.5.1 ignores the key and drops it
    at its own next compaction);
  - a repeat of a live `cid` answers the original `{ok, id, seq}` and commits nothing; a repeat of a tombstoned one
    answers `{ok: true, id, seq, gone: true}`, and the echo goes with "That message was removed."
  - This is the transaction-id rule of Matrix: the server "should return the same HTTP response code and content as the
    original request" (https://spec.matrix.org/latest/client-server-api/).
- **Every repeatable verb answers a repeat with the original answer, or with ok and `already`, never with a refusal for
  something that succeeded:**
  - `room:send` (§4.2) keeps `cid` on S's copy: a repeat answers the original `{ok, id, seq, to}` and writes nothing
    into T;
  - `page:push` (§5.3) keeps the last 200 `by:cid` answers per hall, in memory; after a restart a repeat is a new take of
    the same content, which latest wins makes harmless, and `docs/DISPLAYS.md` says so;
  - `react` gains `on`, a boolean: given, it sets the reaction; absent, it toggles, as today's pages expect;
  - `delete` of an id in the tombstones, and `room:withdraw` of a copy already withdrawn, answer `{ok: true, already:
    true}`;
  - `pin` carries `pinned`, and `actionResponse` keeps one response per person: both are already safe.

**Why:**

- Socket.IO is at most once. At least once needs retries plus server dedupe
  (https://socket.io/docs/v4/delivery-guarantees, https://socket.io/docs/v4/tutorial/step-8).
- Pins, reactions and prompt answers have no answer handler today (`app.js:566`, `:695`, `:1853`). The help request is
  the only path that shows a refusal (`:1953-1957`).
- WhatsApp shows a clock until a message is sent (https://faq.whatsapp.com/665923838265756/). "Attempts are not facts"
  holds on the sender's own screen.

**Tests:**

- `inputs.test.js`: `NULLS` gain `cid`, `on` and `heldMs`; `UNCONVERTIBLE` gains `cid: U` and `heldMs: U`.
- `units.test.js`: `byCid` across `add`, `del`, `reset`, compaction and a reload; the 500 tombstones; a 0.5.1 snapshot
  without `gone` loads.
- A `vm` test loads `outbox.js` with a `crypto` that has `getRandomValues` only, as an insecure page has, and gets a
  22-character `cid`.
- End to end:
  - the same `cid` twice commits once and answers the same `{ok, id, seq}`, also after a restart;
  - a deleted message's `cid` repeated answers `gone` and commits nothing;
  - a `cid` or `heldMs` of the wrong shape is refused with words;
  - `react {on: true}` twice leaves one reaction; a second `delete` answers `already`;
  - `room:send` repeated writes one message into T.
- Smoke:
  - drop the socket, send, reconnect: the message lands once, and the composer empties only after the ok;
  - a refusal keeps the text and shows the words with Retry;
  - a reload with a held send: it lands once;
  - `kicked` with a held send: nothing is sent;
  - a help request held for a minute reads "written … · sent …" on the item and on the halls board.

#### 5-§13.3.5 Pages come back by themselves (unit B)

- **A refused connection is retried at the pace the server gives.**
  - The middleware (`server.js:622-632`) refuses with `err.data = {retryMs}`, where `retryMs = max(waitMs, 1000) +
    randomInt(0, 2000)`: the measured policy of F5, never sooner than the bucket's next token. `guard.Bucket` gains
    `waitMs(n = 1, now)`, the time until it holds `n` tokens, with a unit test (`lib/guard.js:84-95` has only `level`
    and `take`). The HTTPS refusal carries `{retry: false}`.
  - Without the jitter, every page behind one address would get the same 0.33 s (the bucket's 3/s) and retry together.
  - `app.js`, `halls.js` and `admin.js` handle `connect_error`: when `!socket.active` and `retry !== false`, a strip
    reads "Busy — trying again in 3 s", with the real seconds rounded up, and `socket.connect()` runs after `retryMs`.
  - **`display.js` retries silently.** An audience-facing screen never shows "Busy"; it keeps its last take and its
    stale-clock rule. Today it shows only the HTTPS refusal (`display.js:253`).
  - Cause F5. The refusal's own words ("wait a moment") promise a retry that never happens.
- **Back sooner after a drop.**
  - Every page's `io()` (`app.js:89` and the others) sets `reconnectionDelay: 500` and `reconnectionDelayMax: 2000`,
    keeping the jitter of 0.5. Cause F6: p95 4.74 → 1.80 s, at the cost of 201 failed handshakes against 126 while the
    server was down.
  - On `visibilitychange` to visible, and on `online`, a page that is not connected runs `socket.disconnect();
    socket.connect()`. A plain `socket.connect()` does nothing while the manager waits out its backoff
    (`socket.io-client/build/cjs/socket.js:193-202`, `if (!this.io["_reconnecting"]) this.io.open()`);
    `disconnect()` clears the backoff's timer (`manager.js:331-335`, `:346-364`) and `open()` starts afresh.
- **Saying so.** In the full view, after 2 s down, a strip reads "Reconnecting… what you write waits here until we're
  back." It clears on the join answer. In the Board's simple view the dot gains the words "Offline · reconnecting"
  after 5 s down, with no strip and no motion (§15.5).
- **A restart announces nobody.**
  - During `BOOT_SEAT_MS` (`server.js:277`), a join that carries an integer `since` between 0 and `room.seq` counts as
    `returning`, so no "joined as" line is written (`:808`). The restart line already says what happened.
  - This concerns presence words only; no right hangs on it.
  - Cause: one restart added one "joined" line per page (F6), each a broadcast and a line in the room's history.
- **The watchdog's first restart waits 0.5 s instead of 2 s** (`lib/resilience.js:31`; the ladder becomes 0.5, 4, 8,
  15, 30 s, and six crashes in ten minutes still give up). This is decided by a test, not by the owner: the Windows job
  kills the server 20 times and each restart must find the port and the folder lock free and print "is running". Until
  it passes 20 of 20, the 2 s step stays. A port still held would exit with code 3, which stops the watchdog for good,
  so the test is the gate.
- **Tests:**
  - `units.test.js`: `Bucket.waitMs`; `SupervisorPolicy`'s first step.
  - End to end: a socket refused by a drained bucket carries `retryMs` within `[1000, 3000 + waitMs]`; the HTTPS refusal
    carries `retry: false`.
  - `resilience.test.js`: a 3-page hall restarted gets no new "joined" lines, and a join without `since` in the boot
    window is still announced.
  - Smoke (page code): a refused page comes back without a reload; the strip shows after 2 s down and clears on the
    answer; a hidden-then-visible page reconnects at once.

#### 5-§13.3.6 Health reads true, and keeps the readings (unit R)

- **The loop's delay:** `server.js:159-162` pushes `max(0, p99 − 10 ms)`, the sampler's own resolution taken off.
- **Appended to `/api/health`'s detail**, at the end:
  - `elu` per 5 s window (`performance.eventLoopUtilization(prev)`) and `rssMb`;
  - `maxSocketsPerAddress` and `tunnelSockets`, from the open sockets' `socket.data.ip` and `socket.data.viaTunnel`.
    The socket count itself is already `clients` (`server.js:488`);
  - `largestHall: {messages, kb}`. `compact` keeps the snapshot's length as `room.snapKb` when it writes it (it does not
    today), so no fs call is added;
  - `latest` (§13.3.1) and `saves.built` (§14.4 e);
  - **`peaks`**, per day for the last 14 days: `{day, loopMs, elu, socketsPerAddress, tunnelSockets, hallMessages,
    hallKb, joinBurst, compactMs, auditPutMs, at}`, and `pageHiddenMs` from unit 17.
- **The peaks survive the day.** In memory they would be lost to a crash, a restart or the laptop shutting down: the day
  they are for. They are saved in `data/peaks.json` through a `peaks` lane named in `saveLanes()`, latest wins, flushed
  at stop and crash. One look after a show is the reading.
- **Readings 3 and 4 are taken in place, so no bench ships:**
  - `auditPutMs`: `lib/audit.js` times `_put()` (open, write, fsync, close, `:131-153`), which already runs an fsync per
    batch on the show laptop. It is an upper bound on an fdatasync per append to an open file.
  - `compactMs`: `RoomStore` times `compact()` with the room's message count, the stall of F9 on that disk, Defender
    included.
  - `joinBurst`: the most joins one hall took in one 5 s window.
- **The admin page** (`admin-plus.js:67`) reads "loop delay p95 X ms · busy Y % · today's peaks …".
- **Cause F7:** an idle server is shown as "server delay p95 13 ms". ELU is the complementary reading
  (https://nodejs.org/api/perf_hooks.html).
- **Tests:** `units.test.js`: the transform `max(0, p99 − resolution)` on a fake histogram; the per-day peaks and their
  14-day bound. End to end (`server.test.js:255`): the new keys are present (no timing is asserted end to end: the first
  window holds boot work, and CI runs under coverage); after a restart, today's peak is still there.

#### 5-§13.3.7 Compaction trusts its own snapshot, and the papers say what a power cut can lose (unit D)

- **The snapshot's state:** `RoomStore` keeps `room.snapWhole`: true after a successful `compact`, and after a load
  whose main snapshot parsed; false after a load that fell back to `.bak`.
- **The atomic write:** `writeFileAtomic` (`lib/resilience.js:83-88`) takes `knownWhole`. With it, the old file is
  copied to `.bak` without being read and parsed. No synchronous call is added, so the caps hold. Unit H also edits
  `lib/resilience.js` (its cap from 10 to 11, `folderId`); whichever lands second rebases on the other.
- **Cause F9:** the re-read is 13.4 of the 31 ms stall at 5,000 messages, and 42.9 of 128 ms at 20,000.
- **The words:**
  - `README.md:23` and `README.txt:158-159`: "a crash of AGMessage or of a browser loses nothing; a power cut can lose
    the last few seconds";
  - `lib/store.js:15`: "an acknowledged message is in the system's file cache".
  - The medical rule "nothing claimed that was not observed" (`docs/DESIGN.md:5`) applies to the papers too.
- **Test:** `units.test.js`: a torn main file is still parsed before it may replace a good `.bak`; a known-whole save
  copies without reading; a load from `.bak` clears `snapWhole`.

#### 5-§13.3.8 Remote phones through the tunnel: bounds that say what they refused (unit X)

Owner answer 33: remote phones join through the tunnel on mobile data, in numbers nobody knows. X is for that unknown
count. What the code does today:

- **The tunnel is a Quick Tunnel.**
  - `startTunnel` runs `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<PORT>` (`server.js:2336`) and reads a
    `trycloudflare.com` address from its output (`:2316`, `:2346`).
  - Cloudflare: "Each Quick Tunnel supports up to 200 in-flight requests. Additional requests return a `429` response",
    and "Quick Tunnels are for testing and development"
    (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/).
  - A refusal there never reaches the server: no words, and no count.
  - Pages connect WebSocket first (`app.js:89`, `halls.js:258`, `display.js:224`), so each tunnel page holds a request
    open for as long as it lives. Cloudflare's page does not say whether an open WebSocket counts as in flight; reading
    0's tunnel row measures it (§13.4).
- **A tunnel page is keyed by its own address.**
  - cloudflared connects from loopback, and `guard.clientIp` takes Cloudflare's `CF-Connecting-IP` only then, as
    `cf:<address>` (`lib/guard.js:147-153`).
  - Cloudflare: the header "provides the client IP address connecting to Cloudflare to the origin web server"
    (https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/http-headers/).
- **The per-address bounds that exist:**
  - connections: 3 a second, bursts of 30, per key, "tunnels included" (`server.js:622-632`);
  - wrong codes at `join`: 10 a minute (`joinLock`, `:634`, `:711`, `:721`, `:746`);
  - room lookups: 2 a second, and 12 misses a minute (`lookupBuckets` and `lookupLock`, `:505-511`, `:526`).
- **Their faults, read in the code:**
  - **A flood of new addresses resets every bucket.**
    - `connBuckets` clears all its keys once it holds more than 5,000 (`server.js:627`), and `lookupBuckets` does the
      same (`:510`). So 5,000 new addresses hand every drained bucket its burst back.
    - `guard.Buckets` was written to prevent exactly that: "a flood of new keys never hands back the allowance of a key
      that has used its own" (`lib/guard.js:97-116`). It is used only for sign-ins (`lib/http-accounts.js:27`).
    - Through the tunnel, new addresses cost little.
  - **An IPv6 phone has a /64 of addresses.**
    - A 3GPP network "allocates each default bearer a unique /64 prefix" (RFC 6459 §5.2,
      https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6459).
    - A host's temporary addresses change within its prefix (RFC 8981, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8981).
    - Keyed by the full address, one phone can step out of every per-address bound.
  - **One IPv4 address on mobile data is often many phones.**
    - Behind a carrier's address sharing, "one user who fails a number of login attempts may block out other users"
      (RFC 6269 §13.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6269).
    - So one guesser's wrong codes lock `join` for a minute for every phone behind that address (`server.js:711`), and a
      crowd behind one address shares 3 connections a second.
  - **Nothing bounds the tunnel as a whole, and nothing sets it apart from the venue.** A tunnel socket and a venue
    socket are counted together (`clients`, `server.js:488`).
  - **The refusals say little, and nothing counts them.**
    - A refused connection carries "Too many connections — wait a moment." (`:631`), which no page shows (unit B).
    - The join lock's "Too many attempts — wait a minute." (`:711`) names no cause.

**What 0.6.0 adds (unit X):**

- **One key per network.**
  - `guard.limitKey(ip)` (pure, in `lib/guard.js`) is the key every per-address bound uses.
  - A `cf:` IPv6 address is cut to its /64 (`cf6:2001:db8:1:2::/64`). A `cf:` IPv4 address and every venue address are
    kept whole: a venue's IPv6 LAN is one /64 for every device on it, so the cut is for tunnel keys only.
  - `socket.data.ip` and the audit rows keep the full address.
- **Buckets that are never reset.**
  - `connBuckets` (3 a second, burst 30) and `lookupBuckets` (2 a second, burst 10) become `guard.Buckets`, capped at
    5,000 keys and trimming the fullest first, and keyed by `limitKey`.
  - `joinLock` and `lookupLock` are keyed by `limitKey` too.
  - Unit B's `waitMs` lands on `Buckets`, per key.
  - The sign-in's own buckets keep the full address. A tunnel sign-in's lockout is already per name for the whole
    tunnel (`lib/http-accounts.js:95`).
- **The tunnel's places (the global bound).**
  - At most `TUNNEL_MAX` sockets come through the tunnel at once. A socket is through the tunnel when its key is `cf:`.
    The bound is `envNumber('AGM_TUNNEL_MAX', 150)`, the helper of `server.js:57`, so a test sets it small.
  - **Its cause is Cloudflare's 200 in-flight requests.** 150 keeps 50 for page loads, files and uploads. A hall page
    asks for 7 files today (`app.html:7-8`, `:235-238`, and the page itself), and 0.6.0 adds four scripts.
  - If reading 0's tunnel row shows that an open WebSocket does not count against the 200, the ceiling is instead the
    largest count reading 0's fan-out records with delivery p99 under 50 ms. The papers say which cause set it.
  - **The venue never waits for the tunnel.** The places count tunnel sockets only, and no venue socket is refused
    because the tunnel is full.
  - A screen (`/d/`) through the tunnel takes a place like any page.
- **One network's share (a per-address bound).**
  - One tunnel key holds at most half the places (75 of 150).
  - The cause: the places are a new shared resource, and one address could fill them at 3 connections a second. Half
    leaves the rest for every other network, and still seats up to 75 phones behind one carrier's address.
- **A place is for a page in a room.**
  - A tunnel socket is closed and counted when, within 20 s, it has neither joined a room nor carries an account, the
    admin's token or a screen's token. The wait is `AGM_TUNNEL_JOIN_MS` for the test.
  - A hall page joins as soon as it connects (`app.js:92-95`), so 20 s leaves a wide margin.
  - It is one timer per tunnel socket in `server.js`, so fence (o)'s count moves by one, with its words.
- **Each refusal says what it refused:** to the page in `err.data = {retryMs, why}` (unit B shows `why` in its strip
  and retries), and on the admin page, in health and in the log.

| Bound | Counted per | The page's words | `retryMs` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Connections (3 a second, burst 30) | network | "Busy — many phones are connecting from your network. Trying again in 3 s." (on the venue: "Busy — trying again in 3 s.") | unit B's: `max(waitMs, 1000) + randomInt(0, 2000)` |
| One network's share | network | "Many phones from your network are already connected through the internet (75). Trying again in 31 s." | `30000 + randomInt(0, 10000)` |
| The tunnel's places | the whole tunnel | "AGMessage's internet link is full (150 phones). Trying again in 34 s. On the venue's Wi-Fi there is room." | `30000 + randomInt(0, 10000)` |
| Not joined within 20 s | socket | none: a page that had not joined is a probe or a stuck page. A page that reconnects is counted afresh | — |
| Wrong codes at `join` (10 a minute) | network | through the tunnel: "Too many wrong codes from your network — wait a minute." (on the venue, today's words) | — (an answer to `join`, not a refusal at connect) |

- **Health** appends `tunnel: {places, max, share, networks, refused: {rate, share, full, idle, wrongCode}}`, which are
  today's counts, and `refused.venue.rate`.
  - `networks` is the number of keys holding places, never the addresses.
  - Unit R's `tunnelSockets` (in health and in `peaks`) then counts what the places count, the `cf:` keys, and `peaks`
    gains `tunnelRefused`. `maxSocketsPerAddress` and `peaks.socketsPerAddress` are kept per lane (`venue`, `tunnel`).
- **The admin page's tunnel card** (`admin.html:149`) reads "Internet link: 37 of 150 places · 12 networks · refused
  today: 4 full, 1 one network's share". Its acts are unit 3b's catalogue rows.
- **The log:** at most one line a minute while refusing, for example "[tunnel] refused 12 in the last minute: 10 full,
  2 one network's share". There is no audit row: a refusal is no person's act, and health holds the counts.
- **The link, checked before the show** (reading 7's number):
  - When the tunnel's address appears (`server.js:2346`), the server fetches its own address's `/api/health` five
    times, one at a time, each with a 5 s deadline (`AbortSignal.timeout`, so no timer is added). `/api/health` answers
    anyone the base facts (`server.js:485-489`).
  - It does the same when `admin:tunnelStatus` is asked (`server.js:1626`; the admin page asks on load, `admin.js:554`)
    more than 60 s after the last check. The answer is at once, with the last check, and the new one arrives on
    `tunnel:status` (`broadcastTunnelStatus`, `server.js:2318-2321`), whose payload appends `check: {at, ok, p50Ms,
    maxMs, words}` at the end.
  - The card reads "Checked 14:02 · round trip 85 ms (max 140 ms)", or "△ The internet link did not answer: remote
    phones cannot join."
  - **Check again** is the catalogue's `tunnel.check` (verb `admin:tunnelStatus`, mode `now`). Within 60 s of the last
    check it is disabled with "Checked 20 s ago." No verb is added.
  - The request goes out to Cloudflare and back through cloudflared, so it measures the laptop's side of the link,
    never a phone's. The phone's side is reading 7's walk.
- **Tests:**
  - `units.test.js`:
    - `limitKey` cuts the full and the compressed forms of one `cf:` IPv6 address to the same /64; it keeps a `cf:`
      IPv4 address, a venue IPv4 address and a venue IPv6 address whole;
    - `Buckets` past its cap keeps a drained key drained (an injected `now`), and `waitMs` per key;
    - `guard.Places` (pure: `take(key)` answers `null`, `'share'` or `'full'`, and `drop(key)`) at a max of 4: two from
      one key, then `'share'`; four from four keys, then `'full'`; a drop frees one place.
  - End to end, with `AGM_TUNNEL_MAX=4` and `AGM_TUNNEL_JOIN_MS=300`, from 127.0.0.1 with `cf-connecting-ip` and
    `cf-ray`, as `test/sessions.test.js:18-23` builds its visitors:
    - a fifth tunnel socket is refused with the full words, `why: 'full'` and `retryMs` in [30000, 40000]; a venue
      socket still connects; health's `refused.tunnel.full` is 1;
    - a third socket from one network (`2001:db8:1:2::a`, `::b`, `::c`) is refused with the share words, while
      `2001:db8:1:3::a` connects;
    - a tunnel socket that never joins is closed after 300 ms and counted `idle`; one that joins stays; one with an
      account's cookie stays;
    - a place freed by a disconnect is taken by the next socket;
    - from one network in a burst, the 31st connection is refused with the rate words, and 5,001 other networks'
      connections do not refill its bucket;
    - eleven wrong codes through the tunnel answer "Too many wrong codes from your network — wait a minute.", and a
      venue address can still join;
    - with a local HTTP server standing in for the link's address, the check's facts arrive on `tunnel:status`, and a
      second ask within 60 s starts no new check.
  - Smoke (page code): a refused tunnel page shows the server's words in unit B's strip, and comes back by itself once
    a place frees.
  - `test/sessions.test.js:18`'s visitors (`2001:db8::<n>`) share one /64. The file makes 21 of them, inside the burst
    of 30 and the share of 75, so it is unchanged.

Health's `peaks` (unit R) are read on the show laptop after the next show or rehearsal. Each reading goes into a new
table in `docs/DESIGN.md`, **"Measured on the show laptop"**. Until its row is filled it says "not measured", which is a
fact in the papers, not a block.

There is no 0.5.2 (owner answer 29), so a reading is taken from a stamped 0.6.0 development build run at a rehearsal (R
lands first among the lettered units, so such a build carries the peaks), or from 0.6.0 at its first show. Unit 33 lands
in 0.6.0 when reading 3 comes before unit 34, and in 0.6.x otherwise. Every other change a reading triggers (readings

### 5-§13.5 Refused, and why

- **WebTransport** (Socket.IO 4.7+). It became Baseline only in March 2026 (Safari 26.4). It needs an HTTP/3 server
  through the native `@fails-components/webtransport` addon, UDP through venue firewalls, and a browser-trusted or
  hash-pinned certificate (https://socket.io/get-started/webtransport,
  https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransport_API). Venue round trips are milliseconds, chat rates
  are low, and head-of-line blocking has no measured cost.
- **Raw ws or uWebSockets.js instead of Socket.IO.** With deflate off, 200 pages cost 20 µs per delivery. Acks, rooms
  and the polling fallback are used everywhere, and uWS is a native binary outside npm. That is risk without a cause.
- **Joining in the handshake** (the join's facts in `auth`, so buffered emits land after the join). It would close F4's
  class for every emit, but every join refusal would become a middleware refusal, which destroys the socket (F5); the
  join answer would become an event instead of an ack; and every page and test that emits `join` would change. The
  outbox is needed anyway for the lost acknowledgement and for the sender's own screen, and the emits it does not carry
  (`seen`, `userState:*`) are already ignored before a join.
- **A binary or msgpack parser.** The payloads are small JSON; the measured costs were deflate and frame multiplicity,
  not encoding; the pages have no build step.
- **Worker threads for JSON or compaction.** Inbound frames are small. Handing the messages to a worker by structured
  clone costs about what stringify costs. Bounding the payload (unit 32) and skipping the re-parse (unit D) remove the
  cost instead.
- **A per-socket write-buffer cap or a backpressure governor.** A page that stops reading is cut by the heartbeat after
  17.3 s, measured at an extreme write rate. No cause.
- **Volatile emits for state frames.** Volatile drops the last change when the transport is busy, and nothing repairs it
  until the next change. A coalesced frame that is always delivered keeps the newest state without loss.
- **Socket.IO's `connectionStateRecovery`.** It keeps its state in memory, which the watchdog restart loses, and its
  `skipMiddlewares` weakens fail closed. AGMessage's own seq, ring and resume already cover restarts.
- **A Redis adapter, a cluster or several processes.** One show laptop, one process per data folder (the folder lock),
  and about 4 ms of CPU per message at 200 pages once deflate is off.
- **zstd or dictionary compression**, as Discord did with its own client
  (https://discord.com/blog/how-discord-reduced-websocket-traffic-by-40-percent). Browsers' WebSocket offers only
  permessage-deflate, and the fix here is fewer frames, not smaller ones.
- **`content-visibility: auto` alone.** It halved a first open (3,000 messages: 1,729 → 773 ms) but made live appends
  worse at 4× throttle (p95 233 → 651 ms). It is revisited only inside unit 32's window.
- **A per-room or per-room-pair governor** for `room:send` or anything else. No flood is measured, and the writes bucket
  (5/s, bursts of 15) already applies. This agrees with §4.5.
- **A shorter heartbeat.** The 18 s bound was measured adequate. Socket.IO warns that a small `pingTimeout` turns a
  brief server stall into a reconnection storm (https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-options/).
- **Delta-compressing the halls board.** Its frames are one row per hall, already ticked and memoised.
- **An fsync on every append now.** It cost 211 µs p50 here, and the laptop's number is unknown. Reading 3 comes first;
  meanwhile the words are made true (owner answer 28).
- **A global join rate for the tunnel** (unit X). Once unit 32 bounds the first open and unit C coalesces the people
  list, no measured cost of a join is left to govern. The places bound what is open, and reading 8 watches a doors-open
  storm.
- **A tighter share per network, or a cap of a few sockets per address.** A carrier's shared address seats many phones
  (RFC 6269 §13.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6269). A small cap would refuse a real crowd to stop an abuser
  that the share already bounds.
- **Reading the user agent to tell a phone on the tunnel from a laptop.** The bounds key on the network, and nothing in
  them is tuned to a device (owner answer 22).

### 5-§13.6 Against the design's new frames

- **§3.4 `rooms:activity`** is state: the newest seq per room. It goes on `Latest` at 500 ms, keyed by the room, with
  `merge = (a, b) => ({seq: Math.max(a.seq, b.seq), priority: a.priority || b.priority})`. A burst of ten messages is
  at most two frames to each watching socket, and a 🔥 inside it is never folded away.
- **§5.3 `pages:changed`** is `Latest` at 150 ms, keyed by the hall. The design's "like `displaysChanged`" is now the
  same code.
- **§4.2 `room:send`, §4.4 `room:withdraw`, §5.3 `page:push`:** a resend after a lost acknowledgement would otherwise put
  a second copy in a room the sender cannot delete from, or a second take and audit row. `room:send` and `page:push`
  carry a `cid` from their first commit; `room:withdraw` answers a repeat with `already`.
- **§4.5 "no new per-room governor":** agreed. Nothing measured calls for one.
- **§7.7's delegated listeners** replace 5 listeners per message. They are there for correctness (the pinned clones,
  §16.1), not speed.

## 5-§14. Abstraction and modularity

### 5-§14.1 How AGMessage is built today

- **`server.js` (2,510 lines)** is the composition root. It holds 58 `socket.on` registrations of 57 event names (56
  fuzzed: `disconnect` is not). Its connection closure (`:667-1659`, **993 lines**) holds 56 of them, the per-connection
  state (`room`, `me`, four buckets, `uploadToken`) and 15 helpers (`ok`, `limited`, `GUEST_CAPS` `:699`, `allowed`
  `:700`, `need` `:818`, `mayPost` `:825`, `rightsIn` `:918`, `syncPeer`, `runAi`, `canDraft` `:996`, `canDisplays`
  `:1094`, `actor`, `canManageHall` `:1331`, `admin` `:1398`, `leaveRoom` `:1628`). `display:shown` and the screen's
  `disconnect` are registered in `serveDisplay` (`:1697`, `:1702`).
- **The handler domains share one kit.** Measured by `mod/coupling.js`, every domain uses the same connection kit of
  about 11 names: `ok`, `limited`, a bucket, `need` or `admin`, `allowed` or `mayPost`, `actor`, `me` and `room`. The
  display, help, stage and ai domains each need 3-12 module names. The admin group needs 54, because it is four domains
  (rooms, settings, certificates and the tunnel).
- **`lib/` (19 files)** is already in layers:
  - a pure core that requires nothing (board, context, deskresults, rbac, stagelines), whose clocks are default
    arguments (`lib/board.js:67`, `lib/context.js:52`);
  - stores with lanes (store, accounts, displays, audit);
  - edges with I/O (nodes, peerlinks, tls, secretbox, version, resilience, ai, and guard's read of the secret).
  - `lib/http-accounts.js` already has the domain-module shape: `mountAccounts(app, o)` destructures a narrow context in
    its first lines (`:25-26`) and returns what server.js needs (`:285`).
  - The graph is acyclic, and nothing in `lib/` requires server.js.
- **Invariants held by habit, not by a test:**
  - One writer per store: 6 lanes are built (`server.js:83`, `:125`; `lib/accounts.js:161`, `:319`, `:411`;
    `lib/displays.js:80`) and 6 are named in `saveLanes()` (`server.js:130`). "Every store's lane is in `saveLanes()`"
    is CLAUDE.md's rule, and no test checks it.
  - The op → event knowledge sits in three places: `apply()` (`server.js:218-225`), `applyOp` (`app.js:170-185`) and
    the live listeners (`:191-198`, `:219-226`, `:267`, `:269`, `:643`). They have drifted already: for a message whose
    record is missing, the live `proposalUpdate` draws the line (`:225`) and `applyOp` does nothing (`:178`).
- **The fences read one file or a hand list.**
  - The input fuzz takes its event names from server.js alone (`test/inputs.test.js:13`). A handler anywhere else is
    never fuzzed, which is why the plan put every new verb in server.js.
  - The guard rail (`test/resilience.test.js:414`) reads `lib/` without recursion and four of nine page scripts by
    hand. `common.js`, `display.js`, `halls.js`, `theme-init.js` and `users.js` are not scanned.
  - Only `app/lib/**` gets coverage (`app/package.json:11`), the server's lint rules (`eslint.config.mjs:76-84`) and the
    portable copy (`tools/build-portable.ps1:26-28`) for free.
- **The pages.**
  - `app.js` (2,177 lines) is one classic script with 164 top-level bindings, 41 emits, 57 click bindings and no
    `contextmenu` handler. Two IIFE namespaces (`Screens` `:1964`, `ToStagewatch` `:2120`) are the pattern for
    self-contained UI.
  - `common.js` assigns `window.AGM = {…}` whole (`:71`). app.html and admin.html do not load it, and they duplicate the
    escaping, the toast and the theme.
- **Found while measuring** (the prototype fence, `mod/fence-proto.js`, run read-only on the tree):
  - **`typing` is dead.** It is a server verb (`server.js:899-902`) that no page sends, and whose broadcast no page
    hears. `test/halls.test.js:638-648` emits and listens for it, and would pass vacuously once it goes.
  - **`linkedRoomsChanged` is unheard.** It is emitted (`:1514`, `:1529`), and no page listens.
  - **A context object built near `:667` would throw at boot.** `linkFor` (`:1921`), `hallStagewatch` (`:1952`),
    `mayDriveNode` (`:2010`) and `deskFor` (`:2012`) are `const`s declared later (TDZ, the trap `app.js:35` already
    warns of).
  - **The plan's script loading has a gap.** §7.2 puts a right-click menu on the halls board, but §7.7 has only app.html
    and admin.html load `menus.js`. halls.html loads `common.js`, whose whole-object assignment would erase `AGM.menu`,
    or be erased by it, by load order.

### 5-§14.2 The shape

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§14.2: `admin:setClock` and `admin:setOnStage` in `lib/handlers/takes.js`).

**server.js stays the composition root.** It builds every store, lane and link, and it alone requires a handler
module. No container is used and nothing is required by a computed path: `security/detect-non-literal-require` is an
error (`eslint.config.mjs:59`), and the owner's ecosystem chose a composition root, not a container (Patterns' ADR-012,
Patterns' `docs/ADR.md:196-210`).

**The server's layers:**

| Layer | Files | May require | Never |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pure core | `lib/board`, `context`, `deskresults`, `rbac`, `stagelines`, and new: `lib/latest.js` (§13.3.1), `lib/ops.js` (the op table), `lib/gate.js` (the gate) | each other | an I/O built-in (`fs`, `net`, `http`, `https`, `dgram`, `tls`, `os`, `dns`, `child_process`, `ws`) or `process.` |
| Stores, one lane each | `lib/store`, `accounts`, `displays`, `audit`, and `lib/pages.js` (unit 16) | the pure core, `resilience`, `guard`, `ids`, Node's built-ins | a handler module, server.js |
| Edges | `lib/nodes`, `peerlinks`, `tls`, `secretbox`, `version`, `resilience`, `guard`, `ids`, `ai`, and the stage addendum's `zipcheck` and `imagesize` | the pure core, each other, Node's built-ins, their own package (`ai`: the Anthropic SDK). `lib/zipcheck.js` also requires `../public/zipcore.js` (the stage addendum's one core for the server and the worker), by an allow-list row | a handler module, server.js |
| Handler modules | `lib/handlers/rooms.js`, `lib/handlers/takes.js` (new) | the pure core; `guard` for its pure helpers (`str`, `cleanText`, `mac`, `Bucket`; it reads the server secret once, at server.js's first require of it); `ids`; and `lib/handlers/takes.js` → `lib/pages.js` by name, for its pure vocabulary (`cleanPage`, `describePage`, `canShow`, `cleanSnippet`) | `fs`, `child_process`, `resilience`, and every store or edge but that one row: stores and links reach a handler only through its context. No `new` of anything it requires |
| HTTP domain | `lib/http-accounts.js` | as today | server.js |
| Composition root | `server.js` | everything | — |

`lib/handlers/takes.js` is named for what it handles (takes on people's pages), so it shares no basename with
`lib/pages.js`. Files under `app/lib/handlers/` ship (`tools/build-portable.ps1:28` copies `lib` with `-Recurse`), are
covered (`app/package.json:11`'s `lib/**`) and are linted (`eslint.config.mjs:76`) with no edit. `app/handlers/` at the
root would need all three.

**`conn`, the connection context.** Inside `io.on('connection')`, after `guardHandlers(socket)`:

```
const conn = Object.freeze({ socket, room: () => room, me: () => me, ok, limited, writes, chatter,
                             need, mayPost, allowed, admin, actor, canManageHall, gate })
```

- `room` and `me` are functions, so a module cannot capture a stale room by destructuring at registration.
- Unit 5's rights questions (`canIn`, `mayKnowCode`, `canPush`) and the stage addendum's `canShow` join it as they
  land.

**`ctx`, the server context**, built once with `Object.freeze`, at the end of server.js before `holdDataFolder`, after
every `const` it names exists (§14.1, TDZ). The connection callback reads it lazily. It holds:

- the stores' instances and the named effects: `store`, `apply`, `systemMessage`, `buildMessage`, `removeUnused`,
  `fileNamesOf`, `audit`, `accounts`, `pages`, `boardDirty`, `pagesChanged`;
- `settings`, to read, and `setRoomSends`, the one writer of `settings.roomSends`, which dedupes, caps at 50 and saves;
- `linkFor` and `stagePayload`;
- `io`, for the rooms module.

**`takesCtx`** is a second frozen object for `lib/handlers/takes.js`: the same entries without `io`, and with
`sendTo(socketIds, event, payload)`, which emits only to ids found in `io.sockets.sockets`, one socket at a time. A hall
key passed as an id therefore reaches nobody, where `io.to(ids)` would broadcast to the whole hall.

**The gate** (`lib/gate.js`, pure). `conn.gate(ack, {joined, bucket, admin, may})` answers a refusal and returns false.

- **The order is fixed:** joined, and the room still there → the bucket → admin → the right. Nothing is looked up by a
  client's key before a token is taken, so a refused lookup (a stale ref, another hall's code) is never a free oracle.
  `help:respond` takes `chatter` first for that reason today (`server.js:1315`), and `message` already takes its bucket
  before `mayPost` (`:832-834`). A refused request spends a token, as `message`'s does today.
- The words are today's: "Not joined", "Room gone", "Slow down a little.", "Not admin", "Observers can read but not
  post." / "Your account may not share files here."
- Every `socket.on('verb', …)` in `lib/handlers/` starts with exactly one gate call, which names its bucket or says
  `bucket: null` with a reason comment.
- Socket.IO's per-packet `socket.use` cannot be the gate: its `next(err)` becomes a server-side `error` event, not a
  worded refusal to the sender (https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-api/).
- The order differs today between handlers (`message` `:832-834`, `stage:send` `:1022-1024`, `help:respond` `:1315`).
  The existing handlers keep their own lines.

**The handler modules.**

- `rooms.register(socket, conn, ctx)` and `takes.register(socket, conn, takesCtx)` are called from the connection.
- **`lib/handlers/rooms.js`** holds `room:create`, `room:update`, `room:settings`, `room:sendTargets`, `room:send`,
  `room:withdraw` (units 6, 7, 12, 14, 15) and `history:before` (unit 32).
- **`lib/handlers/takes.js`** holds `page:push`, `page:report`, `page:status` and `admin:setView` (units 17, 20), and the
  stage addendum's kinds as they land (units 24, 25, 27-29).
- Each module destructures its context on its first line, as `lib/http-accounts.js:26` does, so that line is its
  dependency list.
- Modules register with a literal `socket.on('verb', …)`, so the fuzz's regex finds them through the shared file list.
- **Three invariants become properties of a file:**
  - `takes.js` has no `io` and names none of `io`, `.to(`, `.in(`, `.broadcast`, `.nsp`, `.server` or `.except(`, so
    §5.3's "never a room op or a room broadcast" holds by construction (`conn.socket` carries `.broadcast`, `.nsp` and
    `.server`, hence the longer list);
  - handler modules never call `rbac.can(` and ask `conn` instead, so §2.1's `ROOM_SCOPED` fence has no new call site
    to guard;
  - handler modules never assign into `settings` (`settings.x =`, `settings[…] =`, `Object.assign(settings`):
    `Object.freeze(ctx)` does not freeze `settings`, so the fence does.
- **The 57 existing handlers stay in server.js.** One moves only when a unit rewrites it (strangler fig: "small
  additions … built on top of, yet separate to the legacy code base",
  https://martinfowler.com/bliki/StranglerFigApplication.html). `admin:deleteRoom`'s cascade (unit 6) is edited in
  place.

**The op table** (`lib/ops.js`, pure, unit O):

```
UPD_EVENTS = { responses: 'actionUpdate', pinned: 'pinUpdate', reactions: 'messageReact', stage: 'stageAck',
               proposal: 'proposalUpdate', help: 'helpUpdate' }        // unit 15 adds sentTo: 'sentUpdate'
```

- `apply()` emits from the table. Every event carries `{messageId, [field], seq}`, as all six do today.
- **An `upd` naming a field outside the table fails the build first.** Fence (k) reads every `o: 'upd'` literal's `f`
  keys in `handlerFiles()` and requires each in `UPD_EVENTS`. At run time `apply()` never throws: it is also called from
  the Stagewatch followers (`server.js:2034`, `:2057`, `:2119`), outside `guardHandlers`, where a throw would be an
  uncaught exception and a watchdog restart. A field outside the table is logged and refused before `store.commit`, and
  `apply()` returns null.
- An op may carry several fields. A page applies two events with one seq both, because `bump` passes any seq not past
  `lastSeq + 1` (`app.js:164-169`), so no one-field rule is needed.
- In `app.js`, one table `field → [event, applyFn]` drives both `applyOp` and the live listeners, which are generated
  from it in place of the six hand-written ones. The drift of §14.1 goes with them.
- Zulip applies one event stream both to a fetched state and to live updates, and tests the two against each other
  (https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/events-system.html).

**Three more moves, each inside a unit that edits those lines anyway:**

- **Unit 5:** `GUEST_CAPS` leaves the connection closure (`server.js:699`) for `rbac.guestCaps(role, kind)`, with
  `GUEST_CAPS_SIDE` beside it. `allowed` (`:700`) and `rightsIn` (`:918`) call it, and `test/accounts.test.js` tests the
  guest table beside the account rights. Every answer to "what may this seat do" is then in one pure module.
- **Unit 14:** `RoomStore` takes `refOf(key)` at construction. server.js passes `(k) => 'r' + guard.mac(SECRET,
  'room-ref:' + k, 16)`, so the store never holds the secret. The store keeps `byRef` beside §1.3's `codes` and
  `retiredCodes` (and `byCid`, §13.3.4), updated at the same sites (`loadAll`, `createIn`, `remove`, `removeHall`).
  Every index of the room set then has one writer.
- **Units 16-19 and the stage addendum's 25:** `pagelayer.mjs`'s `render(box, content, ctx)` gets plain values and
  functions (the stage payload, `now`, `tz`, `hallName`, `holding`, `esc`), never a socket, and returns `{state,
  words}`. `app.js` alone sends `page:report`, so "attempts are not facts" stays in one place.

**The pages' modules:**

| File | Kind | Holds | Never |
|---|---|---|---|
| `public/theme-init.js` | classic, the first script on every page with people (`index.html:8`, `halls.html:8`, `users.html:8`, `admin.html:8`, `app.html:8`; `display.html` loads none, `:38-39`) | the theme, as today, and from unit M the page floor's probe and its words (§15.10) | any other work |
| `public/common.js` | classic; index, halls and users today, and app and admin from unit 3c | `AGM.esc`, `api`, `toast(text, badOrOpts)` (a boolean is today's `bad`, so the 18 callers in halls.js and users.js stay), `theme`, `ago`, `clock`, from unit 31 `AGM.MARKS`, and from unit M `AGM.openDialog`, `AGM.awake` and `AGM.idle` (§15.10) | work on load |
| `public/outbox.js` (new) | classic; app, admin, halls | `AGM.outbox` (§13.3.4) | DOM beyond the echo it is handed |
| `public/catalog.js` (new) | classic, data and pure functions of facts | `AGM.catalog` (§16.2) | DOM, socket |
| `public/menus.js` (plan §7.7) | classic; app, admin, halls, users | `AGM.menu`, `AGM.ask`, `AGM.roving` (§16.5), and the only `contextmenu` listener | a socket |
| `app.js`, `admin.js`, `admin-plus.js`, `halls.js`, `users.js` | classic | each page's runners, `run(id, ctx)`; `users.js` runs through `AGM.api` (no socket) with the same 5 s rule | a `contextmenu` listener, a `cloneNode` of a message, a native dialog, and from unit M a bare `showModal()` or `requestIdleCallback` |
| `public/pagelayer.mjs` (§5.7) and the stage addendum's `docview.mjs`, `docmodel.mjs` | ES modules, loaded with `import()` | rendering | `socket`, `io(`, `.emit(` |

- **Load order** on every page with menus: `theme-init.js`, the socket client, `common.js`, `outbox.js` (app, admin,
  halls), `catalog.js`, `menus.js`, then the page's script. On app.html every one of them is `defer`, as `app.js` is
  today (`app.html:236-238`), so their order holds.
- `common.js:71` becomes `Object.assign(window.AGM = window.AGM || {}, {…})`, and the other three extend `AGM` the same
  way, so no load order can erase a part.
- app.html and admin.html start loading `common.js` in unit 3c. It does nothing on load, and `notify` (`app.js:354`)
  and `flashStatus` (`:1732`) become calls to `AGM.toast`. The duplicated escaping and theme stay, left for later.

### 5-§14.3 The order of moves: behaviour-preserving first

1. **Unit F: the module fence.** No behaviour changes except one fail-closed removal, `typing`.
2. **Unit 30: `conn`, `ctx`, `takesCtx` and the gate.** No behaviour changes; every suite stays green, unchanged.
3. **Unit O: one op table.** The client's drift is fixed.
4. **Unit 5: `guestCaps` into `rbac`.** A move inside a unit that rewrites `allowed` and `rightsIn` anyway.
5. **Unit 4: the any-room readers counted.** A fence written as the readers are sorted.
6. **Units 6, 7, 12, 14 and 15** put their verbs in `lib/handlers/rooms.js`. **Units 17, 20, and the stage addendum's
   24, 25 and 27-29** put theirs in `lib/handlers/takes.js`.
7. **Unit 14:** `store.byRef`. **Units 16-19 and the stage addendum's 25:** `pagelayer.mjs`'s boundary.

### 5-§14.4 The fences

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§14.4 (a): `lib/views.js` in the pure set).

Each `require` is read by regex, as `inputs.test.js` reads event names: every relative path, `./` and `../` alike.

| Fence | Holds | File | Lands |

| (a) the pure set | `lib/board`, `context`, `deskresults`, `rbac`, `stagelines`, `latest`, `ops`, `gate` require only each other, and name no I/O built-in and no `process.` | `modules.test.js` | F (the set grows in 30, O and C) |
| (b) no cycle | no file requires server.js; the `lib/` graph has no cycle | `modules.test.js` | F |
| (c) one root | only server.js requires `lib/http-accounts.js` and `lib/handlers/*` | `modules.test.js` | F |
| (d) narrow handlers | a `lib/handlers/` file requires only what §14.2's row allows, and calls `new` on nothing it requires | `modules.test.js` | 30 |

Exact by objects, so a lane built in any file is held: `lib/audit.js`'s `auditHead` (unit H), `pages` (16) and `peaks` (R) included | `server.test.js`, end to end after boot | F |
| (f) the wire's words, closed both ways | every page emit is a server verb; every server verb is sent by some page; every server emit is heard by some page. A page's emits are read in three forms: `socket.emit('x'`, `AGM.outbox.hold/now/self('x'`, and `verb: 'x'` in `catalog.js`. An allow-list, a reason per row, covers `message` and `system` (named by a ternary in `apply()`) and, until unit 3a hears it for the `forwardable` fact, `linkedRoomsChanged` | `modules.test.js` | F |
| (g) one file list | `handlerFiles()` in `test/helpers.js` returns server.js plus `lib/handlers/*.js`. `inputs.test.js:13` uses it, its regex unchanged; so do (f), (i), (k) and (o) | `helpers.js` | F |
| (h) the guard rail reads folders | `resilience.test.js:414` reads `lib/` recursively, and every `public/*.js` and `*.mjs` except `vendor/`, in place of the hand list. Unit H widens the pattern to count `fs.realpathSync.native(` and raises `lib/resilience.js`'s cap to 11; whichever of F and H lands second carries both | `resilience.test.js` | F |
| (i) one gate per verb | every `socket.on(` in `lib/handlers/` is followed by exactly one `conn.gate(` naming its bucket, or `bucket: null` with a reason | `modules.test.js` | 30 |
| (j) the takes module | `lib/handlers/takes.js` names no `io`, `.to(`, `.in(`, `.broadcast`, `.nsp`, `.server` or `.except(`; no handler module calls `rbac.can(` or assigns into `settings` | `modules.test.js` | 30 |
| (k) one op table | the keys of `UPD_EVENTS` equal the client table's (a source read of `app.js`), and every `o: 'upd'` literal's `f` keys in `handlerFiles()` are among them | `modules.test.js` | O |

| (m) the renderer has no socket | `pagelayer.mjs`, `docview.mjs` and `docmodel.mjs` name no `socket`, `io(` or `.emit(` | `modules.test.js` | 18 (the stage's 23 and 25 extend it) |

- **What the prototype found on today's tree:** (a), (b), (e) and the first half of (f) pass already. (f) fails on
  `typing` and `linkedRoomsChanged`, and (h) on five page scripts. So the fence costs no rewrite, only two decisions:
  `typing` is removed in unit F (it is a rebroadcast surface with no page, and owner answer 26 wants no typing
  indicator), and `linkedRoomsChanged` is heard from unit 3a.
- **Removing `typing`** lowers `inputs.test.js`'s event count by one: the one exception to §9's "the event count only
  grows", stated in the CHANGELOG. The assertion `EVENTS.length > 50` (`:31`) holds. `test/halls.test.js:638-648`
  loses its `typing` emit and listener on purpose, so it no longer passes vacuously. CLAUDE.md's sentence
  "`test/inputs.test.js` reads the event names from `server.js`" becomes "from `handlerFiles()`".

### 5-§14.5 Refused, and why

- **Moving the 57 existing handlers out of server.js in 0.6.0.** About 990 lines would churn, and blame would be lost.
  Units 4 and 5 edit those handlers a line at a time (`store.get` → `store.room`, `can` → `canIn`); a move would turn
  each of those into a relocation, with the risk of a closure name resolving differently.
- **Splitting the admin group** (rooms, settings, certificates, tunnel: 54 module names) now. It is the right
  decomposition, but no 0.6.0 unit rewrites it. It is the first candidate when one does.
- **A container, or a handler folder discovered at boot.** A computed `require` is a lint error, and the ecosystem chose
  a composition root.
- **`socket.onAny` for limits or logging.** It does not see acknowledgements (https://socket.io/docs/v4/server-api/),
  and `guardHandlers` already counts faults.
- **A declarative table of every socket verb (PlayMap's `VerbCatalog`).** It would be a second registration style for
  57 verbs. AGMessage's socket verbs are not offered to an AI or a deck; the only Show Bus verb is `notice`. Revisit
  when they are.
- **dependency-cruiser, eslint-plugin-boundaries or eslint-plugin-import.** Each is a new dev dependency (audit,
  signatures, SBOM) for rules a 100-line node:test reads from `require()` calls.
- **Splitting `app.js` into ES modules, or a bundler.** CLAUDE.md allows no build step, and no parse cost was measured
  on the stage tablets. New self-contained UI follows the IIFE namespaces; `pagelayer.mjs` and the stage addendum's
  readers are the lazy modules.
- **TypeScript or JSDoc type checking.** A toolchain with no ask behind it. The fences catch the cross-file drift types
  would.
- **Splitting `lib/pages.js` into a vocabulary file and a store file.** `lib/displays.js` holds both, the pure functions
  are tested directly, and (d)'s one row covers the handler's use of them.
- **A publish/subscribe bus between server modules.** It hides who causes what. The effects are few and named (`apply`,
  `boardDirty`, `displaysChanged`, `pagesChanged`), and named functions in `ctx` keep the call graph readable.
- **One page holding several rooms on one socket.** The design rejects it (§3.4). In module terms, every frame would
  need a room key.

The heuristic critique's worst findings, by severity (0-4):

- **3: the hall page does not fit a phone** (WCAG 1.4.10). A presenter on a phone reads one message at a time, and help's
  Send is off the screen's edge. It is the worst moment in the product.
- **3: up to 9 tiny icon buttons on every message** (Fitts, WCAG 2.5.8 and 1.4.11), named only by `title`, which a touch
  screen never shows.
- **3: nothing stands out.** Every new message is filled yellow for 30 s (`app.js:1638-1641`, `styles.css:400-421`), so
  after a burst the whole feed is yellow, and a 🔥 differs only by a 10.9 px badge (2.77:1 in dark).
- **3: the "📺 On stage" panel claims what it does not know.** Backstage, it is the page's own last-opened file. The stage
  addendum names it "👁 Preview — the Board does not see this", and the Board chip (§5.9.2) says what the Board sees.
- **3: one thing, four words.** "hall / meeting / room / session", "Board / directors / On stage", "research team /
  Backstage". 0.6.0 gives "room" a new meaning, so drift becomes collision.
- **3: the admin's Logout is covered** by the fixed theme toggle (`admin.html:11`, `.theme-toggle` `styles.css:551`) at
  every size.
- **2:** ↗ ends in an `alert` when no other hall is open (`app.js:1681`), and shows to observers; "Reply with text" and
  delete are a `prompt()` and a `confirm()` (`:707`, `:592`); a failed join leaves by itself; the join page preselects
  Backstage (`index.html:81`); Sound is preselected in help (`app.js:1943`); an observer sees live-looking Yes/No at
  opacity .7 (`styles.css:1093`); eleven ungrouped rights on the Accounts page, with Save below the fold.
- **Kept, because they work:** the "Seen by …" lines; help's ✓ ▶ ■ states with words (`app.js:605-626`); reduced
  motion honoured (`styles.css:1748`); a visible 2 px focus ring; Enter sends; the halls board's help strip and its
  reflow at 390 px; the screen page (`/d/`), whose huge type and shape-plus-word-plus-colour (● ▲ ■) is the model the
  simple view and the take layer borrow.

### 5-§15.2 Simple but rich: the rules every surface follows

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§15.2 rule 8: answers 48 px, every Board control 44 px or more).

1. **Simple by seat, rich by menu.** The Board's simple view shows only large visible buttons, each a catalogue entry,
   and has no menu door. Every other seat gets at most two inline acts and a ⋯; everything else that seat may do is in
   the menu, which right-click, ⋯ and Shift+F10 open alike (§16).
2. **Absent when never, disabled with the reason when not now.** A seat never sees what it may never do. What it may do
   but not now is shown, and says why.
3. **The sender's own screen says what is true.** "◷ sending" until the server takes it; the take's mark and words until
   each page confirms it; "Reconnecting…" while it is.
4. **Nothing blocks the page.** No native `alert`, `confirm` or `prompt`: a page paused by one drops its socket (§16.1,
   measured).
5. **Undo what can be undone; confirm in place what reaches others for good.**
6. **One word per thing**, the same on every page, in the menu and on the button (§15.7).
7. **Colour is never the only cue.** Every state carries one mark and one word, from one table (§15.6).
8. **The most-used control is the biggest.** The text box gets the row; the Board's buttons are 56 px; a touch target is
   44 px.
9. **No dead ends.** A failed join says why and offers the way back; a menu item that cannot run says why; an empty list
   says what fills it.
10. **The reader keeps their place.** A new message never moves a feed the reader has scrolled; it is announced.

**The Escape order:** an open menu closes first; then an open ask (answered "no"); then the take layer (minimised);

**The join page** (`index.html:64-104`, `join.js:96-121`):

- The order becomes Code, the room line ("Legal · Hall 2"), Your name, **Your seat**.
- The code is looked up when six valid characters have been still for 0.5 s, on Enter, or on leaving the field, and never
  twice for the same value. Each miss counts against `lookupLock` (`server.js:505`, 12 a minute per address; `:526`
  fails on any miss), so a lookup on every keystroke would let a corrected typo count, and behind one venue address
  twelve slips a minute would lock the field for everyone at the doors. No measurement this round of how often guests
  mistype a code.
- The seats follow the answer's `main`: On stage (only with an invite link, owner answer 10), Backstage and Observer in
  Main; Member and Observer in a side room.
- No seat is preselected on a first visit (today Backstage is, `index.html:81`); the remembered seat (`agm.role`) and an
  invite's seat still are.
- The code field: `autocomplete=off`, `enterkeyhint=go`, a monospace look, and 16 px so iOS does not zoom.
- Units 2 (no preselected seat) and 7 (code first, seats by room kind).

- Units 10, 11 and 3b. `test/halls.test.js`'s per-watcher rows are unchanged.

### 5-§15.5 The Board's simple view, for a glance under lights (amends §6)

> **Replaced by** 7-§0.2's table, item by item (and 7-§17.2).

The Board's posture is transient: a glance, then back to the audience. Today the Board gets the backstage desk's
sovereign layout with bigger fonts. Added to §6:

- **The header:** the countdown first and largest (`--fs-xl`), with its mark and word as `/d/` has them ("4:30 left", ▲
  in the last minute), as static text with `role=status`, never a menu button; the hall's name at `--fs-md`; Help (or
  its status chip); **Aa−** and **Aa+**; and a 44 px ⋯ that opens the sheet (kind `sheet`: Theme · Full screen · Leave,
  56 px rows). That is four controls (Help, Aa−, Aa+, ⋯), not ten.
- **The type:** message body `--fs-lg` (20 px at zoom 1), prompts `--fs-xl` (24 px), answer buttons at least 56 px
  tall.
- **New messages:** no yellow fill; the New divider and the place kept (§15.4).
- **🔥 messages:** one strip above the feed, under the pinned strip, holds the newest priority message not yet
  acknowledged, with a 56 px **Got it** (a `self` act that also reports `seen`) and "+2 more" when there are several. The
  message also stays in its place in the feed.
- **Hidden:** presence and seen lines (as §6 says). "typing" leaves §6's list: there is no typing indicator.
- **The pinned strip** keeps Answer and Reply in words, through the feed's delegated handler, so a prompt pinned for the
  Board is answered where the Board sees it; only pin management goes (amends §6's "read-only").
- **Prompts:** **Reply in words…** is a 56 px button that opens one field at a time, never a `prompt()`.
- **A phone in portrait:** two big tabs, **Chat** and **📺 On stage · 1**, instead of the 50/50 split; the second tab is
  absent while On stage is empty. **A tablet in landscape:** a 60/40 split for the chat, and the panel collapses to its
  rail while it is empty.
- **The connection:** the dot gains the words "Offline · reconnecting" after 5 s down, with no strip and no motion
  (`app.html:17`'s dot is colour only today, against WCAG 1.4.1).
- **Awake:** in the simple view and while a take shows, the page holds the Screen Wake Lock as `display.js:256-260`
  (`keepAwake`) does for a screen, asked again on `visibilitychange`, through `AGM.awake()` (unit M). It is not a
  governor, so it needs no reading.
  - Where it cannot be had, the sheet says why, by cause, on every device alike (§15.10): not over HTTPS, not in this
    browser, or refused by the device.
  - MDN's data gives the Wake Lock to iOS and iPadOS only from 18.4, so on an older iPad the sheet's words are the
    fallback (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/api/WakeLock.json).
- **Download:** none on a Board seat, except a whole-file take sent with "Let them download it" (owner answers 12 and
  20, as confirmed).
- **Keys:** only Tab, Enter and Escape (Escape minimises a take, §5.4).
- **No menu door** (R7, §16.2): no ⋯ on messages and no right-click; the browser's own menu stays. Every button here is a
  catalogue entry, and the simple view is a view in the catalogue's matrix (§16.8).
- **Test (unit 20's smoke):** four header controls (Help, Aa−, Aa+, ⋯); no `.flash` fill; a 🔥 in the strip with Got
  it; the phone's tabs; a pinned prompt answered in the strip; the dot's words after 5 s down; the simple page's
  `allMessages` still holds the Support Team's messages (`test/browser-smoke.js:262`).

### 5-§15.6 A small token layer, and one table of marks

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§15.6: `--c-on-fault`, `--fs-title`, `--fs-readout`, `--target-answer`, `--c-ask`, `--c-ink-muted`).

The tokens are defined once in `:root` (`styles.css:10-27`) and redefined once under `html[data-theme="dark"]`
(`:566-583`), the mechanism the page already uses. Components then stop carrying their own dark rules; the 140 dark-only
rules retire as each unit touches its files.

```css
:root {
  /* type: one scale of about 1.2, in rem, so text zoom and --zoom-msg still work */
  --fs-xs: .75rem; --fs-sm: .875rem; --fs-md: 1rem;   /* 16 px: body, inputs (no iOS zoom on focus) */
  --fs-lg: 1.25rem;  /* the Board's message body */   --fs-xl: 1.5rem;  /* the Board's prompt and countdown */
  --fs-2xl: 2rem;    /* the take layer */             --fs-stage: clamp(2.5rem, 7vw, 6rem);  /* clock, countdown takes */
  /* space on a 4 px base */
  --sp-1: .25rem; --sp-2: .5rem; --sp-3: .75rem; --sp-4: 1rem; --sp-6: 1.5rem; --sp-8: 2rem;
  /* targets */
  --target-min: 24px;   /* WCAG 2.5.8, every control */
  --target-touch: 44px; /* the simple view, the take layer, the header, coarse pointers */
  --radius-sm: 6px; --radius-md: 10px; --radius-pill: 999px;
  /* layers, today 9 ad hoc values; a menu and an ask open on the take layer, so they sit above it and the dialogs */
  --z-header: 10; --z-panel: 20; --z-layer: 300; --z-dialog: 500; --z-menu: 700; --z-toast: 9999;
  /* colour roles: a role is drawn only with its mark and its word */
  --c-surface; --c-surface-raised; --c-ink; --c-ink-muted;  /* ≥ 4.5:1 on both surfaces; never opacity */
  --c-border; --c-action; --c-on-action;
  --c-ok; --c-warn; --c-fault /* red only here */; --c-info; --c-off;
  --c-seat-board; --c-seat-backstage; --c-seat-observer; --c-other-room;  /* the ↘ From and ↗ Sent edges */
}
```

- Where `showPopover` exists, menus and asks are in the top layer and the z-index does not apply (§16.5).
- **Red is kept** for 🔥, open help and faults. Help at rest becomes neutral (§15.4), so red regains its meaning.
- **No opacity for text or icons.** `.sys.presence` (`:1617`) and the icon buttons (`:353`, `:518`, `:1026`, `:1196`)
  take `--c-ink-muted`, at 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 or more for icons.
- **Three faults fixed now** (unit P):
  - `styles.css:635`'s second selector is not scoped to dark, so light mode draws the ON STAGE tag in dark colours;
  - in dark mode Help loses its red, because `html[data-theme="dark"] .btn` (`:670`) outranks `.help-btn` (`:1751`);
  - text opacity used as muted ink.
- **The fence:** `test/resilience.test.js` counts the hex literals outside the two token blocks of `styles.css`. The
  count, set at unit P's commit, may only go down: the coverage gate's rule.
- **`AGM.MARKS`** (`common.js`, unit 31): one table used by app.js, halls.js and admin.js. `lib/pages.js`'s
  `describePage` and `Pages.status` use the same marks on the server, and fence (n) compares the two. **Each mark has
  one meaning**, and no catalogue icon is a mark (fence n):

| Mark | Means | Colour role | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| ✓ | showing, resolved, on screen | ok | takes, help, screens |
| ◐ | not fully seen: not in view (asleep, another app), under a quote, held under blank | warn | takes |
| ◇ | opened (a web page, which cannot be seen into) | info | web takes |
| ▭ | minimised | info | takes |
| ○ | back to chat; taken down; off | off | takes, links |
| ⊘ | withdrawn | info | Sent-to lines |
| ◷ | sending, waiting | info | takes, the outbox |
| △ | could not | warn | takes, refusals, the outbox |
| ✕ | none, or a fault | fault | takes, links |
| ■ | waiting for someone, urgent | fault | help, the screen page |
| ▶ | on the way | info | help |
| ● ▲ | a note, soon | info, warn | the screen page |

- **The action icons are not marks:** ↩ is Reply only; ↗ is Send to and Send back; **⤴** is Show again; the take-kind
  cards are ⏱ Stagewatch, 🕐 Clock, 🖼 Holding, 🌑 Blank, 🌐 a web page (no AGMessage card: owner answer 31); "…"
  ends the label of an item that opens a dialog and is never a mark.
- **Components to merge as their units touch them:** three toasts into one (3c); the `.fwd-menu`, the reaction picker,
  the admin's link picker and `AGM.menu` into one (3a, 3b); 34 native dialogs into `AGM.ask` and fields in place (3a,
  3b, 3c); five icon-button variants (`.pin-btn`, `.del-btn`, `.reply-btn`, `.react-btn`, `.fwd-btn`) into one at
  ≥ 24 px and ≥ 3:1 (3a); the stage, Board, help and screen chips into one status chip of mark, word and colour (31, E).
- **Refused:** CSS `light-dark()` (Baseline May 2024; a browser without it drops the colours to their initial values, a
  severe failure on the older devices of owner answer 22's mixture), and following `prefers-color-scheme` by default
  (the theme is per person and mirrored to the admin's support view).
- **The simple view starts in Dark** (owner answer 21, by B6). A simple view that has never chosen a theme draws Dark,
  and the sheet keeps Light. The board addendum draws it (its §0.2 and §17.2); every other page keeps light by default.

### 5-§15.7 One word per thing (needed before rooms ship)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§15.7: the copy deck's rows from 7-§17.2), 6-U.9 ("the laptop's admin" beside "admin account").

| Thing | The word | Never |
|---|---|---|
| A venue space with its Main room | **hall** | meeting, session, room |
| Main, Legal, Media | **room** ("Hall 2 › Legal") | hall |
| What guests type | **code**; "guest code" in the admin's words | session code, meeting code |
| Everyone seated On stage in Main | **the Board** | directors |
| Where a person sits | **seat**: On stage · Backstage · Observer · Member. The admin's select is labelled **Seat**; the join page asks **Your seat** | role (in visible text) |
| How a person's chat is laid out | **Chat view**: By seat · Simple · Full | View |
| The backstage seat's people | **backstage** (owner answer 23) | research team, Support Team, in visible text |

The rule: **Show on** a thing (screens); **Show** people (the Board, Ana); **Send** into a room.

**The copy deck** (sentence case, the verb first). Each row lands in the unit given; unit W lands no later than unit

### 5-§15.8 Keyboard and touch

- **Keyboard.**
  - A skip link on every page with a feed or a table ("Skip to message box" or "Skip to messages", "Skip to the halls",
    "Skip to the accounts").
  - The feed, the People list, the screen list, hall rows, account rows and audit rows are roving-tabindex lists: one tab
    stop, ↑ and ↓ between items, Home and End to the first and the newest (`AGM.roving`, §16.5).
  - ↑ from an empty composer focuses the newest message (Slack's habit). Escape follows the Escape order (§15.4).
  - **Single keys act only on the focused object** (WCAG 2.1.4), are shown in the menu beside their item, and **never
    complete an act that reaches other people in one press**, beyond a pin that Undo takes back: they open, focus or
    toggle (§16.5). The UX research refused single keys for fear of accidental takes on a stage tablet's keyboard; that
    fear is answered by these three limits and by the simple view, which has none.
  - F6 is not taken: browsers use it for the address bar.
  - The simple view keeps only Tab, Enter and Escape.
- **Touch.**
  - **⋯ is the touch path.** iOS Safari never fires `contextmenu` on a long press
    (https://github.com/w3c/pointerevents/issues/503). Where a browser fires it on a long press (Chrome on Android, at
    about 500 ms), the same menu opens, except in the Preview, where a long press stays the selection gesture (R6).
    AGMessage runs no long-press timer of its own on any device (owner answer 22; §16.5, §15.10).
  - On a coarse pointer the inline bar shrinks to ↩ and a 44×44 ⋯; the rest is in the menu.
  - At 480 px or less with a coarse pointer, a menu is drawn as a bottom sheet with 48 px rows and a Cancel row.
  - Nothing is hover-only: touch has no hover, and WCAG 1.4.13 makes hover content a liability. On a fine pointer the
    two inline acts are always visible, in muted ink at 3:1 or more; reading 9's walk watches whether the desk reads as
    busy.
