### 5-§15.10 The Board's devices: a mixture (owner answer 22, unit M)

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§15.10: `inset` and the logical properties; the wake-lock and long-press rows) and 7-§17.7; Part 0 §0.8 C1 (#20 makes the floor leg and `docs/DEVICES.md`).

The owner: "Board will use a mixture of devices". The reading: iPads on current and older iPadOS, Android tablets, and
phones (iOS and Android); every Board feature works on each, with a test matrix and fallbacks; nothing is tuned to one
device.

**The stage addendum's revision 4 answers it for the stage** (its §5.15, unit T there):

- the matrix D1–D7, from an iPad below iPadOS 16.4 to an Android phone, plus CI;
- the document floor (Safari 16.4, Chrome 103), which pdf.js's legacy build sets, and a stand-in below it;
- the smoke's device and floor legs;
- `ecmaVersion: 2020` for `app/public/**`;
- the walk in `docs/DEVICES.md` before 0.6.0 is tagged.

It leaves the chat view's rows (the wake lock, a long press, `<dialog>`) to the Board's side. This section is this
addendum's part: the hall page, its menus, its dialogs and its stylesheet, on every row of that one matrix. It makes no
second matrix and no second walk. Every version below is MDN's compatibility data, with the file cited where it is
used. No user agent is read anywhere: each fallback is chosen by a probe or by what failed.

**The page floor: Safari 14.1 (iOS and iPadOS 14.5) and Chrome 84.**

- **Why there:**
  - Today's layout uses flex `gap` (for example `.help-item`, `styles.css:1709`), which arrived in Safari 14.1 and
    Chrome 84 (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/css/properties/gap.json, `flex_context`).
  - The page code's ES2020 parses from Safari 14 (the stage addendum's §5.15.2).
  - The floor sits below the stage addendum's document floor, so its D1 row is above it unless D1's iPad is older than
    iPadOS 14.5, which that row then says.
- **The probe:**
  - `theme-init.js` is the first script of every page with people (`index.html:8`, `halls.html:8`, `users.html:8`,
    `admin.html:8`, `app.html:8`). It tests `typeof WeakRef === 'function'`.
  - `WeakRef` arrived in the same versions as flex `gap`: Safari 14.1, Chrome 84 and Firefox 79
    (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/blob/main/javascript/builtins/WeakRef.json).
- **Below the floor, the page says so in words instead of half working.**
  - `theme-init.js` sets `data-floor="old"`, and the page shows one line: "This browser is too old for AGMessage. Update
    this device (iPadOS or iOS 14.5, or Chrome 84, or later), or use another."
  - Each page's `io(` (`app.js:89`, `halls.js:258`, `admin.js:86`) is not called, so no socket is opened.
  - `theme-init.js` keeps to old syntax, so the words still reach a browser below the floor.
- **Screens are untouched:** `display.html` loads no `theme-init.js` (`display.html:38-39`), and an audience-facing
  screen never shows the words.

**Each feature above the floor, and its fallback.** Each fallback is the same on every device.

| Feature | From (MDN) | Where today | The fallback | Unit |

**The fences** (fence q, §14.4):

- ESLint's `no-restricted-globals` on `app/public/**` refuses `requestIdleCallback` and `cancelIdleCallback`, each with
  the message "use AGM.idle: Safari has none". A use through a test of `window.requestIdleCallback` is not a bare global
  and passes, so the API is reached only behind its probe.
- `resilience.test.js`: `.showModal(` appears only in `public/common.js`. Until 3c and 3b move the rest, the other sites
  are a counted list with their reason.
- `resilience.test.js` reads `styles.css` for each feature above the floor:
  - a `dvh`, `svh` or `lvh` value follows the same property with another value in the same rule;
  - `:focus-visible` and `:has(` never share a selector list with a selector the floor reads;
  - `color-mix(`, `light-dark(`, `@container` and `text-wrap` follow a plain declaration of the same property, or sit
    inside `@supports`.
  - A new feature above the floor joins the list with its fallback, by an edit to the test that says so.
- The syntax is the stage addendum's `ecmaVersion: 2020`.

**How it is proven** (with the stage addendum's §5.15.3):

- **The smoke's floor leg:** the stage addendum's init script (`browser-smoke.js:117`) also removes
  `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal`, `HTMLElement.prototype.showPopover` and `navigator.wakeLock`. Then:
  - Help opens through `AGM.openDialog`'s fallback, takes the focus, sends at a category's tap, and Escape closes it;
  - a message's menu opens from ⋯ and from Shift+F10 without the top layer, and its Escape keeps an open Screens &
    pages open;
  - the simple view's sheet says "This device may sleep: …";
  - a first open draws the newest 60 at once and the rest through `AGM.idle`'s timer;
  - no console error.
- **A leg below the floor:** the init script deletes `WeakRef`. The page shows the floor's words and nothing else, and
  health's `clients` (`server.js:488`) does not move.
- **The device legs** (1180 × 820, 820 × 1180, 390 × 844, with touch) also run this addendum's Board steps (unit 20's
  and the board addendum's 20a smoke).
- **The walk** (`docs/DEVICES.md`, on rows D1–D7, before 0.6.0 is tagged) gains these features on every row:
  - the wake lock held for 10 minutes untouched, or the sheet's words naming the cause;
  - Help opened, sent and closed;
  - ⋯ and a long press on a message in the full view, and on a take in the simple view (nothing opens, nothing saves);
  - a dialog's buttons reachable with the on-screen keyboard up;
  - every mark of `AGM.MARKS` drawn;
  - back by itself after the device slept (unit B's `visibilitychange`);
  - a send written offline lands once (unit Q);
  - on D6 and D7, the same through the tunnel on mobile data (reading 7's walk).
  - A ✕ is a defect, fixed before the tag, or a fallback that the row then names, as the stage addendum rules. The
    floor's words are not such a fallback: a Board device of the owner's below the floor is a ✕ that holds the tag until
    the floor is lowered for it or the owner retires it from the Board (owner answer 22). Which iPadOS the owner's
    oldest Board iPad runs (D1) is recorded before unit M sets the floor.
- **Refused: Playwright's WebKit in CI.**
  - It would be a new dev dependency.
  - Playwright "doesn't work with the branded version of Safari since it relies on patches", and its WebKit is "derived
    from the latest WebKit main branch sources, often before these updates are incorporated into Apple Safari"
    (https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers). So it is not the older iPadOS Safari this answer is about.
  - The floor legs take the features away in Chromium, and the walk runs the real browsers.
- **Refused: NoSleep.js's looping video** (https://github.com/richtr/NoSleep.js) in place of the Wake Lock. A video
  kept playing runs under each browser's own autoplay and power rules, and a fallback that works only by them is
  tuned to devices. The sheet's words point to the device's own setting instead.

## 5-§16. Right-click menus

### 5-§16.1 Today

- **No page has a context menu.** No script listens for `contextmenu`; the walk recorded `research:contextmenu
  {defaultPrevented: false}`. Every act is an inline button or a floating picker.
- **The three floating pickers** (the forward menu `app.js:1688-1730`, the reaction picker `:1860-1890`, the admin's link
  picker `admin.js:437-506`) have no role; focus never moves into them; they have no Escape and no arrows; they close
  only on a click elsewhere.
- **The pinned strip loses handlers.** It clones each message and rebinds pin, answer, reply-text, forward, react and
  reply by hand (`app.js:791-853`). 🖥, 📝, ⧉ and help's buttons are not rebound, so they are dead in the strip.
- **Rules live in CSS.** Pin, react and reply are hidden for observers by CSS (`styles.css:1088-1092`). A locked
  account row's reason sits in a disabled button's `title` (`users.js:72`), which touch cannot read and a keyboard
  cannot reach.
- **Measured this round: a native dialog left open drops the page's socket.** The server pings every 10 s and drops a
  peer after 8 s without an answer (`server.js:615-618`). While `confirm()` is open the browser pauses the page's
  scripts, so the page cannot answer (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/timers-and-user-prompts.html#simple-dialogs).
  With Chromium and a research guest (`menus-bench/blocking.js`, results in `blocking.json`):

| Dialog held | Result |
|---|---|
| 12 s | no drop |
| 20 s | one disconnect, and a reconnect |
| 30 s | one disconnect, and every page in the hall reads "Kim30 left · Kim30 joined as research" |

  The three `prompt()`s that link a node (`admin-plus.js:147-153`) ask the admin to read a fingerprint off another
  machine's screen: the likeliest to stay open past 20 s.

### 5-§16.2 The model: one catalogue, every door

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.2: the facts `pin` and `pinMine`, `fold`, R8's `clock`, `onStage`, `pins`); 4-§0 and owner answer S14: Shift+right-click on On stage content opens AGMessage's menu (Part 0 §0.8 C7).

**The catalogue entry.** `public/catalog.js` is a classic script that sets `AGM.catalog`: one list per object kind, as
data and pure functions of facts, with no DOM and no socket. Each page binds only `run(id, ctx)`. An entry:

```
{ id: 'msg.pin',                      // kind.verb: the test key, data-action, the aria-keyshortcuts owner
  label: 'Pin' | (f, o) => …,         // one string: the button's aria-label, its tooltip, the menu item
  icon: '📌',                         // aria-hidden; never a mark of AGM.MARKS
  key: 'P',                           // a single key on the focused object, shown right-aligned in the menu
  group: '3_keep', order: 10,         // §16.3
  inline: (f, o) => 2 | false,        // a rank: the bar draws the two lowest; else only in ⋯
  verb: 'pin' | 'local' | 'http:PATCH /api/users/:id',   // what its run sends; the fence checks it exists
  mode: 'now' | 'hold' | 'self' | 'local',                 // §13.3.4
  may: (f, o) => bool,                // rights: false = absent; each matches a refusal the server words
  fits: (f, o) => bool,               // view, the object's kind and state: false = absent; never asked of the server
  ready: (f, o) => true | words,      // now: words = shown, aria-disabled, focusable, saying why
  confirm: (f, o) => ({title, words, yes, no, choices}) | null,
  undo: 'msg.unpin' | null,           // the id of the entry that takes it back, run by the page's runner
  submenu: (f, o) => [...] | null }
```

- `f` is the page's facts, read once from the join answer and kept current by its events: `role`, `view`, `main`,
  `account`, `admin`, `post`, `files`, `canSendToStage`, `canPropose`, `canScreens`, `canPush`, `canShow`, `stageWeb`,
  `sends`, `forwardable`, `ai`, `connected`, `mayKnowCode`, `manageHalls`, `manageUsers` and `uid`. `o` is the object.
- **Why data:** buttons, menus, keys, the support view and the tests read one list, so they cannot drift. VS Code declares
  a command once and places it in menus with a per-place `when` and an `enablement` that holds in every menu and key
  (https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/contribution-points); JetBrains puts one `AnAction` in many groups
  (https://plugins.jetbrains.com/docs/intellij/action-system.html); Rocket.Chat registers actions for message, room and
  user contexts (https://developer.rocket.chat/docs/action-buttons).
- **One person catalogue serves the hall page's People panel and the admin page's people rows.** The pages keep their
  own runners and socket state; only the labels and rules are shared, which is exactly what must stay in step.

**The rules:**

- **R1. One list, every door.** Right-click, ⋯ and Shift+F10 (or the ContextMenu key) open the same list: the kind's
  entries whose `may` and `fits` hold, in order. The inline bar is that list's two lowest `inline` ranks. An act is
  never reachable only by right-click: ⋯ is always a visible door, as Apple and NN/g require
  (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/context-menus,
  https://www.nngroup.com/articles/contextual-menus/).
- **R2. Absent by rights or by fit; disabled by state, with the reason** (§16.4). While the socket is down, every `now`
  entry is disabled with "Not connected — AGMessage is reconnecting." (the socket.io client would otherwise send the
  click later); `hold` entries stay live and show ◷; `self` and `local` entries act at once. So a Board member's ✕ Back
  to chat during a Wi-Fi blip works, and their answer to a prompt is held, not refused.
- **R3. The server decides.** Hiding never stands for the check. Every entry with a server verb has a `may` that
  matches one of that verb's refusals, and a test sends the verb as every seat whose `may` is false (§16.8). `fits`
  (the simple view, a kind, a state) is never sent to the server and never asserted as a refusal: the server's checks
  never read the view (design §6).
- **R4. Attempts are not facts.** Every `run` that emits goes through `AGM.outbox` in its entry's mode (§13.3.4); the
  toast says `ok` or the server's words. Today 📌 emits with no ack (`app.js:566`).
- **R5. Latest wins, without moving under the pointer.** While a menu is open, its ids and their order are frozen:
  labels, checks, the header and reasons update in place, and an item that became impossible turns disabled with its
  reason. `pages:changed` arrives every 150 ms and reactions at any time, and a rebuilt list would move the item under
  the pointer. The menu closes only when its object is gone, with "That message is gone."
- **R6. The browser's menu stays where it is the right one:** in inputs and text areas (spellcheck, paste); on a text
  selection inside an object (Copy), **except in the Preview**, where the selection is a pick and kind `pick` opens (the
  stage addendum §5.9.7); on links inside a document drawn in the panel (a DOCX keeps its links, `app.js:924`; message
  text is not linkified today); and always with **Shift+right-click** (the Google Docs convention,
  https://support.google.com/docs/answer/179738; Firefox does it anyway). Object links (rooms, halls) take AGMessage's
  menu, which then carries Open in a new tab and Copy link. In the Preview, a `contextmenu` that follows a touch
  `pointerdown` is ignored, so a long press stays the selection gesture.
- **R7. No menu door in the Board's simple view** (§6). No ⋯ on objects and no right-click; every act there is a large
  visible button, and those buttons are catalogue entries asserted in the matrix. The ⋯ sheet is kind `sheet`, drawn as
  56 px rows. The take layer sets `-webkit-touch-callout: none`, so a long press on an image cannot cover a take.
  Where a long press fires `contextmenu` (Chrome on Android), the stage addendum's handler on On stage content still
  keeps the browser's menu away and here opens none of AGMessage's. So a long press on a take does the same on every
  device: nothing (owner answer 22, §15.10).
- **R8. The admin's support view draws exactly the person's menus**, from the person's facts, which the `adminView` +
  `viewOf` join answer appends at the end (`role`, `view`, `canPush`, `canShow`, `sends`, `forwardable`). Every item is
  disabled with "This is Kim's view — act from your own page.", and nothing is emitted. It answers "what does Kim see
  when she right-clicks?" without acting with the admin's rights.

### 5-§16.3 Order, groups and appearance

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.3: 📌 Pin ▸, the fold).

- **The groups, in order:**
  1. `1_respond`: Reply, React, Answer, On my way / Resolved, ✨ Draft a reply, Mention;
  2. `2_send`: 📺 Show the Board, the speaker's screen, Show on screens, Send to ▸, Send back;
  3. `3_keep`: Pin, Look, Download, Copy text, Open in a new tab, Copy code or link;
  4. `4_manage`: seat, chat view, set up, rename, code, may send in (the admin and managers);
  5. `9_danger`: Withdraw, Delete, Log out, Clear messages, Remove.
- **Separators** go between groups. A menu holds at most 12 items, and at most 2 in the danger group, which is always
  last; its items carry a shape and a word ("🗑 Delete…", "✕ Remove…"), with red only as a second cue. Both caps are
  fenced (§16.8).
- **The order is fixed.** Items never reverse when the menu opens upward (Apple suggests it; refused): the order stays
  learnable, and the smoke's deep-equal stays deterministic.
- **Kind `pick` is the exception:** it is exactly the stage addendum's `previewActions(pick)`, in its order, Copy first.
- **"…"** ends the label of any item that confirms or opens a dialog (the ARIA convention), and is never a status mark.
- **Submenus go one level deep:**
  - **Send to ▸**: one list of rooms. The runner sends with `room:send` when the allow-list holds the room, else with
    `forward`; a forward-only room's item carries a second line, "a forward — no withdraw". The person never chooses
    between two wire verbs (Tesler's law).
  - **React ▸**: the eight emoji as `menuitemcheckbox`, checked when they are mine.
  - **Speaker's screen ▸**: 📝 Ask the operator… · 🖥 Send now (owner answer 16: both, chosen per send).
  - **📺 Show the Board ▸** on a file message: p. 1 as a picture · A page… · The whole file (the stage addendum §5.9.7).
  - **Show them ▸** on a person; **Chat view ▸** and **Seat ▸** (`menuitemradio`).
  - With a fine pointer a submenu flies out on click, Enter or →, or after 200 ms of hover; with a coarse one it drills
    in, in the same panel, with a "‹ Back" row.
- **A header line** may name the object, not focusable: "Message from Kim · 14:02", "The Board · 6 pages · 🕐 Clock ✓ ·
  ❝ Ana's quote ✓ 6/6". On a menu that shows something to the Board, the stage addendum's fresh-push words are a header
  line: "The Board is reading Ben's quote (8 s) — Replace · Show a person instead". They inform; nothing is disabled.
- **Keys are shown** right-aligned beside their items. Apple says not to; Figma, VS Code and Google Docs do, and the
  research desk is a sovereign posture where people learn keys from menus.

### 5-§16.4 Disabled, with the reason

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.4: an observer's Pin for the room, applied in place; For me stays live with ◷).

- **Absent** when the seat may never do it here (`may`): an observer's Pin for the room, a non-author's Delete, a Member's Show the
  Board. Showing a Viewer greyed admin items would clutter the menu and tell them what others may do
  (https://helios.hashicorp.design/patterns/disabled-patterns). **Absent** too when it does not fit (`fits`): Withdraw
  on a message that was not sent elsewhere, a menu in the simple view.
- **Shown with `aria-disabled`, focusable, with a second line saying why**, when the seat may do it but not now
  (https://jakobnielsenphd.substack.com/p/inactive-buttons: a disabled control "must not be a communication dead end").
  Choosing it shows the reason in the toast and emits nothing. The reasons reuse words the server and pages already
  have:
  - "Not connected — AGMessage is reconnecting." (`now` entries only)
  - "Stagewatch is not connected right now — nothing is queued; try again when it is." (`app.js:2146`)
  - "No screens in this hall yet — add one in Screens & pages."
  - "No other room takes this message — ask an admin to let this room send." (Send to ▸, when its list comes back
    empty)
  - "This hall has no Stagewatch linked — link one in Set up." (design §5.1)
  - "Already showing the clock." (re-choosing the current kind in the Board chip, which would otherwise make a second
    take and audit row)
  - "Already on chat."
  - "This is Kim's view — act from your own page." (R8)
  - A locked account row keeps a menu whose Edit item is disabled with `u.locked`'s words (`users.js:72`), so the reason
    can be read on touch.
- A show take never disables a push to the information layer: the stage addendum draws information over the show
  (§5.9.1).

### 5-§16.5 Keyboard, pointer and touch parity

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.5: P runs the pin door).

- **`AGM.menu(items, at)`** (`public/menus.js`) is a WAI-ARIA menu: `role=menu` with `menuitem`, `menuitemcheckbox` and
  `menuitemradio` (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/). Focus goes to the first enabled item; ↑ and ↓
  wrap; Home, End and type-ahead move; Enter and Space activate; → and ← open and close a submenu; Escape closes and
  returns focus to the opener; Tab leaves; disabled items stay focusable.
- **Placement:**
  - a mouse or pen opens it at the pointer + 2 px, flipped and clamped to an 8 px margin;
  - the keyboard (Shift+F10, the ContextMenu key, or an event whose `pointerType` is empty) anchors it at the
    bottom-left of the object's ⋯, as browsers place their own
    (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/contextmenu_event);
  - at 480 px or less with a coarse pointer, it is a bottom sheet (§15.8).
- **In the top layer.** It is a `popover="manual"` where `showPopover` exists (Baseline 2024,
  https://web.dev/blog/popover-api), so it draws above the take layer and any dialog. Otherwise, inside a modal dialog
  (Screens & pages) it is mounted inside the open `dialog`, because `showModal()` makes everything outside it inert
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/showModal), and outside one it is fixed at
  `--z-menu`. Its Escape calls `preventDefault` and `stopPropagation`, so a dialog stays open.
- **Touch:** ⋯ is the path (§15.8), on every device. No timer of AGMessage's own runs, on any device (owner answer 22:
  nothing tuned to one device).
  - A timed long press on iOS needs `-webkit-user-select: none` on message bodies, which would take native selection
    from the researcher's Preview (the stage addendum §5.9.6).
  - On Android the browser's own long press fires `contextmenu` first (§15.8), so one timer would act differently on
    each device.
  - Where a browser fires `contextmenu` on a long press, the same menu opens (R1), within R6 and R7. §15.10 holds the
    rest.
- **`AGM.roving(list, {item, keys})`** makes a list one tab stop with ↑, ↓, Home and End; on a focused object Tab
  enters its buttons, Shift+F10 opens its menu, and Escape returns to the composer. Each object carries
  `aria-keyshortcuts`.
- **Single keys on a focused message** (after Discord and Slack,
  https://discord.com/blog/how-to-navigate-discord-using-only-your-keyboard,
  https://slack.com/help/articles/201374536-Slack-keyboard-shortcuts): R reply (focuses the composer), E react (opens
  the picker), F send to (opens the submenu), P pin (with Undo), S show the Board (opens the submenu), D download, Enter
  look, Delete or Backspace delete… (opens the confirm; a Mac's delete key is Backspace). No key needs Shift, and none
  uses a modifier: browsers and the OS reserve many.
- **Sizes:** on a fine pointer, inline icons have hit areas of at least 24×24 px; on a coarse pointer, ↩ and a 44×44 ⋯.
  Each inline button's `aria-label` is its catalogue label.
- **Focus return:** to the opener; after a delete or a withdraw, to the next object, never to `body`.

### 5-§16.6 Confirm in place, and Undo

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.6: Undo by kind, applied in place; the toasts' words).

- **Undo, no confirm,** for what the system can honestly reverse:
  - Pin and Unpin, for the room or for me (the opposite op of the same kind);
  - Minimise and Show again;
  - Back to chat on one's own page ("Show it again" for 10 s) and a card's Remove (Undo for 10 s), by the server rule
    §0 adds to §5.4;
  - a change to one's own page (text size, theme).
  - The toast holds for 10 s, pauses while hovered or focused, and its action is a focusable button inside
    `role=status`.
- **Takes on people's pages:**
  - **A show take** (`canPush`): the toast's Undo for 10 s (design §7.5). Beyond it, the Board chip's menu offers
    **↶ Back to Chat (undo your Clock, 14:02)**, naming what returns, only to the person whose show take is current, and
    sent with `ifSeq`, so it can never undo someone else's later take. A take made by it offers no Undo of its own. The
    show kinds are live (chat, Stagewatch, the clock, holding, blank), so going back re-shows nothing stale.
  - **An information take** (`canPush` or `canShow`): **Take down** only, `{chat, layer: 'info'}` with `ifSeq` (the stage
    addendum §5.9.7). It never re-sends older content, which could pop a quote the Board had already closed back onto
    every page.
- **Confirm in place, no undo,** for what reaches other people for good: Delete (for everyone), Withdraw, Log out a
  person, a screen's Remove and New link, New code, Code off (the design's three-way choice), Clear messages and Remove
  for a room, an account's Remove, Turn off and New one-time password, a node's Unlink, Accept a certificate.
  - **`AGM.ask(anchor, {title, words, fields, yes, no, choices, danger})`** (`public/menus.js`) is a non-modal
    `role=dialog` with `aria-modal=false`, labelled by its title, anchored to the object (`alertdialog` is modal by
    WAI-ARIA, so it is not used). It names the object and the consequence; its buttons are verbs; focus starts on the
    safe choice, and Escape means no. One is open at a time: opening another answers the first "no", and R5's "gone"
    closes it. The feed and the socket keep running.
  - "Withdraw from Legal? It goes from Legal's chat now; people there may have read it (it was there 40 s)." **[Withdraw]
    [Keep it]**
  - **Log out, by case:**
    - a code guest, code on: "Log Kim out of Legal? Every page Kim has open here closes. Kim can join again with the
      code." **[Log out] [Keep Kim in]**
    - a code guest, after Code off or New code: "… Kim can come back only with the new code or an invite."
    - an account: "… Kim's account still has Legal and can open it again. To keep Kim out, take Legal off the account on
      the Accounts page."
    - The page sent out reads "An admin sent you out of Legal." with **Back to sign-in** (`server.js:1542`).
  - The admin page's in-page Close meeting panel (`admin.html:81-85`) is the house precedent.
- **`prompt()` becomes fields in place** (`AGM.ask` with `fields`): rename a screen; reply in words; a new hall's name;
  the node link, as one form of three fields, with the pairing field `autocomplete=off`.
- **Delete is not an Undo.** Holding the delete back for a few seconds would leave the message on everyone's page
  against the deleter's intent. It moves off the inline bar into ⋯, away from 📌 (24×20 beside 28×20 today).

"—" separates groups. Kinds are named by their id prefix. Each row's verbs are server verbs or routes (§16.8). The unit
is where its rows land; later rows join as their verbs do (§16.10). `may` is the rights column; `fits` and `ready` are
the rest.

**The message menu by seat:**

| Seat | What the message menu holds |
|---|---|
| On stage, simple view | no menu door; the buttons: answers, Reply in words…, 👁 Look, Got it, Help |
| On stage, full view | respond, keep (no Download), Send to ▸ where allowed, Delete own |
| Backstage, Main | adds ✨ Draft a reply (with AI), the speaker's screen, 📺 Show the Board (`canShow` or `canPush`) and ⧉ Show on screens (`display.control`) |
| Observer or Viewer | Copy, and Send to ▸ (forward) for text only, where they may post elsewhere; 📌 Pin for me; no Look and no Download (owner answer 20; the stage addendum's S2: their pages hold no file's link) |
| Side-room Member | respond, keep, Send to ▸ by the allow-list, Delete own; nothing of the stage |
| The admin | everything, plus Delete for everyone (`admin:deleteMessage`) on the admin page |

**`forwardable`** is a fact, not a guess: the join answer appends it at the end (an account that may post in another
hall, or a guest with a linked or open other hall), `linkedRoomsChanged` updates it (heard from unit 3a), and the page
asks `myRooms` once when it becomes visible again, since a person who opened another hall in another tab comes back
through `visibilitychange`.

### 5-§16.8 The in-step fence

> **Amended by** 7-§0.2 (§16.8: the matrix, applied in place for observers and Viewers; the fold fence; the new fixtures).

1. **`test/catalog.test.js`** (pure; it loads `public/catalog.js` with `vm`):
   - ids are unique and shaped `kind.verb`; every group is known; danger entries are last and carry `confirm` or `undo`
     (kind `pick` excepted: it is `previewActions` exactly);
   - keys are unique per kind, a single printable character that needs no Shift or a named key, never with a modifier;
   - every `verb` is a socket verb read from `handlerFiles()` (§14.4 g), an HTTP route the server mounts
     (`app.<method>(` in server.js and `lib/http-accounts.js`, written `http:PATCH /api/users/:id`), or `local`;
   - **the modes:** every `message`, `room:send` and `actionResponse` entry is `hold`; every `page:report` entry is
     `self`; every `local` verb is `local`;
   - **one verb for one act:** every entry that puts something on people's pages is labelled with "Show" (Show the
     Board, Show them, Show Ana), and none says "screen" unless it acts on a `/d/` screen;
   - catalogue icons and `AGM.MARKS` are disjoint (fence n);
   - a required-verbs list holds every 0.6.0 verb of §16.7, and grows in each unit that adds one;
   - **the seat × view matrix:** for fixture facts (Board guest simple and full, a Board account, research locked and
     open, observer, Viewer, Staff with and without `stage.web`, Tech, the admin, a side-room Member), the expected
     shown sets (`may && fits`): an observer and a Viewer have no `msg.pin` and have `msg.pinMine` and no `msg.download`; neither an observer nor a Viewer
     has `msg.look` (the stage addendum's S2); a Member has no `msg.stage`; the simple view has no menu door, and its
     buttons are the asserted inline sets;
   - **the inline bar:** at most two per seat, view and object fixture, and the precedence for the second is the one
     written in §16.7;
   - **the caps:** the richest fixture of each kind shows at most 12 items, at most 2 in danger.
2. **`test/menus.test.js`** (a real server): every entry with a server verb, sent as each seat whose `may` is false with
   the minimal payload, is answered `ok: false` with words. Only `may` is iterated: an entry hidden by `fits` (the
   simple view, a kind, a state) is not sent, so the server is never asked to read the view.
3. **The browser smoke** (raw CDP, `test/browser-smoke.js:59-120`), for each seat × view and each object on the page:
   - right-click's `[data-action]` ids deep-equal the catalogue's shown set; ⋯ deep-equals right-click; Shift+F10 on the
     focused object deep-equals both, with focus on the first enabled item;
   - the inline bar's ids are a subset of the menu's, and each inline button's accessible name equals its menu label;
   - right-click on a selection in the Preview opens exactly `previewActions`, Copy first;
   - Escape follows the Escape order, and inside Screens & pages the dialog stays open;
   - an open menu keeps its ids and order across a `pages:changed`;
   - a disabled item is focusable, shows its reason, and emits nothing (the page's emits counted); the support view's
     menus draw with every item disabled and emit nothing;
   - targets are at least 24 px, or 44 px on a coarse pointer (`Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled`, with
     `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` and `mobile: true` for the 390×844 pass);
   - a dialog guard: a `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` listener fails the run on any native `alert`, `confirm` or
     `prompt`, and `Page.handleJavaScriptDialog` dismisses it so the run ends;
   - both themes, with no console error and no CSP violation.
   This replaces unit 3's deep-equal of menu against buttons, which would fail as soon as a menu holds a ⋯-only item
   such as Copy text.
4. **Source guards** (`test/resilience.test.js`): `addEventListener('contextmenu'` appears only in `public/menus.js`;
   `cloneNode` appears in `app.js` only at the template's site, by name (`tpl.content.firstElementChild.cloneNode(true)`,
   `app.js:434`; `importNode` is refused outside `parseInert` by the stage addendum's lint rule); `public/catalog.js`,
   `public/menus.js` and `public/outbox.js` are in the page list (by §14.4 h, with no hand edit).
5. **ESLint `no-alert`** (https://eslint.org/docs/latest/rules/no-alert): on `app/public/app.js` in unit 3c, widened to
   `app/public/**/*.js` in unit 3b. Its measured cause is §16.1's table.

### 5-§16.9 Fit to the plan's verbs

Every `verb` in the catalogue is checked against the server's own verbs (§16.8 1), and every verb hidden by rights
against its refusal (§16.8 2). A renamed or removed verb therefore fails the build, where today a page that emits it
would wait forever for an ack, with no error. With §14.4 (f), the wire's words are closed in both directions, and the
menus are closed against the wire.

### 5-§16.10 How this extends unit 3, exactly

- **Unit 3 becomes three units.**
  - **Unit 3a: the menus and the message.** `public/menus.js` (`AGM.menu`, `AGM.ask`, top-layer mounting),
    `public/catalog.js`, and the delegated handlers on `#feed` and `#pinnedList` (the pinned strip on the feed's
    handler, no clone). Kinds `msg`, `file` and `screen`, with their confirms through `AGM.ask`, so no menu path opens a
    native dialog. `forwardable` heard. The "What moved" line. Fences 1, 2 and 4 of §16.8 for these kinds, and the smoke
    of §16.8 3 for them.
  - **Unit 3c: the rest of the hall page.** `app.js`'s remaining native dialogs (Reply in words as a field; `alert`s to
    the toast); `notify` and `flashStatus` become `AGM.toast(text, badOrOpts)`, and app.html and admin.html load
    `common.js`; the skip link and the roving feed (`AGM.roving`); observers' prompt options as text; kinds `person`
    (the hall page's half, and the sender's name as its door), `compose`, `chip` and `code` (copy items); `no-alert` on
    `app.js`.
  - **Unit 3b: the other pages.** The admin page (`adminRoom`, `person`'s admin half, the feed's Delete for everyone,
    `link`, the header and Logout), the halls board (`hall`, `help`, the stretched link) and the Accounts page
    (`account`, `audit`), each with its skip link and roving list; the 23 native dialogs of `admin.js`, `admin-plus.js`
    and `users.js` go; halls.html loads `outbox.js`, `catalog.js` and `menus.js` after `common.js`, and users.html
    `catalog.js` and `menus.js`; `common.js:71` extends `AGM`; `no-alert` on every page script.
- **What changes in §7.7's text:**
  - `menus.js` "defines only `AGM.menu`" → it defines `AGM.menu`, `AGM.ask` and `AGM.roving`; `catalog.js` is new.
  - "each page keeps its own `messageActions(msg, ctx)`, `personActions`, `roomActions`, `takeActions`" → each page
    keeps its own **runners**; the lists are catalogue kinds, shared where the object is the same (one `person`
    catalogue for two pages).
  - "app.html and admin.html load it" → app.html, admin.html, halls.html and users.html load it, after `common.js`.
  - §7.7's table → §16.7.
  - "The smoke compares each menu's items with the visible buttons" → §16.8 3.
  - The delegated handlers stay exactly as §7.7 says (`#feed`, `#pinnedList`, `#peopleList`, the admin tables), plus
    the halls list and the accounts table.
- **Each later unit adds its own rows, refusal cases and smoke objects:** unit 6: `adminRoom` (watch, rename, reset,
  remove, create); unit 7: `code` (New code, Code on / off) and `adminRoom`'s code items; unit 10: `adminRoom`'s
  Members…, `hall`'s Set up; unit 11: `room`; unit 12: `adminRoom.sendFrom`; unit 14: `msg.send`, `msg.sendBack`,
  `compose`'s To; unit 15: `msg.withdraw`; units 17-18: `board`, `take`, `card`, `person.show`, `person.chat`; unit 19:
  web in `board` and `take`; unit 20: `person.view`, `account.view`, `sheet`; unit 21: `room.markRead`; the stage
  addendum's 24-29: `person.takeDown`, `board`'s `canShow` rows, `msg.stage`, `file`'s stage items, `pick`, `compose`'s
  Share.
- **Unit 34** asserts the required-verbs list complete.

## 5-§12. Risks, left for later, and the owner's answers (adds to §12)

### 5-Risks

- **A first open of a large hall goes uncompressed** (1.37 MB at 5,000 messages against 112 KB). On the venue LAN that
  is fast; through the tunnel to a phone on mobile data it is not. Unit 32 bounds it in 0.6.0 (owner answer 33).
- **Coalescing delays:** after a burst, a seen receipt up to 1 s, the people list up to 0.1 s, a room's dot up to
  0.5 s. A lone change goes at once. None is a fact a glance can tell apart.
- **A held message is sent late**, however long it waited, and the sender is not asked first (owner answer 27). Its
  `held` says so to every reader.
- **A held message sits in the tab's `sessionStorage`** until sent, on a shared tablet too. It is never sent as another
  person and never outlives the tab; a held file never survives a reload.
- **Old messages carry no `cid`.** A page cached across the upgrade sends without one, and gets today's at-most-once.
- **`page:push`'s repeat memory is in memory:** a repeat after a restart is a second take of the same content and one
  more audit row.
- **Two registration places** (server.js's closure and `lib/handlers/`), until a unit rewrites an old handler. CLAUDE.md
  says so.
- **The catalogue is a list to keep.** A verb renamed without its row fails the build; that is its purpose.
- **34 native dialogs leave in three units across four files.** The smoke's dialog guard fails the run on any left.
- **No long press on iOS.** ⋯ is the touch path on every device; Android's own long press opens the same menu in the
  full view, except in the Preview, and nothing in the simple view (§15.10).
- **Words change** for a crew used to "session" and "meeting", and the restart line changes in every restored hall. The
  CHANGELOG lists them; the words Stagewatch reads do not change (owner answer 30).
- **A doors-open storm still writes one "joined" line per person**, each a broadcast (N²/2 frames). Reading 8 decides
  whether presence lines coalesce.
- **The watchdog's 0.5 s first step** could meet a port Windows has not released, which exits with code 3 and stops the
  watchdog. The Windows test is the gate; until it passes 20 of 20, 2 s stays.
- **The tunnel's ceiling refuses real phones.**
  - Past 150 places a remote phone waits, with words, for one to free. On the venue's Wi-Fi it is never refused for
    the tunnel.
  - The number rests on Cloudflare's documented 200, and on the cautious reading that an open WebSocket counts against
    it, until reading 0's tunnel row says.
- **Cloudflare can still refuse a page's files.** With many phones loading at once, more than the 50 spare in-flight
  requests can be asked for, and Cloudflare answers `429` to a file the server never sees. That refusal has no words
  of AGMessage's, and a page whose script did not load cannot say so. Reading 7's walk and the named tunnel (left for
  later) answer it; the places cannot.
- **One network's crowd waits together.** Behind one carrier's address, phones share 3 connections a second and half
  the places, and one person's wrong codes lock `join` for every phone behind that address for a minute (RFC 6269
  §13.1). The words say "your network", so the person knows it is not their phone.
- **A device below the page floor is refused with words**, not served half a page. An iPad of the owner's that cannot
  reach iPadOS 14.5 is a ✕ in the walk, which holds the tag until the floor is lowered for it or the owner retires it
  from the Board (owner answer 22), and its `docs/DEVICES.md` row says which.
- **The Wake Lock is missing on iPads before iPadOS 18.4** (MDN's data). There the device's own screen setting decides,
  and the sheet says which setting.
- **Nothing here was measured on the show laptop, through a tunnel or on the Board's devices,** and the VM's 25-page
  and coalesced rows are not reproduced. Every threshold of §13.4 waits for its reading, the papers say "not measured"
  until then, and `docs/DEVICES.md` says "not walked" for each row the owner has no device for.

### 5-Left for later

- A command palette (Ctrl+K). The catalogue makes it cheap; nothing measured asks for it.
- Moving the 57 existing handlers; splitting the admin group (rooms, settings, certificates, tunnel). The first
  candidate is whichever group a later unit rewrites.
- `app.js` and `admin.js` using `common.js`'s escaping and theme in place of their copies.
- WebTransport, and zstd or dictionary compression.
- The connection bucket's burst (reading 2), compaction at a quiet moment (reading 4), presence lines coalesced
  (reading 8).
- `content-visibility`, inside unit 32's window.
- Multi-select with bulk actions; swipe gestures on messages.
- An Undo for Delete.
- **A named Cloudflare Tunnel** for shows with remote phones: a fixed address, and Cloudflare's own advice "For stable
  hostnames and production traffic"
  (https://developers.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-one/connections/connect-networks/do-more-with-tunnels/trycloudflare/).
  The install addendum's papers already recommend it (U10). Reading 7 takes it up after a show with refusals or 120
  places used.
- Menus as `popover` only and CSS `light-dark()`: not while the page floor (Safari 14.1, Chrome 84) is below the
  versions that bring them (§15.10).
- No long-press timer of AGMessage's own is left for later: owner answer 22 settles it (§16.5).

### 5-Gaps (not measured, not verified)

- The fan-out bench's 25-page rows, the 200-page CPU per message today, the coalesced variants and isolated seen
  receipts (reading 0).
- `restart.js`, `eld.js`, `compact*.js`, `fsync.js` and the browser renders were printed, not kept in a file (reading 0
  records them).
- Whether help's Send at 390 px can be reached by a pan on a real phone; the walk's automated tap failed with its error
  discarded.
- How often guests mistype a code; how often a Board member taps ✕ by accident.
- The glance test (reading 9).
- Whether an open WebSocket counts against a Quick Tunnel's 200 in-flight requests; the first open's time to a phone on
  mobile data; the laptop's own uplink (reading 0's tunnel row, and reading 7).
- §15.10's fallbacks on real devices: the walk in `docs/DEVICES.md`, until each row is filled. `dvh`'s effect on an
  older iPad is read from the rule, not walked.

### 5-Owner's answers

Every question this section asked (21–33) is answered, and each answer, quoted, with what the plan does, is in **Owner's
answers (2026-10-27)** at the head of this addendum. Nothing here is "(to confirm)", and no question is left open in this
addendum. The plan's one open question (S4, not A4) is not this addendum's.

- **Inline "Ask the operator" whenever `canPropose || canSendToStage`** (design council 6): taken with a correction.
  Without a desk the operator cannot be asked, so the inline act is then 🖥 Send now; both stay in the submenu (owner
  answer 16).
- **"Show to the Board"** (design council 7): taken in another form. The stage addendum's final words, "Show the
  Board", are used everywhere, and the owner kept them (owner answer 24).
- **Amend the stage addendum so the browser's long press opens the menu in the Preview** (design council 12): not
  taken. Its final (§5.9.7) keeps the long press as the selection gesture a pick needs; ⋯ and a second tap are the touch
  doors there, and R6 gains the Preview's exception.
- **"Send to the Board" sends the whole file at the Preview's page** (design council 15): not taken. The final's
  "📺 Show the Board ▸ p. 1 as a picture · A page… · The whole file" supersedes it (owner answer 11: both, per push).
- **The "Board sees" line for `canShow` only** (design council 24): taken in another form. The line goes for everyone:
  the stage addendum gives `canShow` the Board chip, which already says what the Board sees.
