# Part 6: Addendum: a full Windows install, and upgrading the server

*`060/addendum-install.md`, 1630 lines, kept whole. Its headings carry the prefix `6-`; its units carry their global number, [#n] (Part 0 §0.3).*

Requester: the owner's list, verbatim: "Research and assess benefits of a full windows install, including upgrading
server." Then the owner's answers to this addendum's questions 34–45 (2026-10-27), which settle every one of them.
Evidence class: research (Microsoft's, Inno Setup's, Node's, libuv's, shawl's, WinSW's, NSSM's, GitHub's and Mozilla's
own documentation and source), the code (AGMessage on `main` at `89104d8`; PlayMap's installer and supervisor,
Stagewatch's installer and Patterns' updater, read in their trees), measurements on a Linux machine standing in for
Windows (Node 24.22.1, 4 vCPU Xeon 2.8 GHz), two reviews of the draft (the operator and the admin on a show day; security
and the Windows platform), and the owner's answers. Each review finding was checked against the code or its source
before it was taken. **Nothing was run on Windows.** The parts this revision adds for answers 35, 38 and 45 (U.5, U.5.1,
U15, U17, U18) have had no review of their own yet.

Section and unit numbers are placeholders (U.n, unit Un) until this addendum is spliced in after the start-window,
audit-chain and architecture addenda. The draft's letter W is not used, because the architecture addendum's unit W ("one
word per thing") holds it. The owner's questions continued the architecture addendum's numbering, from 34; all twelve are
answered below, and none is left open here. Read with it: `design.md`, `addendum-startup.md` (unit S),
`addendum-audit-hmac.md` (units H, H2 and H3, in its revision for answers 34, 35, 38 and 45), `addendum-arch-ux.md` (in
its final numbers: units Q, B, D and R, readings 0-9, the close at 34) and `DECISIONS.md`.

The scripts and their raw output are under
`060/bench-install/`:
- `scripts/` (the restart gap, the PE signer);
- `upgrade/` (the gap matrix, phases, compaction, requires; `upgrade/out/table.txt`);
- `portable-lens/` (M1-M3);
- `assess/` (the payload count);
- `critique/` (the sleep and throttle proxies);
- `crit-walk/` (modules loaded from outside the app);
- `crit-dl/` (libuv's pipe source);
- `final/` (the three version orders; the watchdog's late-tick prototype, run through the sleep and throttle proxies).

A figure below without one of these files behind it is marked "computed", "documented" or "inferred".

## 6-Owner's answers (2026-10-27)

> **Read with** Part 0 §0.4.9.

The owner answered every question this addendum asked, in one message: "Defaults except for: … 34 - Installer in 0.6.0 ·
35 - Yes · 38 - Whichever account it is installed on. Could be either an admin account or standard. The admin will be
whoever does the install. They can add permissions or handover to another account. · 45 - Archive old event data. A new
event can continue a previous event, copy the settings and structure of a previous event, or start fresh. Keep linking
settings. Carry on audit log with an archive point an entry in it. Admin can choose to split the audit log and archive
the older part." For 36, 37 and 39–44, "Defaults" is the default this addendum proposed, as `DECISIONS.md` states
it. Each question is quoted as it was asked, then answered, then what the plan does.

- **34. "Build the installer in 0.6.0, once U7's readings are in, or keep 0.6.0 to U1-U11 and open 0.7.0 with
  U12-U16?"** → "Installer in 0.6.0"
  - U12–U18 land in 0.6.0 with U1–U11. U7's Windows readings are still taken. They inform the release (its notes,
    `docs/INSTALL.md`, the hour-before-doors card) and never hold it: a reading that misses its mark is written there,
    with the fallback its unit already names (U7).
- **35. "Must the show laptop ever serve with nobody signed in (after a Windows Update restart or a power cut, before
  anyone types a password)?"** → "Yes"
  - The installed node starts with Windows, in session 0, with its data and keys in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`.
    B-session is no longer a shape.
  - B-task is chosen over B-service, with the evidence and what it costs (U.5).
- **36. "Unsigned, as PlayMap is, or signed?"** → "Defaults": unsigned, named `-unsigned`, with SHA256SUMS.
  - Under answer 35 it also decides the shape. B-service's host could never be signed, and Smart App Control treats an
    unsigned program as untrusted (U.5). The Smart App Control words go in `README.txt` and the release notes.
  - An upgrade by an account that is not an administrator is checked against the release's published digest instead of
    a signature (U18).
- **37. "Who may reach it, and when?"** → "Defaults": the local subnet only, and never the Public profile unless chosen
  at install. It starts with Windows (35).
  - Each firewall rule names the program, the protocol and the local port, and allows the local subnet only, which
    Microsoft describes as "only from computers on the same subnet as the local computer"
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/netsecurity/new-netfirewallrule, example 3).
  - The rules cover Private and Domain. Public is added only when the install page's "Also on Public networks" is ticked
    (unticked; silently `/PUBLICFIREWALL=1`).
  - No page asks whether it starts with Windows: it always does.
- **38. "Which Windows account is the show account, is it a standard account, and who holds administrator rights on
  the show laptop?"** → "Whichever account it is installed on. Could be either an admin account or standard. The admin
  will be whoever does the install. They can add permissions or handover to another account."
  - The Windows account that starts the installer is **the laptop's admin**, standard or administrator. It is found as
    U.5.1 says, also when an administrator approves the elevation with their own credentials.
  - A standard account is asked for an administrator's approval once, at the install.
  - The laptop's admin holds the laptop's token and the start, stop and upgrade rights. It gives any of them to another
    Windows account, takes them back, or hands the admin over, through the machine's own commands
    (`DECISIONS.md`'s reading: "the supervisor's own commands"; U17). Each give, take-back and handover is an audit row.
  - An upgrade by the laptop's admin, or by an account given `upgrade`, needs no administrator when the machine can check
    the installer against its release (U18).
- **39. "May an upgrade stop a busy server, and what is busy?"** → "Defaults": busy as proposed, and a busy server is
  stopped only with a typed reason.
  - Busy is activity in the last 10 minutes (a message, a take changed, a help request, input on a seated page) or a
    running Stagewatch countdown (U8). The reason becomes `server.stop.forced`.
- **40. "The token is a file the named show account may read, with no administrator prompt. Is that the 'laptop's
  token' your crew can reach?"** → "Defaults": yes.
  - It is read by the laptop's admin and by each account given `token` (U2, U17).
- **41. "'Session restored' in every hall on every start: keep it, or write it only after a stop that did not save
  cleanly?"** → "Defaults": only after a stop that did not save cleanly (the plan's choice; U4).
- **42. "After a portable folder is imported, the show user's account still holds `secret.key`, the machine key and the
  certificate's private key"** (rotate `secret.key`? keep the certificate?) → "Defaults": the plan's choice.
  - `secret.key` and the certificate are kept, so guests, invites, pins and trusted devices hold.
  - The old copies are removed from that account's profile once the import is verified (U14).
- **43. "On uninstall, keep the data, or ask, offering 'Remove all AGMessage data from this PC'?"** → "Defaults": the
  data is kept, with "Remove all AGMessage data from this PC" offered unticked (silently `/REMOVEDATA`; U13).
- **44. "Do venue laptops (not yours) ever get the installer, or only the portable folder?"** → "Defaults": the plan's
  choice. Venue laptops use the portable folder, and the installer is for the owner's own laptops.
- **45. "What does a new event carry over on an installed node (U15)?"** → "Archive old event data. A new event can
  continue a previous event, copy the settings and structure of a previous event, or start fresh. Keep linking
  settings. Carry on audit log with an archive point an entry in it. Admin can choose to split the audit log and
  archive the older part."
  - U15, on both channels. A new event continues a previous event, copies its settings and structure, or starts fresh.
  - The old event's data is archived, never deleted silently. Linking settings stay in all three.
  - The audit log carries on through an archive point, `audit.archive`, and the admin (the token at the laptop, or an
    account whose role is `admin`) may split it there.
  - The point, the split and the check from the point are unit H3's (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.10). The point is
    U15's one row for archiving an event, and U15's dialog offers the split.
  - The plan's readings beyond the owner's words, said here (U15): under copy, guest codes and invites are new, and
    screen links are new unless "Keep the screens' links" is ticked (unticked), since codes and links are capabilities,
    not structure; start fresh keeps no account, and the token at the laptop makes the first admin account, as at a
    first start; "Delete this archive's contents…", typed by the token at the laptop and audited, removes an archive's
    messages, files and accounts when asked, never on a timer, and keeps its `event.json`.
- **Beside them, answer 29** ("wrap into 0.6.0") means there is no 0.5.2. This addendum's 0.5.2 paths are gone (U6, U9,
  "What can move").
- **Nothing in this addendum is "(to confirm)".** The plan's one open question (S4, not A4) is not this addendum's.

## 6-U.0 The answer on one page

- **The benefits are real, and most come from three things an install does once.**
  - **One fixed path in Program Files.**
    - The firewall is opened before the first start, and it never prompts again for a new version.
    - AppLocker's default rules let every account run programs from there. The same rules block a portable folder in
      Downloads or on a stick for a standard account.
  - **The data apart from the program.** An upgrade keeps every hall, account, sealed key, certificate pin and audit
    head, and a shared program folder never carries data.
  - **One copy per machine, with a defined upgrade.** Only a newer build installs. The running server is asked first.
    The new build's start is verified, and there is a way back that needs no download.
  - **Serving with nobody signed in is the fourth, and the owner asked for it** (answer 35). Only a startup task or a
    service gives it, and it is the one that costs the show day most (U.3, U.5).
- **0.6.0 lands all of it** (answers 29 and 34).
  - **The seams both channels need** (units U1-U11). Each fixes a fault measured or read in today's portable copy, or
    measures what nobody has measured (U7). The faults:
    - the admin token lands in captured output;
    - an unusable folder loops a restarter;
    - keys are written before the folder lock;
    - a 1M-message stop is killed mid-save;
    - the server is killed and restarted unsaved on every wake from sleep;
    - modules load from a parent folder's `node_modules`, `C:\node_modules` on a typical path;
    - a certificate or token is remade on a read error;
    - the tunnel is lost at every restart.
  - **The installer** (units U12-U18). U7's readings are taken beside it and inform the release; none holds it.
- **The installed shape is B-task** (answers 35 and 36; U.5):
  - per machine, the program in Program Files;
  - a Task Scheduler task, `\AGMessage\Server`, starts it at boot, with nobody signed in, as LocalService under a SID of
    its own (`NT TASK\AGMessage-Server`) and without `SeImpersonatePrivilege`;
  - data, uploads, keys, logs and the token in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`, which only SYSTEM, Administrators and that SID
    may use (the token also read by the laptop's admin and the accounts it gives `token`);
  - no unsigned program at run time: the task runs `node.exe`, which carries OpenJS Foundation's signature.
  - **Not B-service:** its host (shawl) stays unsigned under answer 36, and Smart App Control, which "in most cases …
    will automatically turn on", treats an unsigned program as untrusted (U.5).
  - **Not B-session:** it serves only once someone signs in (answer 35).
  - **What B-task costs** (U.5):
    - a Windows shutdown or restart ends the server unsaved. Acknowledged messages are kept; lane writes up to 200 ms
      old and the audit entries since the head's last save are not;
    - a crash of the watchdog itself is started again only if Task Scheduler does so (R12);
    - it listens from boot on every network the laptop joins, to the local subnet only (answer 37);
    - it has no window and no entry in Services.
- **The laptop's admin is the Windows account that runs the install** (answer 38; U.5.1, U17).
  - It may be standard or an administrator. A standard account asks an administrator's approval once, at the install.
  - It holds the laptop's token, start, stop and upgrade. It gives them to another Windows account, takes them back, or
    hands the admin over, through the machine's own commands. Each act is an audit row.
  - An upgrade it starts needs no administrator when the machine can check the installer against its release's published
    digest (U18). Otherwise Windows asks, as at the install.
- **Events** (answer 45; U15):
  - a new event continues a previous event, copies its settings and structure, or starts fresh;
  - the old event's data is archived, never deleted silently, and the links stay;
  - the audit log carries on through an archive point, and an admin may split it there (unit H3).
- **The portable folder stays a first-class channel**, built from the same stage as the installer. It is the channel
  venue laptops use (answer 44).
- **Upgrading the server.**
  - **[A] The install's upgrade path** takes PlayMap's order, refusals and CI proof. It adds three things PlayMap's
    lacks (U.6.1):
    - a verified start of the new build;
    - a way back with no download: the previous installer is kept, and the server backs up its data at the upgrade's
      stop;
    - an upgrade the laptop's admin or a granted account starts without an administrator, checked against the release
      (U18).
  - **[B] The live upgrade:** today's stop-then-start under the watchdog is enough.
    - On typical folders the new server answers in 0.44-0.67 s, and pages are back in 0.7-1.5 s.
    - The cost at size is the server's own full rewrite of every room, at stop and again at boot: health answers
      after 3.1 s at 200k messages and 12.5 s at 1M. U4 removes that cost.
    - Nothing beyond it (socket handoff, a warm spare, a proxy, cluster) is justified by the readings (U.6.2).

## 6-U.1 The question, its readings, and what was not measured

- **"Upgrading server" is read two ways.** Each finding below says which reading it answers:
  - **[A] the install's upgrade path:** a new version over an old one, data kept, a downgrade refused, a portable
    folder's data brought in;
  - **[B] the live upgrade:** the running server upgraded with the least interruption to a show.
  - A third reading, AGMessage on Windows Server, is answered only in passing. Nothing was tested there.
- **Measured here (Linux, as a proxy):**
  - **the restart gap:** stop, boot, and a page back, on seeded folders from 1 hall to 1M messages
    (`upgrade/out/table.txt`, `out/restart-small.txt`, `out/restart-big.txt`);
  - **phases inside one start**, compaction and module requires (`upgrade/out/compact-bench.txt`, `require-bench.txt`);
  - **M1, M2 and M3:** the watchdog run as a service would run it, a copy refused at the lock, and the version orders
    (`portable-lens/out-*.txt`);
  - **the three version orders** of the same seven builds (`final/out-order3.txt`);
  - **sleep and throttling**, with both processes frozen and thawed: today's watchdog (`critique/out-*.txt`) and a
    prototype of U9's late-tick rule (`final/out-*-fix.txt`), which still kills a real hang
    (`final/out-hang-still-fix.txt`);
  - **the module walk:** a `supports-color` and a `bufferutil` planted in a `node_modules` three folders above the app
    were loaded by `require('debug'); require('ws')` (`crit-walk/out.txt`);
  - **the payload:**
    - 104 production packages, 5,077 files and 23.8 MB under `node_modules`;
    - 43 files and 4.9 MB of AGMessage's own (`assess/out-prod-files.txt`);
    - beside them, `node.exe` is 93.9 MB and `cloudflared.exe` 65.8 MB;
  - **signatures, read from each PE file's certificate table:**
    - `node.exe` 24.22.1 carries OpenJS Foundation's signature;
    - `cloudflared.exe` 2026.3.0 carries Cloudflare's;
    - WinSW 2.12.0 and NSSM 2.24-101 carry none;
    - shawl's was not read.
    - The structure was read, but **Windows verified no signature** (`scripts/pe-signer.js`; reading R5).
- **Read in source, not run:**
  - libuv's console handler turns Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Break and a closed console into signals, and leaves
    `CTRL_LOGOFF_EVENT` and `CTRL_SHUTDOWN_EVENT` to Windows' default, with the comment "These signals are only sent to
    services" (`src/win/signal.c`, `uv__signal_control_handler`, v1.x,
    https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.x/src/win/signal.c). So a `node.exe` that is not a service is ended at a
    Windows shutdown without a JavaScript handler running (inferred; lab 5).
  - shawl accepts `STOP | SHUTDOWN`, sends Ctrl-C to its child for both, waits `--stop-timeout` (3,000 ms by default),
    then kills it (`src/service.rs`, https://github.com/mtkennerly/shawl/blob/master/src/service.rs).
- **Not measured.** Each becomes a reading in U7, a lab line, or stays open:
  - anything on Windows: NTFS with Defender scanning each write, the time to replace about 5,120 files and 188 MB, the
    upgrade's backup, and a Windows shutdown reaching the task's `node.exe` in session 0 (lab 5);
  - a LocalService task's `%LOCALAPPDATA%`, `os.homedir()` and privileges, and UDP 9928 and cloudflared under it (R4);
  - whether a standard account may create `C:\node_modules` or `%ProgramData%\AGMessage` on the show laptop (R8);
  - an elevated administrator reading another user's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage`, and Inno Setup's `ExecAsOriginalUser`
    under over-the-shoulder elevation (R6);
  - the access list libuv gives the folder-hold pipe under the task's token, and whether a remote client reaches it (R7);
  - whether a task whose security descriptor gives one account read and execute can be run on demand by that account,
    and by no other (R11);
  - whether Task Scheduler's RestartOnFailure acts on a non-zero exit. Microsoft's schema says the task is restarted "if
    the task fails for any reason"
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/taskschedulerschema-restartonfailure-settingstype-element),
    and the settings page "if the task fails to run (the last run result of the task is not a success)"
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/windows/it-pro/windows-server-2008-r2-and-2008/cc722178(v=ws.11)).
    An informal 2012 report saw no restart after a non-zero exit
    (https://vbdotnetforums.com/threads/returning-run-status-to-wub-7-task-scheduler.50906) (R12);
  - GitHub's release answer reached from a SYSTEM task on the show laptop's networks (R13);
  - whether Smart App Control blocks `.bat` or PowerShell helpers (lab 4);
  - a real laptop's sleep, lid and Fast Startup. The proxies freeze processes; they do not suspend a machine.
- **CI cannot take some readings as it stands.** GitHub's Windows images turn Defender's real-time monitoring off and
  exclude `C:\` and `D:\` (`Set-MpPreference … ExclusionPath = @("D:\", "C:\")`, `DisableRealtimeMonitoring = $true`,
  `actions/runner-images/images/windows/scripts/build/Configure-WindowsDefender.ps1`). Windows Server 2025 has neither
  Modern Standby nor Smart App Control. Those readings are lab lines on the show laptop (U7).
- **Not kept, so not cited:** an earlier restart run at 40 and 200 halls of 2,000 messages. Its figures were in line
  with the table in U.6.2, but its raw output was not kept.

## 6-U.2 How the show network ships today

| Node | Ships as | Upgrade | What AGMessage takes from it |
|---|---|---|---|
| **PlayMap** | Inno Setup 7.1, per machine, Program Files only, unsigned and named `-unsigned` with SHA256SUMS. A LocalSystem service starts the engine in the show user's session; the node's data stays in that user's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PlayMap` (`Mapper/docs/INSTALL.md:8-88`) | An older or equal build is refused with words. A fail-closed armed check comes first, then `upgrade-stop`. An upgrade that does not reach its end rolls back and starts the earlier service again. **After the files are in place**, a failed machine-level setup leaves the new files and the machine unsupervised, so the earlier build is gone (`INSTALL.md`, Upgrades). Uninstall keeps data. CI proves the rest, elevated, on windows-2025 (`installer/tests/…/InstallerTests.cs:160-219`) | The tool, the `.iss` skeleton, the refusal words, the machine-command contract and the CI life cycle. **Not** its session model: AGMessage serves with nobody signed in (answer 35). **Not** its C# supervisor (about 3,500 lines in `src/PlayMap.Supervisor`) |
| **Stagewatch** | Inno Setup 6, per user or all users (`installer/Stagewatch.iss:24-25`). A desktop app with its own watchdog. A firewall rule only in admin mode (`:96-97`) | No downgrade check. `CloseApplications` is left at its default, which closes a running app on a silent setup (https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_setup_closeapplications.htm). Inno Setup comes from unpinned `choco` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:51`), and CI never installs the result | Its reason for the firewall rule. Nothing else: a silent upgrade that can close a live Stagewatch is a finding for its own repository |
| **Patterns** | A portable single exe. An administrator runs `tools/show-machine.ps1` once (`docs/SHOW-MACHINE.md:29-45`) | The watchdog applies a staged update: exit 83, the old files kept as a backup, and two minutes for the new build to prove itself or the backup comes back (`docs/INSTALLS.md:135-168`) | That a failed new build goes back by itself (U.6.1). **Not** a remote `UPDATE APPLY`: under AGMessage's doctrine, new code arrives only through a person's act on the laptop, either an elevated installer or a granted upgrade the machine checks against the release before it runs (U18) |
| **AGMessage** | A portable folder: `node\node.exe app\supervise.js` (`start-agmessage.bat:29`). Data in `app\data` and `app\uploads`; keys and the certificate in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage` (`lib/secretbox.js:17-21`), which stays on the laptop after the folder is deleted | None written. Each zip unpacks to a new versioned folder whose `app\data` is empty (`tools/build-portable.ps1:20,30`), and `README.txt:17` says only "Unzip" | Already ahead of PlayMap on SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and a build-provenance attestation (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:145-189`), though the attestation covers only the zip (`:179-182`) |

## 6-U.3 What an install would change, person by person

Each line names its evidence. "Installed" means the shape answer 35 and U.5 settle on (B-task); the options the owner's
answers set aside are in U.4.

### 6-Who the install defends against

There are four parties:
1. the LAN: every phone and screen that reaches the port;
2. the internet, through the tunnel while it is on;
3. another Windows account on the laptop: a presenter's sign-in, or a venue technician's;
4. the operator's own processes: anything run in the account that is signed in.

Today's portable copy defends against 1 and 2 through the server's own rules (`lib/guard.js`, `lib/rbac.js`). It
defends against none of 3 and 4:
- its keys and data are the signed-in account's files;
- a `C:\node_modules` that any authenticated account may be able to create is loaded into it (U11; reading R8).

**The installed node defends against 3** for the code, which sits in Program Files where no other account can change
it, and for the data and keys, which sit in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage` under U12's access lists. U11 closes the module
walk.

**Against 4 it defends the keys and the data, but not the token.**
- Secrets made after the install, and the imported ones once the import is verified (answer 42; U14), are out of the
  signed-in account's reach.
- The laptop's token is a file the laptop's admin and its grantees read by design (answer 40), so their own processes
  can read it too.
- An account that is a Windows administrator reaches everything through one approved elevation.

Four of the reviews' defects matter only against 3:
- the module walk;
- the machine-folder race;
- pipe and port squatting;
- the import's copies.

### 6-The operator on a show day

- **Benefits**
  - **One copy, and a start that says what it found.**
    - The Start menu's Open AGMessage is a launcher run by the signed `node.exe`, not an unsigned executable (U13).
      - It opens the browser when the installed build answers.
      - Otherwise it says what it found: the state, the log's tail, and what to do.
    - The start-up confusion of `addendum-startup.md` cannot come from a stale folder:
      - the installer refuses while a portable copy holds the port (U12's `preinstall-check`);
      - a portable copy started later says "AGMessage <build> is installed on this PC". Its .bat reads that from
        `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage`.
  - **Nothing to start, and nothing to close by mistake.** A boot trigger starts the task "when the Task Scheduler
    service starts", which happens "when the operating system is booted"
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/boottrigger). Today the guide says "LEAVE IT OPEN"
    (`README.txt:23-24`).
  - **An upgrade asks first.** The busy line (U8) counts what is live. A busy server is stopped only with a reason a
    person types (answer 39). PlayMap's armed check is the precedent (`Mapper/docs/INSTALL.md:52`).
  - **A wake from sleep no longer restarts the server** (U9, both channels).
- **Costs and risks**
  - **Sleep, measured as a proxy.**
    - Today's watchdog compares the wall clock with the last heartbeat (`supervise.js:80`), and the wall clock jumps
      across a sleep.
    - **Both processes frozen for 15 s, then thawed (5 rounds):**
      - the server was killed (SIGKILL, no save) 5 times out of 5;
      - it served again after 4.0, 4.4, 8.5, 15.5 and 30 s, following the backoff ladder;
      - every restart wrote "Session restored" in every hall (`critique/out-sleep-resume.txt`).
    - **1 s of running in every 15 s for 6 minutes**, a proxy for a session-0 process "throttled by the DAM to no more
      than one second of activity every 30 seconds"
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/prepare-software-for-modern-standby):
      - 7 kills, then "giving up";
      - the watchdog exited 3, and nothing was serving after the thaw (`critique/out-throttle.txt`);
      - under "3 stays stopped", the installed node would stay down after the wake.
    - **Which channels are hit, and how.** Standby suspends desktop apps (the portable copy) and throttles session-0
      processes (the installed node). So the installed node is hit harder, not less, until U9 lands.
    - **U9's prototype:** 0 kills in both proxies, and a server frozen alone is still killed at 10 s (U9).
    - **Power requests.** A power request holds off the idle-out: "Power requests will block the NoCS phase
      indefinitely on AC power, and for up to 5 minutes on DC power" (same page). But "the SetThreadExecutionState
      function cannot be used to prevent the user from putting the computer to sleep. Applications should respect that
      the user expects a certain behavior when they close the lid on their laptop or press the power button"
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winbase/nf-winbase-setthreadexecutionstate).
      - U9 holds a request while halls are live.
      - The lid on mains is a line on the hour-before-doors card (U.9).
  - **A Windows shutdown or restart ends the server unsaved** (U.5's first cost). Stop AGMessage before a planned
    restart; the hour-before-doors card says so.
  - **Rights at show time come from the laptop's admin** (U17).
    - By default, local authenticated users get only `READ_CONTROL`, `SERVICE_ENUMERATE_DEPENDENTS`,
      `SERVICE_INTERROGATE`, `SERVICE_QUERY_CONFIG`, `SERVICE_QUERY_STATUS` and `SERVICE_USER_DEFINED_CONTROL` on a
      service: no start, no stop
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/services/service-security-and-access-rights). A task is run only
      by those its security descriptor allows
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/registeredtask-setsecuritydescriptor). Under a protected
      folder, the same holds for reading the token.
    - So Start, Stop, the token and Upgrade come to the operator's own Windows account when the laptop's admin gives
      them, or from an administrator's approval.
    - "Close the black window at the end" (`README.txt:59`) becomes the Start menu's Stop AGMessage.
  - **It listens from boot on every network the laptop joins**, to the local subnet only, on Private and Domain, and on
    Public only when ticked at install (answer 37).
  - **Every restart ends the tunnel**, upgrades and wakes included. The tunnel is started only from
    `admin:tunnelStart` (`server.js:1624`), and a quick tunnel's address changes each time. U10 fixes this.
  - **No window, and today's console-only words.** The LAN address (`server.js:2490-2495`; `README.txt:41-46`) and the
    refusals (`server.js:143`, `:2441`, `:2458`) are said only on the console. U3 puts them on the admin page, in a
    bounded log and in a "This laptop" panel.

### 6-The admin

- **Benefits**
  - **An upgrade never touches the data.**
    - The program is in Program Files; the data, uploads and keys are in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`.
    - Today a portable upgrade starts empty unless `app\data` and `app\uploads` are copied by hand, and nothing says so.
  - **A way back that needs no download.**
    - Two installers are kept in `{app}\installers\`.
    - The server backs up its own data at the upgrade's stop.
    - A new build that does not answer is replaced by the earlier one, verified (U.6.1).
  - **PlayMap's guarantees, proven in CI:**
    - a downgrade or the same build refused with words;
    - a silent server refused, naming its pid;
    - an upgrade that does not reach its end rolled back, with the earlier server started again;
    - an uninstall that keeps the data unless asked (answer 43).
  - **The keys leave the signed-in account's reach**, for secrets made after the install, and for the imported ones
    once the import is verified and their copies in the profile are removed (answer 42; U14).
  - **The rights are the laptop's admin's to give, and each gift is in the log** (U17).
- **Costs and risks**
  - **An elevated, unsigned installer** (answer 36).
    - SmartScreen warns on every new version: "unsigned files must build reputation anew with every update"
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/package-and-deploy/smartscreen-reputation).
    - Smart App Control in enforcement blocks it
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/smart-app-control/overview). Since it then never runs,
      the warning belongs in `README.txt` and the release notes, not on an installer page.
    - The installer and its uninstaller are AGMessage's only unsigned executables. Nothing unsigned runs after the
      install (U.5).
  - **The move from a portable folder is a key migration** (U14).
    - Done wrong, every sealed value opens as `''` with no error (`secretbox.js:46-55`).
    - Worse than a failed read, today's code then **writes**:
      - a new certificate over `tls.json` when the sealed key will not open (`lib/tls.js:130-147`);
      - a new context token over the sealed one (`server.js:103-107`);
      - a new `secret.key` on any read error (`lib/guard.js:12-22`).
    - U1 makes each of these be made only when its file does not exist.
  - **The break-glass token** (`README.txt:141-144`) becomes a file the laptop's admin and its grantees may read (U2;
    answer 40). The owner's answer B to the audit chain ("Accept belongs to the laptop's token alone": "Yes") then holds
    without an administrator.
  - **The first admin account** is made on the installer's last page through `/api/setup`, with the token the
    installer can read (U13).
  - **An upgrade without an administrator needs the internet.** The machine checks the installer against its release on
    GitHub (U18). Offline, Windows asks for an administrator's approval, as at the install.

### 6-The crew joining (phones, tablets, the Board, `/d/` screens)

- **Benefits**
  - **Reachable from a standard Windows account.**
    - Microsoft: "If the user isn't a local admin and they are prompted, block rules are created. It doesn't matter what
      option is selected"
      (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/network-security/windows-firewall/rules).
    - A rule names a full program path, and every portable version is a new path (`build-portable.ps1:20`), so the
      prompt returns with each version.
    - The installer's allow rules remove both. Each rule names the program, the protocol and the local port (U12).
  - **Devices keep trusting the certificate across upgrades**, because the key folder is fixed.
- **Costs and risks**
  - **A new network is Public on Windows 11**
    (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/experience/connectivity-networking/essential-network-settings-and-tasks-in-windows).
    - A Private-and-Domain rule does nothing on fresh venue Wi-Fi, unless Public was ticked at install (answer 37).
    - The local-subnet scope (answer 37) blocks routed AV VLANs. Phones on such a VLAN reach AGMessage through the
      tunnel, or not at all.
    - The "This laptop" panel says which profile is active and whether a rule covers it (U3).
  - **A restart is a blip of about 1 s** for typical folders (measured, U.6.2). Pages resume from the op ring.
  - **After the first upgrade, pages and screens can keep the old build's scripts.**
    - 0.5.1's `display.js` has no reload path at all.
    - 0.5.1's hall, halls-board and admin pages do reload on `account:changed` (`app.js:201`, `halls.js:267`,
      `admin.js:90`).
    - U5 uses that once. 0.5 screens are listed on the admin page and reloaded by hand before doors.

### 6-IT where the owner's laptop is used

Venue laptops get the portable folder, not the installer (answer 44). IT meets the installed node only on the owner's
own laptop, on their network.

- **Benefits**
  - **A footprint they can read:**
    - one folder in Program Files;
    - one Task Scheduler folder, `\AGMessage\`: the server task, and one control task per account the laptop's admin
      gives a right to (U17);
    - named firewall rules by program, protocol, port and the local subnet;
    - data in one place;
    - an uninstall that takes the machine-level parts back, and removes the data when asked.
  - **AppLocker's default rules allow it.** They let Everyone run "executable files in the Program Files folder" and the
    Windows folder, and let administrators run anything
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/applocker/executable-rules-in-applocker).
    The installed copy runs under them; the portable `node.exe` in Downloads or on a stick does not.
  - **The checks they ask for already exist:** SHA256SUMS, an SBOM and a provenance attestation. U16 attests the
    installer too.
- **Costs and risks**
  - **Administrator rights and an unsigned installer**, once, on the owner's laptop. Under AppLocker's defaults the
    portable copy on a venue laptop needs IT always.
  - **Firewall rules under central policy.** Where local policy merge is off, the installer's local rules are ignored,
    and the rule must be pushed centrally (the firewall rules page above).
  - **Where only the firewall blocks**, the tunnel is the one route that needs no administrator, given internet access.
  - An IT sheet is part of the papers (U.9).

### 6-The portable folder's strengths, which must not be lost

- **No administrator rights.** It runs from any folder or a USB stick, on a laptop that is not ours, wherever AppLocker
  does not forbid it, and stops when its window closes. It is the venue laptops' channel (answer 44).
- **Its footprint is small, but it is not nothing.** It leaves `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage` behind: the machine key, the
  certificate with its sealed private key, and, with unit H, the audit records. The papers' clean-up step removes it
  (U.9). The draft's "no footprint" was wrong.
- **One window says it runs, and Ctrl+C stops it.**
- **A copy per event:** a folder of its own, with its own data. Events inside one folder are U15's, on both channels.
- **Every executable it runs carries a vendor's signature.** This was read from the files; Windows has not verified it
  (reading R5).
- **The clean copy hands the program to someone else** (`make-shareable-copy.bat`, once unit S's S.6 fixes it).
- So the installer is a second channel from the same build. It never replaces the folder (option C below is rejected).

The owner's answers settle the columns: B-session is removed by answer 35, B-service is not taken (U.5), and B-task is
the installed shape. The table stays as the evidence for that choice.
