## 6-U.5 The installed shape: B-task, and what it costs

Answer 35 asks for a node that serves with nobody signed in, which means session 0: B-service or B-task. B-session is
removed as the shape. Answer 36 keeps every release unsigned. Between B-service and B-task, the evidence decides for
B-task.

- **Why B-task.**
  1. **No unsigned program at run time.**
     - The task runs `node.exe`, which carries OpenJS Foundation's signature (read; R5 checks that Windows says Valid).
     - B-service needs a host, and shawl is unsigned. Before answer 36, this addendum weighed B-service on the chance
       that a signed release could also sign the host it ships. Answer 36 removes that chance.
     - Smart App Control turns itself on: "In most cases Smart App Control will automatically turn on to protect against
       untrusted or malicious apps", and "If the app is unsigned, or the signature is invalid, Smart App Control will
       consider it untrusted"
       (https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-malware-protection/smart-app-control-frequently-asked-questions).
       It can also be turned on again without a reinstall (same page).
     - So a laptop where Smart App Control comes on after the install would stop starting an unsigned service host,
       with only a code-integrity event as the reason (inferred; lab 4). The task's `node.exe` is signed.
  2. **Least privilege by default.**
     - A task's process gets a SID of its own, and its token's access list allows "full control for the task SID and
       local system SID only".
     - With no `RequiredPrivileges`, the task runs "without the SeImpersonatePrivilege"
       (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/task-security-hardening).
     - U12 sets `RequiredPrivileges` to `SeChangeNotifyPrivilege` alone, which the same page says marks every other
       privilege `SE_PRIVILEGE_REMOVED`.
  3. **A saving stop does not need a host.** AGMessage's stop is the server's own: a request at loopback, carrying a
     proof of the laptop's token (U8). The server saves and exits 0. Task Scheduler's End, which is TerminateProcess, is
     never the Stop.
  4. **The rights do not need a service's access list.** Start, Stop and Upgrade go through each account's own control
     task (U17), the same way for any shape. So B-service's one advantage there, `sc sdset`, buys nothing.
  5. **Less to own.** No host pinned, noticed and proven, and no failure-action mapping. WinSW and NSSM were already not
     candidates: WinSW's `onfailure` acts on every non-zero exit and would undo the watchdog's give-up (exit 3,
     `supervise.js:65-70`), and NSSM is unmaintained since 2017 and unsigned (measured).
- **What B-task costs.** Each cost is said in `docs/INSTALL.md`, `SECURITY.md` and the hour-before-doors card.
  1. **A Windows shutdown or restart ends the server unsaved.**
     - libuv leaves `CTRL_SHUTDOWN_EVENT` to Windows' default (`src/win/signal.c`), and a task is not a service. So
       `node.exe` is ended without the save (inferred; lab 5).
     - shawl, by contrast, takes the SCM's shutdown control and sends Ctrl-C (`src/service.rs`). This is the one thing
       B-service would give that B-task does not.
     - **What is lost:**
       - no acknowledged message: the op is appended before the answer (`lib/store.js:139-147`);
       - lane writes up to 200 ms old;
       - the audit entries written since the head's last save, which the next start reads as entries after the head and
         checks by MAC (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.6).
     - The next start says "Session restored" in every hall, because the stop did not save (answer 41; U4), and health
       names the unclean stop.
     - Fast Startup's Shut down hibernates session 0 instead
       (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/power/system-power-states). So the server should be resumed,
       not ended (inferred; lab 2).
     - **The rule in the papers:** Stop AGMessage before a planned restart. U9's power request keeps idle sleep off
       while a show is live.
  2. **A crash of the watchdog itself may not be restarted.**
     - Microsoft's pages say RestartOnFailure restarts the task "if the task fails for any reason", or when "the last
       run result of the task is not a success"; an informal report saw no restart after a non-zero exit (U.1). R12
       records which holds.
     - Either way "stays stopped" holds. Under `task`, the watchdog's give-up and a configuration refusal end the task
       with 0, after writing why (`watchdog.json`, `supervise.js:68`; the refusal's words in `server.log`, U3). Only an
       unexpected end of the watchdog is non-zero (U12's host contract).
     - If R12 finds that only a failed start counts, a crash of the watchdog leaves AGMessage down until the next boot or
       a Start, and "This laptop" says so.
  3. **No entry in Services.** IT reads it in Task Scheduler's `\AGMessage\` folder. `status` and "This laptop" say its
     state (U3, U12).
  4. **It listens from boot on every network the laptop joins**, to the local subnet only, and on a Public network only
     when ticked at install (answer 37).
  5. **Throttled in Modern Standby**, as any session-0 process, until U9 (U.3).
  6. **No window.** The console's words reach the admin page, a bounded log and "This laptop" (U3).
  7. **A machine folder to defend** (U12's order), and **a key migration** at the import (U14), whose copies answer 42
     removes once verified.
  8. **Rights at show time come from the laptop's admin** (U17), or from an administrator's approval.
- **B-session is removed as the shape** (answer 35). Its logon task, its import as the signed-in user and its data in
  the user's profile are gone from U12-U14. A signed-in operator who wants a window uses the portable folder.
- **Each channel is kept apart from the other by environment alone:**
  - `AGM_RUNS=portable|task`;
  - `AGM_DATA_DIR`, `AGM_UPLOAD_DIR` and `AGM_KEY_DIR`, set as absolute paths by `launch.js` from the task's arguments.
    A task's Exec action passes no environment
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/execaction);
  - `PORT`.
  - The installed node's folders are under `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`. Every portable default stays as it is.
- **The host's contract:**
  - the task starts `node.exe app\launch.js serve` with the folders as arguments. `launch.js` sets the environment and
    runs the watchdog in its own process;
  - the stop is the server's own, at loopback with a proof of the token (U8). It allows at least 7 s before any kill,
    against the watchdog's 4 s kill and 5 s exit (`supervise.js:97-98`);
  - under `task`, the watchdog's 0, its give-up and a configuration refusal end the task with 0, so it stays stopped;
    anything else is a crash.

### 6-U.5.1 The laptop's admin (answer 38)

- **Who.** The Windows account that starts the installer is the laptop's admin, whether it is a standard account or an
  administrator.
  - The installer records its SID in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage` as `Admin`, and its name as `AdminName` for the words.
  - Every check uses the SID, since account names are localised and can be renamed.
  - In the pages, "the laptop's admin" is that Windows account; "admin account" stays an AGMessage account with the
    admin role. Unit W's copy deck gains the row.
  - It is found once, at the first install. An upgrade, by an administrator or a checked one (U18), keeps the record;
    only a handover changes it.
- **A standard account approves elevation once.**
  - A per-machine install needs administrator rights (`PrivilegesRequired=admin`, U13), so Windows asks for an
    administrator's credentials.
  - After the install, the laptop's admin needs them again only for an upgrade the machine cannot check (U18) and for
    the uninstall. Start, Stop, the token and checked upgrades come from its rights (U17).
- **How the account is found when an administrator's credentials run the elevation** (over-the-shoulder elevation):
  - The elevated installer runs as the administrator who typed their credentials. Inno's `{username}` is "The name of
    the user who is running Setup", and its "user" folders "refer to the profile of the user running Setup. This user
    is often not the same as the currently logged-in user" (https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_consts.htm). Neither is
    used.
  - **Reading 1, the account that started Setup.**
    - Inno's `ExecAsOriginalUser` runs a program "using the (normally non-elevated) credentials of the user that
      started Setup initially" (https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_isxfunc_execasoriginaluser.htm).
    - It returns only an exit code. Inno's `ExecAndCaptureOutput` has no original-user form
      (https://jrsoftware.org/ishelp/topic_isxfunc_execandcaptureoutput.htm).
    - So the installer runs `{sys}\whoami.exe /user /fo csv /nh`, through `{cmd}` by its absolute path, into a
      one-time file. The file goes in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\setup\<128 random bits>\`, which the elevated installer
      makes under U12's order, and where any signed-in account may create a file but none may list or read.
  - **Reading 2, the account at the screen.** The owner of `explorer.exe` in the installer's own Windows session, by
    `Win32_Process`'s `GetOwnerSid`
    (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/getownersid-method-in-class-win32-process). It is
    read by one `powershell.exe` child, by absolute path (U11).
  - **Both agree:** that account is the laptop's admin. The page says: "AGMessage's admin on this PC will be LAPTOP\ana,
    the account that started this installer. LAPTOP\it-admin approved it and gets no AGMessage rights."
  - **They disagree, or one cannot be read** (an installer run from another account's elevated prompt, a session with no
    shell): the page shows both and asks the person to choose one of them, never a third.
  - **A silent install** with no original user (a SYSTEM deployment) is refused unless `/ADMIN=<account>` names it:
    "AGMessage needs to know whose it is: add /ADMIN=<account>".
  - R6 records both readings under over-the-shoulder elevation on the show laptop.
- **The rights** (U17):

  | Right | What it lets the account do | How Windows holds it |
  |---|---|---|
  | `token` | read the laptop's token: the break-glass sign-in, Accept (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.8), the token's export, the first admin account | read on `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\token\` (U2) |
  | `start` | Start AGMessage | the account's control task runs the server task |
  | `stop` | Stop AGMessage, with a typed reason when busy | the account's control task stops the server at loopback, saved |
  | `upgrade` | Upgrade AGMessage…, and Go back to build N | the account's control task, after U18's checks |

  - The laptop's admin holds all four, and alone may give them, take them back or hand the admin over. An account given
    rights cannot give them on.
  - Holding the token includes a stop by hand, since the token is the node's whole admin. `stop` alone is for an account
    that should stop the node and never hold the token.
  - A member of Administrators can still do everything through an elevation. The rights are for accounts that are not
    administrators, or that should not need an elevation.
- **Give, take back, hand over** (Start → AGMessage → Who may run AGMessage…, in the laptop's admin's own console):
  - "Give LAPTOP\ben: start, stop". The account is resolved to its SID once, and an unknown name is refused with words.
    A group (Administrators, Users, Everyone) is refused: "Give rights to one person's account."
  - "Take back from LAPTOP\ben: stop", or "all".
  - "Hand over to LAPTOP\ben", confirmed by typing the new account's name.
    - The new admin gets all four rights and the giving.
    - The old admin keeps none unless the new one gives them back.
  - Any administrator may run the same console elevated, for a laptop whose admin account is gone; a handover made so is
    logged as by that administrator.
  - Each act is a machine event (`machine\events.jsonl`) that the server writes as its audit row: `machine.grant`,
    `machine.revoke` or `machine.handover`, naming both accounts and the rights. The install's own record is
    `machine.admin`.
- **Where it shows.**
  - "This laptop" (U3) lists the laptop's admin and each grant, to admin accounts and the token.
  - The context, the hello and the AI's brief carry none of it, because a Windows account's name is not the show
    network's business.

## 6-U.6 Upgrading the server

### 6-U.6.1 [A] The install's upgrade path, and the portable's

- **The order** is PlayMap's, with a verified start and a way back added:
  1. **The version check.**
     - The installer's version is MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD (PlayMap's rule, which MSI can carry next round), read from
       `build.json`.
     - A local build is refused.
     - An older or equal build is refused with PlayMap's words: "AGMessage 0.6.0 (build 41) is newer than this
       installer's 0.6.0 (build 37): uninstall it first to go back, or use Go back to build 37".
  2. **`preinstall-check`, which fails closed.**
     - **The port.** Anything answering on the configured port that is not the installed server is refused. Its version
       comes from `/api/health`: "AGMessage 0.5.1 is running on port 3023 from a folder: press Ctrl+C in its window,
       then continue". Otherwise: "another program (pid 4120) holds port 3023".
     - **The busy line** (U8). A busy server is refused unless a person types a reason (answer 39). A server that does not
       answer within 5 s reads as busy, naming its pid where it is known.
  3. **`upgrade-stop`.**
     - The stop goes to the server at loopback, with a proof of the token (U8), the reason "upgrade", the person's reason
       when forced, and who asked.
     - The server, the one writer:
       - flushes the audit log, the lanes and the dirty rooms (U4);
       - backs up its data to `data\backups\upgrade-<build>-<time>\`: hard links for the files replaced by rename and
         for uploads, and copies of the append-only logs and the audit log. Two are kept, and the time is unmeasured
         (R9);
       - writes `data\last-stop.json` (`{at, build, saved, backup}`);
       - exits 0.
     - `upgrade-stop` reports "saved at 20:31, backup …" or "no save record". With no record, it refuses unless forced.
     - It refuses when free space is below the backup's estimate.
     - Inno then refuses while any other program runs from `{app}` (PlayMap's rule).
  4. **The files are replaced.** An upgrade that does not reach its end has its files rolled back by Inno Setup, and the
     earlier server is started again.
  5. **`install` sets the machine-level parts again** (the server task, the control tasks, the rules, U12), then starts
     the server task.
  6. **The verify.** Loopback `/api/health` must answer with the new build within the watchdog's 30 s start window
     (`AGM_STARTUP_MS`, `supervise.js:27`).
  7. **The way back, by itself, when the new build does not answer.**
     - The installer says why, from `server.log`'s tail, and stops whatever of the new build still runs.
     - It restores that upgrade's backup, elevated or as SYSTEM (U18), since the data is under the protected
       `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`.
     - It then runs the kept installer of the previous build with `/ROLLBACK`. That installer accepts the switch only for
       the build `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage` records as `Previous`. It lays the earlier files down, starts the earlier build,
       and verifies that it answers.
     - The Start menu's "Go back to build N" does the same later, behind the busy check, for the laptop's admin and the
       accounts given `upgrade` (U18), or for an administrator.
     - The way back uses a kept installer, not a copied folder, so Inno's uninstall log and Add/Remove Programs stay
       true.
- **Who starts it.**
  - An administrator, by running the installer, as at the install.
  - The laptop's admin, or an account given `upgrade`, from Start → AGMessage → Upgrade AGMessage…, with no
    administrator, when the machine can check the installer against its release (U18). Its control task then runs the
    same order from step 1, as SYSTEM.
- **"Newer" is one rule across the network.**
  - Three orders were run over the same seven composed builds (21 pairs; `final/out-order3.txt`):
    - SemVer precedence disagrees with MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD on 3 pairs, and with the four-part MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.BUILD on
      2 (M3).
    - MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD and the four-part order disagree on 1 pair: an older PATCH built after a newer PATCH's dev
      build (`0.6.1-dev.31+…` against `0.6.0+32.…`).
  - The rule is PlayMap's MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD.
  - The release job also refuses a release whose SemVer is not above the last release's. PlayMap's `Refusal` compares
    MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD alone (`Install/MsiVersionRule.cs:63`), which would let that one pair through.
  - So among releases, the three orders agree. Dev builds order by build alone, as the papers say.
  - The HKLM key holds `Version` (MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD), `SemVer` and `Previous`, as PlayMap's holds the first two.
- **Downgrades.**
  - The installer refuses one, and U18's control task refuses a release that is not above the installed one before it
    runs anything.
  - The data folder's format refuses one too: 0.6.0 writes format 2 (U6). A folder of a higher format is refused with
    words naming the build that wrote it and its backup (exit 3).
  - 0.5.1 reads no marker, so going back to 0.5.1 on the portable path stays unprotected, as design §1.8 says. Its
    three losses are the words the refusal points to.
- **The data and the keys are never written by an upgrade**, except by the server's own backup and, on the way back, a
  restore. Uninstall keeps both unless the person ticks "Remove all AGMessage data from this PC" (answer 43).
- **The portable path.**
  - Today: unzip a new folder, copy `app\data` and `app\uploads` from the old one, and start it from the same Windows
    account (the keys follow the account). A new folder means a new path, so the firewall prompts again.
  - `README.txt` gains this as "Upgrading" (U6).
  - Unit H's head is found by the log's id, so the moved folder keeps its chain and records `audit.moved`
    (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.5).
- **Portable to installed** is the import (U14).
  - It takes only a source last run by the same build. The person first upgrades the portable folder, rehearses, then
    installs that build and imports.
  - It runs on a wizard page **before the server's first start**, and only then. An installed node that has served has
    its own machine key, `secret.key`, certificate and audit chain, and two of each cannot be merged (never merge). A
    later import is refused with those words. The portable folder's events stay in that folder, or come over to a fresh
    install whose data was removed at the uninstall.
  - It copies and never moves. It verifies after the copy.
  - Once verified, the copies in the profile of the account that ran the portable copy are removed (answer 42), so the
    portable folder no longer starts with those keys. The import page says so before Import is pressed.
  - It marks the source:
    - `moved.json`, which every 0.6.0 source reads because of the same-build rule;
    - the source's .bat is replaced by one that names the installed AGMessage, with the original kept as
      `start-agmessage.bat.moved`.
  - So two nodes never run with one Show Bus id and one certificate.

### 6-U.6.2 [B] The live upgrade: what was measured

Stop-then-start on the checkout's real `server.js` and `supervise.js`. Medians over 5 rounds (3 at 1M), with times from
the IPC stop. "Page back" is a socket.io client with the hall page's options (`app.js:89`) rejoining with `since`. Linux
proxy; the source is `upgrade/out/table.txt` unless named.

| Seeded folder | Stop and save | New server answers `/api/health` | Page back (default client) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 hall, empty | 21 ms | 436 ms | 732 ms |
| 20 halls, empty | 35 ms | 473 ms | 918 ms |
| 100 halls, empty | 130 ms | 665 ms | 1,104 ms |
| 1 hall × 10,000 messages | 94 ms | 629 ms | 1,452 ms |
| 20 halls × 5,000 (`out/restart-big.txt`, 7 rounds) | 389 ms | 1,080 ms from the new start | 1,143 ms from the drop |
| 20 halls × 10,000 (200k messages, 51 MB of snapshots) | 1,059 ms | 3,107 ms | 3,125 ms |
| 100 halls × 10,000 (1M messages, 257 MB) | 4,059 ms: **killed** by the watchdog's 4 s limit | 12,454 ms | 12,474 ms |

- **Where the time goes.**
  - Each start spends 278-328 ms requiring modules. `@anthropic-ai/sdk` alone is about 95 ms (`require-bench.txt`).
  - Loading costs about 2.4 µs per message.
  - The rest is `compactAll`, which rewrites every room's snapshot at stop (`server.js:2401`) and again at boot
    (`:2485`).
    - It took 1,156 ms at 200k and 5,846 ms at 1M. Of that, 1,679 ms is re-reading the `.bak` (`compact-bench.txt`).
    - Compacting only the rooms whose log holds ops took 1 ms.
- **What the runs found.**
  - **A message sent during the gap is lost.** It was answered "Not joined" in every round of every scenario. This is
    the architecture addendum's F4, which its unit Q (the outbox) fixes.
  - **Every start writes "Session restored" into every hall** (`server.js:2486-2488`), so a mid-show upgrade shows on
    the Board. Answer 41: it is written only after a stop that did not save (U4).
  - **At 1M messages the 4 s kill (`supervise.js:97`) cut every stop mid-`compactAll`, before `flushLanes`**
    (`server.js:2401-2402`). It left orphan `<CODE>.json.<pid>.tmp` files of 2.69 MB each, which nothing removes.
    - No acknowledged message was lost, because the op is appended before the answer (`lib/store.js:139-147`).
    - Lane writes up to 200 ms old are lost.
- **The alternatives, measured.**
  - An in-place restart (`EXIT.RESTART` 82, which nothing raises today) is no faster: 409 against 436 ms when empty,
    and 3,267 against 3,107 ms at 200k.
  - A watchdog holding the listening socket gained nothing for the default client.
  - A warm spare saved only the requires. Health answered in 93 ms when empty, but 2,764 ms at 200k and 16,910 ms at
    1M, for a second process of about 95-780 MB.
  - A front proxy would make every LAN client look like the host laptop (`guard.js:169-175`).
  - cluster breaks one writer per folder (`server.js:2445-2459`).
- **What a screen shows.** A `/d/` screen keeps its picture and says "lost" only after 6 s of silence
  (`display.js:234`). Every folder up to 200k messages restarts inside that; 1M does not.
- **The tunnel and sleep are part of the live gap too.** Every restart ends the tunnel and changes a quick tunnel's
  address (U10). A wake from sleep is today a kill and a restart (U.3; U9).
- **Verdict: nothing beyond today's watchdog restart is justified.** What is justified:
  - **U4 removes the measured cause.** Computed from the phases, not measured end to end, it brings 200k from about
    3.1 s to about 0.8 s and 1M from about 12.5 s to about 2.7 s. The stop then fits the watchdog's 4 s kill. A Windows
    shutdown is not a stop under the task (U.5), so U4 does not change what it loses.
  - **The architecture addendum's units Q and B, already planned**, fix the lost send and the slow return.
  - **U5** fixes stale scripts. **U8** keeps an upgrade from cutting a show unasked.
  - **The rule in the papers:** upgrade between shows ("Upgrade between shows", design §12). Never make the first
    install, or a new MINOR, the night before a show: upgrade the portable folder, rehearse, then install the same build.
  - **Revisit handoff only** if, after U4, Q and B, U7's Windows run shows the default page back later than 1.5 s at the
    largest real hall.
- **With an installer, the gap is the stop, the backup, the file replacement and the start.** The backup and the
  replacement are unmeasured on Windows (R2, R9; lab 3). If together they exceed 6 s, side-by-side version folders,
  laid down before the stop, come in from U.10.

## 6-U.7 Units

> **Amended by** Part 0 §0.6 (the global build order; U18 before U16, §0.8 C2); 2-S.2 on U8's busy line (§0.8 C4).

Each is one commit, `AGMessage 0.6.0, unit Un: <what landed>`. Every reader is named in its unit:

- **The context and the admin health** gain `install`. It uses PlayMap's `machine.install` names where the meaning
  matches (`installed`, `dir`, `signed`, `light`, `words`; `Mapper/docs/wire/install.md:19-30`), plus `runs`
  (`portable`, `task`) and `host` (the server task's state).
  - `dir` is `null` unless installed. A folder run's path would name the Windows account (`C:\Users\<name>\…`).
  - The laptop's admin and the grants are in the admin health's "This laptop" only, never in the context (U.5.1).
  - The current event (U15) is in the admin health and on the admin page.
- **The hello is unchanged.** It is unauthenticated, and an `inst` field would be a Show Bus amendment across four
  repositories (U.10).
- **The AI's brief is unchanged**, except that it reads the current event's halls only and never an archive (U15). No
  install fact helps a draft.
- **The audit log** gains these rows:
  - `server.stop.forced`, from the stop's reason (U8);
  - `server.upgraded`, from `format.json`'s build changing (U6);
  - `machine.admin`, `machine.grant`, `machine.revoke`, `machine.handover`, `machine.start`, `machine.stop`,
    `machine.upgrade`, `machine.upgrade.refused` and `machine.import`, each from a machine event (U17);
  - `audit.archive`, the archive point: unit H3 writes it through `audit.point()`, and it is U15's one row for archiving
    an event; the split's rows are H3's (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.10);
  - `event.purged` (U15).
  - No machine command writes to the log: it has one writer. The machine appends to `machine\events.jsonl`, and the
    server turns each event into its row (U17).
- **The admin page's new acts** are rows of unit 3b's catalogue: Copy LAN address, Tunnel until…, Refresh "This
  laptop", Archive this event…, and, on an archived event, Continue this event…, Copy this event… and Delete this
  archive's contents…. The split is unit H3's ("Split the audit log…").
- **The Start menu's items** (U13) are the machine's own surface. The admin page names them in "This laptop" and never
  acts for them.

**Both channels:**

1. **[#26]** **unit U1: a folder or a key that cannot be used stops the start with words, nothing is written before the folder
   is held, and nothing secret is remade on a read error.**
   - **Folders.** `supervise.js:30` and `server.js:66-67` exit 3 with the folder and the reason. Today these are exit 1
     and a loop in any restarter, and a crash ladder that gives up after 7 crashes, 89 s on the default ladder
     (computed).
   - **After the hold only:**
     - the folders' creation;
     - `secret.key` (`server.js:69`);
     - the settings writes (the 0.2 migration and `nodeId`, `:91-99`);
     - the key folder (the machine key, `tls.json`).
     - M2 found a refused copy had already written both keys.
   - **Made only when the file does not exist (ENOENT):**
     - the machine key (unit H's H.2 rule, which this unit relies on);
     - `secret.key`: today `lib/guard.js:12-22` makes one on any read error;
     - `tls.json`: today `lib/tls.js:130-147` writes a new certificate when the sealed key does not open or the JSON
       does not parse;
     - the context token: today `server.js:103-107` saves a new token over a stored one that does not open.
     - Any other failure means this run goes without it, and says so: HTTPS off with the reason, or context reads
       refused with words.
     - Renewal near expiry, with a key that opens, stays (U3's LAN-address rule).
   - **`AGM_RUNS=portable|task`:**
     - absent means portable; an unknown value is refused (exit 3);
     - `task` requires all three folders, absolute and outside the app folder, before any write;
     - under `task`, a key file that cannot be read, or a sealed value that does not open, is exit 3 with words.
       Nothing is remade;
     - under `task`, "port in use" and "folder held" exit 75 (`EXIT.HELD`), not 3. The watchdog retries on its ladder
       without counting a crash, and `status` names the port's holder. Otherwise another account that takes the pipe's
       predictable name (`server.js:2454`), or the freed port, during a restart would keep the node down for good under
       "stays stopped". In the portable channel a person is there to read the words, so these stay exit 3.
   - Unit H's keyless run stays the portable rule.
2. **[#27]** **unit U2: the admin token is said only where a person sits.**
   - `server.js:2501` stops printing it. `supervise.js`, which makes it (`:32`), prints it only to a console
     (`isTTY`). A server run alone, with `AGM_SUPERVISED` unset, prints it as today.
   - **Under `task`:**
     - the watchdog writes it to `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\token\admin-token`, a folder of its own outside `keys\`.
       SYSTEM and Administrators have full control and the task's SID may write. The laptop's admin, and each account
       given `token`, may read it (U17);
     - it never goes into `--out`, the installer's log or a machine event;
     - `/api/setup` takes the token sign-in only, never loopback alone (`lib/http-accounts.js:176`);
     - an `ADMIN_TOKEN` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the watchdog's own environment is exit 3 with words. The machine never
       puts a secret in a task's definition, which every account allowed to read the task can read (R8).
   - Start → AGMessage → Show the admin token prints it in the person's own console, or says "This PC's AGMessage admin
     has not given you the token: ask LAPTOP\ana".
   - `supervise.js`'s synchronous cap rises by one, with its reason.
3. **[#28]** **unit U3: what the console says reaches the admin page, a bounded log, and a "This laptop" panel.**
   - The watchdog pipes the server's output (`supervise.js:48`) to its console and to `data\logs\server.log`, bounded,
     rotated, and never holding the token. "Cannot start as configured" carries the server's reason.
   - The admin acknowledgement (`server.js:1591-1600`) gains `addresses` and `port`, and `tlsFacts` gains why HTTPS is
     off.
   - The certificate is renewed at start only while `lanAddresses()` is non-empty (`lib/tls.js:138,143`). A start
     before the network has an address would otherwise make one with no LAN address for 825 days. This is unmeasured.
     Under the task a boot start is the common case.
   - **"This laptop"** on the admin page: facts, each saying where it was read.
     - **What AGMessage knows:**
       - the serving build and how it runs;
       - the addresses;
       - HTTPS, and why it is off;
       - how many sealed values open (a count, no names);
       - screens confirmed;
       - Stagewatch connected;
       - the tunnel and its end (U10);
       - sleeps recorded and the power request (U9);
       - the last stop: saved, or not (U4).
     - **Read on Windows** by one `powershell.exe` child, at start and on Refresh:
       - the active network's profile, and whether an allow rule covers `node.exe` on it;
       - the AC standby timeout;
       - the lid action on mains;
       - the server task's state and last result, and the laptop's admin and the grants from `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage`
         (names and rights; U17).
       - The child is run by absolute path, with a fixed script and a 5 s timeout. Each fact reads "unknown" when it
         cannot be read.
4. **[#34]** **unit U4: a restart rewrites only the rooms that changed, a stop saves the audit log and the lanes first, says it
   saved, and "Session restored" is written only after a stop that did not save (answer 41).**
   - Rooms are compacted only when dirty, at stop and at boot. Replayed ops count toward `logCount`, so a log stays
     under its 999-line bound.
   - The stop flushes the audit log, then the lanes, then the dirty rooms. It then writes `data\last-stop.json`
     (`{at, build, saved: true}`).
   - **"Session restored"** (`server.js:2486-2488` writes it into every hall on every start today) is written at boot
     only when `last-stop.json` is missing or does not say `saved: true`. The file is then renamed to
     `last-stop.seen.json` after the hold, as `watchdog.json` is (`server.js:158`), so a later crash is never read as a
     clean stop. Health says which it was.
   - After the hold, `*.tmp` files carrying a dead pid are removed.
   - The Anthropic SDK is required on first use (`lib/ai.js:14`).
   - **Needs** the architecture addendum's unit D (`snapWhole`) and unit H's `flushLanes` order. **Lands before** the
     design's unit 7, whose `guestCode` and `retired` are written only by compaction and must mark their room dirty.
5. **[#35]** **unit U5: a page on another build reloads itself at a quiet moment, and the first upgrade reaches 0.5.1's pages.**
   - The join answer and the screen's hello carry `build`. A page on a different build reloads:
     - a screen, between takes;
     - a hall page, with no draft (unit Q's outbox empty), no dialog and no stage document open;
     - the admin page, when the admin agrees.
   - Static scripts and styles are served `no-cache` with their ETag, a 304 on the LAN. Inferred: within the 5-minute
     `maxAge` (`server.js:422`), a reload would otherwise take the old build's scripts from the browser's cache.
   - **0.5.1's pages.** A page that announces no build is sent `account:changed` with "AGMessage was updated —
     reloading", once, on its first reconnect after the upgrade. 0.5.1's hall, halls-board and admin pages reload on it
     (`app.js:201`, `halls.js:267`, `admin.js:90`).
   - **0.5.1's screens.** A 0.5.1 screen has no reload path. The 0.5.1 display protocol keeps working, and the admin
     page lists such screens as "0.5 screens". The papers say "reload each screen once before doors".
   - The admin page lists the pages still on an older build.
   - **Needs** the architecture addendum's unit B. People's pages (units 17-18) adopt it when they land.
6. **[#29]** **unit U6: "newer" is defined, and the data folder says which build and format last wrote it.**
   - stamp-build writes `installVersion` (MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD) into `build.json` (today `{version, build, commit, channel,
     builtAt}`, `tools/stamp-build.js:53`); a local build has none. The release job refuses a release whose SemVer is not
     above the last release's (U.6.1).
   - **`data/format.json`** (`{format, build, at}`) is written after the hold.
     - 0.6.0 writes format 2. A 0.5.x folder, which has no marker, is format 1.
     - A higher format means exit 3, with words naming the build that wrote the folder and its backup.
     - A lower format means a backup first, then the migration steps, then `format.json` written last.
     - A newer build at the same format is said in health's detail and on the admin page. A changed build writes
       `server.upgraded`.
   - 0.5.1 never reads the marker, so it can still open a 0.6 folder (design §1.8). There is no 0.5.2 (answer 29).
   - `README.txt` gains "Upgrading" (U.6.1) and the firewall case (a standard account, a Public network).
7. **[#30]** **unit U7: the Windows evidence lane, and the lab lines.**
   - **The lane.** A CI step on windows-2025, pinned by hash, writing readings.
     - It first turns Defender's real-time monitoring back on, removes the image's `C:\` and `D:\` exclusions, and
       records whether that took (`Get-MpComputerStatus`).
     - These are this addendum's readings R1-R13, not the architecture addendum's readings 0-9.
   - **The readings inform; none holds the release** (answer 34). Each mark stays a mark. A reading that misses it is
     written in the release notes, `docs/INSTALL.md` and the hour-before-doors card, with the fallback its unit names.
     A test in U16's life cycle is not a reading: it is a gate, as every test is.

   | Reading | What | Mark | A miss means |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | R1 | `gap.js` (the stop at loopback with the proof, not SIGUSR2) at an empty hall and at 20 × 10,000 | the default page back ≤ 1.5 s at the largest real hall | handoff is revisited (U.10) |
   | R2 | lay about 5,120 files and 188 MB over the previous payload, Defender on | ≤ 6 s together with R9 (a screen's "lost") | version folders (U.10) |
   | R3 | retired: it was B-service's (shawl's stop under `NT SERVICE\AGMessage`), which is not the shape (U.5) | — | — |
   | R3′ | the task: a stop at loopback with the proof saves and `last-stop.json` says so; the watchdog's give-up and a configuration refusal end the task with 0, and it stays stopped | 10 of 10 | the release notes name the failing case; a stop that does not save is said on "This laptop" |
   | R4 | under the task: `LOCALAPPDATA`, `os.homedir()`, UDP 9928 broadcast heard, a quick tunnel's URL returned with nothing written in the account's profile, a rule by program, protocol and port matching `node.exe` under the task, `whoami /priv` from the server's process, `schtasks /showsid` | `SeImpersonatePrivilege` absent, and the server serves with `SeChangeNotifyPrivilege` alone | the privilege list U12 sets is widened by the one privilege the reading names, with its reason |
   | R5 | `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on `node.exe`, `cloudflared.exe` and the installer | the first two Valid; the installer recorded | `README.txt` names the file Windows does not trust |
   | R6 | over-the-shoulder elevation: U.5.1's two readings of the account that started Setup; the user's own export (U14) run through `ExecAsOriginalUser` into the laptop's admin's inbox; an elevated read of another account's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage` | both readings name the standard account | the admin page asks the person to choose, as U.5.1 says |
   | R7 | the folder pipe's access list as libuv makes it (`CreateNamedPipeW(…, NULL)`, `crit-dl/pipe.c:596-599`) under the task's token, and whether a remote client reaches it | recorded | nothing machine-level writes the pipe any more (U8); the busy line's readers are named |
   | R8 | `icacls C:\` and `icacls %ProgramData%` (may a standard account create `C:\node_modules` or `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`?); `schtasks /query /xml` of each task as a standard account: readable or not, and no secret in it | recorded | U11 and U12's order already assume the worst |
   | R9 | the upgrade backup's time at an empty hall and at 20 × 10,000 | recorded, beside R2 | as R2 |
   | R10 | extracting `node.exe` to `%TEMP%` for each machine command, Defender on | recorded | over 5 s: an upgrade runs its checks with the installed `node.exe` |
   | R11 | a control task whose descriptor gives one standard account read and execute: that account runs it with `schtasks /run`; a second standard account is refused; the task runs as SYSTEM with `--for` that account's SID | 10 of 10 | the Start menu's acts fall back to an administrator's approval, and the release notes say so |
   | R12 | RestartOnFailure on the server task: does a non-zero exit of the action start it again, and does exit 0 leave it stopped | recorded | U.5's second cost reads as measured |
   | R13 | from a control task as SYSTEM, `api.github.com`'s release answer for a published tag: `immutable` and each asset's `digest` read; with no network, the words | recorded | U18's offline words are the ones shown |

   - **The lab lines.** These run on the show laptop (Windows 11), are reported "not run" until taken, and are never
     replaced by a CI reading. They inform the release as the readings do.
     - Lab 1: lid closed and idle-out, on mains and on battery, with and without U9's power request. Serving after,
       sleeps recorded, no kill.
     - Lab 2: Fast Startup's Shut down, then power on, under the task. Fast Startup keeps session 0 across a Shut down
       (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/power/system-power-states), so the server should be resumed,
       not restarted (inferred). Pass: no kill.
     - Lab 3: R2, R9 and R10 with the laptop's own Defender.
     - Lab 4: Smart App Control, evaluating and then enforcing: which of `node.exe`, `cloudflared.exe`, the installer and
       the .bat run.
     - Lab 5: a Windows restart and a shutdown with the server busy, under the task (expected: ended unsaved, U.5) and for
       the portable copy (console close). What `last-stop.json`, the next start's words and the audit head say.
     - Lab 6: an upgrade during a rehearsal, PlayMap's L11 for AGMessage: stop to health, and pages back.
     - Lab 7: the laptop's admin as a standard account: Show the admin token, Start, Stop with a reason, Upgrade (online
       and offline) and Go back; then the same from a second standard account given `start` and `stop` only, and from a
       third given nothing.
8. **[#36]** **unit U8: the busy line, and a stop that saves, at loopback with a proof of the token.**
   - *Read with 2-S.2 (Part 0 §0.8 C4): only the folder-held words read the busy line; a copy refused at the port cannot name the folder pipe (`app/server.js:2453-2454`).*
   - **The busy line.** One line of counts:
     - pages active in the last 10 minutes;
     - takes changed and help requests in that window;
     - running countdowns;
     - idle seats and screens, counted apart;
     - sockets.
   - It carries no names, codes, tokens or paths.
   - **On the folder pipe** (`server.js:2451-2480`), which today ends every connection, it is answered as a read, for
     unit S's port-holder message and the portable channel. A pipe's default access lets Everyone and the anonymous
     account read it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/ipc/named-pipe-security-and-access-rights). The
     line is never taken as authority: anyone who took the pipe's name first could answer "idle".
   - **At loopback, for the machine:**
     - `GET /api/machine/hello` answers a fresh nonce, the build, and a proof that the server holds the token:
       HMAC-SHA256 under the token over `"agmessage machine server\n" + nonce`;
     - `GET /api/machine/busy` and `POST /api/machine/stop {reason, by}` each carry the nonce and the machine's proof:
       HMAC-SHA256 under the token over `"agmessage machine\n"`, the nonce, the method, the path and the body's SHA-256;
     - `POST /api/machine/events` carries the same proof and nothing else: it tells the server to read
       `machine\events.jsonl` (U17).
     - The server answers only when `guard.isHostMachine(req)`, the nonce is one it issued in the last 30 s and not yet
       used, and the proof compares in constant time. A wrong proof counts toward `adminLockout`, as a wrong token does
       (`server.js:443-453`).
     - **The token never crosses the socket.** The machine checks the server's proof before it sends anything, so a
       program that took the port during a restart learns nothing and stops nothing.
     - The machine reads the token from `token\admin-token`, which SYSTEM and Administrators may read (U2).
   - **The stop** saves as U4 says, exits 0, and writes `server.stop.forced` when a busy server is stopped with a typed
     reason (answer 39). The machine event names who asked (`machine.stop`, U17).
   - A server that does not answer within 5 s reads as busy.
   - Unit S's port-holder message and U14 read the busy line too.
9. **[#31]** **unit U9: the watchdog tells a sleep from a hang, and a live show keeps the laptop awake.**
   - **A late tick is a sleep.** A tick of the watchdog's own that comes more than 2 s late means it did not run (the
     machine slept, or both processes were frozen), so it cannot judge the server for that gap.
     - The beat clock starts again.
     - "asleep from … to …" goes to `watchdog.log`, health (beside unit R's peaks) and "This laptop".
     - A sleep is never counted as a crash.
     - A real hang is the watchdog ticking on time with no beats.
     - Tested on a fake clock.
     - **The prototype** (`final/supervise-sleepfix.js`: today's `supervise.js` with this rule, run through the same
       proxies):
       - **Five 15 s freezes:** 0 kills. The same server process served at the proxy's first look, 4.0 s after each
         thaw, and the hall holds one "Session restored", from the first start (`final/out-sleep-resume-fix.txt`).
       - **1 s in 15 s for 6 minutes:** 0 kills, no give-up, and serving 10 s after the thaw
         (`final/out-throttle-fix.txt`).
       - **The server frozen alone, with the watchdog on time:** still killed at 10 s and replaced 12.2 s after the
         freeze (`final/out-hang-still-fix.txt`).
   - **The power request.**
     - While a hall has an active page, a confirmed take other than holding, or a running countdown, the server holds a
       power request.
     - It does so through one `powershell.exe` child, run by absolute path, that calls
       `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS|ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED)` and waits on its stdin. The request ends with the
       server.
     - It reads "held" only when the call returned non-zero. Under Constrained Language Mode, where Add-Type is
       refused, it says so.
     - It keeps off idle sleep. The lid and the power button stay the power plan's (U.3).
   - Both channels. It touches `supervise.js` beside unit B, U2 and U3.
10. **[#32]** **unit U10: the tunnel is remembered until an end time, and comes back after a restart.**
    - "Tunnel on until <time>" (by default, the end of the day) is kept in settings.
      - A restart inside that time starts the tunnel again and tells the admin "new address", since a quick tunnel's
        address changes.
      - Past that time, the tunnel ends and stays off.
    - The time is shown in health and on the admin page. Under `task`, a tunnel can no longer outlive the show because
      nobody closed a window.
    - The papers recommend a named tunnel for shows with remote people.
11. **[#33]** **unit U11: the server loads only what it ships, and runs only what it names by absolute path.**
    - **Optional modules** that would walk up the tree:
      - `supervise.js` sets `WS_NO_BUFFER_UTIL=1` and `WS_NO_UTF_8_VALIDATE=1` for its child, and `server.js` sets them
        before its first require (`node_modules/ws/lib/buffer-util.js:115-117`);
      - `supports-color` (CommonJS, major 8) ships in `app\node_modules` with its notice. That ends `debug`'s walk
        (`node_modules/debug/src/node.js:32`);
      - a fence starts the server under a resolve hook and fails if any module resolves outside `app\`;
      - measured: planted modules three folders above the app were loaded (`crit-walk/out.txt`). A portable folder
        under `C:\Tools` walks to `C:\node_modules` too.
    - **No `spawn` or `execFile` of a bare name anywhere in `app/`** (a source fence). An argument array avoids a shell,
      not the search, and libuv looks in the current folder before `PATH`. The fence covers:
      - cloudflared (`server.js:2326`'s fallback goes);
      - unit S's opener (`explorer.exe`, under `%SystemRoot%`);
      - U3's, U9's and U.5.1's `powershell.exe`;
      - `machine.js`'s `schtasks.exe`, `icacls.exe`, `reg.exe` and `whoami.exe`, from the `{sys}` Inno passes, and
        `launch.js`'s `schtasks.exe`.
    - **`machine.js` and `launch.js` require `node:` built-ins only** (a source fence).

**The installer, in 0.6.0 (answer 34):**

12. **[#72]** **unit U12: `app/machine.js` and `app/launch.js`, the machine's own commands.**
    - **Two files, two privileges.**
      - `machine.js` runs elevated or as SYSTEM only: `prepare`, `install`, `uninstall`, `preinstall-check`,
        `upgrade-stop`, `status`, `restore`, `import`, `control` (U17) and `upgrade` (U18).
      - `launch.js` never asks for an elevation. It is the server task's action (`launch.js serve`), and the person's
        console for the Start menu's items (`token`, `start`, `stop`, `upgrade`, `back`, `rights`, `status`, `export`,
        `forget-keys`).
    - **The contract:**
      - `--out <file>`; exit codes 0, 2, 3 and 64;
      - Inno passes `{sys}`, `{app}` and `{commonappdata}` as arguments, and no machine path is read from
        `process.env`;
      - every program is spawned by absolute path with an explicit working folder;
      - no token or password is ever written to `--out`, a machine event or a task's definition;
      - on an upgrade, the checks run on the installed `node.exe` when R10 says extraction is slow; otherwise on a temp
        copy.
    - **The audit log is the server's alone.** The machine appends to `machine\events.jsonl`, and the server writes the
      rows (U17).
    - **The firewall rules** (answer 37):
      - each names the program, the protocol and the local port (TCP `PORT`, UDP 9928), with the remote address
        `LocalSubnet`, on Private and Domain, and on Public only when ticked at install;
      - each is updated when `PORT` changes;
      - a rule on `node.exe` alone would let any account run any script with inbound traffic.
    - **`HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage` is the one install record:** `InstallDir`, `Version`, `SemVer`, `Previous`, `Runs`
      (`task`), `Admin` and `AdminName` (U.5.1), `Grants` (one value per SID: its rights), `PublicFirewall`, `Signed`.
      Unit S's .bat reads it with `%SystemRoot%\System32\reg.exe`. No `install.json`: one under a folder that denies Users
      would contradict its own access list.
    - **The machine folder, race-free** (no handles needed), made by `prepare` at the installer's start:
      1. a non-recursive `mkdirSync` of `%ProgramData%\AGMessage`. An existing one is accepted only when HKLM shows an
         earlier install, `lstat` shows a real directory, and its owner is SYSTEM or Administrators. Otherwise refuse;
      2. at once, `icacls <root> /inheritance:r /grant:r *S-1-5-18:(OI)(CI)F *S-1-5-32-544:(OI)(CI)F`, by SID (account
         names are localised), never `/T`;
      3. list the root. Anything another account added meanwhile means refuse;
      4. make each child with a non-recursive `mkdirSync`, with its own grants:
         - `data`, `uploads`, `keys`, `logs`: the server task's SID may modify (added once the task exists, by its SID
           from `schtasks /showsid`);
         - `token`: the task's SID may write; the laptop's admin and the accounts given `token` may read (U2, U17);
         - `machine`: SYSTEM and Administrators only, the task's SID may read `events.jsonl`; inside it `inbox\<sid>\`
           (that account may create and write files) and `outbox\<sid>\` (that account may read), one each for the
           laptop's admin and each account given a right; `work\` and `staged\` (SYSTEM and Administrators only);
         - `setup\<128 random bits>\` for U.5.1's reading 1: any signed-in account may create a file, none may list or
           read; removed at the end of the install.
    - **The server task**, `\AGMessage\Server`:
      - LocalService, `ProcessTokenSidType` unrestricted (its SID, `NT TASK\AGMessage-Server`, is derived "from the full
        task path", https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/task-security-hardening),
        `RequiredPrivileges` `SeChangeNotifyPrivilege`;
      - a boot trigger ("Only a member of the Administrators group can create a task with a boot trigger",
        https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/boottrigger);
      - `ExecutionTimeLimit` `PT0S`, both battery settings false, `MultipleInstancesPolicy` `IgnoreNew`,
        `RestartOnFailure` with Count 3 and Interval `PT1M` (R12 records what it does);
      - the action `node.exe app\launch.js serve --data … --uploads … --keys … --logs … --port …`;
      - its descriptor gives read and execute to SYSTEM and Administrators only. People start it through their control
        tasks (U17).
    - **The host contract under `task`** (U.5): `launch.js` sets `AGM_RUNS=task` and the folders, and runs the watchdog in
      its own process. The watchdog's 0, its give-up and a configuration refusal end the process with 0, after writing
      why (`watchdog.json`, `supervise.js:68`; the refusal's words in `server.log`). Only an unexpected end is non-zero.
    - **`status`:**
      - the server task's state and last result, the tails of `watchdog.log` and `server.log`, and the last
        `last-stop.json`;
      - the port's holder pid (`Get-NetTCPConnection`);
      - whether a code-integrity event (Smart App Control) stopped `node.exe`;
      - the laptop's admin and the grants.
13. **[#73]** **unit U13: the installer, `installer/AGMessage.iss`, from the zip's stage minus the two .bat files.**
    - **PlayMap's skeleton:**
      - a fixed `AppId`; Program Files only; no folder page;
      - `PrivilegesRequired=admin`, with `PrivilegesRequiredOverridesAllowed` absent, so there is no per-user override
        of an installer that registers tasks;
      - **`CloseApplications=no`**: Inno must never close a running server on its own;
      - no `[Dirs]`.
    - **The pages:**
      - the laptop's admin: U.5.1's two readings and words, and the choice between them when they disagree;
      - "Also on Public networks (hotels, airports, fresh venue Wi-Fi)", unticked (answer 37);
      - the busy page: the counts, and a required reason when busy (answer 39);
      - the import (before the first start only; U14);
      - the first admin account, through `/api/setup` with the token the installer can read. The password never goes in
        a URL or in the log.
    - **The code:**
      - the refusals in `InitializeSetup`, and `machine.js prepare` and U.5.1's readings once the elevation is in;
      - `preinstall-check` and `upgrade-stop` in `PrepareToInstall`;
      - `install`, the start and the verify after the files;
      - the way back (U.6.1);
      - `uninstall` before any file goes: the tasks, the rules and the HKLM record;
      - the uninstall asks "Remove all AGMessage data from this PC", unticked (answer 43; `/REMOVEDATA`; keys removed
        last).
    - **The silent switches:** `/VERYSILENT`, `/ADMIN=<account>`, `/PUBLICFIREWALL=1`, `/FORCE="reason"`,
      `/REMOVEDATA`, and `/UPGRADEBY=<sid>` (U18's, accepted only from SYSTEM).
    - **The Start menu**, each item a `node.exe app\launch.js <verb>` console run as the person, never elevated by
      itself: Open AGMessage (the launcher), Show the admin token, Start AGMessage, Stop AGMessage…, Upgrade
      AGMessage…, Go back to build N, Who may run AGMessage…, AGMessage status.
    - The installer copies itself into `{app}\installers\` (two kept).
    - **The Smart App Control words** go in `README.txt` and the release notes. Under enforcement the unsigned
      installer never runs. PlayMap's page is shown only while Smart App Control evaluates.
    - `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` names `node.exe`, `cloudflared.exe` and `supports-color`. `node.exe` and `cloudflared.exe`
      ship without their licence texts today. There is no host to name.
14. **[#75]** **unit U14: the portable import, before the installed node's first start.**
    - **It refuses:**
      - while that copy runs (U8, and the port);
      - a source last run by another build (U6's `format.json` and build);
      - a target that has served: any hall, account or audit row (U.6.1). Never merge;
      - a source whose keys are not in the profile of the account that started Setup: "this folder's keys are another
        Windows account's: install from that account".
    - **Two steps:**
      - the user's own `launch.js export`, run through `ExecAsOriginalUser` as the account that started Setup (U.5.1),
        writes a bundle of contents only into that account's `machine\inbox\<sid>\import\`, refusing any link or
        junction in the source;
      - the elevated `machine.js import` copies the bundle's contents, never access lists, refusing links again.
      - The account's `machine.key`, `tls.json` and `audit\` travel as files, so every sealed value, the fingerprint and
        the chain carry over. `secret.key` travels in `data\`. Nothing is rotated (answer 42).
    - **It then verifies, and says which check did not pass:**
      - halls, messages, accounts and screens counted alike;
      - every sealed value opens;
      - the fingerprint is unchanged;
      - the audit chain checks, with the archives in `data\audit-archive\` that it names (H.10.4), which travel in
        `data\`.
    - **Then the old copies go** (answer 42). Run as the same account through `ExecAsOriginalUser`, `launch.js
      forget-keys` removes:
      - that account's `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AGMessage` (`machine.key`, `tls.json`, the audit records);
      - the source folder's `app\data\secret.key`.
      - Each removal is checked and said; one that fails names its path and stays on the import page's last words. None
        happens before the verify.
    - **It marks the source** (U.6.1) and appends `machine.import` to the machine events.
15. **[#76]** **unit U15: an event is archived, never deleted silently; the next one continues a previous event, copies its
    settings and structure, or starts fresh; the links stay; and the audit log carries on through the archive point
    (answer 45).** Both channels.
    - **Where:** Admin → Event, "Archive this event…", a catalogue row (unit 3b) for admin accounts and the token at the
      laptop.
      - **Who:** the admin, through `theAdminReq` (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.10.2): the token at the laptop, or an
        account whose role is `admin`. A manager an admin granted `settings.manage`, whom the admin page admits
        (`isAdminReq`, `server.js:416-420`), is refused with "Only an admin may archive an event.", and the row is drawn
        disabled with those words on that manager's admin page.
      - The dialog asks first what comes next: continue a previous event, copy a previous event's settings and
        structure, or start fresh. Then the new event's name, typed as the confirmation.
      - Unit H3's tick, unticked: "Also split the audit log here…" (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.10.2).
      - Behind the busy check (U8), with a typed reason when busy.
      - The current event's name, kind and start are shown above it, and the archives below it, each with its counts and
        "Continue this event…", "Copy this event…" and "Delete this archive's contents…".
    - **The three kinds:**

      | | Continue a previous event | Copy a previous event's settings and structure | Start fresh |
      |---|---|---|---|
      | From | an archived event | the current event or an archived one | — |
      | What the new event has | that event as it was: its halls with their codes, side rooms, messages, files, help requests, pins, minutes, screens with their links and takes, accounts, views, desk results | halls (names, side rooms, allow-lists, roles, locks and each hall's `guestWeb` with its lock (`addendum-stage.md` §5.9.2.2), each hall's Stagewatch link), screens (names, halls, layouts), accounts with their rights and views, per-person settings (the Board's clock and On stage switches) | no halls, screens or accounts. The token at the laptop makes the first admin account, as at a first start |
      | What it never has | sign-ins: every session and token sign-in ends | messages, files, help requests, transcripts, minutes, desk results, takes and pins; guest codes and invites (new ones are made); screen links, unless "Keep the screens' links" is ticked (unticked); sign-ins | anything of an earlier event but the links below |
      | The current event | archived first | archived first | archived first |

      - Copy makes new codes and invites because they are capabilities, not structure: a code or invite given out for an
        earlier event never opens a new one. Screen links are kept only when ticked, for screens of the owner's own kit.
      - Continuing the current event is no new event, so Continue is offered for archived events only.
    - **Kept in all three, never archived** (the links and the node itself):
      - the Stagewatch link, its sealed key and fingerprint (`settings.stagewatchUrl`, `stagewatchKeySealed`,
        `stagewatchFingerprint`, `server.js:1571-1577`);
      - each hall's Stagewatch link (`settings.hallStagewatch`, `server.js:1364-1374`). Under continue and copy it goes
        with its hall, and copy moves it to the hall's new code. Under fresh it is kept as an earlier hall link, listed
        on Admin → Show network and offered when a hall is made, never deleted silently;
      - Patterns and PlayMap links (`settings.peerLinks`, `server.js:1216-1246`) and the certificate pins
        (`settings.tlsPins`, `server.js:145`);
      - the node's id (`server.js:99`), the context token (`:103-107`), the AI key and the tunnel's settings;
      - the key folder (the machine key, the certificate) and `secret.key`;
      - the audit log, which carries on, and its archives in `data\audit-archive\` (H.10.3), which no event act reaches;
      - the laptop's admin and its grants (U17);
      - the confidential holds, `pages.json`'s `holds` (`addendum-stage.md` §5.11, §5.14): the archive keeps
        `pages.json` whole, and its holds are written into the new event's `pages.json` too, since a hold belongs to a
        kept link and its confidential line may still be on that Stagewatch's frame.
    - **Archived, never deleted:** moved into `data\archive\<time>\`, the archive's time to the millisecond
      (`2026-10-27T14-02-00-000Z`), as H.10.1's target names it:
      - `rooms\` (halls and side rooms, with their messages, help requests (`lib/board.js:18` makes a help request a
        message), pins and minutes);
      - the stage's `stage\` and `pages.json`;
      - `displays.json` (screens and their takes, `server.js:119`) and `desk-results.json` (`server.js:124`);
      - the event's uploads;
      - `accounts.json` (under copy, the new event gets a copy of it), and the ended `sessions.json` and
        `admin-sessions.json` (`server.js:112-116`);
      - `event.json`: `{id, name, began, ended, kind, next, counts}`.
      - **On one volume** each move is a rename. The uploads folder is `AGM_UPLOAD_DIR` (`server.js:56`); where it is on
        another volume, its files are copied, counted and sized alike, and only then removed from the uploads folder.
        A copy refuses when free space is below its size and the 1 GiB floor (`server.js:59`).
    - **The order, by the one writer:**
      1. the busy check. New joins and writes are refused with "AGMessage is starting a new event";
      2. the audit log, the lanes and the dirty rooms flushed (U4's order);
      3. `data\archive\.<time>.partial\event.json` written first, with the kind and what comes next, so a stop part way
         leaves the intent on disk;
      4. the moves into `.partial\`, then the folder renamed to `<time>`;
      5. **the archive point**, the archive's last step and its one audit row. Unit H3 writes `audit.archive` through
         `audit.point()`, as the first line of a new file, with the target `<time>;<run>` and words that name the event,
         where it went, what comes next and "links kept" (H.10.1). U15 writes no `event.archived` of its own: one act,
         one row;
      6. the split, when ticked, as its own act straight after the point (H.10.2);
      7. the next event: continue moves the archive's contents back and its `event.json` gains `continued`; copy writes
         the structure with new codes; fresh writes nothing; under all three, the new event's `pages.json` holds the
         holds of the event just archived;
      8. pages are told (`account:changed` reloads them), screens get their new state, and sign-ins end.
      - A stop before step 3 changes nothing. A `.partial` folder found at the next start is finished from its
        `event.json` before the server serves, then steps 5, 7 and 8 run. No file is ever left in neither place.
    - **The audit log carries on** (answer 45). The point, the split and the check from the point are unit H3's
      (`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.10), and U15 needs H3.
      - Who may split, where the older part goes (`data\audit-archive\`), and how the check walks the live log from the
        point and names the archive are H.10's.
      - The archived part of the log stays checkable on its own and inside every export (H2), and is never inside an
        event archive.
    - **"Delete this archive's contents…"** is for the token at the laptop, typed, and audited (`event.purged`).
      - It removes the archive's messages, files and accounts. Its `event.json` stays, so the archive's existence stays
        recorded. It never reaches `data\audit-archive\`, and nothing is deleted on a timer.
      - Today's "delete `app\uploads` after the event" (`README.txt:146-148`) becomes Archive this event, then this.
        Under the installed node, Explorer's "Continue" on a protected folder adds the person to its access list for
        good (https://support.microsoft.com/kb/950934), so the papers send people here instead.
    - **Readers:** the admin page (Event), the admin health (`event: {id, name, began, kind, archives}`), the halls
      board (the new event's halls only), the context (its halls follow the new event at once; no archive is in it), the
      AI's brief (the current event only), the audit list (the point, and `event.purged`), and the screens (their new
      state).
16. **[#78]** **unit U16: the installer's life cycle in CI, and its provenance.**
    - An elevated windows-2025 job:
      - Inno Setup 7.1.0 installed by PlayMap's pinned step (`Mapper/.github/workflows/build.yml:576-610`);
      - this build and build−1 made from one payload;
      - the release-order check;
      - U7's Defender step first.
    - `installer/test/*.test.js` (node:test), with the executed count checked against the declared count.
    - The release attests the installer and `SHA256SUMS.payload` as well as the zip (today only `dist/*.zip`,
      `ci.yml:179-182`). The release job verifies its own attestations with `gh attestation verify`.
    - **Immutable releases are turned on**, which U18 relies on: "Release assets cannot be modified or deleted" and "Git
      tags cannot be moved" (https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/immutable-releases).
17. **[#74]** **unit U17: the laptop's admin, the rights it gives, and the control tasks (answer 38).**
    - **The record.** `Admin`, `AdminName` and `Grants` in `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage`, written by `machine.js` only
      (U12). The install appends `machine.admin`.
    - **One control task per account with a right**, `\AGMessage\Control-<sid>`:
      - it runs as SYSTEM, with the action `node.exe app\machine.js control --for <sid>`, fixed at registration;
      - its security descriptor gives read and execute to that account (and SYSTEM and Administrators) only. A task's
        descriptor is where "you can specify the access control list … to allow or deny certain users and groups access
        to a task" (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/taskschd/registeredtask-setsecuritydescriptor);
        which rights let an account run it on demand is R11;
      - so which task ran says whose request it is, and nothing the request says can change that.
    - **A request:**
      - `launch.js` (run as the person) writes `request.json` into `machine\inbox\<sid>\`, which only that account may
        write, and runs the account's control task (`schtasks.exe /run`);
      - the control task copies the request by its bytes into `machine\work\`, after `lstat` refuses a link or a reparse
        point, then reads it there;
      - it refuses anything that is not whole JSON of at most 4 KB, a known verb (`start`, `stop`, `upgrade`, `back`,
        `grant`, `revoke`, `handover`) and fields of their types. An unknown word is refused, never defaulted;
      - it checks the right in HKLM at that moment, so a right taken back holds at once, even if removing the task failed;
      - it acts, writes `answer.json` into `machine\outbox\<sid>\` (that account may read it), and appends an event;
      - `launch.js` waits for the answer and prints it in the person's console.
    - **The acts:**
      - `start`: runs the server task (`schtasks.exe /run /tn \AGMessage\Server`) and waits for `/api/health`;
      - `stop`: the busy line, then the stop at loopback with the proof (U8), with the reason the person typed when busy;
      - `upgrade` and `back`: U18;
      - `grant`, `revoke`, `handover`: only from the laptop's admin's own task (U.5.1). A grant adds the account's
        `Grants` value, its inbox and outbox, its control task, and, for `token`, its read on `token\`. A revoke removes
        what the account no longer needs. A handover rewrites `Admin` and `AdminName`, gives the new admin all four
        rights, and takes the old admin's away.
    - **The machine events.** `machine\events.jsonl` is appended by `machine.js` only: `{seq, at, kind, by, for, rights,
      words}`, with no secret. The server reads the events after the hold and when `POST /api/machine/events` nudges it
      (U8), writes one audit row per event, and keeps the last `seq` it wrote in settings, so a restart never writes one
      twice or skips one. The file, not the nudge, is the authority.
    - **The rows:** `machine.admin`, `machine.grant`, `machine.revoke`, `machine.handover`, `machine.start`,
      `machine.stop`, `machine.upgrade`, `machine.upgrade.refused` and `machine.import`. Each names the accounts and the
      rights, and never a token, a password or a path in a profile.
    - **The person's words:** "Started." · "Stopped, saved at 20:31." · "Not stopped: AGMessage is busy (3 pages active,
      a countdown running). Type a reason to stop it anyway." · "You have no AGMessage rights on this PC. Ask LAPTOP\ana,
      or an administrator." · "Only LAPTOP\ana, this PC's AGMessage admin, can give rights."
18. **[#77]** **unit U18: an upgrade the laptop's admin or a granted account starts needs no administrator, when the machine can
    check the installer against its release.**
    - **The person's console** (Start → AGMessage → Upgrade AGMessage…, run as the person) offers the newest release,
      which the control task looks up, or a file the person names (`AGMessage-Setup-<semver>-unsigned.exe`).
      - A named file goes into the person's inbox.
      - The reason is typed when the server is busy.
    - **The control task, as SYSTEM:**
      1. **The file.** A named file is copied by its bytes into `machine\staged\` (SYSTEM and Administrators only),
         after `lstat` refuses a link or a reparse point. Its size is compared with `fstat`'s after the open. For the
         newest release, the asset is downloaded straight into `machine\staged\`. Only the staged copy is ever hashed
         or run.
      2. **The release.** `build.json` gains `repo` at stamp time (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY`), so a build knows its own
         repository. The task asks `https://api.github.com/repos/<repo>/releases/tags/v<semver>`, the semver taken from
         the file's name.
         - The release must read `immutable: true`.
         - One of its assets must have the file's exact name and a `digest` equal to `sha256:` and the staged copy's
           SHA-256. GitHub "computes and displays SHA256 checksums (digests) for all uploaded release assets", generated
           at upload time (https://github.blog/changelog/2025-06-03-releases-now-expose-digests-for-release-assets/), and
           the release object carries `immutable` and each asset's `digest`
           (https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases).
      3. **Newer only.** The release's SemVer must be above the installed one (`HKLM` `SemVer`; the release order of
         U6). The installer's own version check (U.6.1 step 1) then refuses an older or equal build a second time.
      4. **The busy check** (U8): a busy server needs the typed reason.
      5. **The run.** The staged installer runs as SYSTEM with `/VERYSILENT /UPGRADEBY=<sid> /FORCE="<reason>"`, and
         U.6.1's order follows, the way back included.
      - `machine.upgrade` names who, the builds from and to, and the digest. `machine.upgrade.refused` names who and
        why.
    - **Refused, each with its words:**
      - no answer from GitHub: "AGMessage could not check this installer against its release (no internet). Run it
        yourself: Windows will ask for an administrator's approval.";
      - not a release of this repository, not immutable, or no asset of that name;
      - a digest that differs: "This file is not the release's. Do not run it.";
      - not newer;
      - busy, with no reason.
    - **Go back to build N** runs the kept installer of `Previous` from `{app}\installers\` with `/ROLLBACK` (U.6.1).
      An elevated or checked install laid it there, under Program Files, so it needs no network.
    - **Why a digest and not a signature.**
      - Mozilla's maintenance service exists "so that Windows users do not have to accept a User Account Control prompt
        every time Firefox updates". It checks the updater against certificate data the installer wrote where it
        "requires elevation, to prevent tampering"
        (https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/toolkit/mozapps/update/docs/Implementation.html).
      - Answer 36 keeps AGMessage unsigned, so there is no signature to check. The release's published digest, fixed by
        immutable releases (U16), takes its place.
      - The same service was found to run an older signed updater as SYSTEM because it "doesn't check the file version"
        (https://blog.mozilla.org/attack-and-defense/2020/10/12/guest-blog-post-rollback-attack/). Hence newer-only,
        checked twice.
    - **What it costs.**
      - SYSTEM runs an installer at a person's request. Whoever controls an account given `upgrade` can install any
        newer genuine release, and nothing else.
      - The trust is GitHub's: the owner's account and the release job, as for a person who downloads the installer.
      - It needs the internet at the moment of the upgrade (R13).
