## 6-U.10 Risks, left for later, and corrections

**Risks**

- **Silent key loss.** A task run without `AGM_KEY_DIR`, or an import done wrong, opens every sealed value as `''`.
  Today it would also write a new certificate, token and secret over the old. U1 refuses the first and makes creation
  ENOENT-only. U14 verifies the second and says which value failed.
- **Two copies with one identity.** A portable source started after its import would run a second node with the same
  Show Bus id and certificate. `moved.json`, read because the source is the same build, refuses it; its keys are gone
  from the profile once the import is verified (answer 42); and the port refuses it on the same laptop.
- **A Windows restart is an unsaved stop** under the task (U.5). Acknowledged messages are kept; lane writes up to
  200 ms old and the audit tail since the head's save are not. The next start says so (answer 41).
- **A crash of the watchdog itself** may leave the node down until the next boot or a Start, if R12 finds that
  Task Scheduler restarts only a failed start.
- **Sleep.** Until U9, every wake from a sleep longer than 10 s restarts the server unsaved, on either channel, and a
  throttled node gives up and stays down.
- **The module walk.** Until U11, a planted `C:\node_modules` runs inside AGMessage on either channel, if a standard
  account may create it (R8).
- **Pipe and port squatting.** An account that takes the pipe's name or the freed port during a restart can hold the
  node down or serve a fake page. U1's exit 75 retries under `task`, the busy line on the pipe is never authority, the
  machine's requests at loopback check the server's proof first and never send the token (U8), and the port's holder is
  named. A person who types the token into a fake page on `localhost` is outside this, as today.
- **Machine-folder attacks** are closed by U12's order.
- **SYSTEM runs the control tasks.**
  - Each runs only `machine.js control --for <sid>`, and only for its own account's inbox.
  - Requests are refused unless whole, known and within bounds. Files are copied by their bytes after `lstat`, and
    refused when a link or a reparse point. An installer runs only from the staged copy, after U18's checks.
  - A bug in `machine.js` runs as SYSTEM, which is why it requires `node:` built-ins only (U11) and why U17's and U18's
    refusals are tests.
- **A checked upgrade trusts GitHub** (U18): the owner's account and the release job. Whoever controls an account given
  `upgrade` can install any newer genuine release, and nothing else.
- **The laptop's admin lost** (the account removed, its password forgotten): any administrator runs Who may run
  AGMessage… elevated and hands it over. The handover is logged as theirs.
- **Smart App Control turned on after the install** blocks nothing the installed node runs, if lab 4 confirms that it
  passes `node.exe` and `cloudflared.exe`. It blocks the next unsigned installer, which `README.txt` says.
- **The way back depends on the kept installer and the backup.** A disk without room for the backup refuses the
  upgrade (U.6.1).
- **Free space for uploads** is on the system drive. The 1 GiB floor (`server.js:59`) is not reassessed, and an event's
  archive keeps its uploads until its contents are deleted (U15).
- **Every number in U.6.2, U.3 and U9 is a Linux proxy.** The CI runner has neither Modern Standby nor Smart App Control,
  and its Defender is off unless U7 turns it on.

**Left for later**

- **Side-by-side version folders** with a proving period (Patterns' updater), if R2 and R9 together exceed 6 s.
- **An update check** that only notifies and is opt-in. The upgrade itself stays a person's act (U18).
- **A save at a Windows shutdown under the task.** It needs a handler for `CTRL_SHUTDOWN_EVENT`, which libuv leaves to
  Windows, or a service host the release can sign. Revisited when lab 5 has measured what a restart costs, or when
  releases are signed.
- **An upgrade checked offline.** It needs a signature to check (answer 36 keeps releases unsigned).
- **The hello's `inst` field**, a Show Bus amendment across four `SHOWBUS.md` copies.
- **A status app in the signed-in user's session**, over an access-listed channel.
- **winget** (it takes Inno installers that need no interaction), **MSI**, and **signing**.
- **Windows Server**, qualified.
- **A migration runner** beyond format 2, when a format change needs one.
- **Socket handoff or a warm spare**, only on R1's trigger.
- **Importing a portable folder into a node that has served**, which would need a merge of two keys, two secrets and two
  audit chains (U14).
- **For Stagewatch's repository:** `CloseApplications` left at its default, and unpinned Inno Setup.

**Corrections**

- **`addendum-startup.md` S.1** cites `start-agmessage.bat:30` for the `node.exe` line; it is `:29` (`:30` is
  `set CODE`).
- **S.2's port-holder message** gains the installed case, read from `HKLM\SOFTWARE\AGMessage` with
  `%SystemRoot%\System32\reg.exe`. **S.2's opener** spawns `explorer.exe` by its absolute path under `%SystemRoot%`, not
  by its bare name (U11's fence).
- **`addendum-audit-hmac.md` H.2's "one key per Windows account"** reads, for the installed node, "one key per machine":
  `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\keys\`. For the portable copy it stands. The audit addendum's revision says so.
- **The final's own recommendation** (B-session by default, with B-task or B-service only on question 35) is withdrawn
  by answer 35. Its "Why B-session first" argued from show-day costs that B-task now pays and U.5 states.
- **The final's "a later import stops the server and archives the current data"** is withdrawn (U14): it would merge two
  machine keys and two audit chains.
- **The draft's own corrections:**
  - it cited the architecture addendum's draft numbers, and its questions 29-35 collided with that addendum's final
    29-33;
  - it called the portable copy "no footprint";
  - it said "only the power plan prevents" sleep;
  - it said Smart App Control "lets it run", from signatures that Windows never verified;
  - it said "many venue policies refuse all three", with no source;
  - it said a task runs "with no identity of its own";
  - it set "recovery to match 0 and 3", which the SCM cannot do;
  - it named NSSM's 1.5 s among the limits, though NSSM is no candidate;
  - it ordered builds by the four-part version against the network's rule.
  - Each is fixed above.

## 6-Critiques not taken

- **Re-seal every value under a fresh machine key after the import** (security-platform 5b): not taken. It revokes
  nothing the account that ran the portable copy already held. It would also make the chain's earlier entries
  uncheckable on the node (H.4's `audit.rekey`). Answer 42 keeps the secrets and removes the copies instead.
- **`utf-8-validate` is required by all four copies of ws** (security-platform 3): corrected. On Node 24, ws takes
  `buffer.isUtf8` (`node_modules/ws/lib/validation.js:138-141`) and never requires it. `WS_NO_UTF_8_VALIDATE` is set
  anyway, harmlessly; `bufferutil` and `supports-color` are the walk.
- **"Name the tunnel as the only route that needs no administrator" on a managed laptop** (show-day 11): taken only
  where the firewall alone blocks. Under AppLocker's default rules the portable `cloudflared.exe` is blocked with
  `node.exe`.
- **Grant start and stop to the interactive users** (show-day 8): taken in a narrower form. The laptop's admin gives
  each right to one account at a time (U17), and a group is refused.
- **Keep the previous `{app}` and restore that folder** (show-day 2): taken in another form, as a kept installer run
  with `/ROLLBACK`. Inno's uninstall log and Add/Remove Programs then stay true.
- **Keep the installers in `%ProgramData%\AGMessage\installers`** (show-day 2): taken in another form, as
  `{app}\installers\`, under Program Files, where only an administrator or a checked upgrade writes. U18's Go back then
  needs no check.
- **"Reframe question 30: B′ (B-task) is the first candidate"** (security-platform 1): taken, now that answers 35 and 36
  are in (U.5). Its stop concern is met by the server's own stop at loopback (U8), not by Task Scheduler's End.
- **`machine.js archive|export` to a portable folder** (show-day 10): taken in another form. The archive is the
  server's act, as the one writer (U15). An export to a portable folder is not taken: an archive is continued or copied
  on the node itself.
- **A child `powershell.exe` holding a power request "while halls are live" as the sleep fix** (show-day 1): taken
  with a limit. Microsoft says `SetThreadExecutionState` "cannot be used to prevent the user from putting the computer
  to sleep", so the lid and the power button stay the power plan's.
- **The installer's wizard page makes the first admin** (show-day 17): taken. With no window under the task, the
  installer's last page is where a person is.

# Part 7: AGMessage 0.6.0, addendum: the Board's chat view (the chat first and compact, with the clock or countdown beside it)

*`060/addendum-board.md`, 2382 lines, kept whole. Its headings carry the prefix `7-`; its units carry their global number, [#n] (Part 0 §0.3).*

Paths are relative to the repository's root; `app/...` holds the server and its pages. Line numbers are from `main` at
`89104d8` (0.5.1), and each site is also named by its function. Where this addendum and the code disagreed, the code was
read and the code wins. This is revision 7. Revision 2 (the draft, `060/addendum-board-draft.md`, as amended by its two
reviews, a design council and an enforcement review) is kept as `060/addendum-board-v1.md`. Revision 3 applied the
owner's answers to its questions B1-B6 (`DECISIONS.md`, its Board sections) with the readings written there; it is
kept as `060/addendum-board-r3.md`, with its mock in `060/board-view-r3-copy/`. Revision 4 applied the review of
revision 3 (19 findings): an On stage seat sends nothing into another room, a Board account answers no help request in a
room where it sits On stage, a Board member's line to people On stage covers nothing, and "the admin" is one predicate on
every path; it is kept as `060/addendum-board-r4.md`. **Revision 5 applied the owner's pin rule (2026-10-27,
`DECISIONS.md`, "Pins"):** every pin is for the room (the default) or for me; a room pin is seen by everyone in the
room, On stage included, and a question pinned for the room is answered from the Board's pinned bar; every seat may pin
for itself; On stage seats pin for themselves only. §17.5 holds the rule, §0.2 amends arch-ux §16, and §0.4 says where
each line landed. §12 quotes the answers. Revision 5 is kept as `060/addendum-board-r5.md`. **Revision 6 applies the
owner's answers to its three readings (2026-10-27, `DECISIONS.md`, "Pins: the owner's answers to the plan's three
readings"):** in every view, simple and full, a question pinned in a way this person sees (for the room, or for them)
is hidden from their feed while it is pinned and drawn only in their pinned place (the Board's pinned bar, the full
view's pinned strip), where its answers are; it returns to its place in the feed when unpinned. That replaces revision
5's "answers in the bar only while the question is out of view". The room's pins listed first, and Got it never
clearing a pinned message of either kind, are confirmed. §17.5 and §17.2 hold the rule, and §12 quotes the answers. The
reading of "anyone with an On stage seat" (B2) is applied as written, and the owner confirmed it ("yes", 2026-10-26),
so no question is left open. "The reviews' findings, answered" says where
each upheld finding landed, and "Critiques not taken" lists the rest.

**Revision 7 applies the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 to every question left open** (`DECISIONS.md`, its last
section). Two of them are this addendum's. **Answer 22**, "Board will use a mixture of devices", gives the chat view its
rows on the one device matrix (the stage addendum's §5.15, rows D1-D7) and on the page floor (the architecture
addendum's §15.10, unit M): §17.7 is new. The mock, in its revision 5, was measured at 21 viewports of those rows, and
the three layout rules that revision 6 had fitted to its two shot sizes now follow the viewport's size (§17.2, §17.4).
**Answer 21** ("21 dark (B6)") is B6, which revision 3 applied: revision 7 confirms it and changes nothing for it. The
pin rules, B1-B6 and the clock's lock are unchanged. Answer 29 ("wrap into 0.6.0") also moves the three lines that
offered units G and G2 a 0.5.2 to 0.6.0 (§11). Revision 6 is kept as `060/addendum-board-pre-final.md`, and its mock as
`060/board-view-r4-copy/`.

**The owner's ask, verbatim (2026-10-26):**

> "The Boards chat view doesn't need to let them add file attachments or create action prompts. They can chat and
> respond and view pushed documents, but they are there to be supported so only need minimal features. Main focus is
> the chat and messages - this doesn't mean the message container design needs to be huge, rather it needs to be more
> minimal and more focused on direct response and clear communication.
> It should have the local and admin option to include the current time of day or StageWatch data for showing
> countdowns as a secondary object within the design."

**Confirmed the same day:** "Yes, the admin may lock the clock/countdown setting".

**The owner's answers to B1-B6 (2026-10-26), verbatim:**

> **B1.** "they can can pin messages for themselves. they don't need to answer other people's help requests other than
> interact with the usual chat."
> **B2.** "An account seated on stage gets messages on that page. Anyone in that same room sees the messages (they need
> to as support). An admin can choose if messages can go onto other screens - such as on a countdown screen, or anyone
> with an On stage seat."
> **B3.** "Clock on by default."
> **B4.** "Got it tells the backstage team with the members name. Clearing the message is an admin option, off by
> default."
> **B5.** "Yes." **B6.** "Yes."

B5 asked whether Board members send 🔥 Priority, and B6 whether the Board's view starts in Dark.

**The owner's pin rule (2026-10-27), verbatim:**

> "A pin can be for the room (default) (including On stage - essential for action prompts), or personal."

**Confirmed the same day:** "A board member cannot pin for the room, only themselves. So pinning for everyone is for
backroom teams, not the board or presenters on stage."

**The owner's answers to the plan's three pin readings (2026-10-27), verbatim:**

> **1.** "A pinned question becomes hidden in the scrolling chat, and becomes visible in scrolling chat when unpinned."
> **2.** "Yes" **3.** "Correct"

Reading 1 asked where a pinned question is answered, 2 whether the room's pins are listed first, and 3 whether Got it
never clears a pinned message, of either kind (§12).

**The owner's answers to the questions left open (2026-10-27), verbatim, as far as this addendum reads them:**

> "Defaults except for: 4 - Admin defined · 22 - Board will use a mixture of devices · 29 - wrap into 0.6.0 · …"

The defaults, as `DECISIONS.md` lists them, include "**21** dark (B6)". Question 22 asked which devices the Board
uses (the architecture addendum's question 22), and 21 whether the simple view starts in Dark (§12).

**The reading** (`DECISIONS.md`: its Board sections, its pin sections and its last section, as confirmed and
answered):

- A Board seat (On stage in a Main room, a guest or an account) chats, replies, answers questions, asks for help, sends
  🔥 Priority (B5), pins messages for itself (B1), and views what is shown to it. It sees the room's pins, and answers a
  question pinned for the room from its pinned bar, where the question is drawn alone: it leaves the feed while it is
  pinned and returns to its place when unpinned (the owner, 2026-10-27).
- **Every pin is for the room (the default) or for me** (the owner, 2026-10-27, §17.5). A room pin is seen by everyone
  in the room, On stage included. Every seat may pin for itself: backstage, observers, Viewer accounts and On stage.
  Only a seat that may post and is not On stage pins for the room ("pinning for everyone is for backroom teams").
  In every view, a question pinned in a way a person sees is drawn only in their pinned place, where it is answered,
  and is hidden from their feed until it is unpinned. The room's pins are listed first, and Got it never clears a
  pinned message of either kind (the owner's answers, 2026-10-27).
- It never attaches a file, never creates a question (an action prompt), never pins for the room and never answers
  someone else's help request (B1), from its On stage page or, for a Board account, from the halls board. **The server
  refuses each by the seat**, whatever the page sends, whatever the view, and for the admin too while the admin sits On
  stage.
- What it writes is in the room's feed, which everyone in that room reads, "as support" (B2). It goes nowhere else: no
  other room (forward, Send to and Send back are refused On stage), no screen, no person's page, unless the admin has
  allowed it for that person by one of two switches, each off by default and audited: **May send to a countdown
  screen** and **May send to people On stage** (§17.6).
- The chat is the primary object, and it is compact: one response place per screen, no card, no badge.
- **👍 Got it** tells the backstage team, with the Board member's name (B4). The message stays in the person's feed,
  marked "👍 You: got it", unless the admin has turned on **Got it clears the message** for that person, which is off
  by default (§17.6).
- The time of day or Stagewatch's countdown is the chat view's secondary object: **Time of day by default** (B3),
  Countdown or Off. The chat view is the simple view, which every On stage seat gets unless the admin sets its Chat
  view to Full; the full view keeps its own stage chip (arch-ux unit 31).
- Both the Board member (on their device) and the admin (per person) set it. The admin's choice is the default, and the
  device's choice overrides it on that device. While the admin has locked it, the device's choice is not offered and the
  admin's choice is drawn. Unlocking brings the device's choice back. Each lock and unlock is an audit row.
- The view starts in Dark until the person chooses Light (B6, which is also answer 21).
- **Every Board feature works on the mixture of devices** (answer 22): iPads on current and older iPadOS, Android
  tablets, and iOS and Android phones. The layout follows the viewport's size and each feature a probe, never the
  device's name or user agent. The one matrix's rows are smoke-tested at their sizes and walked before the tag (§17.7).

**The evidence class:** the owner's ask, the owner's answers to B1-B6, the owner's pin rule (2026-10-27, confirmed the
same day) and the owner's answers to its three readings (the same day; revisions 5 and 6 add no probe, no shot and no
measurement); the code read at `89104d8` (and Stagewatch's
`TimerPhase` and frame builder, for the countdown's phases; `lib/displays.js` and `public/display.js` for a countdown
screen's line); a probe on a throwaway server; a static mock with screenshots and measurements, in five revisions; two
reviews of the first revision; one piece of research; and, for revision 7 (answer 22), MDN's compatibility data,
Playwright's device descriptors, the makers' pixel densities and the mock re-measured at the matrix's sizes (below).

- **Probed** with the repo's test helper (`app/test/helpers.js`) on throwaway folders; nothing in the repository
  changed (`060/boardprobe/probe.js`, `page.js`).
  - As an On stage code guest in an open hall: an upload of a PNG answered 200, it was posted as a file message, an
    action prompt was posted, and both were forwarded into a second hall. All were accepted.
  - The forward also worked when the admin had only linked the guest to the second hall (`admin:linkRoom`), with no
    seat there.
  - The Board page in Chromium at 1280 px shows **29 controls** (`060/boardprobe/board-desktop.png`, `board-phone.png`).
- **Mocked** as static HTML and CSS on a copy of AGMessage's own `styles.css`: `board-view/index.html` and
  `board.css` (revision 5; revision 1 is kept in `060/board-view-draft-copy/`, revision 2 in `060/board-view-r2-copy/`,
  revision 3 in `060/board-view-r3-copy/`, revision 4 in `060/board-view-r4-copy/`).
  - Shot at 1180×820 (an 11-inch tablet in landscape) and 390×844 (a phone, touch), in both themes, dark being the
    mock's default as it is the view's (B6).
  - Measured by `060/board-view-tools/shoot4.js`: controls per area, a 44 px hit band through each control,
    horizontal overflow, computed contrast, font sizes, the chrome above the feed and message heights
    (`shoot-r4.json`, §17.4; revision 3's `shoot3.js` → `shoot-r3.json` is kept); and by `placeholder.js`, whether the
    composer's placeholder fits its field at 390 px.
- **Researched:** character height at reading distance, from a secondary source (§17.2). The text of ANSI/HFES
  100-2007, to which the figure is usually attributed, was not read.
- **Revision 7 (answer 22):**
  - MDN's browser compatibility data, `@mdn/browser-compat-data` 8.1.7 from npm
    (https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data), read as data in a folder of its own, for every browser version §17.7

  - the viewport sizes and pixel ratios of Playwright's device descriptors (v1.56.0,

- **Not run:** on a Board member's tablet or phone; against the app itself (the mock carries no app code); under stage

## 7-§0. What this addendum changes in the design and the addenda

**Read with it:** `design.md` (§1.8, §1.10, §2.1-§2.7, §3.3, §4.2, §4.3, §5.4, §5.8, §6, §7.3-§7.5, §9-§11), the
architecture and UX addendum (`addendum-arch-ux.md`: §13.3.4, §14.2, §14.4, §15.2-§15.10, §16.2, §16.7, §16.8, §11), the
stage addendum (`addendum-stage.md`: §4.6, §4.6.3, §4.6.6, §5.9.2.2, §5.9.11, §5.14, §5.15, §7.7, §11) and `DECISIONS.md`.
Where those texts predate the owner's ask, the ask wins.

### 7-§0.1 In the design

- **§1.10:** `pages.json`'s `views['u:<uid>']` becomes `{view?, clock?, onStage?, at}`, and `accounts.json` gains
  `clock` (`{show, locked}`) and `onStage` (`{screens, people, clears}`, §17.6), bounded as `view` is, set by `update`
  only (an account is created with neither, so it starts at the owner's defaults). `pages.json`
  gains `pins: {<personKey>: {<room key>: [message id…]}}` (§17.5): at most 50 per person per room, its person records
  inside the views' bound (5,000, the oldest first), pruned with the room.
- **§1.8 (rollback):** "Kept and ignored" adds the accounts' `clock` and `onStage` and the guests' `views[…].clock` and
  `views[…].onStage`. 0.5.1 keeps unknown fields through a load and a save, so going back to 0.6 restores them.
  `pins` lives in `pages.json`, which 0.5.1 never reads.
- **§2.1 (`rbac`):** a seat has a limit, `rbac.seatAllows(seat, cap)` (§17.1). An account seated `board` holds, on that
  page, only what both its rights and the seat allow. `rightsIn`'s account branch reads the target seat's limit.
- **§2.3:** "`GUEST_CAPS` (`server.js:699`) is unchanged for Main" becomes: `GUEST_CAPS.board` is
  `['hall.view', 'hall.post']`. An admin's link (`rightsIn`, `server.js:924`) uses its own named set,
  `rbac.LINKED_CAPS`, which keeps today's `hall.files`.
  - `mayKnowCode` answers `''` for a socket seated On stage (§17.1). A Board account's tablet is not handed the
    guest code.
- **§2.5:** `help:respond` gains the On stage rule first, whatever `code` is sent: from an On stage socket only
  `resolved` on one's own request (unit G2, owner answer B1: "they don't need to answer other people's help
  requests"). The account branch reads the account's seat in the request's room, as `rightsIn`'s does: each of its two
  doors needs `rbac.roomRoleFor(acct, scope) !== 'board'` for its own scope, so the check becomes
  `(canIn(acct, 'hall.post', scopeOf(r)) && roomRoleFor(acct, scopeOf(r)) !== 'board') || (canIn(acct, 'hall.post',
  mainScopeOf(r.hall)) && roomRoleFor(acct, mainScopeOf(r.hall)) !== 'board')`, and "the hall's crew" never includes
  a Board member of that hall. Resolving one's own request stays allowed. The admin's branch is unchanged.
- **§2.6:** `canPush(hall)` reads `allowed('display.control')`, which the seat limit cuts. A Board account never pushes
  from its On stage page.
- **§2.7 (audit):** adds `person.clock` and `person.onStage`, and the `user.update` words `clock → …` and `onStage → …`
  (§17.3, §17.6). A Board member's line on a countdown screen is a `display.take` row, and on people's pages a
  `page.push` row; each names the person and the length, never the text (§17.6). A pin for oneself is not audited: it
  is a person's act on their own page.
- **§3.3 (`join`):** the answer appends **`clock`** (`{show, locked}`, §17.3, unit 20b), then **`pins`** (this
  person's pinned ids in this room, §17.5, unit 20c), then **`onStage`** (`{screens, people, clears,
  countdownScreens?}`, §17.6, unit 20d), in the order their units land, after every key the design and the addenda
  append. `uploadToken` is `null` for a Board seat, and `sends` is `false` while
  On stage (§4.2 below). The socket records its seat in `socket.data.seat`.
- **§4.2 (`room:send`, owner answer B2):** from an On stage socket, `room:send` in both forms, a new message and an
  existing one (and so **Send back**, which is the same path), is refused first, whatever its type: "Messages from On
  stage stay in this room." `room:sendTargets` answers `{ok: true, targets: []}`, so the join answer's `sends` is
  false. The room-level allow-list is not read as the admin's per-person choice of B2. Step 1's "the rights in S
  decide" stays the deliberate exception for the target: the admin's allow-list says that people who may post in S may
  post into T. So a Tech account's file sent from Legal, where it is a Member, into the Main room where it sits On stage
  is allowed and reads "↘ From Legal". It is the backstage team's act, made from a backstage page.
- **§4.3 and `forward`:** from an On stage socket, `forward` is refused first, whatever the message, with the same
  words (unit G, B2). Elsewhere a file moves only from a seat that holds `hall.files` where it is (the stage addendum's
  `mayDownload` rule says so too), and a question never moves into a room where the forwarder would sit `board`.
- **§7.5 (the hall page), for an On stage seat in either view:** no **To:** (its `sends` is false), no ↗ menu (its
  `forwardable` is false, arch-ux §16.7) and no **↩ Send back** on a "↘ From Legal" message.
- **§5.8:** the take layer's 🔥 strip gains **👍 Got it** beside **Open chat** in the simple view (unit 20a). It is the
  only 🔥 strip while a take covers the page: the feed's strip is under the layer and never says "under a take". With

  lines by height, the sheet bounded and scrolled, the placeholder by measured fit, and the sheet's words where the
  device cannot be kept awake (§17.2, §17.7).

## 7-§17. The Board's chat view

### 7-§17.1 What an On stage seat may do, on the server

**Who sits On stage:**

- today: a code guest with role `board`, or an old link's `director` (read as board, `server.js:716`). Accounts never sit
  On stage: `roomRoleFor` gives `research` or `observer` (`lib/rbac.js:161`, used at `server.js:733`);
- under the plan:
  - an invited guest, or one the admin seated (the stage addendum, §5.9.2.1);
  - an account with the hall in `account.board` (design §2.1);
  - the admin, joined with `role: 'board'` from the host token (`server.js:716`, `:741`) or as an admin-role account
    given `board`.

**One question, asked of the socket's own seat:**

```js
// The socket's seat: set at join (cleanRole), changed by admin:setRole, never by the page. The admin's support view is
// unseated (adminView), so it is never On stage.
const onStage = () => !!me && socket.data.seat === 'board' && !socket.data.adminView;
```

- It is keyed on the socket, not on `roomRoleFor(acct, code)`. The same account keeps its crew rights on its side-room
  page and on the halls board, and is limited only on the page where it sits On stage. Two checks also read the
  account's seat in a room, as `rightsIn`'s account branch does, because they act on a room from outside it: a forward
  into the room (below) and `help:respond` from the halls board, which answers no help request of a room where the
  account sits `board` (G2, owner answer B1; design §2.5 as §0.1 amends it).

**The seat limit** (new, pure, in `lib/rbac.js`):

```js
const SEAT_LIMITS = Object.freeze({ board: Object.freeze(['hall.view', 'hall.post']) });
/** Whether a seat allows a right at all: an On stage seat reads and writes messages, and nothing else. */
const seatAllows = (seat, cap) => !Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(SEAT_LIMITS, seat) || SEAT_LIMITS[seat].includes(cap);
const LINKED_CAPS = Object.freeze(['hall.view', 'hall.post', 'hall.files']);   // the admin's link (admin:linkRoom), as today
```

- **`allowed(cap)`** (`server.js:700-705`) gains a first line, before the admin's short-circuit:
  `if (onStage() && !rbac.seatAllows('board', cap)) return false;`. Then today's body (from unit 5, `rbac.canIn` and
  `rbac.guestCaps(role, kind)`).
  - An admin seated On stage is limited on that page, like anyone else there. One seat gives one answer, so the matrix
    holds. Every `admin:*` verb goes through `admin(ack)` (`:1398`), which does not read the seat, and the admin's
    support view is unseated.
- **The checks that do not call `allowed()`** read `onStage()` too, and each refuses with "Do that from a backstage
  page.":
  - `canDisplays` (`:1094`: `display:list`, `:take`, `:create`, `:update`, `:identify`, `:rotate`, `:remove`,
    `:hallHolding`);
  - `canManageHall` (`:1331`: `hall:settings`, `hall:configure`, `hall:acceptCertificate`, and `display:hallHolding`'s
    second door at `:1188`);
  - **`nodes:list`** (`:1200`) and **`nodes:command`** (`:1268`), each with the `onStage()` refusal as its first line.
    `nodes:list`'s own gate (`:1202`, `isAdmin` or `nodes.control`) would let an On stage Tech through, and
    `mayDriveNode` (`:2010`) only filters its list, so reading the seat there would answer `{ok: true}` with an empty
    list instead of refusing. `mayDriveNode` is unchanged: its other user, the halls board (`boardFor`, `:1754-1757`),
    is unseated.
  - `nodes:link`, `nodes:unlink` and `nodes:acceptCertificate` (`:1213`, `:1241`, `:1259`) gate on `isAdmin` alone and
    stay the admin's, like every `admin:*` verb: no Board seat holds them, and an admin On stage keeps them.
- **`forward`** (`:943-968`) refuses an On stage socket first, before it reads the message or the target: "Messages
  from On stage stay in this room." (owner answer B2: what a seat On stage writes goes nowhere else by default, and the
  room-level allow-list or an admin's `admin:linkRoom` is not the per-person choice B2 gives the admin). Text, a file
  and a question are refused alike.
- **`mayAsk()`** is `mayPost` and not `onStage()`. It guards `message {type: 'action'}`. At the target, a forward of an
  action from a backstage page is refused when `rightsIn(dst).role === 'board'`.
- **`canDraft()`** (`:996`) is `me && !onStage() && (me.role === 'research' || isAdmin)`.
- **`rightsIn(r)`** (`:918-926`):
  - the admin's branch is unchanged for the target (the admin may post anywhere); the source rules above still apply
    when the admin sits On stage;
  - **an account** (unit 9): `may: (cap) => rbac.can(acct, cap, r.code) && rbac.seatAllows(rbac.roomRoleFor(acct, r.code), cap)`.
    An account cannot forward a file or a question into the hall where it sits On stage, and a guest cannot either;
  - **a guest:** the seat with the most rights is taken (research, then board, then observer), and its role is
    stamped, so two seats of one uid in one room never give an answer that depends on their order;
  - **a link with no seat:** `rbac.LINKED_CAPS`, never `GUEST_CAPS.board`. Today's behaviour stays for a linked
    backstage guest, and `forward`'s On stage rule still stops a Board guest moving anything through the link.
- **`myRooms`** (`:929-941`) answers `{ok: true, rooms: []}` while `onStage()`, before it lists anything. Elsewhere it
  applies the source rules: `[]` for a file unless the source has `allowed('hall.files')` (and, from stage unit 26,
  `mayDownload`), and for an action it drops each room where `rightsIn(c).role === 'board'`. The picker never offers a
  room that the forward would refuse.
- **`room:send`** (unit 14, design §4.2) refuses an On stage socket first, in both forms, with the same words, and
  **`room:sendTargets`** answers `{ok: true, targets: []}` while `onStage()`. Send back is `room:send`, so it is refused
  too. The join answer's `sends` and `forwardable` are false while `onStage()`, so no page draws To:, ↗ or Send back
  there.
- **`mayKnowCode`** (design §2.3, unit 7) answers `''` while `onStage()`.
- `GUEST_CAPS.board` becomes `['hall.view', 'hall.post']`, so a guest's base and its limit agree. Seats without a limit
  (`research`, `observer`) are unchanged by this addendum.
- **Seen in passing, for the splice:** an account seated `observer` (a Staff or Tech account with `hall.post` revoked)
  keeps `stage.send`, `display.control` and `hall.files` on that page today, because `allowed()` does not read the seat.
  `SEAT_LIMITS.observer = ['hall.view']` would close it, at the cost of one test row. That is outside the owner's ask,
  so it is not in unit G.

**The upload token is checked at use, not only at issue.** The entry made at `server.js:789` gains `may: () =>
allowed('hall.files')` and `seat: () => socket.data.seat`. `POST /api/upload` calls `may()` after the token lookup and
before the disk check; on false it deletes the token and answers 403 with the seat's words above. `admin:setRole`
(`:1466-1485`) sets each changed socket's `data.seat` and deletes its token in the same tick as the change. It does not
wait for the page's reload, just as the stage addendum's `ro:<key>` rule does not.

**What the page is told:** the join answer's `uploadToken: null`. The catalogue's facts gain `ask` (`post && seat !==
'board'`), `pin` (the room's: `post && seat !== 'board'`, from 20c), `pinMine` (`true` for every seat: whoever is
seated in the room may view it, which is all `pin:mine` needs; from 20c, the pin rule of 2026-10-27) and `respondHelp`
(`post && seat !== 'board'`, from G2). In the support view these are the person's facts (R8), so its pin doors are the
person's, drawn disabled, and the server refuses `pin:mine` from it all the same. These are pure functions of facts the
page already has, so the answer gains no key for them. `files` is `false` through the limit, and `sends` and `forwardable` are
`false` while On stage (the server's, as above). `also` reads the join answer's `onStage` (§17.6), and `pins` the
answer's `pins` (§17.5).

**The catalogue's rows** (arch-ux §16.7, amended; ids the matrix names are defined here):

- **`msg`:**
  - **`msg.ack`**, **👍 Got it**: verb `react` (`{emoji: '👍', on: true}`, one per message it answers), mode `hold` (a
    Wi-Fi blip holds it, R2), `may: post`. `fits`, all of:
    - the simple view (the full view's React ▸ 👍 is the same fact, so the full view has no Got it);
    - the author's seat is backstage (`o.from.role === 'research'`), the type is `text` or `file`, it is not a system
      line, and this person has not answered it (§17.2, "Answered");
    - and it is either a 🔥 message, or **the newest waiting plain message**, whose label is "👍 Got it" when it alone
      waits and "👍 Got all N" when N plain messages wait. Got all N answers each of them, held in the outbox as one
      batch of N sends.
    - Its inline rank in the simple view is 1. Another On stage author's message, 🔥 or not, gets Reply only: Got it
      answers the backstage team.
    - With the admin's **Got it clears** on for this person, the page also folds the message into one muted line in
      their feed (§17.6). The act and its `may` are unchanged.
  - **`msg.reply`**: `fits` drops "full view". In the simple view it sits beside Got it, on the newest waiting plain
    message and on each waiting 🔥 message, and on a message tapped again (the second door, §17.2).
  - **`msg.pin`** (for the room, the default): label **Pin for the room** / **Unpin for the room**, `short` **For the
    room**, verb `pin {pinned}`, mode `now`, `may: pin`, `fold: 'pin'`, first in the fold, key P (the fold's), Undo
    the opposite op. `fits`: the full view's message menu (and the pinned strip's copies). Not in the simple view,
    whatever the seat: its hide list keeps the room's pin (design §6, §0.1), so the simple view's one pin door is For
    me.
  - **`msg.pinMine`** (for me): label **Pin for me** / **Unpin for me**, `short` **For me**, verb `pin:mine`, mode
    `hold`, `may: pinMine`, `fold: 'pin'`, second in the fold, key P (the fold's), Undo the opposite op. `fits`: in
    the simple view, the row of a tapped message (the second door, rank 3 after Got it and Reply); in the full view,
    the message menu.
  - Both shown (a seat that may post and is not On stage): one item, **📌 Pin ▸ For the room · For me** (**📌 Unpin ▸**
    while pinned both ways), `menuitemcheckbox` items checked where pinned (§0.2, "Amends arch-ux §16"). `msg.pinMine`
    alone (observer, Viewer, On stage): flat, **📌 Pin for me** / **📌 Unpin for me**.
  - **`msg.helpRespond`** (On my way · Resolved on a help request): verb `help:respond`, `may: respondHelp`, or the
    author's own request for Resolved. Defined for the matrix; the Board's own request is answered from the Help chip
    (It's sorted).
  - Defined for the matrix: **`msg.speaker`** (Speaker's screen ▸), **`msg.screens`** (⧉ Show on screens…),
    **`msg.draft`** (✨ Draft a reply), with today's `may` of §16.7's row.
- **`file`** (the panel's pinned list and the Preview's header): **`file.pin`** and **`file.pinMine`**, as `msg.pin`
  and `msg.pinMine`, in the same fold. The Preview's 📌 button (`app.html:136`) is that fold as a menu button (**📌 Pin
  ▸**, `aria-haspopup="menu"`), or the flat **📌 Pin for me** where only that is shown. A pinned-list entry's ✕ unpins
  the kind it shows ("Unpin for the room" or "Unpin for me" as its name); an entry pinned both ways opens **📌 Unpin ▸
  For the room · For me**; an entry this seat may not unpin (the room's, for an observer or On stage) has no ✕.
- **`compose`:** **`compose.attach`** (📎 Attach a file…) and **`compose.share`** (📎 Share for download) have `may:
  files`. **`compose.ask`** (❓ the question tab: verb `message`, mode `hold`, `may: ask`). **`compose.priority`** (🔥
  Priority: `may: post`; `fits`: both views, owner answer B5; a toggle, off after every send).
  **`compose.also`** (Also on: ⏱ <the screen> · 👥 Everyone On stage, §17.6): verb `message {also}`, mode `now`,
  `may: onStage.screens || onStage.people`, each chip only for its own switch; ⏱ disabled with "No screen in this hall
  shows the countdown now." while `countdownScreens` is empty. `fits` both views: the switches belong to the person and
  the server reads the seat, never the view, so the full view draws the same row above its composer.
- **`card`:** `card.show`'s label follows a fact, as compose's Send does with To: **👁 Look** in the simple view, **⤴
  Show again** in the full view. `card.remove` `fits` the full view only.
- **`sheet`:** Text size · Clock or countdown · Theme · Full screen · Leave the hall (Leave asks in place, §17.2).
- **`person`:** adds **Clock or countdown ▸** (`menuitemradio`: Their choice · Off · Time of day · Stagewatch
  countdown) and **Lock it on their devices** (`menuitemcheckbox`), verb `admin:setClock` (`now`); and, for a person
  seated On stage, three `menuitemcheckbox` entries, **May send to a countdown screen**, **May send to people On
  stage** and **Got it clears the message**, verb `admin:setOnStage` (`now`, §17.6). The choice follows `admin:setView`
  (an `isAdmin` page); the lock and the three switches need the admin (§17.6, "Who sets it"), and an `isAdmin` page
  whose account's role is not `admin` draws them disabled with the refusal's words.
- **`account`:** adds **Clock or countdown ▸** and **Lock it on their devices**, verb `http:PATCH /api/users/:id`. The
  lock needs an admin (§17.3). It adds the same three On stage switches, which need an admin too (§17.6). All of them
  are account fields, drawn once beside **Chat view**, not in a hall's row.

**The message menu by seat**, its two On stage rows replaced:

| Seat | What it holds |
|---|---|
| On stage, simple view | No menu door. The newest waiting plain message from backstage: **👍 Got it** (or **Got all N**) **· ↩ Reply**, after its words. Each waiting 🔥 message: **👍 Got it** (filled) **· ↩ Reply**. A question: its answers and **Answer in words…**. A card in Shown to you, and an Earlier entry: **👁 Look**. The 🔥 strip, and the take layer's 🔥 strip: **👍 Got it** (the layer's beside Open chat). A tapped message (the second door): its own row, **👍 Got it** where it waits **· ↩ Reply · 📌 Pin for me** (or Unpin for me). The pinned bar: one button, the room's pins first, to the message (on a pinned question, to the next pin); a pinned question drawn whole in it, with its answers and **Answer in words…** (and **📌 Unpin for me** on one pinned for oneself), and hidden from the feed (§17.5). A cleared message's line: **Show**. One's own message: no button, its status words. The composer: **🔥 Priority**, the words, **Send**, and **Also on** only with an admin's switch. No Got it (React ▸ 👍 is the same fact), no ↗ Send to ▸, no ↩ Send back and no To: (G and 14, owner answer B2), no Pin for the room (20c), no On my way or Resolved on someone else's help (G2), no Download (but a ticked take), no Show the Board, no speaker's screen, no ⧉, no ✨ |

me** (§17.2), since it is not in the feed to be tapped.

**The matrix** (§16.8 1) asserts, for a Board guest (simple, full), a Board account (simple), a Board guest with

- **the pin rows of every fixture** (the table above): research locked and open, Staff, Tech, a side-room Member and

- `catalog.test.js` asserts that every absent id exists in the catalogue and is shown for at least one other fixture.
- `test/menus.test.js` sends each verb whose `may` is false, as both Board fixtures, and expects the table's words; `pin`
  is sent as the observer and the Viewer too, and answers "Observers can read but not post.".

### 7-§17.2 The view: the chat first

The Board's posture is transient: a glance, a response, back to the room. The owner's words set the order: "Main focus
is the chat and messages", "minimal", "direct response and clear communication". So the page is one reading column of
messages, with one response place per screen, after the words it answers.

**One model at every size** (owner answer 22: the viewport's size decides, never the device; §17.7):

```
tablet 1180×820                                                 phone 390×844
┌ Hall 2 — Annual General Meeting       ┃🕐 14:12       Help ⋯ ┐  ┌ Hall 2 — Ann… ┃🕐 14:12     Help ⋯ ┐ row 1: the clock by default
│ (16 px, muted)                        ┃(or ⏱ + its line)     │  │ Q&A · Wrap up in 2 minutes          │ row 2: only with a countdown line
├ 📌 For you · Resolution 3 proxies… ──────────┬── Shown to you 360 ┤  ├ Chat │ 📺 Shown to you · 1 ──────────┤ only while something is shown
│ one reading column, at most 46 rem, centred  │ cards, Earlier     │  │ 📌 For you · Resolution 3 prox…     │ only with a pin
│ (about 60 characters of 22 px text)          │ (on --bg)          │  │ 🔥 strip, only while out of view    │
│                                              │                    │  │ the feed                            │
├ Also on ✓⏱ Lectern · 👥 Everyone On stage ───┤                    │  │ Also on ✓⏱ Lectern · 👥 On stage    │ only with an admin's switch
├ [🔥 Priority] [Message everyone here…] [Send]┤                    │  │ [🔥] [Message everyone here…] [Send]│
```

- **Which layout, by size** (§17.7 measures each rule on the matrix):
  - the side column, Shown to you at 360 px, at 900 px wide or more. Below 900 px, the two tabs: every phone either way
    up, and every tablet held upright (640 to 834 px wide on the matrix's sizes);
  - 22 px text where the viewport's smaller side is 600 px or more, which is a tablet either way up; 20 px on a phone,
    either way up;
  - the phone's header (one 57 px row) and composer (🔥 alone, a 16 px field) at 600 px wide or less;
  - an iPad's Split View, Slide Over or Stage Manager window draws by the window's size, as any viewport does.
- **The header:** the hall's name (`--fs-title`, 16 px, weight 500, `--c-ink-muted`, cut with "…"); the secondary
  object, **the clock by default** (owner answer B3), the countdown, or nothing when Off (§17.3); **Help** (or its
  status chip, unit E); **⋯**.
  - On a phone, the readout's digits sit on row 1 between the name and Help, and the name shrinks first ("Hall 2 —
    Ann…"). Row 2 is drawn only while Stagewatch has a line, or for "Offline · reconnecting". With the clock, or with
    nothing, the phone's header is one 57 px row.
  - "Offline · reconnecting" after 5 s down: row 2 on a phone; before Help on a tablet.
  - The seat ("On stage") is said in the sheet's footer, not the header: the person knows where they sit.
- **The pinned bar** (owner answer B1 and the pin rule of 2026-10-27, §17.5): under the header and the phone's tabs,
  only while the person or the room has a pin. One line, 48 px on a tablet and 44 px on a phone or under 500 px tall: "📌 For everyone" or
  "📌 For you" ("📌 For everyone · for you" for a message pinned both ways), then the message's words cut to one line,
  then "1 of 2" when there are several. The line is one button: on a message it goes to the message in the feed, and
  the bar then shows the next pin. The room's pins come first (confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-27).
  - **A pinned question is drawn here, and only here** (the owner, 2026-10-27: "A pinned question becomes hidden in the
    scrolling chat, and becomes visible in scrolling chat when unpinned."). A question pinned for the room ("essential
    for action prompts") or for this person leaves their feed while it is pinned, and the bar draws it whole: its
    words, at the body size and weight 600 as in the feed, follow the line's "📌 For everyone · Question" (or "📌 For
    you · Question") and wrap instead of being cut; under them, its answers, 48 px as in the feed, and **Answer in
    words…**, whose field opens in the bar. Answered, the row reads "You answered Yes · 14:10 · **Change**", in the
    bar. A question pinned for this person also has **📌 Unpin for me** beside Answer in words…: it is not in the feed
    to be tapped, so this is its one unpin door in the simple view (one pinned for the room has none there, by the
    hide list). One response place per screen, wherever the feed is scrolled: the feed holds no copy, so the bar reads no
    observer.
  - On a question the line has nowhere to go, since the question is already in the bar: a tap shows the next pin (its
    name says "Next pin"), so with two pinned questions "1 of 2" reaches each one's answers in turn. While the
    question is the only pin, its line is not a button.
  - With a question the bar is taller: about 105 px on a tablet and 101 px on a phone while its words fit the line
    (§17.4, an estimate), up to 30% of the viewport, today's strip's bound (`styles.css:154`), past which the question
    scrolls inside the bar.
  - Unpinned, the question is back in its place in the feed, by its seq, with its answers.
- **Shown to you:** the stage addendum's Board reader (§4.6.3, as §0.3 amends it). A card is a 64 px thumbnail with its
  title, "p. 14 · From Ana · 14:07" and **👁 Look**. Earlier lists what came before, each with **👁 Look**. A page is
  drawn large only when opened. The column sits on `--bg` with its cards on `--card`, so it is never brighter than the
  chat. As a column (900 px wide or more), it collapses to its rail while empty, so the chat takes the whole width; below
  900 px it is the second tab's page.

**A message:**

| Part | Drawn as | Size | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who wrote it | the name at weight 600; **You** for one's own; the word **On stage** after the name only when the author also sits On stage. Backstage is the default author here, so it carries no word on screen, and a visually hidden ", backstage," says it to assistive technology | 16 px | the exception carries the word; no badge, no capitals |
| Its kind | no rule for backstage or one's own. 🔥: a 4 px `--c-fault` rule with **🔥 Priority**; a question: a 4 px `--c-ask` rule with **Question** | the words 18 px, weight 700 | the exception carries the word and the rule, never the colour alone |
| When | `14:05`, tabular | 14 px, `--c-ink-muted` | read on demand, not at a glance |
| The text | 22 px (tablet) or 20 px (phone) × Text size, line height 1.4, at most 36 em; one's own in `--c-ink-muted` (6.16:1) | `--fs-lg` | §17.2's sizes |
| A reply's quote | "↩ You: Could you confirm the proxy count…", one line, cut | 14 px, muted | — |
| **The response** | after the text, left-aligned with it, 6 px below: **👍 Got it** (or **Got all N**) and **↩ Reply**, text actions in `--c-action`, 36 px drawn and 44 px to the finger (a `::before` 4 px above and below). On a 🔥 message Got it is filled. Only where §17.1's `msg.ack` fits | 16 px | one place, once or twice per screen; Tab and a screen reader reach the words first |
| Status words | at the end of the author's line: **👍 You: got it**, **📌 Pinned for everyone**, **📌 Pinned for you** (both: "📌 Pinned for everyone · for you"); on one's own, Sending · Sent · Seen by Ana · △ Not sent, and where it also went (§17.6): ⏱ On Lectern ✓ · 👥 Shown to 5 of 6 On stage | 14 px, muted | read on demand |
| Cleared (B4, with the admin's switch) | in place of a message the person got: one line, "👍 Got and cleared: Ana Ribeiro 14:02 · **Show**", with 🔥 before the name for a priority message ("👍 Got and cleared: 🔥 Tom Okafor 14:06 · **Show**"); a run of them is one line, "3 messages" | 14 px, muted; 44 px tall | the place is kept, and the way back; 🔥 says what kind it was |
| Not drawn | card, border, shadow, seat badge, reaction pills, seen lines under others' messages, presence lines, ⋯, 😊 ↗ ⧉ 🖥 📝 🗑; 📌 only in a tapped message's row (§17.5) | — | — |

**One response place per screen.** Most backstage messages are information, and the person's one act is "I've read
this":

- the **newest waiting plain message** from backstage carries the pair. With one waiting it reads **👍 Got it**; with
  three it reads **👍 Got all 3**, which answers each (three `react {👍, on: true}`, held as one batch);
- **each waiting 🔥 message** keeps its own pair, with Got it filled;
- **a question** keeps its answers in the feed, or, while it is pinned, in the pinned bar alone (§17.5);
- an **older waiting message** draws no buttons. A tap on it, or Enter on it in the roving feed (unit 3c), brings its
  own row back, for that message alone (the second door): Got it where it waits, Reply, and **📌 Pin for me** (or
  **Unpin for me**, owner answer B1). A tap on an answered message brings Reply and 📌 alone;
- on the tablet shot this is 8 feed controls where the first revision drew 12; revision 3 adds none by default (📌 is
  behind the tap).

**Answered, per person:**

- A message from backstage waits for this person until they answer it, by one of:
  - Got it (their 👍 in its `reactions`);
  - a message of theirs whose `replyTo` is it;
  - for a question, their entry in its `responses`.
- Once answered, its line reads **👍 You: got it**, or nothing after a reply, since the reply is in the feed below with
  its quote.
- The page derives all of it from facts the server already sends: no new field and no new verb.

**A question:**

- Its line reads **Question** · the author · the time. Its text is at the body size, weight 600.
- Its answers are buttons 48 px tall (`--target-answer`) with a 2 px control edge (the mock's `--bv-edge`: #737c8c light,
  4.21:1 on `--card`; #6f7c9a dark, 3.88:1), `--c-action` when hovered or chosen, at least 96 px wide on a tablet and sharing
  the row equally on a phone. The ask colour stays on the rule and the word.
- Then **Answer in words…**, a text action (not underlined, like every other text action) that opens one field in
  place: "Your answer…", 200 characters (the server's cap), with **Send answer**. On a phone Send answer wraps under
  the field. Escape closes it.
- Answered: "You answered Yes · 14:10 · **Change**" (Change brings the options back; `actionResponse` replaces one's own
  answer, `:855-859`). In words: "You answered: “…”".
- Others' tallies are not drawn in the simple view. The backstage team reads them.

**🔥 Priority:**

- In the feed: the rule and the word, with **Got it** filled (`--c-action`) and Reply.
- A Board member may send 🔥 too (owner answer B5). Their 🔥 message carries the rule and the word for every reader; on
  another Board member's page it has Reply only, and it never fills the strip, whose Got it answers the backstage
  team.
- **The strip** above the feed holds the newest unanswered priority message **only while that message is out of view**:
  scrolled away (an `IntersectionObserver` on the message), or behind the phone's Shown to you tab. While a take covers
  the page, the take layer's own strip says it (design §5.8, with Got it from 20a).
  - Its words are at the body size and keep three lines: two in a viewport under 700 px tall (an iPhone in Safari,
    whose bars leave 659 of its 852 px) and one under 500 px (a phone held sideways). The whole message is one tap
    away in the feed. The time is left to the feed on a phone.
  - **Got it** follows the words in the page's order. It is drawn at the end of the strip's first line, so the strip
    spends no row of its own on it (140 px on the phone shot).
  - "+2 more" shows when there are several; Got it answers the shown one and the strip moves to the next.

**What is new below:** while the person reads further up, a 48 px **↓ 3 new · 1 question** sits over the composer (unit
P's "↓ 1 new", carried into the simple view, naming a question when one is among them: "↓ 2 new", "↓ 1 question"). A
tap goes to the New divider.

**Nobody backstage:** while no backstage seat has been in the room's `users` for 10 s, one muted line sits over the
composer: "○ Nobody backstage is online. Use Help if you need someone." It clears when one joins. ○ is AGM.MARKS' "off".
Help still reaches the halls board's crew, who answer help from outside the room.

**One's own messages** say what is true, at the end of the line:

- **◷ Sending** while the outbox holds it (unit Q);
- **Sent** once the server took it;
- **Seen by Ana** once a backstage seat's `seen` covers its seq ("Seen by Ana and 2 more" past two names);
- where it also went, with an admin's switch (§17.6): **⏱ Lectern: sending**, then **⏱ On Lectern ✓** once the screen
  confirms, **△ Lectern could not show it**, or **Replaced on Lectern at 14:12**; **👥 Shown to 5 of 6 On stage** once
  their pages confirm the card in Shown to you. Every reader of the room sees the same words;
- **△ Not sent: <the server's words> · Try again**, with the text kept. `app.js:1395` clears the field whatever the ack
  says, so a refused send ("Slow down a little.") loses the text silently today; that clear goes.

**The composer:**

- **🔥 Priority** (owner answer B5), first: a toggle (`aria-pressed`), off after every send, as 0.5.1's
  `consumePriority` is (`app.js:1375-1381`), so a mode is never left on. Pressed, it fills in `--c-fault` with
  `--c-on-fault` words (6.47:1 light, 9.69:1 dark): red is drawn only for 🔥, open help and faults, and this is 🔥.
  On a tablet it reads "🔥 Priority"; on a phone "🔥", with "Priority" for assistive technology. 48 px tall, 44 px or
  more wide. Send keeps its word: the feed's own "🔥 Priority" is the one word for it;
- the field (48 px; 18 px text on a tablet, 16 px on a phone, where 18 px would cut the placeholder beside 🔥 and Send
  at 390 px: 221 px of text in a 204 px box, measured by `placeholder.js`; 16 px or more stops iOS zooming on focus).
  Its placeholder and its label are the same words, "Message everyone here…" (WCAG 2.5.3): the Main room's readers
  include other Board members and observers, the support of the owner's B2. Where those words do not fit the field
  (the page measures them in the field's own font on load and on `resize`, as `placeholder.js` does), the placeholder
  is "Message everyone…", and the label keeps the long words, which contain it (2.5.3). At 375 and 360 px wide the long
  words were cut (§17.4, answer 22);
- **Send**.
- `maxlength` stays 300 (`app.html:50`), and is 160 while ⏱ is chosen under Also on (§17.6); the server takes 4,000.
- Replying: a line above the field, "↩ Replying to **Tom Okafor**: Voting on resolution 4…", with **✕ Cancel** (and
  Escape).
- **Also on** (owner answer B2), only while the admin has turned on one of the person's switches: one row above the
  field, "Also on", a chip per switch that is on (**⏱ Lectern**, **👥 Everyone On stage**, "👥 On stage" on a phone),
  each an `aria-pressed` toggle, ✓ and filled when on, off after every send; under it, with ⏱ chosen,
  "Replaces Lectern's countdown line." and the count, "41 / 160". The feed always gets the message (§17.6).
- No 📎, no question tab, no ✨, no To:.

**The on-screen keyboard:** the viewport meta adds `interactive-widget=resizes-content`, so Chrome on Android shrinks
the layout for the keyboard. iPadOS ignores it and keeps `100dvh`, so there the page sizes `.bv` to
`visualViewport.height` on its `resize` event, and the replying line and Send stay above the keyboard. `interactive-widget` is Chrome on
Android's from 108 and Samsung Internet's from 21, and no other browser's (MDN's
`html.elements.meta.name.viewport.interactive-widget`), so on every iPad and iPhone row the `visualViewport` rule
(Safari 13) does the work. The walk checks it on every row (§17.7).

**Help:** the button and the dialog are unit E's. While this person's request is open, the button is its status chip (■
Help asked → ▶ Ana is on the way → ✓ Resolved). A tap on the chip opens an in-place ask (`AGM.ask`, no menu, so R7
holds):

- **It's sorted** (`help:respond resolved`, own request);
- **Cancel request** (`delete`, own);
- **Keep it open**.

**The ⋯ sheet** (kind `sheet`, 56 px rows; a bottom sheet on a phone; never taller than the viewport and scrolled
within it, so a phone held sideways reaches Leave, §17.7):

- **Text size**: Aa− · 100% · Aa+ (the zoom of `app.js:67-81`, kept per device in `agm.zoom` and mirrored to the
  person's other open pages and the support view by `userState 'zoom'`). It scales the whole chat: the body, names,
  times, the cue words, the answers and the strip. The header and the sheet stay fixed;
- **Clock or countdown**: Time of day · Countdown · Off, Time of day until someone chooses (owner answer B3), or, while
  locked, the admin's choice as text (§17.3);
- **Theme**: Light · Dark, **Dark until the person chooses** (owner answer B6).
  - The choice stays the browser's `agm.theme`, as on every page. The simple view reads an unset `agm.theme` as dark;
    every other page still reads it as light.
  - `theme-init.js` paints before the page knows its view, so the hall page keeps `agm.lastView` (in `try`): a device
    last used in the simple view paints dark before its first frame. `theme-init.js` runs on all five pages, so it reads
    `agm.lastView` only on the hall page, which says so in its markup (`<html data-page="app">` in `app.html`, an
    attribute, not a script). The join page, the halls board, the Accounts page and the admin page read an unset
    `agm.theme` as light, whatever `agm.lastView` holds. On a device's very first join, the page turns dark on the join
    answer, before the feed is drawn.
  - Choosing Light writes `agm.theme`, so it sticks on that device. The support view mirrors the person's theme as
    today, but never sets it: a `theme` relayed from the support view carries `support: true` (§0.2, the
    `userState:push` relay), and the simple view neither writes nor applies it. So only the person, on this device or
    another of their own pages, turns a Board page Light;
- **⛶ Full screen**, only where the device has the Fullscreen API (a probe at load; an iPhone has none, §17.7);
- **the wake lock's words**, a row of their own only while the screen cannot be kept awake (`AGM.awake()`, unit M), by
  cause: "This device may sleep: open AGMessage over HTTPS.", "This device may sleep: set its screen to stay on in its
  own settings (Auto-Lock or Screen timeout)." or "This device would not stay awake (its battery may be low): plug it
  in." (the architecture addendum's §15.10 words);
- **Leave the hall**, which asks in place, 8 px below the row above: "**Leave Hall 2?** You'll stop getting messages
  from backstage." with **Leave** and **Stay**. Leave is not red: red is kept for 🔥, open help and faults;
- the footer: "Margaret Lowe · On stage".

**Sizes**, and why. The figures are character height at the eye, assuming a cap height of 0.7 em (SF Pro, Roboto and
Inter are 0.70-0.73). An 11-inch iPad Air draws 1180 CSS px across 2360 device px at 264 ppi, so 1 CSS px is 0.192 mm.
The commonly used floor is 16′ of arc and the comfortable size about 20′ (Activu, "Optimal Font Size",
https://activu.com/uploads/Optimal-Font-Size.pdf), a secondary source; ANSI/HFES 100-2007, to which the figures are
usually attributed, was not read. A tablet on a board table or a lectern sits 55 to 70 cm from the eye.

| Thing | Size | 50 cm | 55 cm | 60 cm | 70 cm | §15.5 had |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Message text, tablet (the smaller side 600 px or more) | 22 px | 20.3′ | 18.5′ | 16.9′ | 14.5′ (Aa+ ×1.2: 17.4′) | 20 px |
| Message text, phone at 35 cm | 20 px | — | — | — | — (22.8′ at 35 cm) | 20 px |
| A question's text | the body size, weight 600 | as above | | | | 24 px |
| 🔥 Priority, Question, the readout | 18 px | 16.6′ | 15.1′ | 13.9′ | 11.9′ | — / 24 px |
| Names, actions, Stagewatch's line | 16 px | 14.8′ | 13.4′ | 12.3′ | 10.6′ | — |
| Times, status words | 14 px, muted | 12.9′ | 11.8′ | 10.8′ | 9.2′ (read on demand) | — |
| The hall's name | 16 px, weight 500, muted | — | | | | `--fs-md` |
| A question's answers | 48 px tall, 18 px text | — | | | | 56 px |
| Got it, Reply, Answer in words | 36 px drawn, 44 px to the finger | — | | | | — |
| Every other control | 44 px or more | — | | | | 44 / 56 px |

- **16 px body text would be 14.8′ at 50 cm, under the floor**, so the owner's "not huge" is met by taking chrome away,
  not by shrinking the words.
- 22 px on a tablet holds about 60 characters a line in the 46 rem column. A tablet at 70 cm still needs Aa+, and
  reading 9 records the real distance.
- The readout at 18 px is 15.1′ at 55 cm: it is read on demand, and it is the secondary object by the owner's words.
- No measurement this round on a Board member's device or under stage light: reading 9 (the glance test) checks these
  numbers there, in both themes.
- The table is an 11-inch iPad's (264 ppi at a pixel ratio of 2). An iPad mini's CSS pixel is 0.156 mm and an
  iPhone's 0.166 mm, so the same 22 px is 15.0′ at 55 cm on an iPad mini, under the floor. §17.7 gives each family its
  figures (answer 22).

### 7-§17.3 The clock or countdown, set on the device and by the admin

**What it draws** (only in the simple view, the chat view the owner's ask and B3 are about; an On stage seat gets it
unless the admin sets its Chat view to Full, and the full view keeps its own stage chip, arch-ux unit 31):

| Choice | Drawn | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| **Off** | nothing: the header holds the name, Help and ⋯ | chosen on the device or by the admin |
| **Time of day** | 🕐 14:12, a `<time>` | **the default** (owner answer B3: "Clock on by default"), for every On stage seat in the chat view, in a hall with Stagewatch linked too. AGMessage's clock and zone (the join answer's `now`, `tz`, design §3.3), formatted as `display.js:202-217` does, hours and minutes only. It changes on the minute. A browser that does not know the zone shows its own, as `/d/` does |
| **Countdown** | line 1: ⏱ **4:30 left**; line 2: the title and Stagewatch's line, "Q&A · Wrap up in 2 minutes" | The hall's `stage` payload (`stagePayload`, `server.js:1925-1930`), drawn by `/d/`'s rule (`display.js:165-180`): live only while connected or viewing, not stale, and with the socket up. Otherwise `--:--` with "Stagewatch offline", never a confident stale time. Stagewatch's "next" is not drawn (`/d/` and the take draw it) |
| Countdown, with no Stagewatch linked | `--:--` No Stagewatch linked | the device may still choose it; the sheet says "This hall has no Stagewatch linked." under the choice |

**The countdown's words** follow Stagewatch's own phase (`stageView`'s `phase` and `mode`, `lib/nodes.js:250`;
Stagewatch's `TimerPhase` is normal, warning, wrapup or overtime):

- mode `countdown`, phase `normal`: ⏱ **4:30 left**;
- `warning`: ▲ **0:45 left**; `wrapup`: ▲ **Wrap up · 0:45 left**;
- `overtime`: ▲ **0:30 over**. Stagewatch's text is "-0:30" there (`TimerTick.FormatSeconds`); the sign is dropped,
  because "over" says it;
- any other mode: Stagewatch's text alone, with no word;
- the digits are Stagewatch's text as it sends it (`stageView.text`, its speaker format included).
- **Stagewatch's colour** is the readout's 3 px left edge (on a phone, its digits' edge), never the digits' ink: its
  green on white is 3.3:1, under 4.5:1 for text. When the colour is #FFFFFF (`stageView`'s default) or absent, the edge
  is `--border`.
- A confidential line follows the stage addendum §5.14: "🔒 a confidential line" only where it is in use, and nothing
  elsewhere.

**Where:**

- wider than 600 px (a tablet, or a phone held sideways), in the header after the hall's name, before Help; two lines,
  so the header is 71 px with a line and 64 px without;
- at 600 px wide or less, the digits on row 1; row 2, the title and the line, only while Stagewatch has a line;
- never above the feed, never on a fill of its own, never larger than the body text;
- in the take layer's bar, the same readout as set, or none (amends the stage addendum §5.9.11, simple view only).

**The setting:**

- **The value:** `clock: {show: 'off' | 'time' | 'stage' | null, locked: boolean}`.
  - `show: null` means "not set by the admin". `locked` with `show: null` is refused: "Choose one to lock it.".
  - **`cleanClock(c)`** is pure and fails closed, in a new pure module **`lib/views.js`** (fence (a)'s set gains it). It
    is required by `lib/pages.js` and `lib/accounts.js` (stores may require the pure core, never another store) and by
    `lib/handlers/takes.js`. An unknown `show` is refused with "Choose Off, Time of day or Countdown.", and a field of
    the wrong type with the same words. `{toString: 1}` answers 400, never 500.
- **Where it is kept:**

| Who | The admin's choice | The device's choice |
|---|---|---|
| A code guest | `pages.json` `views['u:<uid>'] = {view?, clock?, at}`: the design's record (§1.10), its lane `pages`, its bound (5,000, oldest first) | `localStorage['agm.clock']`, read and written in `try` (arch-ux §7.5's storage rule) |
| An account | `accounts.json` `clock`, beside `view` (lane `accounts`; `lib/accounts.js` `update` takes it and `view()` appends it; `create` neither picks nor stores it, so a new account starts at "their choice", the clock) | `localStorage['agm.clock']` on that device |

- **Which wins** (one pure function, `AGM.clockFor({admin, device})` in `public/catalog.js`, loaded by
  `test/catalog.test.js` with `vm`):
  1. `admin.locked` → `admin.show` (the device's choice is kept, not offered);
  2. else the device's choice, when it has one;
  3. else `admin.show`, when set;
  4. else **Time of day** (owner answer B3).
  - The server never computes it: it cannot read a device's storage. It sends the admin's choice whatever the device
    stored, and the page draws `clockFor`.
- **The device's choice** is made only in the sheet. It is written to `localStorage` and drawn at once (mode `local`).
  - It is never relayed to the person's other devices (the owner's "local").
  - It is relayed to the admin's support view only, as `userState:push {clock}`: unit 2's key allow-list gains `clock`,
    one of three strings, relayed to `adminView` sockets and to nobody else.
- **Locked:** the sheet shows the admin's choice as text, "**Clock or countdown:** Countdown", with "Set by the admin
  for you." under it. No control is drawn, so nothing looks choosable that is not.
  - A lock set while the sheet is open redraws that row in place, with the sheet's ids and order unchanged (R5).
  - Unlocking redraws the three choices with the device's choice checked, live.
- **On the wire:**
  - `join`'s answer appends **`clock: {show, locked}`** at the end (`{show: null, locked: false}` when unset).
  - **`admin:setClock {roomCode, socketId, show, locked}`** lives in `lib/handlers/takes.js` beside `admin:setView`,
    behind `conn.gate(ack, {joined: false, bucket: writes, admin: true})`, as `admin:setView` is. Two more checks,
    before anything is written:
    - a change of `locked` needs **the admin** (§17.6, "Who sets it": the host token or an admin-role account, never an
      `isAdmin` account of another role): otherwise "Only an admin may lock the clock or countdown.";
    - for an account target, when the actor is an account, `rbac.mayChange(actor, target, {clock})` decides as the
      PATCH does, so the socket never reaches an account the Accounts page would refuse (an account by an actor
      without `users.manage`: "You may not manage accounts."; an admin-role account by a manager who holds it: "Only
      an admin may make or change an admin.").

    It resolves the person as `admin:setView` does (design §6):
    - a guest: `pages.setClock(uid, clock | null)`, then a `person.clock` row;
    - an account: `accounts.update(id, {clock})`, then a `user.update` row.
    - It then sends **`clock {show, locked}`** through `takesCtx.sendTo` to every socket of that person in the hall and
      to their support view (`viewOf`, design §5.5). It then calls `ctx.usersChanged(roomCode)`, a named effect the
      server context gains (it runs `emitUsers`, `server.js:253-259`), so the admin's people rows redraw (below).
  - **`PATCH /api/users/:id {clock}`** goes through `rbac.mayChange`:
    - its self-change list adds `'clock' in change`: nobody sets their own (the refusal words stay;
      `test/accounts.test.js` pins them);
    - a change of `locked` needs an admin (role `admin`): otherwise "Only an admin may lock the clock or countdown.".
      A `users.manage` holder may set the choice, as with `view`;
    - `accountChanged(id, 'clock')` sends `clock` live, as design §6 does for `view`, and ends no socket. A change that
      is only `clock` and `view` never reloads.
  - Nobody else is told. The page re-runs `clockFor` with no reload.
- **The admin's three doors, in the same words:**
  - **Clock or countdown:** Their choice (the clock at first) · Time of day · Stagewatch countdown · Off;
  - **☐ Lock it on their devices**, disabled with "Choose one to lock it." while the choice is "Their choice";
  - beside a person whose Chat view is Full: "Applies in the simple view.".
  - Where:
    - **the Accounts page** (`users.html`, design §7.3): once per account, beside **Chat view**, which is an account
      field too; never in a hall's row, since the value is the account's, not the hall's;
    - **the admin page's people rows** (design §7.4): beside **Seat** and **Chat view**;
    - **the hall page's People panel**, the admin only: the person's ⋯ → **Clock or countdown ▸** and **Lock it on
      their devices**.
  - **Their data:** `roomUserSummary(r, {links: true})` (`server.js:241-248`), the admin's list only, appends `view` and
    `clock` (the admin's choice, `{show, locked}`) to each row. The Accounts list carries `clock` through `view()`. R8's
    support-view facts gain `clock` (the device's choice, as relayed).
- **The audit** (design §2.7):

| Action | When | Target | Words |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person.clock` | a guest's setting changed by the admin | hall | `Rita (guest) → clock: countdown, locked` / `… → clock: time of day` / `… unlocked` / `… → clock: their choice` |
| `user.update` | an account's setting changed | username | `clock → time of day (locked)` / `clock → their choice` |

  - Every lock and unlock is a row (the owner). The device's own choice is not audited: it is a person's act on their
    own page (design §2.7's rule).
- **`test/inputs.test.js`:**
  - `NULLS` adds `show` and `locked`; `UNCONVERTIBLE` adds `show: U`;
  - the typed cases add `[ctl, 'admin:setClock', {roomCode: U, socketId: U, show: U, locked: U}]`.
