### 7-§17.5 Pins: for the room or for me (owner answer B1; the owner's pin rule, 2026-10-27)

> "A pin can be for the room (default) (including On stage - essential for action prompts), or personal."

Confirmed the same day: "A board member cannot pin for the room, only themselves. So pinning for everyone is for
backroom teams, not the board or presenters on stage." With B1 ("they can can pin messages for themselves"), every pin
is one of two kinds, offered at one door:

| | **For the room** (the default) | **For me** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | today's pin (`server.js:864-871`): the message's `pinned`, a room op (`upd`, broadcast as `pinUpdate`, `:220`), in the room's record | a message id kept for one person in one room; not a room op, and it never changes the message |
| Who sees it | everyone in the room: backstage, observers, Viewer accounts and every On stage seat, whose pinned bar (in the full view, the pinned strip) draws it first | that person alone, on each of their pages in that room, and in their support view |
| Who pins and unpins | a seat that may post and is not On stage: backstage, a side-room Member, the admin off stage | every seat that may view the room: backstage, observers, Viewer accounts, On stage seats, the admin |
| Refused | On stage, first, the admin On stage included: "Pinning for everyone is for the backstage team."; an observer or a Viewer account by today's `mayPost`: "Observers can read but not post." | from the admin's support view: "Pins are the person's own." |
| Verb and mode | `pin {messageId, pinned}`, mode `now`: it changes what everyone sees | `pin:mine {messageId, on}`, mode `hold`: it sets the person's own state, so a replay is harmless |
| Transcript, minutes | as today: the transcript marks it "📌 pinned" (`server.js:1864`) | never; nor the context, the hello, the halls board or the AI's brief |
| Audited | no, as today: a room op, kept in the room's record | no: a person's act on their own page (design §2.7's rule) |

- **An observer and a Viewer account pin for themselves only.** They cannot post (`hall.post`), and a room pin changes
  what everyone in the room sees, as a post does. So the room's door is absent for them (by `may`) and the server keeps
  today's refusal. A pin for oneself changes nothing anyone else reads, so a seat in the room is all it needs.
- **An On stage seat pins for itself only**, by the owner's confirmation: Board members and presenters alike, since a
  presenter sits On stage in the same `board` seat. The admin seated On stage is refused the room's pin too: one seat
  gives one answer (§17.1).
- The admin's minutes (`admin:postSummary`) are posted pinned (`server.js:1559`), so they are a room pin and reach the
  Board's pinned bar like any other.

**The room's `pin`** (`server.js:864-871`) checks, in this order: `need`; one `writes` token; **`onStage()`**: "Pinning
for everyone is for the backstage team."; then today's `mayPost`; the message in `room.byId` ("Message not found").
Its op, `pinUpdate` and the message's `pinned` are unchanged. Its `{ok: true}` ack is now read by the page (arch-ux R4:
📌 emits with no answer handler today, `app.js:566`).

**For me, `pin:mine {messageId, on}`:**

- **Whose:** the person's key, as design §5.2 names them: `a:<accountId>` for an account, so every device of the
  account shows it; `u:<uid>` for a guest, whose uid is that browser's.
- **Where it is kept:** `pages.json` `pins: {<personKey>: {<room key>: [id…]}}`, through the `pages` lane (design
  §1.10).
  - At most 50 per person per room; a 51st is refused: "50 pins in this room at most: unpin one first."
  - Person records count in the views' bound (5,000, the oldest first).
  - A room removed or reset drops its entries, with design §1.6's sweep.
  - An id whose message has gone (deleted, or out of the room's ring) is ignored by the page and dropped at the
    person's next pin write.
  - **The store and its bounds are unchanged.** Revision 4 already accepted `pin:mine` from any seated socket, so both
    bounds were set for every seat. Drawing the door for every seat adds people who pin, not a way past either bound.
- **The checks:** `need`; not the admin's support view (`socket.data.adminView`), which joins with the admin browser's
  own `uid` (`app.js:99`, `server.js:762`), so a pin made there would land under the admin's key, not the person's:
  "Pins are the person's own."; one `writes` token; `allowed('hall.view')` (it changes nothing anyone else reads); the
  message in `room.byId` ("Message not found"); and `on` a boolean ("Say pin or unpin.").
- Idempotent: `on: true` twice keeps one entry. Mode `hold` (unit Q).
- The server then sends `pins {ids}` to every socket of that person seated in that room, and to their support view
  (`viewOf`), and acks `{ok: true, ids}`. An account's tablet and phone redraw together.
- **Every seat has the door** now. Revision 4 drew it On stage only and left the other seats for later; the owner's
  rule opens it.

**The doors, in step** (§17.1's catalogue and "The pin doors by seat"; arch-ux §16 as §0.2 amends it). The menu, the
buttons, the key and touch read the same entries:

- **A seat that may pin both ways** (backstage, a side-room Member, the admin off stage): **📌 Pin ▸ For the room · For
  me** in the message menu (⋯, right-click, Shift+F10) and on the Preview's 📌 button. **For the room** comes first and
  takes the focus when the menu opens: it is the default, so P then Enter, or a tap on the first item, pins for the
  room. The two items are `menuitemcheckbox`, checked where the message is pinned that way. The item reads **📌 Unpin ▸**
  while the message is pinned both ways. Touch: ⋯ → 📌 Pin ▸ drills in, with "‹ Back".
- **A seat that pins for itself only** (an observer, a Viewer account, an On stage seat in the full view): one flat
  item, **📌 Pin for me** / **📌 Unpin for me**, in the same places; P acts at once.
- **The simple view** (R7, no menu): a tapped message's row draws **📌 Pin for me** / **📌 Unpin for me** (the second
  door, §17.2), whatever the seat; a question pinned for the person, which is not in the feed, has **📌 Unpin for me**
  in the pinned bar instead (§17.2). Its hide list keeps the room's pin (design §6), so a backstage seat the admin set to
  Simple pins for itself there, and for the room once the admin's Chat view gives it the full view again (nobody sets
  their own view, design §6).
- **Undo** for 10 s, by kind (arch-ux §16.6): "Pinned for the room. · Undo", "Pinned for you. · Undo", "Unpinned for
  the room. · Undo", "Unpinned for you. · Undo". A refusal shows the server's words in the toast and changes nothing.
- **Offline:** For the room (`now`) is disabled with "Not connected — AGMessage is reconnecting."; For me (`hold`)
  stays live and shows ◷ until the server answers (R2).
- **An open menu keeps its ids and order** while a `pinUpdate` or `pins` event arrives; only the checks update (R5).

**The pinned place, on every page.** Every page draws the room's pins and the person's own, as the Board's bar does:

- **The simple view: the pinned bar** (§17.2). The room's pins come first (the newest message first), then the person's
  own (the newest pin first), with "1 of 2" when there are several. A tap on a message's line scrolls the feed to the
  message and outlines it for 2 s (no motion under reduced motion); the next tap goes to the next pin. A pinned
  question is drawn whole in the bar, with its answers, and a tap on its line shows the next pin (below, §17.2).
- **The full view: the pinned strip** (`#pinnedList`, read by arch-ux's delegated handler) **and the panel's pinned
  files** (`#docPinnedList`) hold both kinds, in the same order. Each entry's line says "📌 For everyone", "📌 For you"
  or "📌 For everyone · for you", and its ✕ follows §17.1's `file` entries: by kind, and none where this seat may not
  unpin. A question pinned either way is drawn once on that page, in the strip, where it is answered (below).
- **A pinned question, in every view** (the owner, 2026-10-27: "A pinned question becomes hidden in the scrolling
  chat, and becomes visible in scrolling chat when unpinned."):
  - A question pinned in a way this person sees, for the room or for them, is drawn only in their pinned place: the
    Board's pinned bar, or the full view's pinned strip (today's clone, answers included: `refreshPinned`,
    `app.js:791`). That is where its answers are.
  - It is hidden from their feed while it stays pinned, and returns to its place in the feed when unpinned, by its seq
    and with its answers: it was hidden, never moved. ↓ n new does not count it, and the roving feed (unit 3c) skips
    it.
  - Per viewer: a question pinned for the room leaves every reader's feed; one pinned for a person leaves only that
    person's (their pages in that room, and their support view, which draws what their page draws).
  - **One rule:** `styles.css:360` (`.feed .msg[data-type="action"][data-pinned="1"]`) hides a room-pinned question in
    every page's feed in 0.5.1, the Board's included. Unit 20c keeps it in every view, the simple view included, and
    makes it read both kinds: the page marks a question `data-pinned` from the room's `pinned` and `data-pinned-mine`
    from the person's `pins`, and the rule hides either.
  - This replaces revision 5's reading, which kept the question in the simple view's feed and drew its answers in the
    bar only while it was out of view.
- **On the message, on every page:** "📌 Pinned for everyone" or "📌 Pinned for you" ("📌 Pinned for everyone · for
  you" for both) at the end of the author's line, muted.
- **A message pinned both ways** is one entry. Unpinning it for me leaves the room's pin, and unpinning it for the room
  leaves the person's.
- **Why the room's come first** (confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-27: "Yes"): they are what the backstage team needs
  everyone to see ("essential for action prompts"), and the page knows which messages the room has pinned but not
  when. The person's own keep the order they were pinned in (`pins`).
- The history's `pinned` (the room's) and the join answer's `pins` (the person's) draw the place at once; `pinUpdate`
  and `pins` keep it in step.
- **Never cleared by Got it** (§17.6): a message pinned for the room or for the person. The bar and the strip go to it,
  and a pin says "keep this". The owner confirmed it for both kinds (2026-10-27: "Correct", §12). Revision 4 kept the
  person's pins whole, and revision 5 added the room's.
- **The support view** draws the person's pins, both kinds (R8's `pins`), and the person's pin doors, disabled by R8
  and emitting nothing. `pin:mine` sent from it is refused all the same.

**The words** (sentence case; they join §15.7's copy deck in unit 20c): 📌 Pin ▸ · 📌 Unpin ▸ · For the room · For me ·
📌 Pin for me · 📌 Unpin for me · Pin for the room · Unpin for the room · 📌 For everyone · 📌 For you · 📌 For everyone ·
for you · 📌 Pinned for everyone · 📌 Pinned for you · Pinned for the room. · Pinned for you. · Unpinned for the room. ·
Unpinned for you. · Undo. The refusals: Pinning for everyone is for the backstage team. · Observers can read but not
post. (today's) · Pins are the person's own. · Message not found · Say pin or unpin. · 50 pins in this room at most:
unpin one first.

**`test/inputs.test.js`:** the typed case `['pin:mine', {messageId: U, on: U}]` from a seated guest; `NULLS` adds `on`.
`pin`'s case is today's.

### 7-§17.6 The admin's On stage settings: where a Board member's messages go (B2), and what Got it does (B4)

**The rule (B2):** what an On stage seat writes is a message in the room's feed, read by everyone in that room (the
backstage team, observers, the other Board members), "as support". By default it goes nowhere else: no other room
(`forward`, `room:send` and Send back are refused On stage, §17.1), no screen, no speaker's screen, no person's page,
whatever the account's role (the seat limit, §17.1). The admin may allow two more destinations for a person, each its
own switch, off by default. Neither is another room: the room-level allow-list and `admin:linkRoom` are not the
per-person choice B2 gives the admin.

**The setting:** `onStage: {screens: boolean, people: boolean, clears: boolean}`, each `false` when unset.

| Switch | What it allows | The admin's words under it |
|---|---|---|
| `screens`: **May send to a countdown screen** | a message of theirs can also go to the line under the countdown on a `/d/` screen of their hall that shows the countdown now | "Their messages can go to the line under the countdown on this hall's screens." |
| `people`: **May send to people On stage** | a message of theirs can also be shown on the pages of everyone seated On stage in the hall, as a card in their Shown to you, beside their chat and never over it | "Their messages can be shown on the pages of everyone On stage, beside their chat." |
| `clears`: **Got it clears the message** (B4) | their Got it also takes the message off their own feed | "Off: the message stays in their feed, marked got." |

- **Kept** beside `clock`: a guest's in `pages.json` `views['u:<uid>'].onStage`, an account's in `accounts.json`
  `onStage` (`update` takes it and `view()` appends it). `create` neither picks nor stores it: `POST /api/users`
  (`lib/http-accounts.js:213-221`) picks only role, grant, revoke, halls and allHalls, and a `clock` or `onStage` in its
  body is ignored, so a new account starts with every switch off, whoever creates it.
- **Cleaned** by **`cleanOnStage(o)`** in `lib/views.js`, pure and failing closed. It takes an object whose keys are
  only `screens`, `people` and `clears`, each a boolean; anything else is refused with "Choose on or off." (an unknown
  key, a string, `{toString: 1}`: 400, never 500). A change names only the keys it changes.
- **Who sets it:** the admin only, as the owner said ("An admin can choose"). **The admin** is one predicate on every
  path: the host token, or an account whose role is `admin`, through the tunnel only as `isAdmin` allows it.
  - On a socket: `theAdmin = () => !!socket.data.adminSid || (!!socket.data.account && socket.data.account.role ===
    'admin' && socket.data.isAdmin)`. `isAdmin` alone (`server.js:688`) is not it: it holds for any account granted
    `settings.manage`, which an admin may hand to a manager. The last term keeps `isAdmin`'s tunnel rule
    (`web.adminBlocked`).
  - Over HTTP: `req.agm.account.role === 'admin'`, behind `signedIn('users.manage')`, which already refuses an
    admin-only holder through the tunnel (`lib/http-accounts.js:83`).
  - The same predicate gates the lock in `admin:setClock` (§17.3).
  - Every act the owner gave "the admin" reads this one predicate. Its socket form is built first for the stage
    addendum's `admin:guestWeb` (its unit 19, amended), and its HTTP form, `theAdminReq(req)`, for the audit
    addendum's split (unit H3, its H.10.2), which the install addendum's Archive this event… (U15) uses too.
  - **`admin:setOnStage {roomCode, socketId, screens?, people?, clears?}`** lives in `lib/handlers/takes.js` beside
    `admin:setClock`, behind `conn.gate(ack, {joined: false, bucket: writes, admin: true})` and then `theAdmin()`:
    otherwise "Only an admin may choose what an On stage seat may do.". For an account target, when the actor is an
    account, `rbac.mayChange(actor, target, {onStage})` runs too, as the PATCH does. It resolves the person as
    `admin:setView` does: a guest through `pages.setOnStage(uid, …)`, an account through `accounts.update(id,
    {onStage})`. It then sends **`onStage {screens, people, clears, countdownScreens?}`** to every page of that person
    in the hall and to their support view, and calls `ctx.usersChanged(roomCode)`.
  - **`PATCH /api/users/:id {onStage}`** goes through `rbac.mayChange`. Its self-change list adds `'onStage' in
    change`. A `users.manage` holder who is not an admin is refused: "Only an admin may choose what an On stage seat
    may do." `accountChanged(id, 'onStage')` sends it live and ends no socket, as `clock` does.
  - The join answer appends `onStage` after `clock` and `pins` (§0.1).
  - **`countdownScreens`** (names only, never a link, a token or an id) is sent only while `screens` is on: the names of
    the hall's screens showing the countdown now. `displaysChanged(hall)` sends `onStage` again to those pages when the
    list changes.
- **The audit** (design §2.7): `person.onStage` for a guest ("Rita (guest) → may send to a countdown screen: on" / "…
  may send to people On stage: off" / "… Got it clears: on"); `user.update` for an account ("onStage → countdown
  screens on, people On stage off, Got it clears off"). Each change is one row, holding no code and no text.
- **The admin's three doors**, in the same words, each a checkbox:
  - the Accounts page (`users.html`, design §7.3): once per account, beside **Chat view** (the switches are the
    account's, one value whatever the hall), enabled while any hall's **On stage (Board member)** box is ticked and
    disabled with "Applies On stage." otherwise;
  - the admin page's people rows (design §7.4), for a person seated On stage;
  - the hall page's People panel, the admin only: the person's ⋯ → three `menuitemcheckbox` entries.
  - Each door is drawn for the admin by the predicate above. An `isAdmin` page whose account's role is not `admin`
    (its join answer's `account.role`, `/api/halls`' `account` on the admin and Accounts pages) draws them disabled
    with "Only an admin may choose what an On stage seat may do."
  - `roomUserSummary(r, {links: true})`, the admin's list only, appends `onStage` beside `view` and `clock`.

**On the wire:** `message {type: 'text', text, priority?, replyTo?, also: {screens?: true, people?: true}}`.

- `also` is read by type: an object with at least one key, only `screens` and `people`, each `true`. Anything else,
  `{}` included, is refused: "Choose where else it goes: a countdown screen or people On stage."
- **The checks, in this order, all before anything is written**, so a refusal posts nothing and the composer keeps the
  text:
  1. the socket is On stage (`onStage()`); otherwise "Only On stage seats send this way: use ⧉ Show on screens or 📺
     Show the Board.";
  2. the type is `text` (a file and a question are refused before this, §17.1): otherwise "Only a message goes there,
     not a help request.";
  3. per destination, the person's switch as the server holds it now, never the page's word and never a copy taken at
     join: read at each send from the store, `accounts.get(socket.data.accountId).onStage` for an account and
     `pages.views['u:' + me.uid].onStage` for a guest. A switch turned off while the page is open refuses the next send,
     with no reload: "The admin has not let you send to countdown screens." / "The admin has not let you send to people
     On stage.";
  4. screens: the hall's screens whose content is `countdown` now. None: "No screen in this hall shows the countdown
     now." Over 160 characters: "A countdown screen's line holds 160 characters (this is 212)." (`cleanContent`
     keeps 160, `lib/displays.js:55`, and the server never cuts);
  5. people: at least one other page seated On stage in the hall's Main room. Otherwise "Nobody else is On stage
     now.";
  6. one `writes` token per destination, beside the message's own.
- **Then:**
  - the message is added to the feed with `also: {screens: [{name, seq, state}], people: {seq, shown, of, state}}`,
    so the room's record says where it went and every reader sees it. It carries names, never a screen's id, link or
    token: the ids stay on the server, beside the message's id, in the live entries below;
  - **screens:** for each, `displays.take(d.id, {kind: 'countdown', text, tone: priority ? 'urgent' : 'info'}, name)`,
    so the countdown and the hall's timer stay and only the line under them changes. Its `display.take` row names the
    person and the length, never the text ("Lectern → the countdown with a line from Margaret Lowe, On stage (38
    characters)"). Then `displaysChanged(hall)`;
  - **people:** a Board information take, `{kind: 'snippet', unit: 'text', text}`, with `by: {name, onStage: true, op:
    false}`, that **always arrives `side`** (the stage addendum's §5.9.1: "supersedes nothing"). B2 lets a Board
    member's message "appear on the pages of the others"; it does not give it a Board take's power to replace. So it
    is not sent through `page:push`'s step 4 (supersede):
    - it never takes the Board's information slot (`board.info`), never deletes a person's information take or its
      answer, and never covers a chat. A researcher's quote, or the operator's web page, over a Board member's chat
      stays drawn, with its answers;
    - it is numbered as a take (`page:take` with `arrive: 'side'`), entered in the hall's Earlier list as it is sent,
      so a page that reconnects draws it there, and drawn on every Board page as a card in Shown to you, the sender's
      own included (on a phone, the tab reads "📺 Shown to you · 1");
    - its `page.push` row reads "the Board (5 pages) → a line typed by Margaret Lowe, On stage (41 characters), beside
      their chat", and `pagesChanged` runs.
- **The ack:** `{ok, id, seq, also: {screens: [{name, seq, state}], people: {seq, of}}}`, names only, as on the
  message. Its words say "sending", never "shown".
- **Attempts are not facts.** The message's line says where it went and what the targets confirmed, for every reader
  in the room: "⏱ Lectern: sending", "⏱ On Lectern ✓", "△ Lectern could not show it", "Replaced on Lectern at 14:12";
  "👥 On stage: sending", "👥 Shown to 5 of 6 On stage" (a card confirms `shown` "in the side bar", §5.9.1). The server
  keeps the live entries, with the screens' ids (at most the newest per person and destination). When
  `displaysChanged` or `pagesChanged` runs for the hall, it updates the message's `also` by an `upd` op, coalesced to
  once a second, until every target has confirmed, failed or moved on.
- **Mode `now`** (unit Q): a line meant for a screen or for people's pages is never shown late. Offline, the send is
  refused at once and the text kept.
- **Not Stagewatch's speaker's screen.** A countdown screen is AGMessage's own `/d/` page. `stage:send` and
  `stage:propose` stay refused for every On stage seat (§17.1).

**Got it clears (B4):**

- **Off (the default):** Got it is `react {👍, on: true}` (`msg.ack`). The backstage page reads "👍 Margaret got it",
  and the person's feed keeps the message with "👍 You: got it".
- **On:** the same act and the same report to backstage. Then the person's own pages draw the message as one muted
  44 px line in its place, "👍 Got and cleared: Ana Ribeiro 14:02 · **Show**", with 🔥 before the name for a priority
  message, "👍 Got and cleared: 🔥 Tom Okafor 14:06 · **Show**" (a run of them is one line, "👍 Got and cleared: 3
  messages · Show"). Show draws them again, marked "👍 You: got it", until the page reloads; **Hide** folds them back.
  - The page derives it from facts it already has: its person's 👍 in the message's `reactions`, and
    `onStage.clears`. There is no new verb, and an account's devices clear together, since the reaction is the
    account's.
  - A 🔥 message got and cleared leaves the strip too. Got all N clears each of the N.
  - **Never cleared:** a message pinned for the room or for the person (§17.5; confirmed by the owner, 2026-10-27,
    §12), a question (it is answered, not got), one's own message, and anything on anyone else's page. The room's
    record, the backstage page, the transcript and the minutes keep every message.

### 7-§17.7 The Board's devices: the chat view on every row (owner answer 22)

The owner: "Board will use a mixture of devices". The reading (`DECISIONS.md`): iPads on current and older
iPadOS, Android tablets, and phones (iOS and Android); every Board feature works on each, with a test matrix and
fallbacks (Wake Lock, long press, the legacy pdf.js build, `<dialog>` and CSS support), and nothing is tuned to one
device.

**One matrix, one floor, one walk.**

- The stage addendum's §5.15 holds the matrix (D1-D7 and CI), the document floor, the smoke's device and floor legs,
  and the walk in `docs/DEVICES.md`. The architecture addendum's §15.10 (unit M) holds the page floor (Safari 14.1, iOS
  and iPadOS 14.5, Chrome 84), `AGM.awake()`, `AGM.openDialog()`, `AGM.idle()` and the CSS fences.
- Both leave the chat view's rows to this addendum: "The Board's chat view (the wake lock, a long press, `<dialog>`)
  is the board addendum's; its rows join the same matrix and the same walk" (stage §5.15). This section is those rows.
  It makes no second matrix, floor or walk.
- Every browser version below is MDN's compatibility data (`@mdn/browser-compat-data` 8.1.7,
  https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data), named by its path there. No user agent is read: each rule follows the
  viewport's size or a probe, so a device nobody listed draws by what it is.

**What revision 6 had fitted to two devices.** Its layout rules were set on its two shot sizes, 1180×820 and 390×844.
At the matrix's sizes (§17.4) they failed three times:

- **Upright tablets** (640 to 834 px wide) kept the 360 px column, so the chat was 280 to 474 px wide and the field had
  0 to 171 px for its 221 px placeholder. On a Galaxy Tab S9's 640 px, the field itself was 34 px wide. Their text was
  20 px, since the 22 px rule read "900 px wide or more".
- **Phones held sideways** (734×343, 863×360) drew the tablet's column, and the ⋯ sheet's last rows sat below the screen
  with no way to scroll to them, Leave among them.
- **At 375 and 360 px wide** (an iPhone SE, a Galaxy S24), "Message everyone here…" was cut: revision 4's iteration 12
  had fitted it at 390 px only.

**The rules, by size** (§17.2; the mock's revision 5 holds each, §17.4):

| Rule | Where it applies | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The side column, Shown to you at 360 px | 900 px wide or more | it needs a chat of 540 px or more beside it |
| The two tabs, Chat and 📺 Shown to you · 1 | under 900 px wide: every phone, and every tablet upright | an upright tablet keeps its whole width for the chat (640 to 834 px) |
| 22 px text | the viewport's smaller side 600 px or more: a tablet, either way up | a phone held sideways (343 and 360 px tall in the descriptors) keeps 20 px |
| The phone's header (one 57 px row) and composer (🔥 alone, a 16 px field) | 600 px wide or less | as revision 4 measured them at 390 px |
| The 🔥 strip | three lines; two under 700 px tall; one under 500 px | an iPhone in Safari keeps 659 of its 852 px ("iPhone 15"), and the strip's third line was the feed's |
| The ⋯ sheet | never taller than the viewport, and scrolled within it | a phone held sideways reaches Leave |
| The placeholder | "Message everyone here…" where it fits the field, measured on load and on `resize`; "Message everyone…" where not | the field's room varies with the device's font and width; the label keeps the long words |
| An iPad's Split View, Slide Over or Stage Manager window | by the window's size, as any viewport | — |

**Text at the eye, by family.** §17.2's sizes are an 11-inch iPad's. A CSS pixel is 25.4 mm ÷ the screen's pixels per
inch × the device's pixel ratio, so it is not the same size on every row:

| Family | Pixels per inch (the maker) | Pixel ratio (Playwright's descriptors) | 1 CSS px | The body at the eye |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| iPad, iPad Air | 264 (https://www.apple.com/ipad-11/specs/, https://www.apple.com/ipad-air/specs/) | 2 ("iPad (gen 7)", "iPad Pro 11") | 0.192 mm | 22 px: 18.5′ at 55 cm, 14.6′ at 70 cm (§17.2's table) |
| iPad mini | 326 (https://www.apple.com/ipad-mini/specs/) | 2 ("iPad Mini") | 0.156 mm | 22 px: 16.5′ at 50 cm, **15.0′ at 55 cm**, 13.7′ at 60 cm, 11.8′ at 70 cm |
| iPhone | 460 (https://www.apple.com/iphone-17/specs/) | 3 ("iPhone 15") | 0.166 mm | 20 px: 22.8′ at 35 cm, 19.9′ at 40 cm (§17.2's phone figure) |
| Android tablets and phones | the maker's, at the density the device is set to | 2 to 4.5 across the descriptors | measured on the walk | — |

- An iPad mini at a board table's 55 cm is under the 16′ floor. One Aa+ (110 %: a step of 0.1, `app.js:72-81`) gives
  16.5′; at 60 cm two steps, at 70 cm four.
- The page cannot choose this for the person: CSS lengths are anchored to the reference pixel, which the browser maps
  to the screen's pixels by its own ratio, and no web API reports a screen's physical size (CSS Values 4,
  https://www.w3.org/TR/css-values-4/#absolute-lengths). So Text size stays per device (`agm.zoom`), the admin sees it in
  the support view, README.txt names the iPad mini, and the walk records each device's distance and Text size
  (reading 9).

**Each feature of the chat view, on every row** (the fallback is the same on every device):

| Feature | Support (MDN) | Where it differs | The fallback | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kept awake (the Screen Wake Lock) | `api.WakeLock`: Safari 16.4; iOS and iPadOS 16.4 in a Safari tab, and from the Home Screen only from 18.4 ("Does not work in standalone Home Screen Web Apps. See bug 254545."); Chrome 84; Samsung Internet 14.0; "available only in secure contexts (HTTPS)" (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WakeLock/request) | D1 (before iPadOS 16.4) has none. Every row over plain HTTP has none: one port serves HTTP and HTTPS (`server.js:610-612`), and HTTPS needs the certificate trusted once on each device (`/tls`, `server.js:385`) | unit M's `AGM.awake()`, asked at join and again on `visibilitychange`. Where it cannot be held, the sheet draws M's words by cause as a row of its own (`role="status"`), the one row of the sheet that comes and goes: "This device may sleep: open AGMessage over HTTPS." · "This device may sleep: set its screen to stay on in its own settings (Auto-Lock or Screen timeout)." · "This device would not stay awake (its battery may be low): plug it in." | M; 20a |
| ⛶ Full screen (the sheet's row, the take layer's button) | `api.Element.requestFullscreen` and `api.Document.fullscreenEnabled`: on iOS "Only available on iPad, not on iPhone", unprefixed from iPadOS 16.4 and as `webkitRequestFullscreen` from iPadOS 12; Chrome 71; Samsung Internet 10.0 | D6 (an iPhone) has none; D1 has only the prefixed call | a probe at load, `document.fullscreenEnabled === true \|\| document.webkitFullscreenEnabled === true`, is the catalogue's fact `fullscreen`, kept on the page and sent nowhere. The row and the button are drawn only with it, and call the unprefixed method where it exists, else the prefixed one. An iPhone's sheet has no Full screen row, so nothing is offered that would do nothing | 20a |
| A long press | `api.Element.contextmenu_event`: iOS fires none on a long press (`safari_ios` false); Chrome on Android (18) and Samsung Internet (1.0) do | D1-D3 and D6 against D4, D5 and D7 | the simple view needs none: its second door is a tap (§17.2), and its tabs, bar, chips and buttons are taps. AGMessage opens no menu there, on a long press or a right-click (R7), and runs no timer of its own (arch-ux §15.10). On words, the browser's own selection stays (Copy, Speak, Translate). On On stage content (the take layer, a card's thumbnail in Shown to you, a page opened by 👁 Look), the stage addendum's no-save measures hold on every row: `-webkit-touch-callout: none` on iOS (`css.properties.-webkit-touch-callout`, iOS 2), AGMessage's `contextmenu` handler where a long press fires one, and `draggable="false"` (stage §4.6, as §0.3 extends it) | 20a; stage |
| The Help dialog (unit E) | `<dialog>` and `showModal()`: Safari 15.4 (arch-ux §15.10) | D1, where it is older than iPadOS 15.4 | unit M's `AGM.openDialog()`. The ⋯ sheet, Leave's ask and the Help chip's ask are no `<dialog>` (`AGM.ask`) | M; E |
| The on-screen keyboard | `html.elements.meta.name.viewport.interactive-widget`: Chrome on Android 108 and Samsung Internet 21.0 only. `api.VisualViewport` and its `resize`: Safari 13, iOS 13, Chrome 62 | D1-D3 and D6 ignore the meta | §17.2's rule: `.bv` follows `visualViewport.height` on its `resize` wherever the meta has not resized the layout | 20a |
| The page's height | `dvh`: Safari 15.4, Chrome 108 (arch-ux §15.10) | the older rows | `100vh` first, then `100dvh` (fence q), with the `visualViewport` rule above | M; 20a |
| The 🔥 strip's "out of view" | `api.IntersectionObserver`: Safari 12.1, iOS 12.2, Chrome 51 | none above the page floor | without it the strip always shows (§12, Risks) | 20a |
| A notch or a home indicator | `css.types.env`: Safari 11.1, iOS 11.3, Chrome 69; `css.types.max`: Safari 11.1, Chrome 79 | none above the page floor | `viewport-fit=cover`, which `app.html:5` already sets, with the header's and composer's paddings `max(16px, env(safe-area-inset-*))`, as the mock draws them | 20a |
| Moving focus (Reply, Answer in words…, Escape back to the composer) | `api.HTMLElement.focus`'s note on iOS: with no hardware keyboard, `focus()` on an input does nothing until the person has interacted with the page | D1-D3 and D6 | the composer is never focused at load; Reply and Answer in words… move focus inside their own tap's handler | 20a |
| A tapped row's tint, an action's hover | `color-mix()`: Safari 16.2, Chrome 111 (arch-ux §15.10) | D1, D2 | a plain colour first (fence q) | M; 20a |
| Box offsets and logical properties | `css.properties.inset`, `margin-inline`, `padding-inline`, `margin-block`, `padding-block`, `border-block`: Safari 14.1, Chrome 87 | Chrome 84 to 86, inside the page floor | the simple view's CSS writes `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`, `margin-left` and `margin-right`; fence q gains the pairs, and 0.5.1's three `inset: 0` (`styles.css:406`, `:954`, `:1125`) gain their four sides (§0.2) | M; 20a |
| Marks and emoji (🕐 ⏱ ▲ 🔥 📌 👍 📺) | each device's own fonts | — | every mark carries its word (§17.2's marks table), so a glyph a device lacks never takes the meaning away; the walk checks each draws (M's row) | 20a |
| Dark before the first frame (B6) | `localStorage`, read in `try` | a private window, or storage blocked | an unreadable `agm.theme` reads as unset, so the simple view paints dark | 20a |

**The smoke** (Chromium, every push; it adds to stage §5.15.3 and arch-ux §15.10):

- **The device legs** (the stage addendum's: 1180×820, 820×1180 and 390×844, `mobile: true`, with touch) run units
  20a-20d's Board steps: in both themes at 1180×820 and 390×844, and in dark at 820×1180, where the tabs are drawn and
  the column is not.
- **The layout leg** (new, unit 20a) loads the Board page as a Board guest at nine more of §17.4's sizes, each across
  one of the rules: 640×1024 (an Android tablet upright: tabs, 22 px), 1024×640 (the same sideways: the column at its
  lowest), 768×1024 and 1024×768 ("iPad (gen 5)" and "iPad Mini", upright and sideways), 375×667 (an iPhone SE: the short
  placeholder, two strip lines), 393×659 (an iPhone in Safari), 360×780 (the narrowest phone), and 734×343 and 863×360
  (phones held sideways: one strip line, the sheet scrolled). At each it asserts what `shoot5.js` measures:
  - the layout by the rule: `.bv-side` drawn at 900 px wide or more, the tabs below;
  - the body's computed size: 22 px where the smaller side is 600 px or more, else 20 px;
  - `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`;
  - a 44 px band through every visible control whose band is on screen hits it;
  - the drawn placeholder fits its field;
  - the sheet's last row scrolls into view, and Leave asks in place;
  - no console error.
  - The feed's height at each size goes into the smoke's report as a record, not a pass mark; §17.4's figures are its
    first values.
- **The floor leg** (arch-ux §15.10's init script, which already removes `navigator.wakeLock`, `showModal` and
  `showPopover`) also deletes `Element.prototype.requestFullscreen`, `Element.prototype.webkitRequestFullscreen`,
  `Document.prototype.fullscreenEnabled` and `Document.prototype.webkitFullscreenEnabled` (Chromium keeps the prefixed
  pair beside the plain one, MDN's `api.Document.fullscreenEnabled`). The sheet then has no Full screen row, the take layer no ⛶, and the sheet's
  row reads "This device may sleep: set its screen to stay on in its own settings (Auto-Lock or Screen timeout)." Two
  more runs: with `isSecureContext` defined false by the init script, "This device may sleep: open AGMessage over
  HTTPS."; with `navigator.wakeLock.request` rejecting a `NotAllowedError`, "This device would not stay awake (its
  battery may be low): plug it in."
- **Not in CI:** Safari, Samsung Internet and WebView. The architecture addendum refuses Playwright's WebKit
  (§15.10), so the walk is where they are read.

**The walk** (`docs/DEVICES.md`, on every row, before 0.6.0 is tagged: the stage addendum's unit 32, 34 after the
splice). The chat view's rows, beside the stage's and M's:

- the device's `innerWidth` × `innerHeight` and `devicePixelRatio`, upright and sideways, so §17.4's sizes are checked
  against the device's own;
- the layout the rules draw, upright and sideways, and the feed's height in each;
- 🕐 HH:MM in the hall's zone; the countdown's words, mark and edge;
- a tap on an older message brings its own row; a long press on a message opens nothing of AGMessage's; a long press
  on a card's thumbnail and on a take offers no save;
- Got it, Reply and Answer in words… with the on-screen keyboard up: the replying line and Send stay in view;
- 🔥 Priority sent, and the strip while its message is out of view;
- the sheet: Text size, Clock or countdown, Theme, Full screen where offered (absent on D6), Leave; the wake lock held
  for 10 minutes untouched, or the words naming why (M's row, read here in the simple view);
- dark before the first frame, on a device last used in the simple view;
- the placeholder whole, or the short words;
- the reading distance and the Text size the Board member chose (reading 9).
- A ✕ is a defect fixed before the tag, or a fallback that the row then names (stage §5.15.3). A row with no device
  reads "not walked", which is a fact in the paper, never a pass. A Board device of the owner's below the page floor
  (arch-ux §15.10) is a ✕ that holds the tag until the floor is lowered for it or the owner retires it from the Board
  (owner answer 22).

**What it costs:** nothing on the server and nothing on the wire. On the page: one probe (`fullscreen`), one measured
placeholder, and CSS rules by size. No new verb, no new dependency.

## 7-§9. Tests (adds to the table; the rule for each unit is unchanged)

| Unit | What its tests prove | Red first because… |

## 7-§12. Risks, left for later, and the owner's answers (adds to §12)

### 7-Risks

- **A Board account is a Board member on its On stage page, whatever else it is.** A Tech given `board` for Hall 2 sits
  On stage in Hall 2's Main room. There it may not drive screens, the speaker's screen or people's pages, send into
  another room, or answer someone else's help request, and is not handed the guest code. It keeps the screens, the
  stage and the show network from a side room of the same hall where it is a Member, from another hall and from the
  halls board, because the limit is keyed on the socket's own seat. Help is the exception, by the owner's B1: from the
  halls board too, it answers no request of a room where it sits On stage (Hall 2's Main room, and Hall 2's side rooms
  it reaches only as the hall's crew), while it answers in Legal, where it is a Member, and in a hall where it is crew.
  The Accounts page says so beside **On stage (Board member)**. The owner confirmed the page rule (B2: "An account
  seated on stage gets messages on that page").
- **The admin On stage is limited on that page too.** An admin testing the Board's tablet sees what the Board sees and
  is refused what the Board is refused. The admin page and the support view are unseated and keep everything.
- **"Got all 3" answers messages the person may have skimmed.** That is the act it names, and its count is in its words.
  A message they want to answer apart is tapped first, which brings its own pair.
- **"Answered" counts a reply only when it quotes.** A Board member who answers with a plain message leaves the
  original waiting. That is honest, since nothing ties the two, and harmless: Got it clears it in one tap.
- **Got it rides on `react`.** A page cached across the upgrade still offers the 😊 picker, so its 👍 is the same fact.
  If the backstage team reads a 👍 pill as a mood rather than an acknowledgement, the words of unit 20a ("👍 Margaret got
  it") carry it. A verb of its own (`ack`) is left for later, to be measured first.
- **The strip keeps three lines.** A long 🔥 message is cut in the strip and whole in the feed, one tap away.
- **A Board member can no longer mark a colleague's help request "on the way"** (G2, owner answer B1), from the
  On stage page or, for a Board account, from the halls board. The backstage team answers. The Board's own request can
  be marked sorted or cancelled.
- **A Board member's line replaces the operator's on a countdown screen** (B2, with the switch on). The chip's words
  say so before sending ("Replaces Lectern's countdown line."); the operator's console shows the new content at once
  (`displays:changed`) and can put any line back; the take row names the person. A countdown screen is often the one
  the speaker reads, which is why the switch is off by default and the admin's alone.
- **A Board member's line to everyone On stage is easy to miss on a phone** (B2, with the switch on). It always arrives
  as a card in Shown to you, beside the chat, and never covers or replaces anything (stage §5.9.1's `side`), so a
  researcher's quote or the operator's take stays drawn with its answers. On a phone, Shown to you is a tab ("📺 Shown
  to you · 1"), so the line waits a tap away; its sender reads "👥 Shown to 5 of 6 On stage" only once the cards are
  drawn. Whether a Board member's line should ever cover the chat is left to the owner, if reading 9 finds it missed.
- **Got it clears a message the person may want back** (B4, with the switch on). Its line stays in place with Show;
  a message pinned for the room or for the person is never cleared; Got all N, which names its count, clears N.
- **A guest's pins live on that browser** (a guest's uid is per device). An account's follow the account.
- **A backstage person who meant "for me" pins for everyone.** For the room is the owner's default, so it is first and
  focused. The item says which ("For the room"), the toast says it ("Pinned for the room."), and Undo takes it back for
  10 s. A room pin was 0.5.1's only pin, so nobody loses a habit.
- **A Board page cached across the upgrade still draws 0.5.1's 📌**, which sends the room's `pin`. The server refuses
  it ("Pinning for everyone is for the backstage team.") and nothing reaches the room, but 0.5.1's pin buttons read no
  answer (`app.js:566`, `:808`, `:1196`, `:1209`), so the press does nothing visible until the page reloads. An
  observer's or a Viewer's 0.5.1 page draws no 📌 (`styles.css:1086-1092`); a `pin` sent from one anyway is refused
  with today's "Observers can read but not post.".
- **A pinned question makes the Board's bar taller** whenever one is pinned, for the room or for the person, answered
  or not: about 105 px on a tablet and 101 px on a phone while its words fit the line, about 31 px (28 px) more for
  each further line, and at most 30% of the viewport (§17.4, an estimate, not a measurement). It is the owner's
  "essential for action prompts", it is never drawn twice (the feed holds no copy while it is pinned), and an unpin
  gives the height back.
- **A pinned question behind another pin is a tap away.** The bar shows one pin at a time. The room's pins come first,
  the newest message first, so a question posted and pinned at once leads; an older question pinned later can sit
  behind a newer room pin, with "1 of 2" saying there is more. Left for later, below.
- **More people hold pins of their own.** Every seat may now pin for itself, under bounds that were already set for
  every seat (50 per person per room; the views' 5,000 persons).
- **The pinned bar costs 45-49 px** while a pin exists, and more while it draws a pinned question (above). On a
  phone, with a countdown line, a 🔥 strip and a reply in progress, the feed keeps 385 px of 844 (§17.4).
- **`countdownScreens` names screens to a Board seat**, and the message's `also` names them to everyone in the room.
  Names only, never a link, an id or a token (the ids stay in the server's live entries), and `countdownScreens` only
  while the admin's `screens` switch is on for that person.
- **The strip's "out of view"** relies on `IntersectionObserver` (Baseline since 2019). Without it, the strip always
  shows: §15.5's rule, the safe failure. The pinned bar reads no observer: a pinned question is never in the feed, so
  the bar always draws its answers.
- **"Nobody backstage is online"** reads the room's `users`. A crew member watching the halls board is not in the room,
  so the line can show while someone who would answer Help is reachable. Its words point at Help for that reason.
- **The device's choice does not follow the person to another device** (the owner's "local"). The admin's choice, with
  the lock, is how a choice follows a person.
- **At 70 cm, 22 px text is 14.5′**, under the floor. Text size is in the sheet, and the admin sees it in the support
  view. No measurement on the Board's devices this round (reading 9).
- **An iPad mini's text is small at a board table** (answer 22). Its CSS pixel is 0.156 mm, so 22 px is 15.0′ at 55
  cm, under the 16′ floor. One Aa+ (110 %) gives 16.5′; at 60 cm two steps, at 70 cm four. No web API gives a screen's
  size, so the page cannot choose it: README.txt says so, and the walk records each device's distance and Text size.
- **An iPhone in Safari keeps 659 of its 852 px** ("iPhone 15"): the feed is 313 px with the clock, and 228 px with a
  countdown line and a reply, against the mock's 470 and 385 px at the whole screen. An iPhone has no Fullscreen API to
  win them back, and AGMessage has no web app manifest (`public/*.html`: none).
- **A phone held sideways is cramped:** 116 to 133 px of feed with the clock, 57 to 74 px while replying under a
  countdown line. It works and the sheet scrolls; upright, the same phone keeps 313 to 493 px. Left for later, below.
- **Over plain HTTP, the page keeps no device awake.** The Wake Lock needs a secure context, and one port serves HTTP
  and HTTPS (`server.js:610-612`), with the certificate trusted once per device (`/tls`, `server.js:385`). The sheet
  says "This device may sleep: open AGMessage over HTTPS." On an iPad before iPadOS 16.4 (D1) there is no Wake Lock at
  all, and the words point to the device's own setting.
- **Chrome 84 to 86 drop `inset` and the logical properties**, inside M's page floor, so 0.5.1's Shown to you rail
  would have no size there. Unit M's pairs and the simple view's physical properties close it (§0.2).
- **Every figure of §17.4's matrix is Chromium's**, drawn in Inter. Safari's, Samsung Internet's and WebView's own
  layout, fonts and keyboards are read only on the walk, where a ✕ is a defect fixed before the tag (§17.7).
- **Files and questions posted by On stage seats before the upgrade stay as they were.** Nothing is rewritten, as the
  design's migration rule says.

### 7-Left for later

- A verb of its own for Got it (`ack`, an `acks` field), if reading 9 or the backstage team finds the reaction unclear.
- A per-hall default for the clock or countdown (a hall setting), if the admin sets the same choice for every Board
  member of a hall. Measure how often first.
- "Next" in the countdown, and seconds on the clock: both are motion or width that a secondary object should not spend.
- A seat of its own for presenters, apart from board members (design question 3).
- The observer seat's limit (`SEAT_LIMITS.observer`), seen in passing (§17.1).
- A pin for the On stage group only (seen by the Board, not the room): not asked. The owner's two kinds are for the
  room and for me.
- When a room pin was made (`pinnedAt`), to order the room's pins by it rather than by message: the page orders them
  by message today. Add it only if the backstage team finds the order wrong.
- A pinned question this person has not answered ahead of the other pins of its kind, if reading 9 finds one missed
  behind "1 of 2". No measurement this round.
- Choosing one of several countdown screens in Also on: the chip sends to every screen of the hall showing the
  countdown, and names them ("⏱ 2 countdown screens"). Measure how often a hall has more than one first.
- A Take down for a Board member's line on a screen: the operator's console clears it today.
- A per-hall default for the On stage switches, if the admin sets the same ones for every Board member of a hall.
- A Board member's line to people On stage that covers their chat, if reading 9 finds the side card missed on phones;
  it would need the owner's word, since it would supersede what the backstage team showed (stage §5.9.1).
- A header for short viewports (Shown to you as a header button, the readout on one 48 px row), if the walk finds
  Board members holding phones sideways: about 60 px more feed. No measurement of the posture this round.
- A web app manifest, for an iPhone's whole height from its Home Screen: not asked, and the Wake Lock works in a Home
  Screen web app only from iOS 18.4 (MDN's `api.WakeLock` note, WebKit bug 254545).
- A default Text size per device family: no web API gives a screen's physical size, so Text size stays the person's,
  per device.

### 7-The owner's answers (2026-10-26)

Revision 2 asked B1-B6. The answers are quoted exactly; "Reading" is how this revision applies each, as
`DECISIONS.md` (last section) writes it.

- **B1. Beyond files and questions, should an On stage seat also pin nothing and answer no one else's help request?**
  → "they can can pin messages for themselves. they don't need to answer other people's help requests other than
  interact with the usual chat."
  - Reading: an On stage seat pins for itself only. A pin for oneself is kept for that person (an account's on every
    device, a guest's on that browser) and is never a room pin others see. The room's `pin` is refused On stage.
  - It cannot answer or take other people's help requests: `help:respond` is refused on the server. It still asks for
    help itself and chats as usual. This revision reads "they" as the person, not only the page: a Board account's
    halls board answers no help request of a room where it sits On stage either (§0.1, design §2.5 and §7.2).
  - Landed in: §17.1, §17.5, §17.2, units G2, 9 and 20c. The owner's pin rule (2026-10-27, below) keeps this, confirms
    that the room's pins reach every On stage seat (the bar already drew them), and has a question pinned for the room
    answered from the bar; the owner's answers to its readings (below) take a pinned question out of the feed while it
    is pinned.
- **B2. An account seated On stage holds only messages on that page. Right?**
  → "An account seated on stage gets messages on that page. Anyone in that same room sees the messages (they need to as
  support). An admin can choose if messages can go onto other screens - such as on a countdown screen, or anyone with an
  On stage seat."
  - Reading: what an On stage seat writes is in the room's feed, and everyone in that room sees it. By default it goes
    nowhere else: no screens, no speaker's screen, no people's pages, whatever the account's role. This revision reads
    "nowhere else" as including another room: an On stage seat forwards nothing and uses no Send to or Send back, and
    the room-level allow-list is not read as the admin's per-person choice.
  - The admin may allow it per person, in two separate switches, each off by default and audited: **May send to a
    countdown screen** (the line under the countdown on a `/d/` screen of that hall) and **May send to people On
    stage** (shown on the pages of the hall's On stage seats, as a card beside their chat that covers nothing).
    Confirmed by the owner (2026-10-26): "yes".
  - Landed in: §17.1, §17.6, §17.2, units G, 14 and 20d.
- **B3. Off by default, even in a hall with Stagewatch linked?** → "Clock on by default."
  - Reading: the secondary object starts as the time of day for every On stage seat. The device or the admin may change
    it to the countdown or Off, subject to the admin's lock. The question was about the chat view, so the default is
    the chat view's (the simple view, every On stage seat's unless the admin sets Full); an On stage seat in the full
    view keeps arch-ux unit 31's stage chip.
  - Landed in: §17.3 (`clockFor`'s last step), §17.2, unit 20b.
- **B4. 👍 Got it tells the backstage team, with the Board member's name. Is that the acknowledgement you want, or
  should Got it only clear the message from the Board's own screen?** → "Got it tells the backstage team with the
  members name. Clearing the message is an admin option, off by default."
  - Reading: Got it reports to backstage with the name. Whether it also clears the message from that Board member's
    screen is the admin's setting per person, off by default; off, the message stays in the feed, marked got.
  - With the setting on, a message pinned for the room or for the person is never cleared by Got it, since a pin says
    "keep this" (§17.5, §17.6). Revision 3 read it for the person's pins and revision 5 for the room's, as the plan's
    own reading; the owner confirmed both kinds (2026-10-27: "Correct", below).
  - Landed in: §17.6, §17.2, units 20a and 20d.

  - Reading: Board members may send 🔥 Priority messages; the composer keeps 🔥.
  - Landed in: §17.1, §17.2 (the composer), unit 20a.

### 7-The owner's pin rule (2026-10-27)

Quoted exactly, as `DECISIONS.md` ("Pins") has them; "Reading" is how this revision applies them.

- **The rule:** → "A pin can be for the room (default) (including On stage - essential for action prompts), or
  personal."
- **Confirmed (2026-10-27):** → "A board member cannot pin for the room, only themselves. So pinning for everyone is for
  backroom teams, not the board or presenters on stage."
  - Reading: every pin is **for the room** (the default) or **for me**. A room pin is seen by everyone in the room, On
    stage included, so a question pinned for the room reaches the Board's pinned bar, where it is answered.
  - Personal pins are open to every seat and account that may view the room, not only On stage: backstage, observers,
    Viewer accounts and On stage seats. The admin's support view makes none.
  - On stage seats (Board members and presenters) pin for themselves only, and the server refuses a room pin from
    them: "Pinning for everyone is for the backstage team." The admin seated On stage is refused too.
  - A seat that may post and is not On stage chooses **📌 Pin ▸ For the room** (the default, first) **· For me**, with
    the same pair to unpin. An observer and a Viewer account cannot post, so they pin for themselves only, and the
    server keeps today's refusal of their room pin ("Observers can read but not post.").
  - Revision 5 marked three readings as the plan's own, not the owner's words: a question in the bar draws its answers
    there only while it is out of view in the feed; the room's pins come before the person's own; a message pinned for
    the room is never cleared by Got it, as one pinned for the person was not. The owner answered all three the same
    day (below).
  - Landed in: the reading's top, §0.1 (§6, §7.5), §0.2 (§15.5 and "Amends arch-ux §16"), §0.3, §17.1 (the `pin` and
    `pin:mine` rows, the facts, the catalogue, "The pin doors by seat", the matrix), §17.2, §17.5, §17.6, §9 (20c,
    3a), §10, §11 (unit 20c).

## 7-Alternatives not taken, and why

- **The countdown first and largest** (arch-ux §15.5): not taken. The owner's ask makes it a secondary object, and
  optional.
- **24 px questions and 56 px answers** (§15.5): not taken. The body size at weight 600 and 48 px answers meet the floor
  and the owner's "not huge"; the gap from body text is carried by weight and the word **Question**.
- **Smaller body text (16-18 px) for compactness:** not taken. 16 px is 14.8′ at 50 cm, under the floor; compactness
  comes from removing chrome.
- **Bubbles, left and right** (the messenger convention): not taken. Bubbles spend width and a border per message; the
  author's line says who wrote it in less.
- **Got it and Reply on every waiting message:** not taken (revision 1 did it): 12 controls in the feed outweighed the
  text. One response place per screen, with the second door on a tap.
- **The clock or countdown at the top of the Shown to you column:** not taken. The column collapses to its rail while
  empty, which would hide the object, or would keep the column open for a clock and take 360 px from the chat.
- **The Stagewatch line as a band under the header:** not taken. It moves the feed when it comes and goes, and sits
  beside the 🔥 strip, where it would compete with the Board's own messages.
- **"Stagewatch" as the sheet's word:** not taken. Board members know "the countdown"; the admin's doors keep
  "Stagewatch countdown".
- **Pins for oneself in the Shown to you column** (B1): not taken. The column collapses to its rail while empty and is a
  tab away on a phone; a pin is a message, so it stays with the chat, in the bar over it.
- **A pin door on every message** (B1): not taken. It would add a control to every message and undo "one response
  place per screen"; 📌 is in the row a tap brings back.
- **Clearing a got message with nothing left in its place** (B4): not taken. The feed would close over a gap, and a
  person who wants it back would have to know where it was; one muted 44 px line keeps the place and the way back.
- **Also on as a To: select** (B2): not taken. To: means "instead of here" in the full view (design §7.5); a Board
  member's message always reaches the room's feed, so the chips add a destination and never redirect one.
- **A Board member's line to people On stage as a second chat message** (B2): not taken. They already read the feed;
  "onto other screens" is the page itself, which the take layer is.
- **"🔥 Urgent" and "Send urgent"** (revision 2's suggestion under B5): not taken. The feed's word is "🔥 Priority", one
  word per thing; the pressed toggle says it, and Send keeps its word.
- **18 px in the phone's field beside 🔥** (B5): not taken. The placeholder was cut at 390 px; 16 px still stops iOS
  zooming on focus.
- **For me as the default** (the pin rule): not taken. The owner named the room the default; For the room is first and
  focused, and For me is one ↓ away.
- **One press of 📌 or P pinning for the room at once, with For me behind a second control:** not taken. Both kinds are
  the owner's, so they sit at one door, side by side; the default costs one Enter more than 0.5.1's 📌, and a pin meant
  for oneself never reaches everyone by a press.
- **Two flat items, Pin for the room and Pin for me, in every menu:** not taken. One 📌 Pin ▸ keeps the keep group
  short under the 12-item cap, one key (P), and a mixed state readable as two checkboxes. Where only one kind is
  allowed, it is drawn flat, so an observer or a Board member never opens a submenu of one.
- **A strip of one's own pins beside the room's:** not taken. One pinned place per page, both kinds marked, keeps the
  Board's bar one pin at a time (45-49 px, taller only while it draws a pinned question) and the backstage strip one
  list.
- **A Board member's room pin held for the backstage team to approve:** not taken. The owner's rule refuses it ("only
  themselves"); a Board member who wants the room to see something writes to it.
- **A question pinned for the room answered only in the feed, the bar a link to it:** not taken. The owner calls the
  room's pin "essential for action prompts" on stage, and answered that a pinned question leaves the feed (2026-10-27).
- **A pinned question kept in the feed, its answers in the bar only while it is out of view** (revision 5): replaced by
  the owner's answer 1. The question moved between two places as the person scrolled, an observer decided which, and
  its words were on the page twice.
- **A pinned question in the bar as one cut line, a tap opening it:** not taken. The bar is now its only place, so its
  words and answers are drawn there whole, and the tap is kept for the next pin.
- **Rules by device** (a user agent, a list of models): not taken (owner answer 22: nothing tuned to one device). A
  size or a probe decides, so a device nobody listed draws by what it is.
- **The side column above 600 px** (revision 6): replaced. On the matrix's upright tablets it left a chat of 280 to 474
  px and a field with 0 to 171 px for its placeholder (§17.4).
- **22 px only at 900 px wide** (revision 6): replaced by the smaller side, so a tablet keeps 22 px upright.
- **"Message everyone…" on every device:** not taken. "here" says whose screen it reaches wherever it fits, and the
  label keeps it on every device.
- **Full screen drawn disabled on an iPhone, with words:** not taken. A row that can never act is not drawn, as a
  locked clock is drawn as text (§17.3).
- **A long-press timer of AGMessage's own, NoSleep.js's video in place of the Wake Lock, and Playwright's WebKit in
  CI:** refused in the architecture addendum's §15.10, and not taken here.
- **A layout of its own for a phone held sideways** (the tabs moved into the header): left for later, until the walk
  measures the posture (§12).
